parole.significato: Forms the partitive case of nouns, adjectives, numbers and some pronouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-da (variant of *-ta, whence -ta), from the Proto-Uralic ablative case *-ta.

parole.significato: Forms the short form of the first infinitive of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-dak.
From Proto-Finnic *-ahtadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-ašta-.

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs, often from onomatopoeic stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ait'ak. Dialectally the infinitive stem may also be -a(i)ta.
From Proto-Finnic *-altadak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?].

parole.significato: Forms the impersonal indicative present forms of verbs, appended to the first infinitive.
parole.testo: From earlier -han, -hVn (now dialectal), from Proto-Finnic *-hën, *-sën (passive or reflexive suffix), the same as the third-person singular possessive suffix (see the possessive suffix entry on -Vn). Initial -ta- is from the passive marker *-tta-.
From Proto-Finnic *-as, a variant of *-s (adjective-forming suffix), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-s.

parole.significato: A suffix present in certain first infinitives, short form, the citation form of Finnish verbs.
parole.testo: Variously from Proto-Finnic *-dak, *-tak.

parole.significato: Used for forming nouns from verbs or adjectives.
parole.testo: Conflated: * Proto-Finnic *-ëk, from Proto-Uralic *-ek * Proto-Finnic *-ëh, from Proto-Uralic *-eš; cognate with Proto-Samic *-ës Historically, *-ëk was deverbal, while *-ëh was denominal.
From Proto-Finnic *-dë-.

parole.significato: A suffix for making adjectives from some nouns and verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ëda, from Proto-Uralic *-(e)ta.

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs. The resulting verb often describes a more or less leisurely or long-lasting activity, or an…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-(ë)ldak, from Proto-Uralic *-le-.

parole.significato: Suffix for the genitive plural. Usually preceded by the plural marker -i- or -j-, but may also have a consonant separat…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-dën, probably equivalent to *-t (nominative plural marker) + *-n (genitive marker).

parole.significato: Forms translative verbs from adjectives, meaning "to become (adjective)" or "to become more (adjective)".
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak (stem *-në-), from Proto-Uralic *-me-. Related to Estonian -nema, -neda and Veps -eta. The stem has been reworked considerably in some forms; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more details.

parole.significato: Forms nouns or adjectives of belonging to or possessing a particular quality.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-hinën, a variant of -inen with a -h- (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more details).

From Proto-Finnic *-hën, a variant of *-sën, probably related to *-lën (allative case suffix) and composed of -s- (internal locative suffix; see -ssa) + Proto-Uralic *-ŋ (lative or dative suffix) (with an epenthetic *-e-). The preceding vowel began to assimilate the vowel in the suffix.

parole.significato: A non-productive nominal suffix deriving nouns from nominal stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-i, from Proto-Uralic *-j (specifically its fusion with the stem vowel). Originally allomorphic with -o (< *-oi, in which the *-i- caused labialization of the preceding *a). In many derived suffixes, both variants can be seen, such as in -kki, -kko, both from < *-kka-i. The former
Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-i (from Proto-Uralic *-j (lative suffix)) * from *-ik (from earlier *-jek, probably a combination of the aforementioned and Proto-Uralic *-k (lative suffix)).

parole.significato: Plural marker in nominal forms, except in nominative case, in which it is -t.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-i-, from Proto-Uralic *-j (oblique plural marker).
From Proto-Finnic *-i-, from Proto-Uralic *-j (past tense marker).

parole.significato: Forms primarily transitive verbs describing repeating (frequentative) or continuous (continuative) action.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-idak, from Proto-Uralic *-j-.

parole.significato: Forms some adverbs, mainly with a directional meaning.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-jak, an old *k-lative (-(k)) of *-ja (denominative place name suffix).
From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-te-.

parole.significato: Forms inanimate instrumental nouns from verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-in (instrumental suffix), probably from Proto-Uralic *-ma.
From Proto-Finnic *-in (superlative suffix) (related to Karelian -in), probably from Proto-Uralic *-ma. The oblique stem -impA, -immA is influenced by the oblique stem -mpA, -mmA of comparatives.
From Proto-Finnic *-in (adjectival suffix), a variant of the diminutive suffix Proto-Finnic *-ma.
From Proto-Finnic *-den (genitive plural suffix for some nouns), from the nominative plural ending *-t + genitive ending *-n (with an epenthetic *-e-).
From Proto-Finnic *-inën. Originally also had the variant -nen, but in the standard language, the two variants have been made distinct by giving them different uses.

parole.significato: A suffix for making adjectives from some nouns and verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-isa, possibly from Proto-Uralic. Related to Estonian -s (such as in jõudus (gen. jõudsa) ~ joutuisa), Ingrian -isa, Votic -zõ.

parole.significato: Marker of conditional mood in verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ici- (related to Karelian -si- and Veps -isi-), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-ńće-j, *-nśe-j; derived from the same ending as in -ista (see *-istak).
From Proto-Finnic *-icin. Related to Estonian -si and Livonian -ž. Probably originally an instructive plural form of *-inën (-inen), at least in the non-temporal sense.

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs, often from onomatopoeic stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-istak. Details Certain verbs inherited from Proto-Finnic have had the strong stem generalized by analogy, e.g. vavista (stem vapise-) → vapista.

From Proto-Finnic *-it'ak, from Proto-Uralic *-ńće-, *-nśe- (probably akin to the diminutive ending -ise-). The original stem before preceding endings other than original *-et-, is *-icc- (e.g. *valic'en, *valiccepi, but *valit'ak). However, potential forms were replaced with ones in -nn- by semi-re

parole.significato: A diminutive suffix. No longer productive.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-icca, from Proto-Uralic [Term?]. Cognate with Livvi -čču.

parole.significato: by, through; the suffix of the prolative, determines the channel by which something takes place.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ic'ëC, consisting of the suffix *-icci plus an additional consonant. The additional consonant is found in Finnish, Ingrian and Votic; most other Finnic languages have forms deriving from the vowel-final form. Cognate with Estonian -itsi, Karelian -ičči, Veps -iči, Ingrian -itse,

parole.significato: Forms agent nouns, especially human ones; -er
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ja (agent noun suffix), from Proto-Uralic *-ja (present participle ending).

parole.significato: functionally a conjunction, suffixed to the negation verb to join two main clauses; and (not) (see eikä)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ka, from Proto-Uralic *-ka. Originally probably an emphatic particle.

parole.significato: -y, -ful; a suffix that can be used to turn many, but not all, nouns into adjectives that indicate abundant presence of…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-k'as. Equivalent to -kka + -as.
From Proto-Finnic *-këda.

From Proto-Finnic *-gik, from *-ka + suffix (possibly lative *-ik). Cognate to Estonian -gi, Votic -či. The final -n is by analogy with -kaan. The form *-gik was historically standard, and variation is found in some lexicalized terms (e.g. jotain ~ jotakin). The strong grade -k- was originally only
From Proto-Finnic *-kka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-kka (compare Erzya -ка (-ka), Hungarian -ka).
From Proto-Finnic *-kkëi, cognate with Estonian -k(i), Erzya -ке (-ke). Equivalent to -kka + -i, and originally allomorphic with some uses of -kko (see -o).
From Proto-Finnic *-kkoi. Equivalent to -kka + -i (compare -kki, see -i for more on the duality). Cognate with Estonian -k(u).

parole.significato: Turns a clause interrogative. It is appended to the element of the clause that is questioned most. English equivalents…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ko, probably ultimately from Proto-Uralic *ko-.

parole.significato: Marker of imperative mood in verbs in the third person, first-person plural and second-person plural.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ko-.

parole.significato: used to form the translative case
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ksi, from Proto-Uralic *-kse. Related to Erzya -кс (-ks, translative suffix) and Moksha -кс (-ks, translative suffix).

parole.significato: Forms nouns that signify a place, such as an abode, a house, a land of, a farm, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-la, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?]. Cognate with Estonian -la.

parole.significato: Combined with a place name, forms the noun for the inhabitant of a place; or an adjective meaning "of or relating to (t…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-lainën; equivalent to -la (toponym suffix) + -inen. Cognate with Estonian -lane, Veps -laine. Attested since at least the Bible translation of 1548, which uses it in Mark 7.26 (Grekilainen) and Luke 4.27 (Syrialainen), among other places.

parole.significato: Forms some nouns from verbs or adjectives from nominal stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-lis, probably -l- + -i + -(a)s.

parole.significato: Case suffix of the adessive case.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-lla, from earlier *-l-na, composed of an element *-l(l)- (external locative infix; see -lle) and the essive/locative suffix *-na. Compare Moksha -ла (-la) in фтала (ftala, “behind”).

parole.significato: forms the allative case of a noun, adjective, numeral or pronoun
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-(l)lëk, a variant of *-(l)lën (whence dialectal -len, -llen), which is related to *-sën (illative case suffix) and is composed of -l(l)- (external locative suffix) + Proto-Uralic *-ŋ (lative or dative suffix) (with an epenthetic *-e-). Compare Erzya and Moksha -нень (-neń, allati
From Proto-Finnic *-lta, from *-l(l)- (external locative infix; see -lle) + *-ta (ablative/separative case suffix). Compare -лдо (-ldo) in Erzya васолдо (vasoldo, “from afar”).
From Proto-Finnic *-ma, from Proto-Uralic *-ma (compare Moksha -ма (-ma) in эряма (eŕama, “life”), кулома (kuloma, “death”)).

parole.significato: The suffix of the agent participle.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ma, from Proto-Uralic *-ma.

parole.significato: Forms negative adjectives indicating lack of an action from intransitive verbs; un- -ed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-mat'oin. Equivalent to -ma + -ton.

parole.significato: Forms action nouns (verbal nouns) from verbs, mostly corresponds to the English gerund suffix -ing.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-minën. Equivalent to -m- + -inen.

parole.significato: Forms the first-person plural of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-kma (< *-k-ma), from *-k (marker for the present tense) + *-ma (from Proto-Uralic). Form influenced by me, the first-person plural personal pronoun. In the past tense, there was originally -i- in place of -k- (*-ima > *-imë), but the present suffix has been generalized to all ten
From Proto-Finnic *-mpi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-mpa. Cognate with Hungarian -bb and the element -mb- in Moksha сембе (sembe, “all”) and Erzya омбо (ombo, “other”), томбале (tombale, “beyond”).

parole.significato: Used to form the genitive case.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-n, conflated from Proto-Uralic *-n (genitive suffix) and from Proto-Uralic *-m (accusative suffix).

parole.significato: Used to form the instructive case, usually only in the plural.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-n, probably of the same origin as the genitive suffix (see -n, etymology 1). The instructive singular only exists for a few nouns in modern Finnish (such as jalan from jalka); the case is usually used in the plural (-in).

parole.significato: the first-person singular suffix for verbs
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-n, from Proto-Uralic *-m, probably connected to the first-person singular personal pronoun minä.
From Proto-Finnic *-na, from the Proto-Uralic locative case ending *-na.

parole.significato: Forms action nouns from certain verbs, mainly related to sound, whose first infinitive ends in -sta.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-na, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-na.

parole.significato: The suffix used to form the comitative case. It denotes companionship and ownership, and is written where English would…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-(i)nëk.

parole.significato: Marker of potential mood in verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-në-, probably from Proto-Uralic *-ne. Related to Ingrian -ne-, Karelian -ne-, Votic -ne-, and probably Hungarian -na-, -ne- (conditional mood markers).

parole.significato: First-person singular possessive suffix used with or without minun (the genitive of the personal pronoun minä), corresp…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ni, from Proto-Uralic *-ne. Originally *-mi was the first-person singular possessive suffix used in the nominative singular, but -ni has replaced it, and it is now only found in dialects. Compare Erzya -м (-m).

parole.significato: Forms nouns, mainly bird names (in dialects) and some toponyms.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nka, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *-nka.

parole.significato: The second-person plural possessive suffix. Used when addressing many persons or one person in a polite or formal manne…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ndak (originally the oblique/plural possessive ending with a second-person plural possessor), from Proto-Uralic *-nta[t/k]. The vowel is influenced by the second-person plural pronouns like te. Cognates include Moksha and Erzya -нк (-nk).
From Proto-Finnic *-nnëk.

parole.significato: Third-person possessive suffix, used with the genitive forms of the third-person pronouns hän sg (hänen) and he pl (hei…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nsak, from Proto-Uralic *-nsa[t/k]. In Finnic, this was a third-person plural oblique possessive suffix (i.e. for a third-person plural possessor and all cases except the nominative singular). Third-person singular and plural possessive forms merged quite early on. Adopted in wes

parole.significato: Forms nouns that describe an action.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nta, from Proto-Uralic *-nta. Related to Karelian -nta, Livvi -ndu and Veps -nd, as well as to Estonian -nd, possibly borrowed from Finnish.
From Proto-Finnic *-nta, equal to -na (essive suffix) + -ta (partitive suffix, from Uralic ablative). Cognate with Estonian -nt and Ingrian -nt.

parole.significato: Forms certain nouns, mainly for people.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nta.

parole.significato: Forms factitive verbs from adjectives and names of languages, meaning "causing to become" or "making"; -en, -fy
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ntadak, possibly even from Proto-Uralic *-mta-, but in any case equal to -(e)n(e)- + -taa (the causative form of -eta, with which the stem-final vowel change is shared).

parole.significato: Used to form past active participle forms of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nut.

parole.significato: Forms result or action nouns from verbs.
parole.testo: Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-o (forms action/result nouns), from Proto-Uralic *-w (originally as applied to stems ending in -a). * from Proto-Finnic *-oi (variant/diminutive), from Proto-Uralic *-j (diminutive ending), Originally, the -j labialized the preceding -a- when appended to an a-stem, r

parole.significato: Forms frequentative and continuative verbs, primarily from nouns or verbs ending in -ta or -ata, but also from adverbs.
parole.testo: Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-odak, from Proto-Uralic *-w- (as applied to stems ending in -a-, compare -o). * from Proto-Finnic *-oidak, from Proto-Uralic *-j- (like in *-idak, -ia, as applied to stems ending in -a-, compare -o; the -o- is a re-extraction from the suffix being applied to stems en

parole.significato: Forms nouns denoting the result of the action of a verb.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-os. Equivalent to -o + -s, or re-extracted from verbs with stems ending in o.
From Proto-Finnic *-ot'ak. Roughly equivalent to -o- + -ta.

parole.significato: Expresses that the speaker is surprised at or astonished by something.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-pa (clitic) (see it for more).

parole.significato: Forms the third-person singular indicative present of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-pi, derived from Proto-Finnic *-pa (participle ending).

parole.significato: Forms some nouns, mainly clippings and in slang.
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *-ppa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-ppa, but the narrow distribution and rarity means this is highly uncertain. At least in slang the suffix may instead be a more recent labialized form of -kka.

parole.significato: Forms nouns or adjectives, mostly from nominal stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ra, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *-s, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-kse (compare Erzya and Moksha -кс (-ks, nominalizing suffix)).

parole.significato: Forms ordinal numbers from cardinal numbers, or ordinal pronouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nci, from Proto-Uralic *-mte.
From earlier *-sehen, a combination of the Proto-Finnic illative suffixes *-sën and *-hën.

parole.significato: Second-person singular possessive suffix used with or without sinun (the genitive form of the personal pronoun sinä): y…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ci, from Proto-Uralic *-te. Compare Erzya -т (-t).

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs, chiefly from bisyllabic stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-skëldak, initial component from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-śk- and the latter equivalent to -ella.

parole.significato: The marker of inessive case; in, inside
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ssa, from earlier *-s-na, from *-s- (internal locative infix; see Proto-Finnic *-s-) + *-na (locative case suffix). Cognate with Erzya -со (-so), -сэ (-së).

parole.significato: indicates the elative case of a noun, adjective, numeral or pronoun
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-sta, from *-s- (internal locative infix; see -ssa) + *-ta (ablative/separative case suffix). Compare Erzya -сто (-sto), -стэ (-stë), Moksha -ста (-sta).

parole.significato: Forms adverbs from adjectives describing the manner in which something is done; corresponds to the English suffix -ly.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-stik, equivalent to -sta (elative suffix) + -i (lative suffix). Cognate to Estonian -sti. For the use of an elative ending to derive such adverbs, compare Erzya -сто (-sto), -стэ (-stë), (-сте (-ste)) e.g. in вадрясто (vadŕasto), парсте (parste, “well, good”).

parole.significato: Forms the nominative and accusative plural.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t, from Proto-Uralic *-t.

parole.significato: Forms the second person singular of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t, from Proto-Uralic *-t, probably related to second-person pronouns *tinä, *te.

parole.significato: Forms verbs from nouns, generally with a causative, factitive or instrumental meaning.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak, from Proto-Uralic *-ta- (verbalizer) (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: Forms verbs from nouns with a translative or reflexive meaning.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak.

parole.significato: A suffix for the partitive singular case.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ta, ultimately from the Proto-Uralic ablative case *-ta (compare to Moksha -да, -та (-da, -ta) and Erzya -до (-do)).
From Proto-Finnic *-tadak, from Proto-Uralic *-ta- (verbalizer).
From Proto-Finnic *-ttapa, Proto-Finnic *-tapa (-ttava, -tava), from *-tta- (passive infix) + *-pa (active participle). The weak grade has been generalized like in -va.

From Proto-Finnic *-t'ën. Related to Karelian -ten and Veps -te. Originally from an instructive form, probably by analogy of instructive forms of the second infinitive forms of verbs (such as arvata > arvaten, whence arvatenkin with an additional clitic).
From Proto-Finnic *-t'ik. Equivalent to the abessive case ending -tta + -i.
From Proto-Finnic *-t'ik. Equivalent to -tta + -i.

parole.significato: Indicates lack of something; -less, un-, in-, non-, -free.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'oin (compare Estonian -tu), from Proto-Uralic *-ktama (compare Northern Sami -heapme and Moksha -фтома (-ftoma), Erzya -(в)томо (-(v)tomo), Udmurt -тэм (-tem)).

parole.significato: Suffix for the abessive case: without
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-tta, from Proto-Uralic *-pta.

parole.significato: Forms certain adverbs, typically of manner.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-tta, from Proto-Finno-Permic *-kta.

parole.significato: Forms causative verbs from verbs and nominals.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ttadak, from Proto-Uralic *-kta-, *-pta- (conflated).

parole.significato: Forms the second-person plural of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-kta (< *-k-ta), from *-k (marker for the present tense) + *-ta (from Proto-Uralic). Form influenced by te, the second-person plural personal pronoun. In the past tense, there was originally -i- in place of -k- (*-ita > *-itë), but the present suffix has been generalized to all te

parole.significato: Forms the past passive participle of a verb, which is normally used like an adjective. The English equivalent is normal…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ttu, from *-tta- (passive infix) + an uncertain suffix, probably either *-u or *-ut (compare *-nut). The final gemination may represent a lost final consonant (< *-ttu-t), possibly reflected in South Ostrobothnian dialectal forms like otettuen (< *otettu-ẟ-en, the same dialects a

parole.significato: Forms passive or translative intransitive verbs from transitive verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-tudak, equivalent to -taa + -ua. Cognates include Estonian -tuma.

parole.significato: Forms nouns from verbs. Most common with e- and i-stem verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-u, from Proto-Uralic *-w (originally as applied to stems ending in -e or -ä). Cognate with Estonian -u.

parole.significato: Forms passive (including stative) or translative (including inchoative) intransitive verbs from transitive verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-udak, from Proto-Uralic *-w-. Cognates include Estonian -uma/-uda.
Probably from Proto-Finnic *-ovëh, from earlier *-w-eš and equivalent to -u + -e (< *-ëh), or alternatively possibly from the same stem as -(u)us. Cognate with Livvi -oveh.

parole.significato: Forms nouns from verbs, describing an action, event or a result of that action.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-us, partly equivalent to -u + -s, and partly generalized from (what were originally) -s-derivatives of u-stem verbs (e.g. ihastua → ihastus, menestyä → menestys). Compare -os.
From Proto-Finnic *-ut.

From earlier *-au < *-ao < *-ado, from Proto-Finnic *-o (whence also Finnish -o) plus the inflectional stem of verbs ending in *-at'ak (stem *-ada-). Originally a characteristically Eastern Finnish suffix. Cognates include Karelian -avo.

parole.significato: Forms nouns from adjectives or other nouns, expressing a quality of being that which is described: -ness, -hood, -ity,…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-uc ~ *-uuc; traditionally it has been argued that the short vowel is original, and that the development of the suffix has been significantly influenced by analogy (see details below); however, a long vowel has also been proposed as primary. Analogical developments of the declensi

parole.significato: Forms the present active participle of a verb, which is normally used like an adjective. The English equivalent is norm…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-pa, from Proto-Uralic *-pa. The weak-grade variant *-ba was eventually extended by analogy to all verbs. The original strong grade remains as -pa in a few words (e.g. syöpä, käypä, kaikkivoipa), but these have lost their verbal meaning.

parole.significato: An archaic/poetic variant of the standard third-person present.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-bi, weak grade of *-pi, derived from Proto-Finnic *-pa (participle ending). Compare Estonian -b.

From Proto-Finnic *-hën. Originally a reflexive suffix, which developed into a third-person possessive suffix in Eastern Finnish, Karelian and Ingrian. Thus this was at first found only in the eastern dialects, but adopted into the standard language in the 19th century.
From Proto-Finnic *-k.
From Proto-Finnic *-k, from Proto-Uralic *-k.

From Proto-Finnic *akja (“edge”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *agjō. The semantic shift likely occurred via a derived adjective aajaton (“boundless”) (still found in dialects), originally literally “edgeless”; after the original word was forgotten, aaja (“broad, vast”) was then derived as a back-fo

parole.significato: wave (on the surface of a liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alto, borrowed from Proto-Norse, from Proto-Germanic *aldǭ, whence also allas and Old Norse alda (“wave”). Cognate with Ingrian alto, Ludian aldo, Veps ald.

parole.significato: dry and cold wind, especially in the spring
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahava (compare dialectal Estonian ahav, Karelian ahava, Votic ahavõ, Veps ahau), of unknown further origin. Appears to be analyzable as containing the adjectival/participle suffix -va, but no root word *aha is known. First attested in Daniel Juslenius: Suomalaisen Sana-Lugun Coetu

parole.significato: tight, narrow, cramped (such that it is difficult for something or someone to pass through it; uncomfortably restricted…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahtas (compare Estonian ahas), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *anśtas (compare Lithuanian ankštas), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énǵʰus.

parole.significato: to distress, bother, make anxious, cause anxiety to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahtistadak, equivalent to ahd- (“tight, cramped”) + -istaa (factitive verb)
From Proto-Finnic *ahjo (compare Estonian ahi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *asjǭ (whence Swedish ässja).

parole.significato: akja, large pulk (low-slung boat-like sled), suitable for carrying goods or people in deep snow, usually drawn by a man…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian ahkivo), possibly from Proto-Uralic *aškɜ (compare Northern Khanty өхәԓ (øhəł)). The narrow distribution in just northern Finnish dialects and Karelian could also imply a Sami intermediate, but no related Sami words appear to exist (akio, akia are apparent

parole.significato: to wolf down, eat quickly, gulp, gobble, hog, stuff oneself with, engorge oneself (without regard for table manners)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahmidak, equivalent to ahma (“glutton”) + -ia. Cognate with Estonian ahmima
From Proto-Finnic *ahnas, borrowed from Proto-Indo-Aryan *Háćnas (compare Sanskrit अश्न (aśna, “gluttonous”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ahnëh. Equivalent to ahn- + -e; a variant of ahnas (which see for more).

parole.significato: abandoned swidden; a grassy open or cleared space in a (former) forest cleared by slash-and-burn cultivation, but, due…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *askǭ (compare English ashes and Swedish aska).

parole.significato: to cram, stuff, fill, pack full
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aktadak (“to hang up to dry, to fill a grain-drying cabin”), from Proto-Uralic *ëkta- (“to hang up, to set up a trap”) (compare Moksha афтомс (aftoms, “to set a trap, to cast a net”), Northern Khanty ихәт (ihət, “to hang up (to dry, etc.)”), Tundra Nenets ӈыдась (ŋidasʹ°, “to hang

From Proto-Finnic *ahtëra, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *akšterɜ, but in any case potentially borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?] (compare Sanskrit अक्षेत्र (ákṣetra, “destitute of fields, uncultivated”)) Akin to Erzya якстерь (jaksteŕ).

parole.significato: perch (any fish in the genus Perca)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahvën.

parole.significato: time (inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: to plan to do, intend to do, aim to do; to be going to do, will do
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aikoidak, equivalent to aika (“time”) + -oa.

parole.significato: An intensifier, used to emphasize quality in a positive sense.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Ingrian aima, Votic aimõ, dialectal Estonian aima).
From Proto-Finnic *aina (compare Estonian aina), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian ainat (“always, constantly”) and Lithuanian vienàt (“only”)).

parole.significato: the string in the upper or lower edge of a fishing net or seine; line in a gillnet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aina (compare Estonian ain), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ajna.

From Proto-Finnic *ainaga (compare Estonian ainus, Ingrian ainava, Livonian āinagi, Ludian ainag, Votic ainõgo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz (“sole”) (from *ainaz (“one”), compare Latin unicus (“unique”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ainut. Derived from the same root as ainoa; ain- + -ut.

parole.significato: oar (implement used to row a boat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *airo (compare Estonian aer), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *airō (“oar”) (compare Swedish åra). First attested in 1452 (in the place name Ayrosalmj, modern Airosalmi).
From Proto-Finnic *airu-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *airuz. The -t in the singular forms is likely analogous.

parole.significato: shaft, thill (one of the poles between which an animal is harnessed to a vehicle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aisa (compare Estonian ais), most likely borrowed from Proto-Baltic *ajesa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂oyHsos. The word has also been compared with Erzya ажия (ažija), which may be a borrowing from Proto-Iranian *Hay(H)ša- (from the same aforementioned Proto-Indo-European word).
From Proto-Finnic *aita (compare Estonian aed, Karelian aita /aida, Livvi aidu), from Proto-Uralic *ajta (compare Northern Khanty ощ (osj)).

parole.significato: granary or other unheated farm storehouse of relatively firm build, used as a storage of various goods which are relati…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aitta (compare Estonian ait).
From Proto-Finnic *aivastadak. Cognate with Estonian aevastama, Ingrian aivastaa, Võro aivastama and Votic aivassaa.
From Proto-Finnic *aivo (compare Estonian aju (“brain, mind”)), from Proto-Uralic *ajŋe (compare Hungarian agy (“brain”) and possibly Moksha уй (uj, “brain”)).

parole.significato: to drive, ride, travel (in a vehicle), transport (e.g. in a car)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ajadak (compare Estonian ajama), from Proto-Uralic *aja- (compare Northern Sami vuodjit, Udmurt уйыны (ujyny), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (wujt-)). Probably an old borrowing from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ- or one of its descendants; see the Proto-Uralic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *ajaja. Equivalent to ajaa (“to drive”) + -ja.

From Proto-Finnic *aigasta-aika, equivalent to ajast’ (“from time”, elative) + aika (“time”); refers to the cyclical nature of time. The same derivation can be found in other Finnic languages as well; compare Votic aigassaika (Pummala), Estonian aasta.
From Proto-Finnic *ajo. Equivalent to ajaa (“to drive”) + -o.

parole.significato: husk (of a grain); (in the plural) chaff (inedible parts of a plant whose seeds are eaten as grain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *akana (compare Estonian agan, Livonian agānd, Votic akanõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aganō (“chaff”) (compare Swedish agn). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).
From Proto-Finnic *akka. Northern Sami áhkku is possibly an old loan from Finnish, explaining the irregular correspondence of -a- to -á-.

parole.significato: area (measure of the extent of a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ala; see ala- for more. Already in Finnic, this stem, originally meaning “lower, under” was repurposed as a noun meaning “underside, lower side”, whence “area”, whence the other senses like “domain”, “field”, “sector”.
From Proto-Finnic *alak, equivalent to ala- + -(k) (k-lative singular). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

From Proto-Finnic *ala (compare Estonian ala-), from Proto-Uralic *ëla (compare Northern Sami vuolli, Erzya ало (alo), Eastern Mari ӱлан (ülan), Udmurt ул (ul), Eastern Khanty ыл (yl), Hungarian al-, Tundra Nenets ӈылʼ (ŋil)).
From Proto-Finnic *alaictoin. Equivalent to alaise- + -ton.
From Proto-Finnic *alas. Equivalent to ala- (“lower, under”) + -s (s-lative singular).
From Proto-Finnic *alacin, derived from *ala. Cognate to Estonian alasi, Karelian alasin and Votic alazi. Equivalent to ala- + -sin.
From Proto-Finnic *alaictik, morphologically equivalent to alainen + -ti.
From Proto-Finnic *alaictoin, a consonant-stem caritive derivative equivalent to alainen (“underwear”) + -ton.
From Proto-Finnic *alat'ik, equivalent to ala (“area”) + -ti, literally, “over the (entire) area”.

parole.significato: to begin, start, initiate, set in, be initiated, originate, be originated, take its origin
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alkadak (compare Estonian algama), possibly from Proto-Uralic *alka- (“to begin”) (compare Northern Mansi о̄вл (ōvl, “head”)).
From Proto-Finnic *alku, equivalent to alkaa (“to begin”) + -u.

From Proto-Finnic *alla (compare Estonian all), from older *alna < *ala-na, an archaic locative formed with Proto-Uralic *-na (whence the essive suffix -na) from ala- (“below, lower”). Now analyzed as a consonant-stem adessive of the stem ala-.

parole.significato: a closed body of water, e.g. a lagoon
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aldas (compare Karelian allaš (“trough”)), derived from a root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aldǭ (“trough”) (whence e.g. Norwegian olda and separately also aalto). The ending has probably been modified to -as by analogy with other Germanic loans (such as valas).

From Proto-Finnic *allëk, now analyzed as the consonant-stem allative of the stem ala- (“lower, below”). alle is not attested in Agricola's texts (which instead use ala < *ala-k). alle seems to first be attested short of a century later in 1621.

parole.significato: from under, from underneath, from beneath
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alta (compare Estonian alt), from older *alta < *ala-ta, an archaic inflected form with the ablative suffix Proto-Uralic *-ta onto ala- (“below, lower”). Now analyzed as the ablative singular of the stem ala-.

parole.significato: area, region (any considerable and connected part of a space or surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alovëh. Equivalent to ala (“area”) + -ue. First attested in 1829 in an edition of the newspaper Oulun Wiikko-Sanomia. According to SSA, the form alue may have been adopted in the standard language as a result of Karelian influence (Karelian aloveh), being native only in the 'easte
From Proto-Finnic *alus. Equivalent to ala- (“under”) + -us.

parole.significato: to initiate, get going, set on foot, put into (initial) action
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alustadak. Equivalent to alus (“base, underlay”) + -taa.

parole.significato: bathtub, tub (large container for holding water in which a person may bathe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammëh, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *amma- (compare Erzya амолямс (amoľams), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (ūmp)).

parole.significato: something that widens on a mouth section, like a mouth or a cavity
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammo, from Proto-Uralic *aŋma-w. Cognate to Ingrian ammillaa, Votic ammulla, Estonian ammuli, Estonian ammu, Livonian amtlõ (“to yawn”), Skolt Sami ämmsõddâd (“to yawn”), Western Mari [script needed] (omeštaš, “to talk or move while in sleep or to talk unclearly”), Southern Selkup

parole.significato: Very long ago, in the time immemorial.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammo- (compare Estonian ammu (“once upon a time, long ago”)), probably from Proto-Uralic *amme (“old, previous”) + -oin (temporal singular) (compare Northern Sami oamis (“past, old”), Erzya умок (umok, “a long time ago”), Hungarian ó (“ancient, in previous”)).

From Proto-Finnic *ambudak, of onomatopoeic origin. Cognate to Karelian ammuo, Livvi ampuo, Votic ammua, Estonian ammuda, Eastern Khanty [script needed] (ŏmõj-), Northern Khanty [script needed] (ŏmĭj-).

parole.significato: to shoot, fire (fire a projectile or a weapon that fires a projectile)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ampudak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ampe-. Probably cognate to Erzya аволдамс (avoldams, “to swing”).
From Proto-Finnic *ani (compare Karelian ani, Veps ani), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *an + -i.

parole.significato: eel (any fish in the order Anguilliformes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ankërijas (compare Estonian angerjas), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *angurjás (compare Lithuanian ungurys).
From Proto-Finnic *andëk, equivalent to antaa (“to give”) + -e. Cognates include Võro annõq.
From Proto-Finnic *andos. Equivalent to antaa (“to give”) + -os.

parole.significato: to plead, beg, ask, request, implore, entreat, petition, solicit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *anodak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ana- (compare Erzya анамс (anams, “to ask, beg”)).
From Proto-Finnic *anoppi (compare Veps anopʹ), from Proto-Uralic *ënɜppe (compare Tundra Nenets ӈынаб (ŋinab°)).

From Proto-Finnic *ansa (compare Estonian aas), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ansā (compare Old Prussian ansis (“hook, latch”), Latvian osa), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂emseh₂ (compare Latin ānsa (“handle”)).

parole.significato: to earn, make, win, gain (e.g. money)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian ašnita); originally *asnaita, asnata (attested in 1787). The modern form is probably by folk etymology with ansa (“trap”) (and to avoid the hard-to-pronounce -sn-; compare känsä from earlier käsnä). The Finnic word is probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic

parole.significato: truss (structure made up of one or more triangular units made from straight beams of wood or metal, which is used to su…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ansas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ansaz.

parole.significato: to give [with allative ‘to’] (transfer possession of to someone else)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *antadak (compare Estonian andma), from Proto-Uralic *amta- (compare Northern Sami vuovdit (“to sell”), Erzya андомс (andoms, “to feed”), Eastern Mari омдеш (omdeš), Komi-Zyrian удны (udny), Hungarian ad).
From Proto-Finnic *antaja. Equivalent to antaa (“to give”) + -ja (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *anti, equivalent to antaa (“to give”) + -i. Cognate with Estonian and.

parole.significato: sole, outsole (of a foot or shoe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *antura, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *anduraz. Cognate with Ingrian antura, Estonian andur (“keel”), Old Norse ǫndurr (“snowshoe”) and Swedish andor.
From Proto-Finnic *apaja (compare Ingrian apaja, Votic apajõ), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*abjō) or earlier Proto-Germanic *abjǭ (compare dialectal Swedish ävja, Old Norse efja).
From Proto-Finnic *apara, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse afr).
From Proto-Finnic *ap'ëk. Equivalent to appaa + -e
From Proto-Finnic *apila, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian wobilis (“clover”)).

From Proto-Finnic *appadak (compare Estonian apama, Karelian appoa, Veps apta), from Proto-Uralic *appa- (compare Northern Sami vuohpput, Eastern Mari уваш (uvaš), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (ŋabə[r]-)).
From Proto-Finnic *appi, from Proto-Uralic *ëppe (compare Northern Sami vuohppa, archaic Hungarian ipa).
From Proto-Finnic *apu.
From Proto-Finnic *arina, borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚨᛉᛁᚾᚨᛉ (aʀinaʀ).
From Proto-Finnic *arka (compare Estonian arg), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *argaz (compare Old Norse argr).

parole.significato: everyday life, daily life, normal life (ordinary, mundane or non-special days in life)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arki, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *argį̄ (“wickedness”).
From Proto-Finnic *arkku, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚨᚱᚲᚢ (*arku) (compare Proto-Germanic *arkō and Old Norse ǫrk), from Latin arca.

parole.significato: to pardon, reprieve, grant amnesty to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *armahtadak, from the same stem as armas and armo. Doublet of armastaa (“to love”).
From Proto-Finnic *armas (compare Estonian armas, Veps armaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *armaz (“pitiful, pitiable”).
From Proto-Finnic *armastadak. Equivalent to armas (“dear, beloved”) + -taa. Doublet of armahtaa (“to pardon; to pity”).
From Proto-Finnic *armo (compare Estonian arm, Ingrian armo, Livonian arm, Votic armo). Probably equivalent to arma- + -o.

parole.significato: steppe; flat, vast, temperate but relatively dry grassland
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aro (compare Estonian aru), probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *arɜ (compare Erzya аразь (araź, “lack”), Northern Khanty [script needed] (wuri), Northern Mansi [script needed] (ūraj)).

parole.significato: lot (anything, as a die, pebble, ball, or slip of paper, used in determining a question by chance)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arpa (compare Ingrian arpa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arbaz (whence Old Norse arfr, Swedish arv).
From Proto-Finnic *arpi (compare Livonian ärb), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arwaz, *arwiz (“scar”).

parole.significato: to draw lots, to raffle, to cast lots
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arpoidak. Equivalent to arpa (“lots”) + -oa. Cognate with Veps arboida.
From Proto-Finnic *arvat'ak, probably from *arvo and influenced by *arpa, or the other way around.

parole.significato: value, worth (quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *arvo (compare Estonian arv), borrowed from Iranian. Probably also cognate with Erzya арсемс (arsems, “to think”) and Moksha -ара (-ara) in мъзяра (məzära, “how much”), as well as Hungarian ár, which was separately borrowed from the same Iranian source.
From Proto-Finnic *asëk (“weapon, tool”). Equivalent to asea + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *asëdak, from Proto-Uralic *ëśe-.

parole.significato: position, state, situation (status with regard to conditions and circumstances)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *asën ~ *asëma, equivalent to asea (“to place”) (obsolete) + -ma

parole.significato: to put, place, set, (move into) position, locate
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *asëttadak. Equivalent to asea + -ttaa.

parole.significato: matter, issue, affair, concern, business, subject, case, thing (any abstract thing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *asja.

parole.significato: step, pace (advance or movement made from one foot to the other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *askël (compare Livvi askel), from Proto-Uralic *aśkele ~ *aśka-le (compare Erzya эскелькс (eskeľks), Eastern Mari ошкыл (oškyl), Komi-Zyrian воськов (vośkov), Northern Mansi ӯсыл (ūsyl)).

parole.significato: container, vessel, receptacle (item in which objects or materials can be stored or transported)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *astija. Cognate with Estonian astja, Ingrian astia, Karelian aštie, Veps astii and Votic astjõ.
From Proto-Finnic *astudak (compare Estonian astuma, Karelian aštuo), from the same root as askel (“step”).

parole.significato: attire, dress, suit, raiment, costume, outfit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *asu, equivalent to as- + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *asudak, from Proto-Uralic *ëśew-. Equivalent to asea + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *audër.
] From Proto-Finnic *atra (compare Estonian ader), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *arþrą (compare Old Norse arðr), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érh₃trom.
From Proto-Finnic *autijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *auþijaz.

parole.significato: to help, assist, give assistance, lend a hand, aid
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *abuttadak, derived from *apu (“help”) (whence Finnish apu); equivalent to a(v)u- + -ttaa. Compare Estonian aitama.
From Proto-Finnic *autugas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *audagaz. Compare Gothic 𐌰𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌲𐍃 (audags, “blessed”).
From Proto-Finnic *auvo, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *aują (compare Proto-Norse ᚨᚢᛃᚨ (auja), Old Norse ey (“luck, heavenly aid”)). Cognate with Estonian au, Karelian auvo and Livonian o’v.

parole.significato: ice hole; a hole, either man-made or natural, in the ice of a frozen body of water.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *avanto, equivalent to avata (“to open”) + -nto.
From Proto-Finnic *avara, from the same root as avata (“to open”), avo- (“open”); equivalent to ava- + -ra. Related to Estonian avar, Ingrian avaro, Karelian avara, Livonian ovār and Veps avar.

From Proto-Finnic *avait'ak (compare Estonian avama, Veps avaita, Votic avatõ), derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aŋa- (compare Hungarian old (“to untie, to solve”), Erzya анксема (anksema, “ice hole”), автемс (avtems, “to open”) (from *aŋta-), Northern Mansi [script needed] (āŋkwi, “to open, to take
From Proto-Finnic *apjo, further origin uncertain.
From Proto-Finnic *avoi. Related to avata and avoin.

parole.significato: open (not closed, not physically drawn together)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *avoin, from the same root as avata (“to open”); ava- + -(o)in.
From Proto-Finnic *ehkä (compare Estonian ehk, Ingrian ehkä, Karelian ehki, Livvi ehki, Votic ehči; see for further etymology).

parole.significato: to make it, arrive or reach (in time or before something else happens)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ehtidäk (compare Estonian ehtima), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ešte- (“to make, prepare; to get ready, prepare; to ripen”) (compare Northern Sami astat, Eastern Mari ышташ (yštaš), Komi-Zyrian эштыны (eštyny), the last of these possibly borrowed from Finnic). The shift to the current

From Proto-Finnic *ëktago (compare Estonian õhtu, Votic ohtogo), derived from *ektä (whence dialectal ehtä), likely related to Northern Sami ikte (“yesterday”) (possibly borrowed from Finnic). Replaced in the standard language in the 19th century with ilta, which was traditionally used in the easter

parole.significato: to dry up, run dry, run out
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ehtüdäk, possibly e- + -htyä or alternatively from the same root as ehtiä. Also akin to Karelian ehtyö.
From Proto-Finnic *ektä.

parole.significato: The negative verb or negation verb; not, be not, do not, etc.
parole.testo: The indicative forms are from Proto-Finnic *e-, from Proto-Uralic *e- (negative verb stem). The imperative forms are from Proto-Finnic *älä-, from the Proto-Finno-Ugric negative imperative verb stem *älä- ~ *elä-. Details and cognates Noteworthy forms include eivät (replacing earlier evät by influen
From Proto-Finnic *eklen, of uncertain earlier origin. Seemingly an instructive singular case.
From Proto-Finnic *eklinen. Equivalent to eil- (“yesterday”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *eineh, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚨᚠᚾᛁᛃᚨ (*afnija). Related to Estonian eine.
From Proto-Finnic *eksüttädäk, equivalent to eksyä (“to get lost”) + -ttää (causative aspect)

parole.significato: to get lost, stray, go astray, lose one's way
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *eksüdäk. Related to Estonian eksima, Ingrian eksyä, Karelian ekšyö, Livonian jeksõ and Votic öhsüä.
From Proto-Finnic *elki, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse illr).
From Proto-Finnic *ellä, from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) + -llä (adessive case marker).
From Proto-Finnic *elo (compare Estonian elu, Karelian elo, Livonian jel, Veps elo, Votic elo), equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -o.

parole.significato: liver (one who lives, usually in some a specified way)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *eläjä, equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -jä (“-er”)

parole.significato: life (state of being alive, existence of a person or creature; experience of living, description of (a person's) day-to…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *elämä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *elämä, equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -mä.

parole.significato: to maintain; to support (living of), provide for; feed, provide food (and other necessities of life) for
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *elättädäk. Equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -ttää (causative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *eläbä, from Proto-Uralic *eläpä. Equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -vä (present active participle).
From Proto-Finnic *elädäk (compare Estonian elama), from Proto-Uralic *elä- (compare Northern Sami eallit, Eastern Mari илаш (ilaš), Hungarian él, Tundra Nenets илесь (yilyesʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *emäkko (compare Karelian emäkkö), equivalent to emä + -kko.
From Proto-Finnic *emintimä, derived from *emä (“mother”) (whence emä).

From Proto-Finnic *emä (compare Estonian ema), from Proto-Uralic *emä (compare Hungarian eme (“sow”), Tundra Nenets небя (nyebya)). Mostly displaced in the sense “mother (of a person)” by the borrowed äiti.

parole.significato: mistress, lady (of a household or estate)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *emäntä. Equivalent to emä (“mother”) (archaic) + -ntä.
From Proto-Finnic *enden, instructive singular of ensi-.

parole.significato: to predict, prophesy, foretell, foresee, divine, tell (the future/fortunes), read (the signs)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *endustadak. Equivalent to ennus (“prediction”) (archaic, poetic) + -taa. Cognates include Karelian einuštua, Estonian ennustama, Veps endustada.

parole.significato: to make it (in time), arrive (in time), reach (in time) [with allative or illative ‘to/at/in’] (e.g. when in a hurry)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *endättädäk, equivalent to entää (“to hurry, rush”) + -ttää
From Proto-Finnic *enoi. Equivalent to enä + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *enci, probably from the same root as että.

From Proto-Finnic *encimeinen. Derived from the superlative of ensi (with the superlative ending -in: *ensin, genitive *ensim(m)än) with + -inen. The geminated -mm- is due to the word falling in line with other superlative words in Finnish (see -in) which have been influenced by the comparative suff
From Proto-Finnic *entinen. Equivalent to ensi- + -inen.

parole.significato: to fly (to move in air or quickly)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *entädäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse inna).
From Proto-Finnic *enä, from Proto-Uralic *enä (compare Skolt Sami jõnn, Erzya ине (ine, “large, great”)).

parole.significato: Used to invert the meaning of a word: in-, non-, un-, dis-, mis-, mal-
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *epä. Originally active present participle (-pä) of the negative verb stem *e-; see ei. Cognate with Estonian eba-, Livonian äb, Moksha аф (af), Erzya апак (apak). The original use of this prefix was in words like epäkelpo (originally “that does not suffice”) and epänäköinen (from
From Proto-Finnic *erei, derived from *erä (see erä for more). Cognate with Estonian eri.

parole.significato: batch (quantity of anything produced at one operation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *erä (compare Estonian ära (“away”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *erä (“apart”).
From Proto-Finnic *es, derived from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) (the same root as in että) + -s. Cognate with obsolete Võro es (“if, (even) though”).
From Proto-Finnic *eci (compare Estonian esi), from Proto-Uralic *ede (compare Northern Mansi эла (èla), Hungarian elé).

parole.significato: slug (any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *etana, further origin unknown. Possibly related to Proto-Germanic *etaną (“to eat”) and/or *etunaz (“overeater, glutton”).

From Proto-Finnic *etelä (“south, southwest”) (compare Estonian edel (“southwest”)). Equivalent of esi- (“front”) + -lä, meaning something like “the direction towards which entrances in houses/huts face”; named so because dwellings tended to be built facing south, as it was the warmest direction (as
From Proto-Finnic *eccidäk (compare Estonian otsima, Karelian eččie, Ludian eččida, Veps ectä).
From Proto-Finnic *ettoneh, somehow derived from Proto-Germanic *etaną.

parole.significato: that (conjunction indicating that the subordinate clause is the object of the verb of the main clause)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *että, from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) + -tta (suffix indicating manner). Cognate with Estonian et, Erzya эте (ete), while the Uralic root is also found in Hungarian ez. According to Häkkinen (2004), the original sense was probably “like this, thus”; semantic influence from the simi

parole.significato: advantage, benefit [with elative ‘from’ and allative ‘who or what benefits’] (any condition, circumstance, opportunity,…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *etu. Equivalent to esi- (“front, fore-”) + -u; originally "the area in front of something" (now all but confined to etu-), from which the other senses have developed through figurative use, perhaps already in Proto-Finnic. However, Häkkinen (2004) notes that the abstract senses ar
From Proto-Finnic *etä.
From Proto-Finnic *evä.

parole.significato: provisions (food e.g. for a picnic or journey)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *eväs, possibly borrowed from Indo-Iranian (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more). Related to Ingrian eväs and Karelian eväs.
From Proto-Finnic *hahka (“gray?”), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ačka (“gray? white?”). If so, may be related to Erzya ашо (ašo, “white”).

parole.significato: trammel hook (kitchen utensil used to hang a pot over an open fire hearth and to regulate its height over the fire)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hahila (compare Estonian ahel, Ingrian hahlat, Karelian hoahla, Ludian huahlad, Veps hahl and Votic ahilõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old High German hāhala, hāhal, Luxembourgish Héil, Alemannic German Hääli).
From Proto-Finnic *hakci, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šakče. Cognates include Erzya чакш (čakš).

From Proto-Finnic *halëda (compare Estonian hale, Ingrian haalia), derived from *haljas (whence haljas) by replacing the apparent suffix *-(j)as with *-ëda (-ea). The sense “tepid, lukewarm” developed from the original sense “faded, pale” in Finnish.

parole.significato: ghost, spirit (disembodied soul; the soul or spirit of a deceased person; a spirit appearing after death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haamu. Cognates include Karelian huamu, Votic aamo, and dialectal Finnish hahmo, haamo, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šamɜ. Other cognates include Erzya чама (čama, “face”), Moksha шама (šama, “face”).

From Proto-Finnic *haapa (compare Estonian haab). Further origin uncertain. It is likely in some way related to local Indo-European words (e.g. Proto-Germanic *aspō, Latvian apse), and the Finnic word has been considered a borrowing from an Indo-European source. However, they may all rather be borro
From Proto-Finnic *haara (compare Estonian haar, Ingrian haara, Karelian huara, Votic aarõ), a variant of Proto-Finnic *hara (whence hara).
From Proto-Finnic *haasja, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (whence Norwegian Nynorsk hesje and Swedish hässja).

parole.significato: wound, sore (injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haava (compare Estonian haav), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hawwa-/*hagwa-) (compare Swedish hugg), from Proto-Germanic *hawwą (“blow, hit”) (compare Proto-Germanic *hawwaną).

parole.significato: heron (any wading bird of the Ardeidae family in order Pelecaniformes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haikara (variant of *haikari), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *haigrô (compare English heron).

parole.significato: wistful, longing (full of yearning or longing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haikëda. Cognate with Estonian haige, Võro haigõ.

parole.significato: puff, whiff (act of inhaling tobacco smoke)
parole.testo: From dialectal haika + -u, from Proto-Finnic *haika; cognates include Estonian haige (~ haikea) and furthermore also Lule Sami suoikē.

parole.significato: fresh Baltic herring (Baltic herring that is sold fresh, i.e. not salted, smoked, pickled or preserved in any other way)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Cognates include Karelian hallei, Ingrian haili, dialectal Estonian ail and Votic aili.

parole.significato: to smell, to have a smell/scent/odor [with ablative or allative]; to stink
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haistak. Related to Estonian haistma, Ingrian haissa (“to stink, to smell”), Livvi haižuo (“to stink”), Veps haišta and Votic aisõa (“to stink, to smell”) (Kattila). Probably ultimately derived from Proto-Finnic *haja- (whence haja- and haju (“smell”)).
From Proto-Finnic *haistadak. Equivalent to hais(e)- (“to smell”) + -taa.
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *haisu, equivalent to haista (“to smell, stink”) + -u.

parole.significato: A single, usually thin hair or fiber.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haiva-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hawją (“hay”) (whence e.g. Swedish hö, English hay); modern form and meaning via contamination by haven (“hair”).
From Proto-Finnic *haja- (compare Estonian hajuma, Veps hajeta), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sājan-, *sēaną (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌹𐌰𐌽 (saian), Swedish så).
From Proto-Finnic *haju, possibly equivalent to haja- (“dispersed”) + -u.

parole.significato: to hit something repeatedly (as a nail with a hammer or a log with an axe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hak'at'ak (compare Estonian hakkama, Livonian akkõ, Votic akatõ). Further origin is disputed, with possible links to Uralic (compare Moksha [script needed] (tšakams), Udmurt шуккыны (šukkyny)) and Germanic (compare Swedish hacka, English hack, from Proto-Germanic *hakkōną) words.

parole.significato: to (go) get, fetch, retrieve, (find and) bring
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hakëdak, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *sākija- (later *sōkijaną, compare English seek).

From Proto-Finnic *hako (compare Estonian hago, Ingrian hako, Karelian hako, Livvi hago, Ludian hago, Veps hago and Votic hako), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šaka (“branch (of a tree)”)).
From Proto-Finnic *halait'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *halōną, *halōjaną.
From Proto-Finnic *hala(ga).

parole.significato: the flesh side of split leather (haljasnahka)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haljas, borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian zaļš, Lithuanian žãlias).
From Proto-Finnic *halgët'ak (compare Ingrian haleta, Veps haugeta). Equivalent to halje- + -ta, in which the stem is also seen in halki, halko and halkoa.

parole.significato: piece of firewood cut to about one meter in length and usually split
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *halko. By surface analysis, haljeta (“to split”) + -o.

parole.significato: frost, killing frost (below-freezing temperature that occurs at night during the growing season)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *halla (compare Estonian hall), from earlier *šalna (compare Northern Sami suoldni), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šalnà and Latvian salna).
From Proto-Finnic *halli (compare Estonian hall), from Balto-Slavic; compare Latvian salnis, Lithuanian šalnis (“off-white, roan”).

parole.significato: to rule, govern, reign, administer, command
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haldit'ak, the root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *haldaną and derived with + -ita.
From Proto-Finnic *halpa (compare Estonian halb (“bad”)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *halu, possibly from halata (“to want”) + -u
From Proto-Finnic *halvat'ak. Cognate with Estonian halvama (“to paralyse”). The gradation -v- ~ -p- is analogous (compare halpa).

parole.significato: distant (when speaking of an unspecified period of time; no longer productive as an adjective, see the usage notes belo…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hama.

parole.significato: poll, butt (broad or butt end of an axe head)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hamara.
From Proto-Finnic *hamëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hamiz (compare Old Norse hamr) or *hamô (“shirt”) (compare Old English hama).

parole.significato: tooth (hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hambas (compare Estonian hammas), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źámbas (replacing native Uralic pii < *piŋe; compare Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ, Lithuanian žam̃bas, Latvian zòbs), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos. Doublet of kampa.

From Proto-Finnic *hanhi (compare Estonian hani), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źansís (compare Lithuanian žąsis). Compare Erzya шенже (šenže, “duck”), which was probably borrowed from the same Balto-Slavic source.

parole.significato: fork (of a tree and its branch, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hanka, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian atšanka with an extra prefix).
From Proto-Finnic *hanki.
From Proto-Finnic *hankkidak. Cognates include Estonian hankima, Ingrian hankkia and Karelian hankkie.
From Proto-Finnic *hanko, equivalent to hanka (“fork, forked tool”) + -o. Cognate with Estonian hang.

From Proto-Finnic *hap'oin (compare Estonian hapu), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šappa (compare Erzya чапамо (čapamo), Moksha шапама (šapama), Eastern Mari шопо (šopo)). The declension has been levelled to a plain m-stem with two variants happama- and happame- (see usage notes below for original dialect
From Proto-Finnic *hap'at'ak, equivalent to happa- (“to sour”) + -(e)ta

parole.significato: A single hair, especially a grey hair of an ageing person.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hapci, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ëpte (but see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: fork hoe, hand hoe, hand cultivator
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hara (“branch; forked tool”). Related to Estonian haru, Karelian hara, Veps aro, and more distantly to Northern Sami suorri (“branch of river”).
From Proto-Finnic *harava, derived from *hara. Cognate with Ingrian harava, Karelian harava and Veps harav.

parole.significato: brush (implement consisting of multiple bristles or other filaments)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harja (compare Estonian hari, Karelian harja, Livvi harju), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šerys).

parole.significato: bristle (stiff or coarse hair; a hair or similar filament on a broom, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harjas, equivalent to harja (“brush, crest”) + -s
From Proto-Finnic *harjat'ak. Equivalent to harja (“brush”) + -ta.

parole.significato: to practise (perform or execute a craft or skill)
parole.testo: From harj- + -oittaa, from Proto-Finnic [Term?] (like harjaantua). Related to Estonian harjuma, possibly also hargnema, Karelian harjavuo, harjoitella, Veps hargeta and harjoitada. Probably unrelated to harja (“brush”).
From Proto-Finnic *harjus, probably equivalent to harja + -us. Related to Estonian harjus, Karelian harjus and Veps harjus. Borrowed from Finnic into Russian as Russian хариус (xarius).

parole.significato: tow distaff (a type of distaff used to hold crash)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harkki (compare Estonian hark, Livonian ärk).
From Proto-Finnic *harmaga, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śirˀmas (compare Lithuanian širmas). Erzya шерже (šerže, “hoar, gray hair”) borrowed from the same root.

parole.significato: to stride, to leap (take one long step)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harp'at'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *hardas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harduz.

parole.significato: shoulder (joint between the arm and the torso)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hartija, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Icelandic herðar and Faroese herðar (“shoulders”)), from Proto-Germanic *hardį̄ (“shoulder”). Compare Karelian hartie.
From Proto-Finnic *harva (compare Estonian harv, Ingrian harva), from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Erzya чуро (čuro, “rare, sparse”) and Southern Khanty турәп (turəp, “sparse”)).

parole.significato: cotton candy (US, Canada), candy floss (UK, NZ), fairy floss (Australia)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hattara. Originally meant "rag, tatter".

parole.significato: to bite, take a bite out of, bite a piece off food to eat
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hauk'ait'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *hauki (compare Estonian haug, Veps haugʹ). Likely related to Proto-Slavic *ščuka; the words may be of common substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *habukka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *habukaz.
From Proto-Finnic *haukkudak, ultimately onomatopoeic.
From Proto-Finnic *haikko + -ttaa. The -au- was taken from haukkoa, but -ai- can also be found in dialects.

parole.significato: brittle, fragile, frail, friable, crumbly, rickety (breaking easily in smaller parts, easily broken physically; weak, i…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hapras. Cognate with Estonian habras, Karelian hapras.

Probably Proto-Finnic *ha(a)v- + -us (< *ha(a)vus), related to Karelian hoavo (“sack, bag”), Ludian havado (“sack”) and Veps havad (“sack”) (< *havado), tentatively from Proto-Finnic *haava-. In this case, the word must have originally meant "sack, bag" too, before its shift to refer to the sack as
From Proto-Finnic *hauta (compare Estonian haud), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sauþaz (compare Old English sēaþ).
From Proto-Finnic *hautodak. Equivalent to hauta (“pit”) + -oa.

parole.significato: to observe, detect, perceive, find, spot, notice
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *havait'ak (compare Ingrian havaita, Karelian havaittšuo, Ludian havaitšuda, Votic havattsaassõ); the root is a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hawāną (“to observe”) + -ita.

parole.significato: The mesh fabric of a fishnet or fish-trap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *habas, borrowed from early Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hābaz) (later *ᚺᚨᛒᚨᛉ (*hābaʀ)), from Proto-Germanic *hēbaz. Doublet of haavi.
From Proto-Finnic *habën, possibly a Baltic loan.
From Proto-Finnic *habistak, from an Onomatopoeic root + -ista; the original weak grade -v- has been levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: fresh sprig or small branch of a coniferous tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *havu.

From Proto-Finnic *hek, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sej (compare Northern Sami sii, Erzya сынь (sïń), Northern Khanty [script needed] (ᴧĭw)). The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (het). See hän for more details on history of usage.
From Proto-Finnic *häidelmä (compare Votic edʹdʹõlmo), a derivation of Proto-Finnic *häici (see it and heisi for more). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).
From Proto-Finnic *hëhku.
From Proto-Finnic *hei (compare Estonian hei, Ingrian hei, Karelian hei, Ludian hei, Veps hei). Compare also Old Norse hei (whence Swedish hej) and English hey.

parole.significato: to swing, to sway, to rock (to move backward and forward)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëiludak. Cognates include Karelian heiluo, Veps heiluda. Also compare häilyä, Votic häülüä.
From Proto-Finnic *haimo (compare Estonian hõim), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *šáimas (compare Latvian saime), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos, *tḱóymos.

parole.significato: hay (grass cut and dried for use as animal fodder)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haina (compare Estonian hein, Võro hain), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *śaina- (compare Lithuanian šienas, Proto-Slavic *sěno).

From Proto-Finnic *häici (“flower, inflorescence”) (compare Estonian õis (“flower”)), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian žiedas). The words heitiä and hedelmä (“fruit”) are derived from the same Proto-Finnic root. The modern meaning "viburnum" is a backformation from heisipuu.
Compound of heisi (“string, thread”, dialectal) + mato (“worm”), the initial component from Proto-Finnic *häici (“string, thread”), which is borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saidô.

From Proto-Finnic *heittädäk (compare Estonian heitma, Livonian eitõ, Veps heitta), possibly from earlier *šej-ttä- and borrowed from Early Proto-Germanic *sēja-/*sēje- (later Proto-Germanic *sēaną; compare Swedish så (“to sow (seeds)”)).
From Proto-Finnic *hëk'ottadak, from onomatopoeic root + -ttaa
From Proto-Finnic *heledä.
From Proto-Finnic *helistäk. Equivalent to hel- + -istä, of onomatopoeic origin; compare heleä.
From Proto-Finnic *helkkädäk, of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *heldeh (compare Karelian helleh), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šiltis).
From Proto-Finnic *hellä. Cognate to Estonian hell and Votic ellä.

parole.significato: pearl (rounded shelly concretion produced by certain mollusks)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *helmi, which may be a substrate word.
From Proto-Finnic *hëlppo (compare Estonian hõlp, Ingrian helppo, Karelian helppo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *helpō (compare English help and Swedish hjälp).
From Proto-Finnic *henki (“breath; soul, life force”).

From Proto-Finnic *hëpo, cognate with Estonian hobu, Karelian hepo /hebo, Veps hepo, Livonian ibbi, Votic opo. Possibly a loan from a descendant of Proto-Indo-European *h₁éḱwos, such as Proto-Germanic *ehwaz.
From Proto-Finnic *hëra.

parole.significato: abundant, ample (especially of something flowing, figuratively also of certain emotions such as laughter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *heredä. Equivalent to hera + -eä; compare herua.
From Proto-Finnic *herhiläinen (compare Estonian herilane (“wasp”)), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śirˀšṓ (compare Lithuanian širšė) and derived with *-läinen.
From Proto-Finnic *hërkku. Cognates include Estonian hõrk, Karelian herkku and Votic erkku (Mati), herkku. Probably equivalent to herkkä (“delicate”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *herkkä. Cognates include Estonian erk (“lively”), Ingrian herkkä, Karelian herkkä, Livonian erk (“lively”), Veps herk (“perky”) and Votic herkkõ.
From Proto-Finnic *hërmo (“sinew? blood vessel?”). Furthermore perhaps in some way related to hervota.

parole.significato: pea (plant, Pisum sativum, syn. Lathyrus oleraceus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *herneh (compare Estonian hernes), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źírˀnan (compare Lithuanian žirnis).
From Proto-Finnic *heräit'äk. Cognates include Estonian äratama, Võro heränemä and Veps heraštuda.
From Proto-Finnic *hetki.

From Proto-Finnic *hëpoinën, roughly equivalent to hepo (“horse”) (now poetic) + -(i)nen (diminutive suffix). The weak grade -v- originates from the southwestern dialects, while the expected strong-grade heponen is only found in dialects, mainly in the southeast. Compare cognates in other Finnic lan

parole.significato: slow (at a low speed; not fast, not quick)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hidas (compare Karelian hijaš), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīþaz (compare German seit).

parole.significato: heifer (young female cow, particularly one which has not yet calved)
parole.testo: PIE word  *h₁éḱwos From Proto-Finnic *hëhva (compare dialectal hiehvo, Estonian õhv, Livonian õ’v, Votic õhvõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *éśwāˀ (compare Lithuanian ašva (“mare”)).

parole.significato: fine (particularly slender; especially thin, narrow, or of small girth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëëno. Cognates include Karelian hieno and Veps hen, as well as probably Estonian hõõnukene. The semantic shift from “fine, slender, fine-grained” to “fine, refined, elegant” is common across European languages and probably represents foreign influence in Finnish.
From Proto-Finnic *hëërodak.

parole.significato: silt, fine sand (technical definition: mineral soil with dominating particle size from 20 μm to 60 μm)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëëta, from earlier *šeeta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēda-, *sēdiz.

parole.significato: sleeve, arm (part of a piece of clothing that covers the arm)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hiha, probably from earlier Proto-Finno-Permic *(š)iša. Cognates include Proto-Samic *sësē, Erzya and Moksha ожа (oža).

parole.significato: strap, band; especially one that is made of leather or other strong material
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hihna, from earlier *ši(k)šna, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šikšnà (“strap, belt, leather”)), if the Baltic and Finnic words are not from a substrate. Related to Erzya кшна (kšna, “strap”) (of the same origin).
From Proto-Finnic *hihtädäk (compare Veps hihtta), probably ultimately onomatopoeic.

parole.significato: coal (black or brownish black rock formed from prehistoric plant remains)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hiili, of unknown further origin. * (carbon): Compare German Kohlenstoff (with Kohle (“coal”)).

parole.significato: mouse (used rather indiscriminately for a number of small mouse-resembling rodents mostly in the zoologic family Murida…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hiiri (compare Estonian hiir), from Proto-Uralic *šiŋere (compare Erzya чеерь (čejeŕ), Northern Mansi таӈкер (taňker), Hungarian egér). * (computer mouse): Semantic loan from English mouse.
From Proto-Finnic *hiici.
From Proto-Finnic *hiiva, with multiple theories of origin (see entry).
From Proto-Finnic *hiki, of unknown further origin. Cognate with Estonian higi.
From Proto-Finnic *hikinen. Equivalent to hiki (“sweat”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *hilja, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *silāną.
From Proto-Finnic *hiljada, the partitive singular of *hilja (whence dialectal hilja).
From Proto-Finnic *hiljainën. Equivalent to hilja + -inen.

From Proto-Finnic *hilla (compare Karelian hillo, hilloi, Ludian hillo, Veps hil). Originally probably meaning "mash, jam, purée" (like in the derived term hillo), with the current meaning “cloudberry” being a back-formation of hillamarja.
From Proto-Finnic *himo (compare Estonian himu, Veps himo, Võro himo).

parole.significato: price (cost to purchase; cost of an action)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hinta (compare Estonian hind), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śímta (compare Lithuanian šimtas (“hundred”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm (“hundred”), and thereby a distant doublet of sata. However, the Baltic etymology is uncertain, since the semantic develop

parole.significato: to grind, sharpen, whet (make sharper by rubbing against something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hijodak (compare Estonian ihuma, Livonian jõ’vvõ, Veps hijoda), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šiŋa- (compare Northern Sami sadjit (“to hone, file”), Skolt Sami sââjjad (“to hone, grind, file”), Erzya човамс (čovams), Moksha шовамс (šovams, “to hone, file, grind”), Eastern Mari шумем (š
From Proto-Finnic *higot'ak. Equivalent to hiki (“sweat”) + -ota. Related to Veps higota. Compare also Veps higo (“sweat”, noun).
From Proto-Finnic *hipjä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hiwją. Cognate to English hue.
From Proto-Finnic *hirmu (compare Estonian hirm, Livonian irm), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian širmuļi, Lithuanian šiurpus). Probably also related to hirveä.

parole.significato: to neigh, to whinny, to make the sound of a horse
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hirnudak, originally onomatopoetic.

parole.significato: log, timber (heavy wooden beam used or carved ready for use in construction of a log house or similar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hirci (compare Ingrian hersi, Karelian hirsi, Estonian hirs, Votic irsi), borrowed from Proto-Slavic *žьrdь (compare Russian жердь (žerdʹ)).

From Proto-Finnic *hirvi (compare Estonian hirv, Veps hirbʹ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *širˀwis (compare Old Prussian sirwis (“deer”), Proto-Balto-Slavic *śírˀnāˀ (“roe deer”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂- (“head, top, horn”) (compare Latin cervus). Doublet of sarvi.
From Proto-Finnic *hiuka (“hunger, starvation”) (compare Ingrian hiuvata, Karelian hiuvata, Votic iukaa (“to torment”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sūganą.
From Proto-Finnic *hiukka.

parole.significato: a single hair, strand of hair (on a human head)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hibus, equivalent to hipiä (“smooth skin, scalp”) + -us.
From Proto-Finnic *hoikka. Cognate with Karelian hoikka and Veps hoik.

parole.significato: to nurse, care for, take care of, look after
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoitadak (compare Estonian hoidma), possibly borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *śćaHyáH (if so, distantly related to suoja).

parole.significato: mold, mildew (furry or woolly growth of tiny fungi)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *homëh (compare Karelian homeh, Votic õmõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swammaz.

parole.significato: A large, old pine tree with a straight trunk.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *honka, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Estonian hong.
From Proto-Finnic *hopëda (compare Estonian hõbe), from earlier *šopeta, originally meaning "soft", possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *samftijaz (“soft”).
From Proto-Finnic *hopëdainen, equivalent to hopea (“silver”) + -inen.

parole.significato: to stagger, totter, lurch, teeter, sway (also figuratively)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *horjudak. Cognate with Ingrian horjua, Karelian horjuo and Votic õrjua (Mati).

From Proto-Finnic *horma. Has many dialectal variants (e.g. horma, hormu, forsma). The intrusive -s- is unexplained. Also related to Karelian horma, the initial component in Veps hormhein and dialectal Estonian vorm, vormikene (“meadowsweet”).
From Proto-Finnic *hosja.

parole.significato: to rush (to perform a task with great haste, with a suggestion of carelessness)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hosudak (compare Karelian hosuo and dialectal Estonian õsuma (“to reap grain with a scythe”)).

parole.significato: to tempt; to draw, attract or allure
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian houkuttoa, Livonian uktõ and dialectal Estonian augutama).

From Proto-Finnic *humar (compare Estonian uhmer), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šu(š)mar ~ *šuwar (compare Erzya човар (čovar), Eastern Mari шуар (šuar)). The medial -h- is irregular and might have developed through an itself irregular lengthening of the -u- vowel.

parole.significato: swidden; woodland cleared and burned for cultivation according to slash-and-burn agriculture
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hukta, probably borrowed from Proto-Iranian [Term?] (compare Persian سوختن (sôxtan, “to burn”)). Related also to Erzya чувто (čuvto, “tree”), Moksha шуфта (šufta, “tree”), but these were probably borrowed separately from the same source.
From Proto-Finnic *hoi ~ *hui, from Proto-Finno-Permic *šoje ~ *šuje.

parole.significato: to call out, holler (to vocalize audibly; announce)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huik'at'ak, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: very large; immense, enormous, huge, whopping, incomparable
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huikëda, the root of which is possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką. Related to Karelian huikie (“shameful”) and Veps huiged (“indecent, shameful”).
From Proto-Finnic *huimat'ak, equivalent to huima- + -ta

parole.significato: to lose, misplace (place somewhere and forget, so that one can no longer find it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huk'at'ak. Equivalent to huka- (“waste; being misplaced”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *hukka (“loss, ruin”), with uncertain links to Permic and Germanic languages. The meaning "wolf", characteristic of the Eastern Finnish dialects, is originally euphemistic.
From Proto-Finnic *hukkudak. Equivalent to hukka- (“loss; being misplaced”) + -ua.

parole.significato: grain that is rejected in threshing due to lightness of seeds
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *hulëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hul- (compare English hull).
From Proto-Finnic *huljudak. According to SSA, probably sound-symbolic.
From Proto-Finnic *hullu.
