parole.significato: selvage (edge of a woven fabric, where the weft threads run around the warp, creating a finished edge)
parole.testo: From hulpa + -io, from Proto-Finnic *hulpa.
From Proto-Finnic *humala, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*humalā) (compare Swedish humle), itself probably borrowed from Proto-Slavic *xъmelь.
From Proto-Finnic *hoogat'ak (compare Estonian hoog, Ingrian hoovvata, Karelian huokavuo, Votic oogõtõ), probably ultimately of imitative origin.
From Proto-Finnic *hookjas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hōgjaz. Compare huojentaa, huojentua.
From Proto-Finnic *hookëda. Equivalent to huojas + -ea.
From Proto-Finnic *hooku, equivalent to huoata (“to yawn”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *hooli (compare Estonian hool, Ingrian hooli, Karelian huoli), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian žala (“damage, harm”)).

parole.significato: to notice, take notice, take note, note, see, discern, tell, spot
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hooma(i)t'ak, possibly borrowed from Germanic.
From Proto-Finnic *hoomën.

parole.significato: room (separate part of a building, enclosed by walls, a floor and a ceiling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoonëh (compare Estonian hoone).

parole.significato: bad, poor (of low quality, not very useful or effective; incompetent, unskilled, untalented)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoono.

parole.significato: felt (matted, non-woven material of wool or other fibre)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoopa, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚦᛟᛒᛟ (*þōbō), from Proto-Germanic *þōbô, whence Old Norse þófi (“felt”). Cognate with Ingrian hoopa, Karelian huopa, Veps hob.
From Proto-Finnic *hoora, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *hōrǭ (“whore, adultress”).
From Proto-Finnic *hootava.
From Proto-Finnic *hootra, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą.

parole.significato: to back water, back the oars
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoobat'ak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *hupa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *šupa (compare Erzya чова (čova), Moksha шуваня (šuvanä, “thin”), Eastern Mari шуэ (šue)).

parole.significato: to hum, whirr, buzz, drone (to produce a low-pitched sound like that of a smoothly running motor)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huristak, from an onomatopoeic root; hur- + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *hurma. Cognates include Estonian urm (“blood”), Karelian hurmata (“to stun”), Livonian ūrmatõ (“to stun”).
From Proto-Finnic *hurskas (compare Karelian hurskas (“brisk, quick”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hurskaz.

parole.significato: dog, hound; especially a large one
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hurtta, borrowed from Slavic, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *xъrtъ.
Probably a variant of hutra, from Proto-Finnic *hutra.
From Proto-Finnic *hutja. According to SSA, probably from the same onomatopoeic or sound-symbolic root as hutkia (“to whack”) and dialectal hutjua (“to swing, shake”).

parole.significato: porridge (especially one made of flour as opposed to groats), gruel
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huttu, possibly an old past passive participle of a verb borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian šusti (“to stew”)). Cognate to Karelian huttu, Ludian huttu. May also be related to Proto-Permic *šu̇d (“soup”), if it is derived from the same Baltic root.
From Proto-Finnic *huudëh.

parole.significato: to rinse, wash (to move by the force of water in motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huhtodak (compare Ingrian huuhtoa, Livonian ū’dõ), from Proto-Finno-Permic *šukštɜ- (compare Erzya кштамс (kštams), Moksha штамс (štams)).

parole.significato: lip, labium (either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huuli (compare Estonian huul, Veps hulʹ, Votic uuli), from Proto-Uralic *šuwle (compare Eastern Khanty лул (lul)).
From Proto-Finnic *hühmä, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *šɜšmɜ. Compare Erzya шушмо (šušmo, “snowbank”).

parole.significato: seal (common language term for smaller pinnipeds; used mainly of earless or true seals but sometimes also covering the…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hülgeh (see it for more details). Cognate with Estonian hüljes.

parole.significato: to shake, jiggle, wiggle (to move softly from side to side)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hüllüdäk. According to SSA, of sound-symbolic origin; possibly a blend from heilua + lyllyä.

parole.significato: to reject, turn down, discard (e.g. a plan)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hülgäit'äk (compare Ingrian hylätä, Ludian hülgäitä, Veps hül’gäita).
From Proto-Finnic *hümistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä (compare Karelian hymissä, Estonian ümisema and likewise onomatopoeic English hum, Middle High German hommen)

parole.significato: continuative of hypätä (“to jump, hop”); to jump (around), hop (around), skip; to jump (up and down), bounce
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hüppeidäk. Equivalent to hypätä (“to jump”) + -iä (continuative verb).

From Proto-Finnic *hüp'äit'äk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *huppōną, *huppijaną (“to move up and down; hop”), compare German hüpfen (“to hop”). Compare also Erzya чопавтомс (čopavtoms, “to dive”).

parole.significato: to purr, whirr, hum, drone (make a quiet, continuous sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hüristäk, from an onomatopoeic root hyr- also seen in hyrrätä. Contains the derivational suffix + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *hüdistäk, from a sound-symbolic root (per SSA) + -istä; compare Karelian hytissä, Estonian hüdisema and further hyllyä, tytistä.
From Proto-Finnic *hüvüc. Equivalent to hyvä (“good”) + -yys (“-ness”).
From Proto-Finnic *hüvä (compare Estonian hea, Veps hüvä). Likely further related to Sami words like Northern Sami savvit (“to heal”); ultimate origin unknown.
From Proto-Finnic *hüü.
From Proto-Finnic *hüüpi- (“Eurasian eagle owl”).

parole.significato: to freeze (lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hüütädäk, equivalent to hyy (“slush”) (dialectal) + -tää. Compare Karelian hyyteä.
From Proto-Finnic *höö, variant of *hek.
From Proto-Finnic *hähnä. Possibly related to Estonian rähn, which may also be a metathesized form of Proto-Finnic *närhi.

häikä- + -äistä, from the stem *häikä-, akin to Ingrian häjätä, Karelian häijätä, Votic häigete (probably borrowed from another Finnic language), from Proto-Finnic *häikä-. If it goes back to a root *häi-, it could possibly be a loan from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian seja), an etymology ori
From Proto-Finnic *häilüdäk.
From Proto-Finnic *häirit'äk, from earlier *šajri-/*šäjri-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sairijaną (compare Icelandic særa).

parole.significato: fumes rich in carbon monoxide caused by partial or incomplete combustion
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häkä (compare Estonian hägu, Ingrian hägä); possibly also cognate with Northern Sami ciehka.

parole.significato: to clear, disperse, dissipate, disappear (of clouds, smoke, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hälbet'äk. Related to Estonian hälbima and Karelian hälvetä. The weak grade -v- has been applied to all forms.
From Proto-Finnic *hämä-. Cognates include Estonian ämblik, Ingrian hämö, Karelian hämehikki, Livvi hämähäkki, Ludian hämähäkki, Veps hämähouk and Võro hämbläne.

parole.significato: he, she, one, they sg (only of a human being; gender-neutral)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hän (compare Estonian enda, Veps hän), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sän (compare Northern Sami son, Erzya сон (son), Komi-Zyrian сійӧ (sijö), Hungarian ő). In practically all dialects (except potentially Ingrian Finnish), se is the most common third-person pronoun for people, and this

parole.significato: a narrow tail (e.g., of most mammals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häntä.

parole.significato: shame (uncomfortable or painful feeling; something to regret; reproach incurred or suffered; dishonour; ignominy; deris…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häpedä (compare Estonian häbe, Votic äppiä), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hawiþą (compare Old Norse háð (“mockery”)).
From Proto-Finnic [Term?], if related to Estonian apa, app (“drink”).
From Proto-Finnic *häpü, equivalent to häpe- (“shame”) + -y.
From Proto-Finnic *häristäk, from an onomatopoeic root. här- + -istä
From Proto-Finnic *härkä (compare Estonian härg), probably borrowed from Baltic. * (Taurus): Semantic loan from Latin taurus. * (Ox in the Chinese zodiac): Semantic loan from Chinese 牛宿 (Niúxiù).
From Proto-Finnic *härmä (compare Estonian härm, Karelian härmä, Livonian ǟrma; from earlier *šärmä), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian sarma, Lithuanian šarma).
From Proto-Finnic *härnät'äk, possibly originally ideophonic. Cognates include Karelian härnätä, Votic ärnähtellä (Kattila), northeastern Estonian ärnima.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Cognate with Ingrian hässiä, Karelian häššie and dialectal Estonian häss (“vulva”).
From Proto-Finnic *hätä (compare Estonian häda, Ludian hädä, Veps häda), borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *sētā (later *sētō, compare Swedish såt, försåt (“ambush”), Old English sǣt (“ambush”)).
From Proto-Finnic *hävittädäk. Equivalent to hävitä (“to be lost”) + -ttää (causative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *hävit'äk. Related to Estonian hävima, Ingrian hävitä, Karelian hävitä and Ludian hävitä.

parole.significato: to drive away (force someone or something to leave)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häätädäk. Cognate with Karelian heäteä, Ludian hiättä, Veps häta, Votic äävüttää (Mati), and possibly Southern Sami sietedh (from Proto-Samic *seatētēk).
From Proto-Finnic *heühen (compare Karelian heyhen, Veps hüuneh), further also akin to Proto-Samic *sëvsëm.

parole.significato: vapor (gaseous state of a substance that is normally a solid or liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *heürü. Related to Ingrian höyry, Karelian höyry and Ludian höur.
From Proto-Finnic *igen (compare Estonian ige), from Proto-Uralic *jiken (compare Hungarian íny).

parole.significato: yoke (bar or frame by which two draught animals are joined at their necks)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *iges, borrowed from Proto-Slavic *jьgo (gen. *jьga, *jьžese; compare Old East Slavic иго (igo), gen. ига (iga), *ижесе (*ižese)), from earlier *jъgo (gen. *jъga, *jъgese), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *juga-, from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm.

Probably the instructive singular of obsolete ihta (“opportunity, chance”), from Proto-Finnic *ihta, possibly from Indo-Iranian. The regular standard form would be ihdan, attested fragmentarily in Old Literary Finnish; variants of this like ihran and ihlan are also found in some dialects. The form i

parole.significato: marvel, wonder, prodigy (something that causes amazement or awe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *imeh (compare Estonian ime, Votic ime, Karelian imeh), derived from Proto-Uralic *jemä (compare Northern Sami amas, Northern Khanty йєм (jêm, “prohibited; sacred”)).
From Proto-Finnic *imehteldäk, a derivative based on *imeh (“wonder”) (compare ihme). Remains analyzable as ihme + -tellä.

Haplologically from earlier inhiminen (compare inhimillinen), from Proto-Finnic *inhiminen (compare Estonian inimene, Karelian ihmini), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *jenše (compare Erzya инже (inže, “guest”)); alternative explanations also exist.
From Proto-Finnic *iho (compare Estonian ihu), probably from Proto-Uralic *iša (compare Moksha ёжа (joža, “skin”), Erzya ёжо (jožo, “surface”)).

parole.significato: fat (adipose tissue of an animal, especially of a pig)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *icra (compare Karelian isra, Veps izr), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *instraz (compare Icelandic ístra, Swedish ister).
From Proto-Finnic *iki, equivalent to ikä (“age”) + -i.

parole.significato: age (time which someone or something has been alive or existed)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ikä (compare Estonian iga), from Proto-Uralic *jekä (compare Northern Sami jahki, Erzya ие (ije, “year”), Eastern Mari ий (ij), Hungarian év).
From Proto-Finnic *ikähinen, equivalent to ikä (“age”) + -(h)inen.
From Proto-Finnic *ikäbä. Equivalent to ikä (“age; (long) time”) + -va.
ilja- + -nne, from Proto-Finnic *iljen.
From Proto-Finnic *ilkëda, probably borrowed (and derived) from Proto-Germanic *ilhilaz (“bad, evil”). Cognates include Karelian ilkie, Estonian ilge, English ill.
From Proto-Finnic *ilma (“air, sky, weather”), from Proto-Uralic *jilma (“sky, weather, god”).
From Proto-Finnic *ilman; the instructive or genitive singular of ilma.

From Proto-Finnic *ilo (compare Estonian ilu (“beauty”), Karelian ilo, Ludian ilo, Veps ilo), of unknown further origin, but possibly also cognate with Livonian īla (“nature”) and Pite Sami âllo (“urge”).
From Proto-Finnic *ilta. Introduced into the standard language from Eastern Finnish in the 19th century, replacing the Western Finnish word ehtoo.

parole.significato: lynx (any of the four species in the genus Lynx)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ilbes.
From Proto-Finnic *imelä (Proto-Finnic *imä + -lä).
From Proto-Finnic *imettädäk, equivalent to imeä (“to suck”) + -ttää.
From Proto-Finnic *imedäk (compare Estonian imema, Karelian imie), from Proto-Uralic *ime- (compare Hungarian emik).
From Proto-Finnic *inha (compare Estonian inetu, Ingrian inho, Karelian inho, Votic inõa).

parole.significato: to buzz on a relatively high frequency, as a mosquito
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *inistäk, of onomatopoeic origin.
From *irta + -i (irto- < *irtoi < *irta-i), from Proto-Finnic *irta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian irti (“to fall apart, to separate”)).

parole.significato: in a grin or grimace, grinning or grimacing
parole.testo: Inessive singular of the root *irvi, from Proto-Finnic *irvi.
From Proto-Finnic *icintimä, derived from *icä (“father”) (whence isä).
From Proto-Finnic *iskedäk (“to hit, strike; to ply (thread)”).
From Proto-Finnic *istudak (compare Karelian istuo, Estonian istuma, Ludian ištuda), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *isɜ- (compare Erzya озамс (ozams)).

parole.significato: to plant (place a seed or plant in soil or other substrate in order that it may live and grow)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *istuttadak, equivalent to istua (“to sit”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: master, lord, householder (of a household or estate)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *icäntä. Equivalent to isä (“father”) + -ntä.

parole.significato: any small insect, especially a stinging one like a mosquito
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *itikka. Compare dialectal Estonian itikad, Ingrian itikka, Karelian itikkä, Livvi itikky, Votic itikkõ.
From Proto-Finnic *itkedäk. Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: crier, weeper (one who cries or weeps)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *itkejä. Equivalent to itkeä (“to cry, weep; to lament”) + -jä (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *itku. Equivalent to itkeä (“to cry”) + -u.

parole.significato: oneself, itself (used to emphasize the person or thing acting as the headword)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *icek ~ *ic'ek (compare Estonian ise), from Proto-Uralic *iće (compare Northern Sami ieš, Erzya эсь (eś, “own, oneself”), Eastern Mari шке (ške), Udmurt ачим (aćim), Northern Mansi [script needed] (is), Northern Khanty ис (is, “soul”)). The original meaning in Proto-Uralic was “sha

parole.significato: sprout (a germinated seed or grain; the first phase of a plant growing from a seed or grain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *itu (compare Estonian idu), derived from itää; equivalent to itää (“to sprout, germinate”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *itä, from Proto-Uralic *itä- (“to appear”) (whence also itää); the sun rises (appears) in the east.
From Proto-Finnic *itädäk, from Proto-Uralic *itä- (“to appear, become visible”) (compare Northern Khanty єтты (êtty, “to grow”), Nganasan ӈәтәдя (ŋətədja)).
From Proto-Finnic *igäk'äs, equivalent to ikä (“age”) + -käs.

From Proto-Finnic *ja (compare Estonian ja, Ingrian ja, Livonian ja, Votic ja), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *jahw (“and”) (compare Gothic 𐌾𐌰𐌷 (jah), Old High German ja, joh). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: to divide, split into parts, cut up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jakadak (compare Estonian jagama), from Proto-Uralic *jëk(k)a- ~ *jak(k)a- (compare Northern Sami juohkit, Erzya явомс (javoms), Udmurt люкыны (ľukyny) and possibly Tundra Nenets яхӑсь (yaxăsʹ°)).

parole.significato: division, distribution, sharing, dealing (an act of division etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jako. Equivalent to jakaa (“to divide, distribute, share”) + -o.

parole.significato: to manage, to get by, to have strength, energy, or stamina
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jaksadak (compare Estonian jaksama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jaksa- / *jëksa- (“to untie, to unfasten; to take off (clothes)”) (compare Erzya юксемс (juksems, “untie”), Udmurt юскыны (juskyny)).

parole.significato: runner (mechanical part in a vehicle or other structure intended to slide against a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jalgas, equivalent to jalka (“foot”) + -s.
From Proto-Finnic *jalaga (compare Estonian jalakas).

parole.significato: foot, leg; a lower supporting limb of a human or animal
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jalka (compare Estonian jalg, Livonian jālga), from Proto-Uralic *jalka (compare Northern Sami juolgi, Erzya ялго (jalgo, “on foot”), Eastern Mari йол (jol), Hungarian gyalog (“on foot”)).
From Proto-Finnic *jalkaicin, equivalent to jalka (“foot”) + -isin.

From Proto-Finnic *jalo (compare archaic Estonian jalu (“fierce”), Karelian jalo (“strong, powerful; large; vicious”), Veps jalo (“brisk”)). The original sense of the Finnic word is not entirely clear, but was perhaps “large, bulky”.

parole.significato: seam, joint (point where two things meet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jama, probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *yámHas.

parole.significato: thirst (sensation of dryness, craving for liquids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jano, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Estonian janu, Karelian jano, Votic jano.

parole.significato: A line of fishnets that are connected together.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jata.

parole.significato: to continue, keep on, go on, proceed, keep going; to resume
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jatkadak.

parole.significato: to grind, mill, crush (reduce to smaller pieces, especially by lateral crushing motions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jauhadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *jaŋša- (compare Erzya яжамс (jažams)).
From Proto-Finnic *jauhattadak, equivalent to jauhaa (“to grind”) + -ttaa

parole.significato: flour (milled grain, cereal or other foodstuff)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jauho. Equivalent to jauhaa (“to grind”) + -o.

parole.significato: already (prior to some time; so soon)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jo (compare Estonian ju, Ingrian jo, Karelian jo, Livonian jo, Veps jo, Votic jo), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *jau (*iou) (compare Latvian jau, Lithuanian jaũ). Theories about a Germanic origin, often repeated in earlier sources, have issues; see the Proto-Finnic en

parole.significato: to lead (guide or conduct with the hand, or by means of some physical contact connection)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *johtattadak. Equivalent to johtaa + -ttaa. Cognate with Estonian juhatama.

parole.significato: to lead, take, show someone the way to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *johtadak (compare Estonian juhtima (“to steer, to lead”), Livonian jū’odõ, Livvi juohattua). The base verb johtaa was rather rare in Old Literary Finnish, with derivatives like johdattaa and now dialectal johdata being more common. * (to derive): Semantic loan from Swedish avleda,

parole.significato: to result from, attributed to, be caused by, stem from
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *johtudak, equivalent to johtaa (“to lead, guide, conduct”) + -ua.

parole.significato: who, which, that (referring to the previous word or phrase; see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joka (compare Karelian joka, Votic jõka), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jo (compare Northern Sami juohkẹ, juogọ, Erzya ю- (ju-) in юза-тоза (juza-toza, “back and forth”), Eastern Mari южо (južo, “some”), Western Mari юж (juž, “some”)). The nominative and genitive singular forms, which
From Proto-Finnic *jokahinën, equivalent to joka (“every, each”) + -(h)inen.

parole.significato: river (large stream which drains a landmass)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joki (compare Estonian jõgi (“river”), Karelian joki /jogi (“river”), Veps jogi (“river”)), from Proto-Uralic *joke (compare Northern Sami johka, Moksha Йов (Jov, “Moksha river”), Northern Mansi я̄ (â̄, “river”), archaic Hungarian jó).

parole.significato: transom, putlog (horizontal or transverse beam of scaffolding that is perpendicular to a wall)
parole.testo: From earlier jotka, possibly from Proto-Finnic *jotka (without any Finnic cognates), if from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Erzya [script needed] (jutko, “gap”), Moksha [script needed] (jutka), [script needed] (jotka, “gap”), Southern Mansi [script needed] (jät, “middle”), Eastern Mansi [script neede
From Proto-Finnic *joristak, of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *jos. Originally the lative singular of joka (relative pronoun); jo- + -s (lative suffix).

parole.significato: so that, in order that, for the purpose that
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jotta. Equivalent to jo- (relative pronoun) + -tta.

parole.significato: hair, horsehair (long, relatively stiff hair of an animal, such as on horse's mane or tail)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jouhi.
From Proto-Finnic *joulu, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛃᛖᚢᛚᚢ (*jeulu). Doublet of juhla.

From Proto-Finnic *jousi (“bow”), from Proto-Uralic *joŋse (compare Erzya ёнкс (jonks, “bow”), Northern Mansi ё̄вт (jōvt, “bow”), Hungarian íj (“bow”), Tundra Nenets ӈын (ŋin°)). * (unit of taxation): Supposedly originally a tax based on the number of men who were strong enough to cock a crossbow (l
From Proto-Finnic *joutadak, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian jaudāt).

parole.significato: swan (any bird in the genus Cygnus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jouc'ën (compare Karelian joučen), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *joŋkće (compare Northern Sami njukča, Erzya локсей (loksej), Moksha локсти (loksti), Eastern Mari йӱксӧ (jüksö), Komi-Permyak юсь (juś)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: to get [with illative] (into a negative position or situation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joutudak. Equivalent to joutaa (“to find time; be free to; be ready”) + -ua (passive verb).

parole.significato: party, celebration, carnival, fiesta, jubilee (social gathering of usually invited guests for entertainment, fun and so…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *juhla (compare dialectal Estonian juhlad), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *jehwlą. Doublet of joulu.
From Proto-Finnic *jukta, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian jūgt), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yugtós; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *juka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *juka.

parole.significato: a rope used to draw a sledge or toboggan
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *juko, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Norwegian oke (“crossbeam”)).

parole.significato: to have the impudence/nerve to, dare to, can
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *julgët'ak. Equivalent to julkea (“impudent, blatant, arrogant”) + -ta. The inflection with julkene- could be interpreted as julkea + -eta, but is likely by later analogy.
From Proto-Finnic *julkëda. Related to Estonian julge, Ingrian julkia, Karelian julgei, Livonian julgi and Votic julka.

From Proto-Finnic *jumala (compare Estonian jumal (“god”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *juma(-la) (“sky, god”), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dyumā (compare Sanskrit द्युम्न (dyumna, “splendor”), Sanskrit द्युमत् (dyumat, “bright; an epithet of Indra”)) or earlier Indo-European.
Inessive singular of jumi-, from Proto-Finnic *juma-, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *juma-.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian junta, junda, Livvi jundu, Ludian dund, Veps dund).

From Proto-Finnic *joodak (compare Estonian jooma), from Proto-Uralic *jëxe- (compare Northern Sami juhkat, Komi-Zyrian юны (juny), Northern Mansi аюӈкве (aûňkve), Hungarian iszik, Tundra Nenets ӈэ̇рпӑсь (ŋėrpăsʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *jooksu, equivalent to juosta (“to run”) + -u.

juolu- + -kka (probably the origin of the form -ukka seen also in puolukka, vatukka), from Proto-Finnic *joo-, which is further related to Proto-Samic *joŋë (“lingonberry”), suggesting earlier *juŋe. Details The forms of this word vary widely, but the forms in Finnish, Ingrian and Votic generally fo

parole.significato: drink, beverage (something to drink, or a serving thereof)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jooma. Equivalent to juoda (“to drink”) + -ma.

parole.significato: plot, scheme, conspiracy, intrigue, stratagem; ploy, ruse (secret plan to achieve an end, the end or means usually bein…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jooni (“path”) (compare Estonian joon), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jëne (compare Southern Sami joene (“road”), Erzya ян (jan, “path”)), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *yáHnam. Sense diversification from original “path” is particular to Finnic. Compare dialectal juntu (“pa
From Proto-Finnic *joopudak, equivalent to juoda (“to drink”) + -pua (passive verb).
From Proto-Finnic *joostak, possibly from Proto-Uralic.
From Proto-Finnic *joottadak. Equivalent to juo- (“to drink”) + -ttaa (curative verb).

parole.significato: streak (irregular line, e.g. one left from smearing or motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jooma (compare Estonian joom (“wake, trail; stream”), Ingrian jooma (“route, passage”), Livonian jūom (“depression; deep part in a body of water”), Votic joomõ (“waterway”)), possibly derived from *joodak (“to drink”) (whence juoda).
From Proto-Finnic *jut'ëldak, equivalent to juttu (“talk”) + -ella. Cognate with Estonian ütlema.
From Proto-Finnic *jutta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *jutas.
From Proto-Finnic *juttu (compare Estonian jutt), from Proto-Uralic *jupta- (“to speak, to tell”) + -u (compare Erzya ёвтамс (jovtams, “to say, to tell a story”), Nganasan дебтудя (djebtudja)).
From Proto-Finnic *juusto (compare Estonian juust), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*jūstaʀ) (compare Swedish ost) or Proto-Germanic *justaz.
From Proto-Finnic *juuttudak. Related to Karelian juuttuo, Ludian dʹuuttuda and Veps jutuda.
From Proto-Finnic *jüristäk, of onomatopoeic origin + -istä. Compare Karelian jurissa, Veps jurišta and Votic jürisse.
From Proto-Finnic *jürkkä. Cognates include Karelian jyrkkä, Livvi jyrkky and Votic jürkkü.
Derived from Proto-Finnic *jürädäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *jürä-. The nature of the suffix -si- is uncertain (? < *-ci- < *-tV-i-, containing the ancestors of Finnish -ta- and -i-).
From Proto-Finnic *jürü, onomatopoeic; compare jyrinä, jyristä, jyrähtää.

parole.significato: grain, kernel, corn (single seed of grain)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jüvä (compare Veps jüvä), from earlier *jewä, borrowed from an Indo-European language (probably Proto-Balto-Slavic *jéwos), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yéwos (“barley, cereal”). Compare Moksha юв (juv, “chaff, empty glume”).
From Proto-Finnic *jäinen. Equivalent to jää (“ice”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *jäkälä, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *jäkälä ~ *jekäl.

parole.significato: track, trail (mark left as a sign of passage of a person or animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jälki (compare Estonian jälg), from Proto-Uralic *jälke (compare Hungarian jel).
From Proto-Finnic *jälkimäinen, from *jäljin + -inen, as if from the superlative of jälki (a noun).
From Proto-Finnic *jämedä (compare Estonian jäme, Votic jämmiä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jämä-.

parole.significato: hare (any of several plant-eating animals of the family Leporidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jänis. * (stowaway): Semantic loan from Russian за́яц (zájac, “hare; stowaway”).
From Proto-Finnic *jändek (compare Veps jände), from Proto-Uralic *jänte(ŋ) (compare Eastern Mari йыдаҥ (jydaŋ), Eastern Khanty јӫнтӛɣ, Tundra Nenets ен (yen°)).
From Proto-Finnic *jänoi, analyzable as jän- + -ö.
From Proto-Finnic *järedä.

parole.significato: to quake, tremble, shake (e.g. of the ground or buildings)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *järistäk.

From Proto-Finnic *järki (“order, row”), of unknown further origin. The original sense can be seen in derived terms like järjestää. The sense of "order" would have later shifted to that which provides order, or sense, i.e. the faculty of reason.

From Proto-Finnic *jäsen (compare Estonian jäse), from Proto-Finno-Permic *jäsene (“joint”) (compare Erzya эзне (ezne, “joint”) and Udmurt ёз (joz, “joint”)). * (member (part of a group, etc.)): Probably a semantic loan from another language, compare German Glied (“limb”) → Mitglied (“member”). * (t

parole.significato: to leave, leave behind (a thing, place, person, group, traces, etc.) (cause or allow to remain as available; cause, res…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jättädäk. Probably equivalent to jä(ä)- (“to stay, be left”) + -ttää.

parole.significato: to gnaw, eat away, wear (to destroy gradually as by taking tiny little bites)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jäütädäk, derived from a borrowing from early Balto-Slavic.

From Proto-Finnic *jää (compare Estonian jää), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäŋe (compare Northern Sami jiekŋa, Erzya эй (ej), Eastern Mari ий (ij), Udmurt йӧ (jö), Northern Mansi я̄ӈк (â̄ňk), Eastern Khanty йӛӈк (jjəṇk), Hungarian jég).
From Proto-Finnic *jäädäk (compare Estonian jääma, Karelian jiähä, Livonian īedõ).
From Proto-Finnic *jähtüdäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäkše-. Cognate with Erzya экше (ekše), экшемемс (ekšemems).

parole.significato: to freeze (of a liquid, especially water, to become solid due to low temperature)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jäätüdäk, equivalent to jää (“ice”) + -tyä or jäätää (“to freeze”) + -yä. Formally equivalent to Estonian jäätuma.
From Proto-Finnic *kaak'attadak, of onomatopoeic origin + -ttaa

From Proto-Finnic *kakko ~ *kaakko (“southeast”). Cognate to Estonian kagu and Ingrian kakko. Possibly related to kaakkuri, in which case the cardinal direction meaning could derive from a meaning like "the direction where migratory birds come from".

parole.significato: to scrape (to remove, dislodge, clean, empty with a scraping movement or action)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaap(p)idak (compare Estonian kaapima, Karelian koapie, Livonian kōpšõ, Ludian kuabita, Veps kabita), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skabaną (“to scrape”).

From Proto-Finnic *kaari, from Proto-Uralic *këŋere. Cognate with Estonian kaar. * ((law) code, act): Semantic loan from Swedish balk (literally “beam”), perhaps by comparison with the rib of a boat or ship. * ((taxonomy) division, phylum): Semantic development from “(law) code, act”.

From Proto-Finnic *karnëh (compare Estonian kaaren), from Proto-Uralic *karne (compare Northern Sami gáranas, Inari Sami káránâs, Erzya кренч (krenč), Komi-Zyrian кырныш (kyrnyš), Tundra Nenets хӑрна (xărna)). Displaced by the borrowed korppi.
From Proto-Finnic *kaartadak, equivalent to kaari (“bow, arch, curve”) + -taa.

parole.significato: to knock/tip/turn over, overturn, upset, knock down
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaatadak. Compare Karelian kuatua. Semantic development * (to knock over, tip over, overturn): From Proto-Finnic. * (to fell, cut down): From “to knock over, tip over”. * (to pour, tip, dump): Already in Proto-Finnic; when pouring something from an upright container, one will slig

parole.significato: to fall from an upright position; to fall down, to fall over
parole.testo: kaataa (“to overturn; to pour; to overthrow”) + -ua (automative verb). Possibly already as Proto-Finnic *kaatudak (compare Ingrian kaatua, Karelian kuatuo). * (to fall (die in combat)): Semantic loan from Swedish falla or German fallen.

parole.significato: decoy (for hunting, especially for birds where the decoy is an image of a bird)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaavëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skawwiz.
From Proto-Finnic *kadëh (compare Estonian kade, Karelian kajeh, Livonian ka’d, Veps kadeh, Võro kadõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaþiz (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌸𐌹𐍃 (skaþis)).

From Proto-Finnic *kadot'ak (compare Estonian kaduma), from Proto-Uralic *kaďa(w)- (“to leave”) (compare Northern Sami guođđit (“to leave something, to depart”), Erzya кадомс (kadoms, “to leave”), Eastern Mari кодаш (kodaš, “to stay”), Udmurt кыльыны (kyľyny, “to stay”), Hungarian hagy (“to let; to

parole.significato: to lose, misplace (to cause to cease to be in one's possession or capability due to unfortunate or unknown circumstance…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kadottadak. Equivalent to kadota (“to be lost, disappear”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: a type of traditional trap for catching birds, especially black grouse
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaha, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kazą.
From Proto-Finnic *kaktëksa kümmentä. Equivalent to kahdeksan (“eight”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).

From Proto-Finnic *kaktëksa(n) toicta (kümmentä) (literally “eight of the second decade”). Equivalent to kahdeksan (“eight”) + -toista (“of the second”) (see kahdeksan for more information on its development).
From Proto-Finnic *kaktëksanci. Equivalent to kahdeksa- (“eight”) + -s (“-th”).

parole.significato: to rustle (to move something, such as leaves, with a soft crackling sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kahistak. kah- + -ista, with an onomatopoeic root.

parole.significato: cupped hands, (Scotland) gowpen (two hands held together in a concave shape, usually to hold something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kamahlo.

parole.significato: handle, grip (part by which something is held with the hand)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kahva. Related to Karelian kahva, Livvi kahvu and possibly Ludian kahv.

parole.significato: railing, rail (fence or barrier consisting of one or more horizontal rails and vertical supports)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaidëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaidiz (compare Old Norse skeiðir). The weaving sense “reed” appears to have been the original one.
From Proto-Finnic *kaiho (“harm, damage, loss”) (compare Estonian kahju, Ingrian kaiho, Livonian ka’j), from Proto-Uralic *kajša-w (“sickness”). Compare Erzya кажо (kažo, “misfortune, disaster”).
From Proto-Finnic *kaikki, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kajakei.
From Proto-Finnic *kaikudak.

parole.significato: namesake (a person with the same name as another person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaima (compare Estonian kaim, Proto-Samic *kuojmē), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian káimas, Latvian ciems). Northern Sami gaiˈbmât (“to adapt to a companion, to enjoy company”), from Proto-Samic *kājmē, is a later borrowing from Finnic.
From Proto-Finnic *kainalo.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian kaine, Ingrian kainu, Karelian kainu, kaino).

parole.significato: rush, bulrush, club-rush (grass-like plants of the genus Scirpus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaisla (*kaisila), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaisilaz (“staff, whip”) (compare German Geißel and Swedish gissel).
From Proto-Finnic *kaita (compare Ingrian kaita, Karelian kaita, Livvi kaidu, Ludian kaid, Veps kaid), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaidō (compare English goad).
From Proto-Finnic *kaiccëdak. Cognate with Estonian kaitsma, Veps kaita, Võro kaitsma.

parole.significato: to dig, dig up, dig out, excavate
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaivadak (compare Estonian kaevama), from Proto-Uralic *kajwa- (compare Northern Sami goaivut, Komi-Zyrian койны (kojny, “to pour”), Tundra Nenets сива (syiwa, “shovel”)).

parole.significato: to long for, yearn for, pine for, miss
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaibait'ak (compare Estonian kaebama, Karelian kaivata, Livonian kaibõ, Võro kaibama), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kawjaną, which is ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gewH- (“to call, cry out”).
From Proto-Finnic *kaivo. Equivalent to kaivaa (“to dig”) + -o. Cognate with Estonian kaev.

parole.significato: to echo, ring out, sound (to produce a vibrant sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kajahtadak, equivalent to kaj- + -ahtaa
From Proto-Finnic *kajaga (compare Estonian kajakas, Veps kajag and Votic kajagõ), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kaja.

parole.significato: to touch [with illative] (to physically disturb; to interfere with, molest, or attempt to harm through contact)
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Finnic *kajadak + -ota, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kajɜ-.
From Proto-Finnic *kakara. The original meaning was likely "clod, lump". Related to kakkara.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?].

From Proto-Finnic *kakci (compare Estonian kaks), from Proto-Uralic *käktä ~ *kakta (compare Northern Sami guoktẹ, Erzya кавто (kavto), Eastern Mari кок (kok), Komi-Zyrian кык (kyk), Northern Khanty кӑт (kăt), Hungarian két, Tundra Nenets сидя (syidya)).

parole.significato: twosome, two, duet, duo, pair, doublet, twin, dyad (group of two; two similar or closely related objects, entities etc.…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kakcikkoi. Equivalent to kaksi (“two”) + -ikko. Compare Estonian kaksik.
From Proto-Finnic *kakci kümmentä. Equivalent to kaksi (“two”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).
From Proto-Finnic *kakci toicta (kümmentä) (literally “two of the second decade”). Equivalent to kaksi (“two”) + -toista (“of the second”).
From Proto-Finnic *kala (compare Estonian kala), from Proto-Uralic *kala (compare Northern Sami guolli, Erzya кал (kal), Eastern Mari кол (kol), Hungarian hal, Tundra Nenets халя (xalya)).
From Proto-Finnic *kalëh (“husk; chaff”), probably borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *skalō.

parole.significato: stick, billet (relatively large but thin and round piece of something, especially wood)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kadikka, with influence from onomatopoeic kalista (in those dialects where -d- is not regularly reflected by -l-) and/or kalu.

parole.significato: A traditional fermented, homemade, weak table drink made of malt and sugar, closely resembling kvass; its alcohol conte…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kalja (cognate with Estonian kali). According to one theory, possibly borrowed from an early Indo-European language; compare Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-u-t- (“beer”) (Proto-Slavic *olъ, Proto-Germanic *alu, Old Prussian alu, Old Armenian աւղի (awłi)), *h₂al-ew-yo-, but this is unce

parole.significato: a wooden log (often a debarked one) laid under something for transportation, e.g. laid diagonally while building a log…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kalju, possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *kalki.

parole.significato: synonym of äyräs (“bank (of a river, etc.)”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaldas (compare Estonian kallas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *halþaz (compare Old Norse hallr).

parole.significato: rock (the aggregate of solid mineral matter (stone) that constitutes a significant part of the earth's crust)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kallijo (compare Estonian kalju, Ingrian kallio, Karelian kallivo, Veps kal, Votic kalʹlʹo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hallijǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *kallis.

From Proto-Finnic *kalma, likely from Proto-Uralic *kalma (compare Erzya калмо (kalmo, “grave”)), formed as *kale- (“to die”) + *-ma (compare kuolema, formed as kuole- + -ma, both from the same verb with the same suffix, but at different times; kuolema is still recognizable as a deverbal noun, while
From Proto-Finnic *kalsu.
From Proto-Finnic *kalu. Possibly related to Northern Sami gálvu.
From Proto-Finnic *kalvadak, borrowed by metathesis from Proto-Germanic *klawjaną.
From Proto-Finnic *kalbas, possibly ultimately borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *h₂elbʰós.

parole.significato: gauge, spacer (a stick or plate, often made of wood, used to define the mesh size when making a net)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian kaluin, Votic kaluvi and also Estonian kalasi, Ingrian kalve, Veps kalud). Also cognate with Northern Sami guollạdat.
From Proto-Finnic *kamara, from Proto-Uralic *kama (“skin”) + *-ra.
From Proto-Finnic *kammijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skammijǭ), from Proto-Germanic *skammijǭ (“little house”). Compare Icelandic skemma (“a storehouse”).
From Proto-Finnic *kambicca (compare Estonian kammits, Livvi kampičču, Votic kammittsõ, Võro kammits). Equivalent to kampi (“crank”) + -itsa.

From Proto-Finnic *kampala/*kampëla. Perhaps equivalent to kampi (“crank”) + -la, derived from kampi, originally in the sense "crooked, slanted, clunky". Related to Estonian kammeljas (“turbot”), Karelian kampala and Livonian kǭma. Russian ка́мбала (kámbala, “flounder”) is borrowed from Finnic.
From Proto-Finnic *kampi, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kampas). Doublet of kamppi.
From Proto-Finnic *kampsu.

parole.significato: chicken (domestic fowl of species Gallus gallus, Gallus domesticus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kana (compare Estonian kana), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hanô (“rooster, cock”) (compare German Hahn).
From Proto-Finnic *kanarba.

From Proto-Finnic *kangas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gangaz (compare Danish gang (“forty warp threads”), Middle High German ganc (“warp count (in weaving)”), Middle Low German ganc (“warp count (in weaving)”)).

parole.significato: A soil type: firm, moraine ground covered with a relatively thin layer of organic topsoil called podsol.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kangas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gangaz (“way, passage”) (compare German Gang), boreal forests being easily passable.

parole.significato: stiff (rigid, hard to bend, inflexible; e.g. of body parts that are more rigid than usual)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kankëda, possibly from Proto-Uralic *kënka-, *kënke-, whence Erzya канкстомомс (kankstomoms, “to stiffen; to get numb”).

parole.significato: bar, stick (long piece of metal or wood, especially one used as a lever)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanki. Cognate with Estonian kang, Ingrian kanki, Karelian kanki, Livvi kangi and Veps kang.

parole.significato: to support, bear up, hold up, prop up, carry (support physically)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kandattadak (compare Estonian kannatama (“to tolerate, to suffer”), Ingrian kannattaa (“to survive”)), equivalent to kantaa (“to carry”) + -ttaa (curative verb), literally “to have somebody/something carried”. The senses “to support, second, back; to be worthwhile, be worth; to be

parole.significato: heel, crust; the crust end-piece of bread, cheese or similar food
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kandikka. Equivalent to kanta (“heel, base”) + -ikka.

From Proto-Finnic *kandus, equivalent to kanta (“heel”) + -us. * (Sami drum): A phono-semantic matching/semantic loan from a Sami term; compare Northern Sami goavddis, derived from goavdi (cognate with kansi (“lid, cap, top”)).

parole.significato: people, nation (community of people united by shared culture or ethnicity, or the inhabitants of a country)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kansa (compare Livvi kanzu, Veps kanz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hansō (earlier *hansā, compare Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌽𐍃𐌰 (hansa)).

parole.significato: lid, top, cover (generally flat cover of a hole or a container such as a jar or a box)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanci (compare Estonian kaas), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kamte (compare Northern Sami goavdi, Erzya кундо (kundo, “lid”), Eastern Mari комдыш (komdyš)).

parole.significato: base (supporting component of a structure or object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanta (compare Estonian kand), from Proto-Uralic *kënta (compare Erzya кандо (kando, “log, load”), Moksha канда (kanda), Northern Khanty ҳонт (ḥont), Northern Mansi [script needed] (χānta)). * (position, opinion, point of view, stance): Coined by Finnish physician and translator W

From Proto-Finnic *kantadak (compare Estonian kandma), from Proto-Uralic *kanta- (compare Northern Sami guoddit, Erzya кандомс (kandoms), Eastern Mari кондеш (kondeš), Northern Mansi хӯнт (hūnt), Tundra Nenets ханась (xanasʹ°)). * (to wear (clothing)): Compare Swedish bära (“to bear, carry; to wear
From Proto-Finnic *kandël (kannel), *kantëlëh (cognate with Estonian kannel). Ultimate etymology contested; see Proto-Finnic *kandël for theories.
From Proto-Finnic *kanto, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kënta-w, borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *skandʰás, whence Sanskrit स्कन्ध (skandha). Uralic cognates include Erzya кандо (kando, “block, log”).
From Proto-Finnic *kapalo. Cognates include dialectal Estonian kabalo, Ingrian kapalo, Karelian kapalo, Ludian kabal, Veps kabal and Votic kapalod.
From Proto-Finnic *kapëda (compare Estonian kabe (“lively, brisk”)).

parole.significato: rebellion, revolt, mutiny, insurrection, insurgency, uprising, sedition
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapina. Equivalent to kapista + -na; meanings through figurative use.

parole.significato: trousseaux (clothes, linen etc. collected or brought by the bride to their new home after being married)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapijot, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence dialectal Swedish gävo), from Proto-Germanic *gebaną.
From Proto-Finnic *kabistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. The strong grade -p- has been levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: stanchion; a support between a skid and the frame on a sleigh
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaplas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian kablis, Lithuanian kablys).

parole.significato: a unit of measure for the volume of dry goods, equivalent to 1/32 of a tynnyri or 4.58 litres in the Kingdom of Sweden…
parole.testo: [Alt: A cubical wooden measuring vessel, a kappa.] From Proto-Finnic *kappa (compare Estonian kapp, Ingrian kappa, Karelian kappa, Kukkuzi kappa, Ludian kappe), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skapaz (compare Old Saxon skap (“a measure”), Old High German scaf (“vessel”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kappalëh ~ *kapalëh (compare Livonian kabāl), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian gabals (“piece”), Lithuanian gabalas), somewhat nativized with the -e suffix.

parole.significato: a dried branch, rib of a leaf or other similar dried part of a plant
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kara.

parole.significato: to harden, to toughen up (character, personality, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kargaictak.

parole.significato: to escape, run away, flee, fly, get away (from captivity)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kargait'ak (compare Estonian kargama (“to jump, hop”), Livonian kargõ (“to jump”), Ludian kargaita (“to run”), Veps kargata (“to dance”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *karka- (compare Erzya кра- (kra-) in кравтомс (kravtoms, “to drive away, drive out, oust”)).
From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Ingrian kare, Karelian kare, Ludian kare).
From Proto-Finnic *karhëk, possibly from the same stem as karhea.
From Proto-Finnic *karhëda.

parole.significato: bear (large omnivorous mammal of the family Ursidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karhu, probably derived from *karhëda; equivalent to karhea (“rough, coarse”) + -u. Originally a euphemism for *okci (whence oksi, ohto, and otso). Sense 3 is a semantic loan from Swedish björn and sense 4 from English bear.

parole.significato: rock (mass of stone projecting out of water or just underwater)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kari (compare Estonian kari), borrowed from late Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skarj(a)-) (compare Swedish skär, English skerry), from Proto-Germanic *skarją.
From Proto-Finnic *karistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. Compare karahtaa, karauttaa.
From Proto-Finnic *kargicca (compare Ingrian karitsa, Veps kargitš), probably equivalent to karata (“to run away; (archaic) to jump, hop, run”) + -itsa.

parole.significato: cattle (domesticated bovine animals) (sometimes with a specifier: nautakarja, lehmikarja)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karja (compare Estonian kari, Livonian kōŗa), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harjaz (“army”) (compare Swedish här (“land army”), German Heer (“army”)). The original sense "army, forces" may survive in Karjala.
From Proto-Finnic *karjudak (compare Karelian karjuo and Estonian karjuma), ultimately onomatopoeic.

From Proto-Finnic *karkëda, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *karke. * (unrefined): A semantic loan from other European languages; compare French gros, German grob. The antonym hieno (“fine; refined”) is likewise similarly semantically informed by other languages.

parole.significato: flight, escape (mostly used in the illative, inessive and elative cases)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karku. Equivalent to karata (“to escape, run away, flee”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *karmëda.

parole.significato: cranberry (shrub belonging to the section Vaccinium sect. Oxycoccus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karpa-(la-) (compare Karelian karpalo, Kukkuzi karpolo, Livonian gārban, Livvi garbalo, Veps garbal), possibly from Baltic.

parole.significato: not straight: twisted, crooked, wry, warped
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karsas.

parole.significato: char, that has been burned and charred
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karci, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *karte-.

parole.significato: card (comb- or brush-like device or tool to raise the nap on a fabric)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karsta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian karsti).
From Proto-Finnic *karta, borrowed from a Baltic or Germanic language. Cognates include Estonian kard and Ingrian karta.
From Proto-Finnic *kartano (compare Karelian kartano, Livonian kǭrand (with metathesis), Votic kartõno), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gardô (“enclosure, yard, garden”).

parole.significato: to avoid, stay away (from), shun, steer clear of
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karttadak. Possibly cognate with Erzya кардамс (kardams, “to ban, stop”).

parole.significato: hair (single hair on human or animal) (not used of human head hair except in a technical sense)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karva (compare Estonian karv, Livonian kǭra, Veps karv), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian gaũras). In the first texts, karva is attested only in the sense “color”; in its current meaning, it is first mentioned in a biblical text in 1621. Displaced in the sense “color” by v
From Proto-Finnic *karvainën, equivalent to karva (“hair, fur; (archaic) color”) + -inen.

From Proto-Finnic *karvas (compare Livonian kǭraz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harwaz (compare Middle High German hare, German herb) or (less likely) derived from Proto-Uralic *karwa (compare Udmurt курыт (kuryt), Komi-Permyak курыт (kuryt), Komi-Zyrian курыд (kuryd), Eastern Khanty корә

parole.significato: Any lichen of the family Parmeliaceae; parmeliaceous lichen.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karbëk, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian karpitnes (“lichen”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kasa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Swedish kasi, Swedish kase (“heap, collection of something”), Old Norse kǫs (“heap, pile”)), from Proto-Germanic *kasō.
From Proto-Finnic *kaca (see it for more).
From Proto-Finnic *kasi, from Proto-Uralic *käsä.

parole.significato: slashed forest; a plot of forestland that has been slashed (cleared) and ready to be burned (and turned into a swidden)…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaski.

parole.significato: to dip, sop, dunk, douse (to imbue or immerse briefly in a liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kastadak. Equivalent to kasi (“dew”) (archaic, dialectal) + -taa.

parole.significato: dew (moisture in the air that settles on plants, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kastëk. Equivalent to kastaa (“to wet, soak”) + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *kastudak, equivalent to kastaa (“to wet, soak”) + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *kasvadak (compare Estonian kasvama, Livonian ka’zzõ, Votic kazva), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kaswa- (compare Erzya касомс (kasoms)).
From Proto-Finnic *kasvattadak. Equivalent to kasva- (“to grow”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: face (front of the head) (always in the plural; see kasvot)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kasvo, derived from kasvaa (“to grow”), equivalent to kasvaa + -o.

parole.significato: juniper (any shrub or tree of the genus Juniperus of the cypress family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kataga (compare Estonian kadakas, Votic katagõ).
Proto-Finnic *katala. Compare kavala and kamala (from Proto-Finnic *kavala and *kamala) as well as ketale. Cognates include Estonian kadal (“bad, weak, miserable”) and Karelian katala (“pitiful”).
From Proto-Finnic *kat'ëk, equivalent to kattaa (“to cover”) + -e.

parole.significato: bitter, resentful (of a person: feeling bitterness or having a bitter temperament; of events: leaving someone feeling b…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kackëra, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kačka-.

parole.significato: to break, snap, (be) cut (often in half)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *katkët'ak. Related to Estonian katkema, Karelian kateta, Livonian katkõ, Veps kattõta and Votic kadgõtõ. Compare ratketa.

parole.significato: to cut, break or snap into several pieces, or cut several objects into two or more pieces
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *katkoidak.

parole.significato: fume(s) (strong, unpleasant and stinging smell caused by something burning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kacku, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kačka- (“to bite”), the same root as in katkera.
From Proto-Finnic *kato, from the same root as *katodak (see kadota).

parole.significato: shed that has at least one wall missing
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kat'os. Equivalent to kattaa (“to cover”) + -os.
From Proto-Finnic *katras, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaduraz (whence Old English geador); no other Finnic cognates are known.

parole.significato: to look, have a look, take a look (+ at)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaccodak (compare Estonian katsuma). * (to regard, deem): Semantic loan, ultimately from Latin videō. * ((gambling) to see (a bet)): Presumably a semantic loan from English see.

From Proto-Finnic *kattadak. Equivalent to kansi (“lid, top, cover”) + -taa (causative verb), with (once upon a time) regular consonant cluster simplification *-ntt- > *-tt-. * (to set, lay (the table)): Compare German decken. * (to cover (costs, demand, etc.)): Compare German decken. * (to roof): C

parole.significato: pot, cooking pot, stockpot, saucepot, kettle (often cylindrical or nearly cylindrical cooking vessel for fast cooking o…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kattila, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *katilaz.
From Proto-Finnic *katto, equivalent to kattaa (“to cover”) + -o. Compare also Veps katuz, Estonian katus, which use a different suffix.

parole.significato: shade, shadow (relative darkness caused by the interruption of light)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *katvëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skaduz ~ *skadwaz (compare English shade, shadow). No cognates in the other Finnic languages are known.

parole.significato: ladle, dipper (cup-shaped vessel with a long handle, for dipping out liquids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kauha, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *káuˀ-, from Proto-Indo-European *kowh₂-, from the root *kewh₂-. Compare Lithuanian káušas (“ladle, dipper, big spoon”).
From Proto-Finnic *kauhëda. Cognates include Karelian kauhie and Votic kauhaa (“nastily, disgustingly, awfully, terribly”) (Lempola).

parole.significato: trough, manger (long, narrow container, open on top, for feeding or watering animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaukalo (compare Ingrian kaukalo, Livonian kougõl, Votic kaukolo).
From the stem *kauka, from Proto-Finnic *kauka-, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hauhaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kewk-. Cognate to Estonian kauge and Votic kauga.

parole.significato: neck (part of the body connecting the head and the trunk)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kakla (compare Estonian kael), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kaklas (compare Lithuanian kaklas). Distant doublet of chakra, kekri, and sykli.

parole.significato: collar, neck (part of clothing around throat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaklus. Equivalent to kaula (“neck”) + -us.
From Proto-Finnic *kauna.
From Proto-Finnic *kaunis (compare Estonian kaunis), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skauniz (compare English sheen, German schön, Swedish skön).

parole.significato: trade, commerce, buying and selling, trading, dealing, business, traffic
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kauppa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse kaupa, Old English ċēap and German Kauf), which in turn from Latin caupo.

From Proto-Finnic *kakra (compare Estonian kaer, North Karelian kakra, Livonian ka’ggõrz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hagrō (compare Old Swedish haghre, dialectal Swedish hagre, Old Gutnish hagri).

parole.significato: deer (any relatively small deer of unspecified species, especially roe deer) (not as a zoological term)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapris, borrowing from Proto-Germanic *habraz, *hafraz (“he-goat”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kápros. Cognates include Estonian kaber, Karelian kabris.
From Proto-Finnic *kauci. Related to Proto-Samic *kuovtë (“central?”) (Northern Sami guovda). The modern meaning is a re-extraction from compounds such as kuukausi and vuorokausi.

parole.significato: top rail; beam above and parallel to the runner that holds the tops of the supports between the skid and the frame on a…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kausta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *skaustas (whence Latvian skausts).
From Proto-Finnic *kauto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skautaz.
From Proto-Finnic *kautta, the partitive singular of kausi; the adpositions are derived through an older meaning of “road, way” or “passage (of a journey)”.
From Proto-Finnic *kavala.

parole.significato: to betray (as a secret, a person [into hostile hands], one's comrades or country)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kavaltadak. Equivalent to kavala (“treacherous, sly”) + -taa.

parole.significato: a creature related to the moon, sky or air
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kabëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skapiz (compare Proto-Germanic *skapą, Old English gesceap). Cognate with Estonian kabu, Karelian kaveh, Võro kabo and Proto-Samic *kuopës (“witch”).

parole.significato: hoof (thick keratin covering of the tip of a toe of an ungulate)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kapja + -o (compare dialectal kapia, Estonian kabi, Votic kabjõ), ultimately perhaps borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hāfaz.
From Proto-Finnic *kabut'ak (compare Karelian kavuta and Veps kabuta).

parole.significato: to be able to bring oneself to do something, dare, venture, have the nerve (confidence, courage)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këhtat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *kehkedä, possibly a derivation from *kehä.

parole.significato: A mass of fluff, dandruff or similar dirt.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kehnä.

From Proto-Finnic *kecrä (compare Estonian keder, North Karelian kesrä, Veps kezr), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kečrä, borrowed from early Proto-Indo-Iranian *ketstram (later *čatstram). Cognates include Erzya штере (štere).

parole.significato: to spin (to convert fibres into yarn or thread)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kecrät'äk, equivalent to kehrä (“spindle”) + -tä. * (to purr): Analogous to the sound of a spinning wheel; compare Swedish spinna.

parole.significato: circle, ring (enclosure, perimeter, a circular arrangement of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kehä (compare Estonian keha (“body”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *keč(č)ä (compare Northern Sami giessat (“to wrap”), Erzya чи (či, “sun, da”), Eastern Mari кече (keče, “sun, day”), Udmurt киш (kiš, “snare”), Northern Mansi кис (kis, “hoop”)).

parole.significato: spear (long stick with a sharp tip used as a weapon for throwing or thrusting)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaihas (compare Ingrian keihäs, Veps keihaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gaizaz (compare Old Norse geirr, German Ger). Doublet of kaira.
From Proto-Finnic *këikkudak.
From Proto-Finnic *keittädäk ~ *keettädäk (compare Estonian keetma, Karelian keittyä /keittiä, Livonian kīetõ, Veps keitta), derived from *keedäk, the same root as in kiehua.

parole.significato: stack (large pile of hay, grain, straw, or the like, larger at the bottom than the top)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këko. Related to Karelian keko, Ludian keko and Veps kego.

parole.significato: harvest festival (old Finnish feast celebrated between Michaelmas and Halloween, exact time depending on annual conditi…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kekri (perhaps from earlier *kekrä), possibly borrowed from early Proto-Indo-Iranian *ḱekrám (later *čakrám), in which case a distant doublet of chakra, kaula, and sykli. See the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: ember (glowing piece of coal, wood or other solid fuel)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kekäleh.

parole.significato: reel, spool, bobbin (device around which thread, wire, cable or something similar is wound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këla, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian kelan (“wheel”)).

parole.significato: weather conditions relating specifically to surfaces for travel (such as road conditions or skiing conditions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keli, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *keljas (compare Latvian ceļš (“road”), Lithuanian kelias (“road”)).
From Proto-Finnic *keldeh, probably ultimately borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skelduz, or less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian ski̇̀ltis).

From Proto-Finnic *kello (compare Karelian kello, Ludian kello, Veps kelo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skellǭ (“bell”) (compare German Schelle and Swedish skälla (“bell”)). The original sense is “bell”; the second sense “clock” developed from the fact that time was traditionally marked by church

parole.significato: The white surface layer of the bark of a birch.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kelmeh, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *kelmä.
From Proto-Finnic *këlta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *gilˀtos (compare Lithuanian geltas). May be a distant doublet of kulta.
From Proto-Finnic *këltainën, equivalent to kelta (“yellow”) + -inen.

parole.significato: who; (when followed by a modifier in the elative case) which one (of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ken (compare Votic čen), from Proto-Uralic *ke (compare Ter Sami kie, Erzya ки (ki), кие (kije), Udmurt кин (kin), Hungarian ki).

parole.significato: to shoe, put on shoes (primarily on oneself)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kenkidäk. Equivalent to kenkä (“shoe”) + -iä.
From Proto-Finnic *kenkä, possibly borrowed from pre-Germanic *(s)keng- (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more). Cognate with Estonian king.
From Proto-Finnic *këno (compare Estonian kenus), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kenwuz (later *kinnuz), albeit the semantic development would not be entirely clear.
From Proto-Finnic *kepedä, probably from Proto-Uralic *kepä (whence also keveä).

parole.significato: A circular or near-circular, usually wooden, rim, edge, wheel or ring.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keri, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kere.

parole.significato: to make it (in time), arrive (in time), reach (in time)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kergit'äk, equivalent to ker- (“prompt, quick”) + -itä.

parole.significato: to shear (remove the fleece from a sheep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerit'äk, derived from a root borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skeraną, as ker- + -itä.

parole.significato: to wind, reel, coil (to turn coils around something, such as a reel or coil)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keridäk, equivalent to kerä (“ball, something wound up”) + -iä.

parole.significato: to beg (for) (request the help of someone, often in the form of money; plead for help)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerjät'äk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kerjä- (“to request”) (compare Hungarian kér).

From Proto-Finnic *kerkedä. Cognate to Estonian kerge (“light”), Ingrian kerkiä, Karelian kerkie, Livonian kierdõ, Ludian kerged (“in a rush”), Votic kerkiä and possibly also Erzya курок (kurok, “soon”).

parole.significato: young shoot, bud or tip of a conifer tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerkkä ~ *kärkkä.
From Proto-Finnic *kërnas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gernaz (“eager, willing”).
From Proto-Finnic *keroi.

parole.significato: a traditional measure for sold lampreys, consisting of 31 lampreys (30 in a bunch tied and held together with one more)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kërpo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kerbą (whence Old Norse kerfi (“bundle”), Swedish kärve).

parole.significato: to repeat (do or say again (and again))
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kërdat'ak. Equivalent to kerta (“time, instance, layer”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *kërsa (compare Võro kõrźo), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse kjarr (“copsewood”)). The meaning "kid, child, brat" would in this case be a re-extraction from kersalapsi (“bastard, illegitimate child”, literally “a child conceived/born in the bushes”)

From Proto-Finnic *kërta (compare Estonian kord), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kartas (compare Old Prussian kērdan (accusative singular), Lithuanian kartas), although other Indo-European etyma have also been proposed (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: ball, clew (quantity of string, thread, etc., wound into a spherical shape)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerä (compare Estonian kera, Livonian kierā, Votic čerä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kerä (compare Erzya кире (kire)).
From Proto-Finnic *kerät'äk, probably from kerä (“ball (of material)”) + -tä.

parole.significato: The thin outer layer of skin.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keci, from Proto-Uralic *kete.
From Proto-Finnic *keski (compare Estonian kesk-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *keske (compare Northern Sami gaska, Moksha кеска (keska, “waist”), Udmurt кусып (kusyp)).

From Proto-Finnic *kesä (compare Estonian kesa (“fallow”), Veps keza (“summer”), Võro kesä (“fallow”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kesä (“summer”) (compare Northern Sami geassi, Erzya кизэ (kizë)), possibly a loanword from Indo-European; see it for more. Introduced into the standard language from East
From Proto-Finnic *këtara, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian ketera, ketaras). Erzya кодор (kodor, “stake, plant’s stake”) borrowed from the same Baltic root.
A southwestern dialectal form keviä adopted into the standard language as if it were originally an adjective ending in -eä (although it is not), from Proto-Finnic *kepjä.
From Proto-Finnic *kevät, from Proto-Finno-Permic *keŋä.

parole.significato: crystal (a grain or piece of a crystalline substance, an array of atoms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kidek. Originally referring to a snowflake or crystal of ice; related to dialectal kiteä, Estonian kidu (“light snow that wind blows around”), Karelian kitie (“cold (sub-zero) weather”), Veps kidegi (“very cold weather”). The modern meaning "crystal" was coined by Finnish clergyma

parole.significato: to boil ((begin to) turn into a gas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keehudak (compare Karelian kiehuo, Veps kehda, Votic čihhua), an irregular passive derivation of *keedäk (compare Estonian keema, Livonian kīedõ), from Proto-Uralic *keje- (compare Eastern Mari кӱаш (küaš, “to boil, to cook, to sunbathe”), Hungarian köved, köveszt, küeszt (“to boi

From Proto-Finnic *keeli (compare Estonian keel, Karelian kieli), from Proto-Uralic *käle (compare Northern Sami giella, Erzya кель (keľ), Moksha кяль (käľ), Udmurt кыл (kyl), Eastern Khanty кӧԓ (köł), Nganasan сиәде (siədje)).
From Proto-Finnic *keeltädäk, equivalently kiel- (“tongue”) + -tää; the original meaning was likely simply “to speak”.

parole.significato: to roll, roll over (revolve by turning over and over, turn around one's own axis, either in place or in motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keeridäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *käre-.
From Proto-Finnic *keero, equivalent to kierä + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *keertüdäk. Equivalent to kiertää (“to turn, twist; to wind”) + -yä.
From Proto-Finnic *keertädäk, equivalent to kier- (“to roll”) + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *keerä. Cognates include Karelian kierä, Veps ker.
From Proto-Finnic *kihara.
From Proto-Finnic *kihistäk, from onomatopoeic root + -ista
From Proto-Finnic *kihla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gīslaz (“hostage”).

parole.significato: bubble (air or gas bubble in water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kiho. The colloquial sense boss, big shot probably developed from the earlier sense “bubble, something rising to the top”.

parole.significato: unsteady, wobbly, rickety (tending to swing back and forth, of e.g. a boat or bridge)
parole.testo: Variant of kikkerä, from Proto-Finnic *kikkerä, probably ultimately sound-symbolic. The long vowel is probably by contamination with kiikkua.
From Proto-Finnic *kiikkudak, ultimately possibly onomatopoeic. Related to Estonian kiikuma and Karelian kiikkuo.

parole.significato: to shine, glitter (to reflect light because of shiny surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kiiltädäk.

From Proto-Finnic *kiima (compare Estonian kiim, Karelian kiima, Veps kim), from Proto-Uralic *kixe-ma, derived from *kixe- (compare Northern Sami gihkat, Northern Khanty [script needed] (koj-), Northern Mansi [script needed] (kaj-), Hungarian kéj).
From Proto-Finnic *kindik. Related to kiinteä. Compare Karelian kiini and Estonian kinni.
From Proto-Finnic *kindittädäk, equivalent to kiinni (“attached, fixed”) + -ttää.

parole.significato: solid, firm, rigid (in the solid state; having at least a somewhat unyielding texture or structure, tangible but diffic…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kintedä (compare Estonian kindel, Ingrian kiintiä, Ludian kińďed), from the same root as kiinni (“attached, fixed”) with the adjectival suffix -eä.
From Proto-Finnic *kiireh (compare Estonian kiire, Votic čiire).
From Proto-Finnic *kiirek, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian šķire, Lithuanian skỹris).
From Proto-Finnic *kiiruh, a variant of *kiireh (whence kiire).
From Proto-Finnic *kiiski, possibly from Proto-Uralic *kiśkɜ.

parole.significato: to deny (to assert that something is not true)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ki(i)städäk.
From Proto-Finnic *kiit'os, equivalent to kiittää (“to thank”) + -os.

parole.significato: to thank [with elative ‘for’], express one's gratitude
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kiittädäk.

parole.significato: to race, speed, fly, dash, scud
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kiitädäk, possibly ultimately sound-symbolic. Cognate with Ingrian kiitää, Karelian kiiteä and possibly dialectal Estonian kiiama.

parole.significato: to tinkle, jingle, clink, ring (to make light high-pitched metallic sounds, rather like a very small bell)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kilistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *kiljudak (compare Estonian kiljuma), ultimately onomatopoeic.
From Proto-Finnic *kilkkadak; onomatopoeic
From Proto-Finnic *kilkki (“(very) small animal”).
From Proto-Finnic *killittädäk, sound-symbolic root + -ttää

parole.significato: sprat, European sprat, brisling, brisling sardine, garvock (Scotland), Sprattus sprattus (species of small marine fish…
parole.testo: kilo + haili, from Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian kilu).
From Proto-Finnic *kilpi (compare Estonian kilp, Livonian kiļb, more distantly also Northern Sami galba), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlībō (compare Old Norse hlíf).

From Proto-Finnic *kimalainën. Possibly a borrowing from Proto-Slavic *čьmeľь, itself likely onomatopoetic; attempts at deriving from kimeä (“shrill”) or kimaltaa (“to glitter”) are semantically unconvincing, since bumblebees don't glitter and the sound they emit is the opposite of shrill. Compare K
From Proto-Finnic *kimppu (compare Estonian kimp, Ingrian kimppu, Karelian kimppu, Livonian kimp).

parole.significato: mitten, mitt (type of glove or garment that covers a hand with a separate sheath for the thumb, but not for other finge…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kindas (compare Estonian kinnas, Ingrian kinnas, Karelian kinnaš, Livonian kīndaz, Ludian kindaz, Veps kindaz, Votic činnõz), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kimdas (compare Latvian cimds).

parole.significato: hock (tarsal joint of a digitigrade quadruped)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kinder. Cognate with Estonian kinner, Karelian kinner and Votic činner.

parole.significato: tarsus (of an animal; the part of the foot between the main part of the hindlimb and the metatarsus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kinttu, from the same root as *kinder (whence kinner). Cognate with Ingrian kinttu (“thigh”), Karelian kinttu (“foot, calf, thigh, ham”), Estonian kint.
From Proto-Finnic *kip'at'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *kiperä. May be related to Erzya кеверемс (keverems, “to roll down”).
From Proto-Finnic *kipedä. Related to Ingrian kippiä, Karelian kibie, Livvi kibei, Estonian kibe and Votic čippa.
From Proto-Finnic *kipinä (compare Veps kibin). The word has multiple variants in Proto-Finnic, resulting in different forms in related languages (e.g. Estonian kibe, Ingrian kipuna, Võro kipõń).
From Proto-Finnic *kippo, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kippǭ.

parole.significato: pain, ache, hurt (bodily suffering, sometimes also figuratively other kinds of suffering)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kipu. Equivalent to kipeä (“sore, painful; ill, sick”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *kipuna, a variant of kipinä.
From Proto-Finnic *kiredä (compare Karelian kirie), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kirɜ (compare Northern Sami garas, Moksha киремс (kirems)).

parole.significato: book (collection of sheets of paper bound together containing printed or written material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirja. Originally meant something like "carved mark or decoration" or "embroidered decoration", and some derived terms get their meaning from these former senses (e.g. kirjonta (“embroidery”)). The modern sense developed after the introduction of writing and has developed somewhat

parole.significato: colorful, colored, mottled, iridescent, multicolored, variegated
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirjaba, equivalent to kirja + -va.
From Proto-Finnic *kirjoi. Equivalent to kirja (“embroidery”) + -o.

parole.significato: bright (emitting or reflecting much light; luminous, intense, brilliant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirk'as. Cognate to Ingrian kirkas, Karelian kirkas and Votic čirkaz (Mati). Estonian kirgas is borrowed from Finnish.

parole.significato: to scream, shriek, cry out (let out a high-pitched scream)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirkudak, possibly borrowed by metathesis from Proto-Germanic *skrīkijaną, if not onomatopoeic.
From Proto-Finnic *kirnu, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *kirnijǭ (“churn”).
From Proto-Finnic *kiro, from Proto-Uralic *kira-(w-).
From Proto-Finnic *kirot'ak (compare Estonian kiruma, Votic čirotõ), equivalent to kiro (“curse”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *kirpedä, derived from a root borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kirpti); according to EVE, the adjective may be a back-formation from the now dialectal verb kirventää, which would derive from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *kirppu. Cognate to Estonian kirp, Votic čirppu.

parole.significato: ground frost (frozen top layer of soil caused by cold weather in winter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirci (compare Estonian kirs, Ingrian kersi, Karelian kirsi, Livonian kirt), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian apskirsti (“to freeze”)).

From Proto-Finnic *kirstu (compare Estonian kirst, Votic kirstu), of unknown further origin, but related to Latvian šķirsts (“chest, coffin”) and dialectal Russian ке́рста (kérsta); there is no consensus on the direction of borrowing. The word however cannot be older than Finnic due to the consonant
From Proto-Finnic *kirves (compare Estonian kirves), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian cirvis, Lithuanian kirvis).

parole.significato: to slip (move or slide out of something that is holding it in place, especially from someone's grip)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirbot'ak. Related to Karelian kirvota, Salaca Livonian ḱirb and Veps kirbota.
From Proto-Finnic *kisa (compare Karelian kisa (“dance, play”)).

From Proto-Finnic *kiskoidak (compare Estonian kiskuma), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kiśka- (compare Northern Sami gaikut, Moksha [script needed] (kəśkəŕams) and possibly Udmurt [script needed] (keśni̮)).

parole.significato: mouth, especially a large, wide open mouth
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kita (compare Estonian kida, Karelian kita, Livonian ki’d, Ludian kida, Veps kida).

parole.significato: to squeak, squeal, grate (to emit a high-pitched sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kidistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä. The strong grade -t- was levelled to all forms.
From Proto-Finnic *kickedäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kičke- (compare Erzya кочкомс (kočkoms, “to root out”), кочкамс (kočkams, “to choose”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kic'as (“narrow”) (compare Estonian kitsas, Ingrian kitsas, Livonian kitsāz).

parole.significato: to suffer pain (particularly on the brink of death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kitudak, possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *kiče (“illness”).

parole.significato: sauna stove, sauna heater; a traditionally wood-burning stove, but now possibly an electrical heater; it is covered wit…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kiukasa, a contracted compound of kivi (“stone”) + kasa (“heap, pile”). Compare Karelian kiukua.

From Proto-Finnic *kiuru (compare Ingrian kiuru, Karelian kiuru, Votic čiuru and dialectal Estonian kiur). Possibly related to Latvian cīrulis, in which case the Finnic word might be borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *kiusat'ak (compare Estonian kiusama, Karelian kiusata, Livonian kiužõ, Votic čiuzõtõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *keusaną (compare Gothic 𐌺𐌹𐌿𐍃𐌰𐌽 (kiusan, “to test, to prove”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kives, equivalent to kivi (“stone”) + -s.
From Proto-Finnic *lonk'at'ak. The initial k- in Western Finnish is prothetic, perhaps representing onomatopoeic or sound-symbolic influence.
From Proto-Finnic *koktat'ak. Equivalent to kohda- (“spot, place”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *kohëlo, of sound-symbolic origin.

parole.significato: wash (the sound of the breaking seas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kohina, equivalent to kohista + -na.
From Proto-Finnic *kohistak. koh- + -ista; of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *kohma.
From Proto-Finnic *kohot'ak. Cognate with Estonian kohuma, Ingrian kohota and Votic kohotõ.

parole.significato: to raise, elevate, lift, uplift, hold up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kohottadak, equivalent to kohota (“to rise”) + -ttaa.

parole.significato: spot, location (especially a more exact location of or within something else)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kokta (compare Estonian koht), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kokto (compare Latvian kakts (“corner, nook”), Lithuanian kakta (“forehead”)).
From Proto-Finnic *koktu (compare Estonian kõht), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *koktɜ (compare Erzya кувтёл (kuvťol, “pod, husk (seed case)”) and Udmurt кӧт (köt, “belly, stomach, body cavity”)).

parole.significato: moth: common clothes moth, Tineola bisselliella
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *käjä. Cognate with Estonian koi, Erzya ки (ki).
