From Proto-Finnic *koi, from Proto-Uralic *koje.
From Proto-Finnic *koinat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *koipi (compare Ingrian koipi, Karelian koipi), a variant of *koipa (compare Estonian koib, Livonian kūoiba, Votic koipõ).
From Proto-Finnic *koiras, from Proto-Uralic *kojera (the same root as in koira (“dog”)).
From Proto-Finnic *koiruc, equivalent to koira + -uus
From Proto-Finnic *koittadak, equivalent to koi (“dawn”) + -ttaa.

parole.significato: to experience, trial, undergo; to suffer

From Proto-Finnic *kokka.

parole.significato: bonfire (large, controlled outdoor fire, as a signal or to celebrate something)

From Proto-Finnic *kokkoi (“eagle”).

From Proto-Finnic *kolistak, equivalent to kol- + -ista; from kolata (“to clatter”).

From Proto-Finnic *kolmanci, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kolmamte; roughly equivalent to kolme (“three”) + -s (“-th”) (for the -a-, see the Proto-Finno-Permic entry).
From Proto-Finnic *kolmë(t) (compare Estonian kolm), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kolme (compare Erzya колмо (kolmo), Northern Khanty хәԯум (həłum), Northern Mansi хӯрум (hūrum), Hungarian három).
From Proto-Finnic *kolmë(t) kümmentä. Equivalent to kolme (“three”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).
From Proto-Finnic *kolmë(t) toicta (kümmentä) (literally “three of the second decade”). Equivalent to kolme (“three”) + -toista (“of the second”).

parole.significato: threesome, group of three, trio, triplet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kolmikkoi. Equivalent to kolme (“three”) + -ikko.

parole.significato: hole, dent, groove, nook (hollow place or cavity, especially a small one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kolo, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kolɜ.

parole.significato: wooden trunk, chest, large wooden box
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *komëi (if akin to dialectal Karelian komeikko (“rocky ground”), komu (“flax or hemp chaff”), Estonian komin (“canopy, storage place; range or oven hood”) < *kom(ë)ina).
From Proto-Finnic *komistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *kombëh (compare Estonian komme).
From Proto-Finnic *kompidak.

parole.significato: to hop or move on one foot
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *konk'at'ak (compare Estonian konkama).
From Proto-Finnic *konna, of unknown further origin. Cognate with Estonian konn, Votic konnõ.
From Proto-Finnic *konsa (compare Karelian konša, Veps konz), derived from *ko-.

parole.significato: to move or crawl slowly and/or clumsily
parole.testo: Likely from Proto-Finnic *kontidak, probably equivalent to kontti + -ia.
From Proto-Finnic *kontija.
From Proto-Finnic *kontta.

parole.significato: traditional type of knapsack made of birch bark
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kontti, possibly from Proto-Uralic *konte. Cognate to Karelian kontti and Livonian kōņtad (“testicles”).
From Proto-Finnic *kontti, possibly from Proto-Uralic *konte. Cognate to Estonian kont (“bone”).
From Proto-Finnic *kontu.
From Proto-Finnic *kogot'ak, equivalent to koko (“whole, entire”) + -ta. Cognate with Estonian koguma.
From Proto-Finnic *kopëda.

From Proto-Finnic *koppala, from Proto-Finno-Permic *koppala.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *korëda.
From Proto-Finnic *korënta (compare dialectal korenta, Estonian kõrend, Ingrian korenta, Karelian korento /korenda, Veps korend, Votic kõrõta).

parole.significato: to wheeze (breathe with difficulty and loud), rattle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. Compare Erzya корномс (kornoms, “to snore”).
From Proto-Finnic *korja.

parole.significato: to repair, fix, mend, remedy (restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korjat'ak (compare Estonian korjama (“to collect, pick”), Votic kõrjõtõ (“to bury; to hide”)), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *korja-.

parole.significato: high (physically elevated, extending above a base or average level; located at a great altitude)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korkëda.

parole.significato: synonym of palokärki (“black woodpecker; Dryocopus martius”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koroi, of onomatopoeic origin.

From Proto-Finnic *korpi (“deep forest”) (compare Estonian kõrb, Livvi korbi (“big spruce forest”), Veps korb), probably from Proto-Uralic *korpe, in which case cognate with Erzya куро (kuro), Northern Khanty [script needed] (χăr), Western Mansi [script needed] (kōrp) and Forest Nenets [script neede

parole.significato: culm; stem of a grass or sedge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korci, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *karti (compare Lithuanian kartis (“thin rod, mowing, raking”)).

parole.significato: horsetail (any of the pteridophytic plants in the taxonomic genus Equisetum of the family Equisetacae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kort'ëh. Cognates include Karelian korteh and Veps kortez.
From Proto-Finnic *korva (compare Estonian kõrv).

parole.significato: to scorch, parch, sear (to burn the surface of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korbëntadak. Equivalent to korveta + -ntaa.

parole.significato: to annoy, irritate, vex; (impersonal) to be annoyed, irritated, vexed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korbët'ak, from Proto-Uralic *korpe-. Cognates include Erzya курвамс (kurvams) and possibly Hungarian hervad.

parole.significato: to propose (marriage) to, pop the question (ask to marry)

From Proto-Finnic *koskëlo, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kośka.

parole.significato: rapid(s) (a rough section of a river or stream)

parole.significato: to get moist, to get damp
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kostudak, reflexive derivative kostaa + -ua, originally meaning “to return” (intransitive). parole.significato: home (house or structure in which one lives; place of the affections, or of refuge or rest)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kotëi. Equivalent to kota + -i.

From Proto-Finnic *koto. Equivalent to kota + -o. Cognate with Estonian kodu.
From Proto-Finnic *kotti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kuddô.

parole.significato: moment, short while (short period of time)

From Proto-Finnic *kouko (compare Estonian kõuk), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian kaukas).
From Proto-Finnic *kopra, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kopra.
From Proto-Finnic *kokri (compare Estonian koger, Livonian ko’ggõrz).

From Proto-Finnic *kovëra.
From Proto-Finnic *kovët'ak. Equivalent to kova (“hard”) + -eta.

From Proto-Finnic *kuhilas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skūilaz.

From Proto-Finnic *kukku.

parole.significato: to wear (out) (cause to wear, cause wear on) (e.g. clothes or parts)

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kumartadak, equivalent to kumara (“hunch”) + -taa.

From Proto-Finnic *kumpi. Equivalent to ku- (interrogative stem) + -mpi.

parole.significato: to castrate, geld (to remove the testicles of an animal; to castrate a male animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koohit'ak. Equivalent to kuohia + -ita.

parole.significato: foam, froth, spray, spume; turbulence or bubbling of water or a similar fluid caused by rapid movement, boiling or erup…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koohu (compare Estonian kohuma, Ingrian koohu, Karelian kuohu).

parole.significato: hoe (agricultural tool consisting of a long handle with a flat blade fixed perpendicular to it at the end)

Uncertain. Possibly from Proto-Finnic *koona, from Proto-Uralic *kane ~ *kana. Related to Karelian kuona.

parole.significato: snout, muzzle (protruding part of an animal's head which includes the nose, mouth and jaws)

parole.significato: to become, develop to something, grow up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koontudak.

From Proto-Finnic *koovi, of onomatopoeic origin. Cognate with dialectal Estonian koov.

parole.significato: bubble (spherically contained volume of air or other gas)

From Proto-Finnic *kupu. Related to Karelian kupu, Ludian kubu and Veps kubu.

From Proto-Finnic *kurmicca.

From Proto-Finnic *kuti-, which is of sound-symbolic origin. Possibly also related to Lithuanian kuténti (“to tickle, titillate”); the words may both be separately sound-symbolic or, alternatively, one might be borrowed from the other. Compare also Erzya кутямс (kuťams, “to tickle”).
kut- + -istaa, from Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Related to Karelian kutšistuo and dialectal Estonian kuduma (“to rot, soak”).

parole.significato: to weave (form a fabric or textile by passing strands of yarn or threads over and under one another, often on a loom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kutodak (compare Estonian kuduma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kuδa- (compare Erzya кодамс (kodams)).
From Proto-Finnic *kuccudak.

parole.significato: spawn (eggs of an aquatic organism, such as fish or frogs)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kutu. Equivalent to kutea (“to spawn”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *kuu, from Proto-Uralic *kuŋe. Cognates include Estonian kuu, Erzya ков (kov) and Hungarian hold.

parole.significato: animal fat, fat, tallow, especially reindeer fat
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuu, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric; see the Proto-Finnic entry for details.
From Proto-Finnic *kuudënci, equivalent to kuusi (“six”) + -s (“-th”).

From Proto-Finnic *kuuldak (compare Estonian kuulma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuwle- (compare Northern Sami gullat, Moksha кулемс (kulems), Eastern Mari колаш (kolaš), Northern Mansi хӯлуӈкве (hūluňkve), Hungarian hall).

From Proto-Finnic *kuuludak. Equivalent to kuulla (“to hear”) + -ua (passive verb). * (to belong; to concern): According to Hakulinen, these abstract senses are a semantic loan from Swedish höra, tillhöra, itself a semantic loan from Middle High German hœrec (“obedient; (literally) one who hears”) (

parole.significato: to announce, make an audible announcement (on)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuuluttadak. Equivalent to kuulua (“to be heard”) + -ttaa (curative verb), literally “to make heard”. Compare Estonian kuulutama.
From Proto-Finnic *kuuma.
From Proto-Finnic *kuumëntadak, equivalent to kuuma (“hot”) + -ntaa (factitive verb)

From Proto-Finnic *kundëldak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuntale- (compare Hungarian hall), frequentative of *kunta- (“to hunt, catch”) (compare Erzya verbs кундамс (kundams, “to catch; to grip”) and кунсоломс (kunsoloms, “to listen; to comply, obey”)). The long vowel -uu- is by contamination with kuul

parole.significato: groove, ridge (long, narrow channel or depression)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kurna, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kurńa.

Somehow from Proto-Finnic *kurdëh ~ *kurnëh ~ *kurnës (difficult to reconstruct due to seemingly irregular sound changes, but compare dialectal kuurne, Estonian kurt, Karelian kuurnis, Ludian kuurniž, Veps kurdiž, Võro kurt'), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian kurls (“deaf”) and Lithuan
From Proto-Finnic *kuuro (compare Karelian kuuro- in kuuropeä, Veps kuro, Votic kuuro), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skūrō (“storm, rain shower”) (compare Swedish skur, English shower).
From Proto-Finnic *kusa- (compare Estonian kuslapuu, Karelian kuusain), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *kusa (compare Western Mari кузъ (kuz), Udmurt гузем-пу (guźem-pu)).
From Proto-Finnic *kuuci (compare Estonian kuus), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kutte (compare Erzya кото (koto), Northern Khanty хәт (hət), Northern Mansi хо̄т (hōt), Hungarian hat).

parole.significato: spruce (any tree in the genus Picea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuusi (compare Estonian kuusk), from Proto-Uralic *kowse (compare Northern Sami guossa, Erzya куз (kuz), Eastern Mari кож (kož), Udmurt кыз (kyz), Tundra Nenets хады (xadi)).
From Proto-Finnic *kuucikkoi. Equivalent to kuusi (“six”) + -ikko.
From Proto-Finnic *kuusikkoi. Equivalent to kuusi (“spruce”) + -ikko.
From Proto-Finnic *kuuci kümmentä. Equivalent to kuusi (“six”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).
From Proto-Finnic *kuuci toicta (kümmentä) (literally “six of the second decade”). Equivalent to kuusi (“six”) + -toista (“of the second”).

parole.significato: picture, figure (representation of visible reality produced by e.g. drawing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skuwwô (“shadow, reflection”) (whence Swedish skugga (“shadow”), Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌿𐌲𐌲𐍅𐌰 (skuggwa, “mirror”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kubas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kūbaz (whence Icelandic kúfur, Old Norse *kúfr (“elevation, heap, bulge, round top”)).

parole.significato: loin (part of the body between the ribs and hips)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kubëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hupiz.

parole.significato: side (of a human or an animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *külki (compare Estonian külg, Veps külʹg). Initially likely an anatomical term, although it has also developed the more abstract meaning “side” in most other Finnic languages as well.

parole.significato: an intensifier; corresponds to the English auxiliary do in many cases
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küllä (compare Estonian küll, Ingrian kyl, Livonian ki’l), from earlier *küllä (compare Northern Sami galˈle), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *k⁽ʷ⁾el- (compare Lithuanian keli̇̀ (“how many, some, few, several”)). The adverb developed from the noun, while the interjectio
From Proto-Finnic *külläinen, equivalent to kyllä (“abundance, plenty”) (this sense no longer used in modern Finnish) + -inen.

From Proto-Finnic *külmä (compare Estonian külm), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *külmä (compare Ter Sami kallm, Erzya кельме (keľme), Eastern Mari кылме (kylme)), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gélmō.

parole.significato: to bathe, take a bath (previously, to bathe in a sauna in particular; now more often to bathe in a bathtub)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *külpedäk.

parole.significato: to bathe, bath (clean someone by immersion in water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *külbettädäk, equivalent to kylpeä (“to bathe”) + -ttää.
From Proto-Finnic *külvädäk (compare Estonian külvama, Livonian ki’llõ, Ludian külvädä, Votic čülvä).

parole.significato: village (rural habitation smaller than a town)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *külä (compare Estonian küla), from Proto-Uralic *külä (“dwelling”) (compare Northern Sami gallet (“to visit”), Northern Mansi кол (kol, “house”)). First attested in 1330 in the place name Ylyskølum.
Proto-Finnic *kümmen, see kymmenen

From Proto-Finnic *kümmen, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kümme-ne (compare Erzya кемень (kemeń)). The original nominative singular form (kymmen) was replaced by the genitive singular form under the influence of kahdeksan and yhdeksän for which the nominative and genitive singular forms are also identical
From Proto-Finnic *kümmenenci. Equivalent to kymmen (“ten”) + -s (“-th”).
From Proto-Finnic *kündäp'äs.

parole.significato: threshold, doorsill, sill, doorstep (lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kündüs (compare Estonian künnis, Ingrian kynnys, Karelian kynnyš, Veps künduz, Votic čünnüz), possibly equivalent to kynsi (“(finger)nail”) + -ys (compare Erzya кенкш (kenkš, “door”), possibly from кенже (kenže, “(finger)nail”)).
From Proto-Finnic *künci (compare Estonian küüs), from Proto-Uralic *künče (compare Ter Sami kannc, Erzya кенже (kenže), Hungarian köröm).

parole.significato: to plough/plow, till (prepare soil for planting with a tool)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küntädäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *künčä- (“to dig”).
From Proto-Finnic *küpci; see kypsä or Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: ripe, mature, matured (ready for reaping or use)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küpci, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian cepts; see Proto-Finnic entry for more). The inflection type has been analogically remodelled; earlier inflection kypsi (genitive kypsen, partitive kystä) still survives in some dialects, usually as a noun. In others, the parti
From Proto-Finnic *küpärä (“hat”), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kepur- (compare Latvian cepure (“hat”)).

From Proto-Finnic *kürpä (compare Estonian kürb, Ingrian kyrpä, Karelian kyrpä, Ludian kürb, Votic čürpä (Pummala)). The word is first attested in the writings of Christfrid Ganander in 1786, with its first appearance in a dictionary dating back to 1848. The word is sometimes said to have originally

parole.significato: synonym of reikäleipä (“type of rye bread”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kürsä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *kürsä (compare Erzya кши (kši, “bread”)).
From Proto-Finnic *küsüdäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *küśe-w-. Compare Karelian kyšyö, Estonian küsida, Erzya кевкстемс (kevkstems) and Moksha кизефтемс (kizeftems).

parole.significato: to smolder/smoulder (burn with no flame and little smoke)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütedäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *küče-.

parole.significato: to hook, hook up, connect, couple
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütkedäk, from Proto-Uralic *kütke- (compare Eastern Mari кычкаш (kyčkaš), Udmurt кыткыны (kytkyny), Hungarian köt).

parole.significato: short tether used to hook up animals in a barn
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütküt, equivalent to kytkeä (“to hook up”) + -yt. Compare kytky (“rope's bend; attachment”).

parole.significato: brother-in-law of a woman; brother of one's husband
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütü.
From Proto-Finnic *küben.

parole.significato: pigeon, dove (bird of the family Columbidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kühkü, probably of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *kükkidäk. Equivalent to kyykky (“squat, crouch”) + -iä.

parole.significato: squat, crouch (position assumed by bending deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kükkü. Possibly ultimately sound-symbolic, but may also be a loan from Proto-Germanic *hukkōną or *hūkaną (compare Old Norse húka). Cognate with Estonian kükk, Karelian kyykkä, Livonian kikkõ and Veps kükta.

parole.significato: tear, teardrop (drop of clear, salty liquid produced from the eyes by crying or irritation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küünel, from Proto-Uralic *küńele. Cognates include Karelian kyynäl, Northern Sami ganjal, Hungarian könny.

From Proto-Finnic *küünärä, from Proto-Uralic *küńä. Cognates include Estonian küünar, Livonian kīndõr, Northern Sami gardnjil, Erzya кенере (kenere), Komi-Permyak гырддза (gyrddźa, “elbow”), the initial component of Udmurt гырпум (gyrpum, “elbow”) and Hungarian könyök.

parole.significato: striped animal, especially a cow that has a white area along the spine
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küüttoi, possibly from *küü (kyy (“viper”)) in reference to the stripes.
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *kügäs ~ *kük'äs, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skukkaz (compare Old Saxon skok). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.

parole.significato: to croak (utter in a low, hoarse voice)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kähistäk, ultimately onomatopoeic.
From Proto-Finnic *kähärä.
From Proto-Finnic *käkoi, equivalent to käki (“cuckoo”) + -ö.

parole.significato: sister-in-law (sister of one's spouse; wife of one's sibling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kälü (compare Estonian käli, Karelian käly), from Proto-Uralic *kälew (compare Moksha [script needed] (ḱel), Komi-Zyrian кев (kev), Tundra Nenets сел (syel°)).

parole.significato: palm (inner, concave part of hand; corresponding part of the forefoot of a lower mammal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kämmen (compare Estonian kämmal, Veps kämen), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kämmen.
From earlier käsnä, from Proto-Finnic *käsnä.
From Proto-Finnic *käppä (compare Estonian käpp (“paw”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *käppä (“paw, hand”) (compare Erzya кепе (kepe, “barefoot”)).
From Proto-Finnic *käpsä. Thought to have originally meant the skin from the paw of an animal.
From Proto-Finnic *käpü.
From Proto-Finnic *käpälä, probably from *käppä. Related to Estonian käbalad, Karelian käpälä, Veps käbäl and Erzya кепе (kepe, “barefoot”).
From Proto-Finnic *käredä.

From Proto-Finnic *kärki (“black woodpecker”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *kärke (“woodpecker”). Cognates include Karelian kärki /kärgi, Võro kärgʼ (“woodpecker”), Veps kärg (“woodpecker”) and Erzya керьгата (keŕgata, “woodpecker”).

parole.significato: stoat, short-tailed weasel; ermine (especially in the white winter coat), Mustela erminea
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kärppä (compare Estonian kärp, Livonian kǟrpa (“polecat”), Votic čärppe), of unknown further origin.

parole.significato: fly (dipteran insect of the family Muscidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kärpähinen, equivalent to dialectal kärväs (“fly egg”) + -(i)nen. Exact cognate with Ingrian kärpäin, Karelian kärbäne and Veps kärbhaine, more distantly Estonian kärbes, likely also Erzya карво (karvo), Moksha кару (karu), Eastern Mari карме (karme).
From Proto-Finnic *kärcidäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hardijaną (“to harden, endure”).

parole.significato: a wooden rack with many branches used to dry grain
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kärbäs ~ *kärbis, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harbaz.
From Proto-Finnic *kärbäs.

parole.significato: fume (gas or vapour/vapor that is strong-smelling or dangerous to inhale, especially one that emerges from burning or s…
parole.testo: käristä (“to crackle”) + -y or, a variant of dialectal kärty, from Proto-Finnic *kärtä.

parole.significato: a session of a rural district court before the reform of 1993
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerägä, derived from kerätä. A variant of dialectal keräjät, and related to obsolete Estonian kära, Ingrian keräjät, Karelian keräjät and Veps kerag.

parole.significato: hand, arm; an upper limb of a human or certain animals
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käci (compare Estonian käsi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *käte (compare Northern Sami giehta, Erzya кедь (keď), Eastern Mari кид (kid), Komi-Zyrian ки (ki), Hungarian kéz).

From Proto-Finnic *käcittädäk (“to handle, touch with one's hands; to seize, grasp”). Equivalent to käsi (“hand”) + -ittää, originally "to grasp, seize, catch". The meaning "to understand, to comprehend" is possibly a calque of Swedish begripa (“to grasp, to understand”) (compare Swedish gripa (“to

parole.significato: arm (appendage from the shoulder to the wrist, usually excluding the hand)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käcivarci. Equivalent to käsi (“hand, arm”) + varsi (“shaft”).
From Proto-Finnic *käskedäk, from Proto-Uralic *käske-.
From Proto-Finnic *käskü, equivalent to käskeä (“to order, command, tell”) + -y
From Proto-Finnic *kätkedäk (compare Estonian kätkema), from Proto-Uralic *kätke- (compare Northern Sami gietkat, Tundra Nenets седӑсь (syedăsʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *kätküt, equivalent to kätkeä (“to hide, conceal”) + -yt. Cognate to Karelian kätyt and Estonian kätki. Mostly displaced (at least in the standard language) by kehto.

parole.significato: to walk (move on the feet; travel by moving on the feet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käveldäk. Equivalent to käydä (“to walk”) + -ella (frequentative verb), although the sense “to walk” of käydä is no longer the primary one.

parole.significato: visitor, goer (one who visits or goes somewhere)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kävejä. Equivalent to kävi- (“to visit”) + -jä (“-er”), but compare käyjä.

parole.significato: to visit, go to (and return), attend (a place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käüdäk (“to walk; to ferment”) (compare Karelian käyvvä, Estonian käima), from earlier *käwe-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skēwijaną (compare Gothic 𐍃𐌺𐌴𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (skēwjan), Old Norse skæva).
From Proto-Finnic *käkrä. Related to Karelian käkrä and Northern Sami geavri. Meaning extended from original "crooked" to first "curve" then "plot, graph".

parole.significato: to use, make use of‚ employ, apply, utilize, exploit, take advantage of, exert, exercise
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käüttädäk. Equivalent to käydä (“to walk; to happen, occur; to run, operate; to ferment”) + -ttää (causative verb).

parole.significato: to turn, reorient (change the direction or orientation of); to turn (around), reverse, invert
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käntädäk (“to turn; to bend”) (compare Estonian käänama, Veps käta). Semantic development * (to turn): From Proto-Finnic or earlier. * (to invert): Semantic loan from Latin invertō. * (to bend, fold): At least from Proto-Finnic. * (to translate): Attested since the time of Mikael

parole.significato: heap of stones, especially when erected as a sepulchral monument
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kääppä.

parole.significato: to wrap (put something inside a wrapper)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kääridäk (compare Estonian käärima, Ingrian kääriä, Karelian kiärie, Veps kärdä, Votic čääriä; further also with Samic cognates, like Ter Sami кӣррэд (kīrred), possibly from Proto-Uralic *käre-.

PIE word  *kʷŕ̥mis From Proto-Finnic *kärmeh, borrowed from an East Baltic descendant of Proto-Balto-Slavic *kirmis (compare Latvian cirmenis (“maggot”), Lithuanian kirmis (“worm, (dialectal) snake”)), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷr̥mis.
From Proto-Finnic *köhidäk. Equivalent to köhä (“(dry) cough”) + -ia.
From Proto-Finnic *köhä, of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *köntti.

parole.significato: poor (with few or no possessions or money)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keühä, likely borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skeuhaz (“shy”).
From Proto-Finnic *keüci (compare Estonian köis), from Proto-Uralic *käwde (compare Komi-Zyrian кӧв (köv), Northern Mansi ква̄лыг (kvālyg)).

parole.significato: to rope, tie up (to tie with rope)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keüttädäk. Equivalent to köysi (“rope”) + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *laaka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*lāgaʀ).
From Proto-Finnic *lakso, possibly borrowed from Baltic. Related to Ingrian laksu, Karelian lakšu and Veps laks.
From Proto-Finnic *lagës, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slagiz. Doublet of laji.

From Proto-Finnic *lahja, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛒᛚᚨᚺᛃᛟ (*blahjo), from Proto-Germanic *blahjōn (“sheet, cloth”) (compare Icelandic blæja (“veil”)). Cognates include Votic lahjõ (“wedding gift”) and Ingrian lahja (“gift”).
From Proto-Finnic *lahna, akin to Karelian lahna, Livonian lō’nõz and Veps lahn, of unknown further origin.

parole.significato: rotten (of wood or a similar solid material: overridden with bacteria, thus decayed and no longer able to e.g. support…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (“fallen tree”), compare Old Norse lág (“lying tree”). Doublet of lieka and lieko

parole.significato: bay, gulf, inlet (portion of a body of water extending into the land)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lakci (compare Karelian laksi, Veps laht, Estonian laht, Votic lahti, Northern Sami luokta), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian lanktis (“arc”)). -ht- in the nominative is by analogy with the oblique case forms; the expected form laksi (compare the declension o

parole.significato: A type of trap for hunting birds, especially grouses.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lahto, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *laidun, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*laidu).

parole.significato: thin, lean, meagre, slim, skinny (of a human or animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laiha (compare Estonian lahja), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian liesas).
From Proto-Finnic *laihvo (compare Estonian lõiv, dialectal Finnish laihvo, Ingrian laiho, Karelian laiho, Votic laivo), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic leiga).

parole.significato: to lose weight, slim down (to become less heavy)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laihtudak. Equivalent to laiha (“skinny, thin”) + -tua.
From Proto-Finnic *laikka (compare Estonian laik), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blaikaz (“pale, white”).
From Proto-Finnic *laihna, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laihną (compare Swedish lån, English loan).
From Proto-Finnic *laihnat'ak, equivalent to laina (“loan”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *lainat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *lainëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlainiz (“leaning”).

From Proto-Finnic *laupijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laubijǭ (compare Proto-West Germanic *laubijā). The word also has the dialectal variant laupio; the -ai- ~ -au- variation remains unexplained.

parole.significato: flange (external or internal rib or rim, used either to add strength or to hold something in place)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *laippa.

parole.significato: lazy (disinclined to do work or to exertion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laiska. Cognate with Estonian laisk, Veps lašk.

parole.significato: edge, margin, border, verge, brink, side (outer limit, or the area right beside the outer limit, of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laita (“edge, border”) (compare Estonian laid, Ingrian laita, Karelian laita, Veps laid, Votic laitõ). Probably related to *laita (“route, way”) (which could rather be the direct origin of the sense "state of affairs"), in which case borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laidō.
From Proto-Finnic *laito.
From Proto-Finnic *lagittadak (“to place”), borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *lagjaną (“to lay”).
From Proto-Finnic *lagittadak (“to criticize”), borrowed and derived from Proto-Germanic *lahaną (“to blame”), or of the same origin as laittaa (etymology 1).
From Proto-Finnic *laiva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flawją; cognates include Estonian laev. Compare also Lithuanian lai̇̃vas (“ship”).
From Proto-Finnic *lakëda (compare Ingrian lakkia, Ludian laged, Votic lakka), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flakaz and nativized with *-ëda.

parole.significato: summit (topmost point of e.g. a hill or trajectory)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laki (compare Estonian lagi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flakô (compare Old Norse flaki).
From Proto-Finnic *lakka, probably at least partially from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse flaki (“wicker fence or barrier”)).
From Proto-Finnic *lakki, equivalent to lakka (“shelter, canopy, lean-to”) + -i.

parole.significato: lodging (condition of a plant that has been flattened in the field)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lako (compare Estonian lagu, Ingrian lako), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lagą (compare Old Norse lag (“stratum, layer”)).
From Proto-Finnic *lalli.

parole.significato: sheep (woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis; either used generically or referring more specifically to a female mature one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lambas (compare Estonian lammas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lambaz (“lamb”) (compare Swedish lamm, English lamb).

parole.significato: pond (inland body of standing water, usually natural, that is smaller than a lake)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lampi, from Proto-Uralic *lëmpe.

parole.significato: to be cast, be projected, fall, descend (of light, a shadow, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *langët'ak. Related to Estonian langema, Ingrian langeta, Karelian lanketa, Livonian langõ, Ludian langeta, Veps langeta and Votic langõtõ. Semantic development * (to fall, fall down): Original Proto-Finnic sense. * (to be cast, projected, fall): From “to fall (down)”. * (to fall f

parole.significato: thread (twisted strand of fiber used in sewing, weaving or in the construction of string)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lanka (compare Livonian lānga, Veps lang), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *langô.

parole.significato: brother-in-law (brother of one's spouse; husband of one's sibling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lanko, borrowed from an unknown derivation of Proto-Germanic *langōną (whence Old English ġelangian, Old High German gilangōn). The original meaning was simply "relative", shifting into "relative by marriage, in-law" and finally "brother-in-law".
From Proto-Finnic *landëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *landį̄ (“loin”). Cognates include Veps landeh, Ludian landeh, Karelian lanneh.
From Proto-Finnic *lanci, from Proto-Uralic *lënte. Cognates include Erzya ландямс (lanďams, “to squat”).

parole.significato: to fall down en masse, lodge (like e.g. grain as a result of heavy rainfall, or soldiers in a devastating battle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lagot'ak, equivalent to lao- (“lodging”) + -ta.

parole.significato: to lodge, cause to flatten (of grain, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lagottadak, equivalent to laota (“to lodge, flatten”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: shoulder (the region around the shoulder blade)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapa, from Proto-Uralic *lapa.

parole.significato: shovel (tool for moving portions of material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapido (compare Estonian labidas, Livvi labju, Veps labid), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian lópeta (“shovel”), Old Prussian lopto (“spade”)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: to scoop, shovel, draw; to lift (and throw) with a scoop, ladle, shovel, spoon, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lappadak. Cognates include Estonian lappama, Ingrian lappaa and Livvi lappua.

parole.significato: child (person who is below the age of adulthood)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapci (compare Estonian laps), probably from Proto-Uralic *lëpće (“cradle”) (compare Erzya лавсь (lavś, “cradle”), Eastern Mari лепш (ĺepš, “cradle”), Tundra Nenets ебц (yebc°, “cradle”)).

parole.significato: descent, fall, an instance of descending or moving lower down, sliding down a hill, landing of an airplane etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lasku. Equivalent to laskea (“to lower, put down; to move down, come down, descend; to count, calculate”) + -u.

parole.significato: a tool with a handle and a wide, flat blade
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lasta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian lazda (“hazel”)), as hazelwood was a common material for utensils.

parole.significato: shaving (thin, shaved off slice of wood, metal, or other material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lastu, equivalent to lasta (“splint”) + -u.

parole.significato: to lap (take liquid into the mouth with the tongue), slurp like a dog
parole.testo: Probably a variant of dialectal lakkia, from Proto-Finnic *lakkidak.

parole.significato: barn, hovel, hayshed (unheated, inexpensively built roofed storage for agricultural equipment or products, especially h…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lato (compare Estonian ladu), borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚺᛚᚨᚦᛟ (*hlaþō) (compare Old Norse hlaða, Swedish lada).

parole.significato: to stack, pile up, line up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *latoidak (compare Estonian laduma, Votic lattoa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaþaną (compare Icelandic hlaða (“to pile, to stack”)).
From Proto-Finnic *latta-, possibly from Proto-Uralic *lapta.
From Proto-Finnic *lattija, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚠᛚᚨᛏᛃᚨ (*flatja), from Proto-Germanic *flatją. Compare Karelian late.
From Proto-Finnic *latu (compare Karelian latu, Veps ladu).

parole.significato: treetop, crown (the very top of a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *latva (compare Estonian latv, Ingrian latva, Karelian latva, Veps ladv).

parole.significato: to (suddenly) open up wide, to burst open; be released, come off (suddenly come free from tension, a constriction, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laugët'ak (compare Ingrian lauvveta (“to break apart”) and dialectal Estonian laugema (“to break (of ice), thaw”)), equivalent to laukea + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *lauhtudak, equivalent to lauha (“mild, temperate”) + -tua.
From Proto-Finnic *laukëda.

parole.significato: onion (any plant of the genus Allium); (in the plural) the genus Allium
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laukka (compare Estonian lauk, Livonian lōka), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laukaz (“leek”) (compare Swedish lök, German Lauch, English leek).

parole.significato: blaze (white or lighter-coloured markings on a horse's face)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laukki, probably borrowed from Baltic.

From Proto-Finnic *lauladak. Cognate with Estonian laulma, Võro laulma, Northern Sami lávlut. Possibly ultimately onomatopoeic, as sounds like tra-la-la, "la-la" or similar are associated with singing in many languages.
From Proto-Finnic *laulaja. Equivalent to laulaa (“to sing”) + -ja (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *laulattadak, equivalent to laulaa (“to sing”) + -ttaa
From Proto-Finnic *laulu. Equivalent to laulaa (“to sing”) + -u. Compare Estonian laul, Northern Sami lávlla, Votic laulu.
From Proto-Finnic *lauma, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flaumaz. No cognates in other Finnic languages are known (other than a marginal Livvi borrowing from Finnish).

parole.significato: a kind of old fish hook; a stick tapered on both ends
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *launi. Cognate with Karelian launi and Proto-Samic *luovnë.
From Proto-Finnic *lausas (“loose”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lausaz.
From Proto-Finnic *lautta (compare Karelian lautta, Veps laut), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flautaz (“float, stream”).

A southwestern dialectal form lavia adopted into the standard language as if it were originally an adjective ending in -eä (although it is not), from Proto-Finnic *lakja (whence also laaja), adopted through literary language.

parole.significato: linden, lime (tree from the genus Tilia)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëhmus (compare Estonian lõhmus, Veps lehmuz).
From Proto-Finnic *lehmä (“cow”) (compare Estonian lehm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lešmä (“large domesticated animal?”) (compare Erzya лишме (lišme, “horse”)), possibly of substrate origin.

parole.significato: to cut (divide with a sharp instrument)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëik'at'ak (compare Estonian lõikama (“to cut”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blaikijaną; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more details.
From Proto-Finnic *leinä + -o, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *laipoidak, equivalent to leipä (“bread”) + -oa.

From Proto-Finnic *laipa (compare Estonian leib (“bread”)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaibaz (compare German Laib (“loaf”), English loaf, Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌰𐌹𐍆𐍃 (hlaifs, “bread”)). Slavic words like Russian хлеб (xleb, “bread”) are likewise borrowed from Germanic.
From Proto-Finnic *lëivo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laiwaz (whence *laiwazikǭ). Related to Estonian lõo.
From Proto-Finnic *lempi, possibly originally meaning "heat, burning". Compare dialectal Estonian lemme (“spark”). Related to lämmin.

parole.significato: to fly around; to fly back and forth at least seemingly aimlessly
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lendeldäk, equivalent to lentää (“to fly”) + -ella (frequentative verb).

parole.significato: flying, flight (act of flying or being in the air)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lento. Equivalent to lentää (“to fly”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *lentädäk.

parole.significato: to calm down, stop being angry [with illative ‘at’], forgive, come around
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leppüdäk, possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *leppɜ (“soft”).

parole.significato: alder (any of the trees in the genus Alnus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leppä (compare Estonian lepp, Veps lep), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *léiˀpāˀ (“linden tree”) (compare Latvian liepa), if the Finnic and Baltic words are not of common substrate origin. Also related to Erzya лепе (lepe). * (blood): Euphemistic; refers to the fact that the
From Proto-Finnic *leski (compare Estonian lesk).

parole.significato: to dehusk (to remove the husk from)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lestäk (Karelian lessä is an exact cognate; also compare Ingrian lesemet, Votic lesemed and dialectal Estonian lesemed), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lesaną.

parole.significato: jaw (part of the face below the mouth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëuka, possibly borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *lebeh.

parole.significato: wide (having a large physical extent from side to side)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *levedä (compare Ingrian levviä, Karelian levie, Veps leved), equivalent to levä- + -eä.
From Proto-Finnic *levittädäk. Equivalent to levitä (“to spread (out)”) (intransitive) + -ttää (causative verb).
The adessive of the stem levä- with a possessive suffix, from Proto-Finnic *levä- (compare Karelian levälläh, Votic levällä), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lewō (compare Old Norse ljá).
From Proto-Finnic *lebäit'äk (compare Estonian lebama, Veps lebeita, Votic leväte), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slēpaną.

parole.significato: to wave, to waft (to float easily in or through the air)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leühüdäk (compare Estonian lehvima, Karelian leyhyö, Veps leihta), of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: tether (rope, cable etc. that holds something in place whilst allowing some movement)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëka, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *lēgā (later Proto-Germanic *lēgō). Compare Middle Dutch lage (“trap, snare”). Doublet of laho and lieko

parole.significato: fallen, rotten tree, especially one that is in water
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lēgō. Doublet of laho and lieka.

parole.significato: broth, stock, liquor (water in which food, such as meat or vegetables, has been boiled)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leemi (compare Estonian leem), from Proto-Uralic *läme (compare Northern Sami liepma, Erzya лем (lem, “fat”), Eastern Mari лем (ĺem), Udmurt лым (lym), Hungarian lé, Tundra Nenets евэй (yewey°)).
From Proto-Finnic *leentüdäk.
From Proto-Finnic *leepedä (compare Estonian leebe), from the same root as lievä.

parole.significato: stove, range, cooker (device for heating or cooking food)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leeci.
From Proto-Finnic *lëëska, cognate to Estonian lõõsk, Ingrian leeska, Votic lõõska (Kattila).
From Proto-Finnic *lëëskat'ak. Equivalent to lieska (“flame”) + -ta.

parole.significato: silt, sludge, slurry (any flowable suspension of small particles in liquid, such as fine earth deposited by water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leet'ek. Akin to Estonian leede, Ingrian leede, Livonian līedõg, Ludian ľiete, Veps lete (“sand”), Võro leedeq and Karelian lieto (“sand”).

parole.significato: to blow air on a fire or embers (to make them burn better or at a higher temperature)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lëëccodak (compare Estonian lõõtsuma), from *lëëcca, possibly of Baltic origin.

parole.significato: hem, skirt (the lower edge of a garment)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leebek (compare Veps ĺebe), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian klēpis (“lap”)).
From Proto-Finnic *leevä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlēwaz.
From Proto-Finnic *lihaba. Equivalent to liha (“flesh”) + -va.

parole.significato: excess, overabundance, glut (the state of being excessive or too much, or that which is excessive or too much)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liika (compare Estonian liig, Karelian liika, Veps liig, Votic liikõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian lieks), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *leykʷ-. Erzya лия (lija, “other, else”) possibly borrowed from the same root.

parole.significato: to move a small amount, budge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liik'ahtadak, equivalent to liikkua (“to move”) + -ahtaa (momentane verb).
From Proto-Finnic *liik'at'ak. Possibly a back-formation from liikkua (“to move”), with influence from linkata (“to limp”).
From Proto-Finnic *liikkijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *flikkiją.

parole.significato: to move, stir (change places, change one's location or position)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liikkudak (compare Estonian liikuma, Livonian likkõ, Veps likuda), possibly from Proto-Uralic *likke-(w-).
From Proto-Finnic *liik'uttadak, equivalent to liikkua (“to move”) + -ttaa.

parole.significato: cloth (piece of garment used on furniture, for cleaning, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liina (compare Karelian liina, Veps lin), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *līną (“flax”) (compare English linen, German Lein, Swedish lin). Related also to Estonian lina (“flax, linen”), which was borrowed separately from Slavic or Baltic.

parole.significato: to join, connect, attach, fasten, couple
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ligittädäk, equivalent to liki- (“close, nearby”) + -ittää.

Formally, an -e-derivative from a causative in -ttaa, though no verb *liivattaa is attested. The root is the now-obsolete liiva (“slime”), from Proto-Finnic *liiva, ultimately a loan from Proto-Germanic *slīwą (whence also e.g. Icelandic slý). First attested in 1896.

parole.significato: dirt, filth, stain, muck (foreign substance that makes something unclean)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slīką. Related to Estonian liga, Ingrian lika, Karelian lika /liga and Ludian lʹiga.
From Proto-Finnic *liki (compare Estonian ligi, Ingrian liki, Votic liči). Further cognate with Northern Sami lahka.

parole.significato: soaking; the state of being soaked
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liko.
From Proto-Finnic *lima, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slīmą.
From Proto-Finnic *litna.

parole.significato: bird (animal in the class Aves, having a beaked mouth and usually capable of flight)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lintu (compare Estonian lind), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lunta (compare Ter Sami lonnˈt, Northern Mansi лунт (lunt), Hungarian lúd); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: to soak (be saturated with liquid by being immersed in it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ligot'ak (compare Estonian liguma, Livonian li’ggõ, Veps ligota); equivalent to liko (“soaking”) + -ta.

parole.significato: to run, scoot, scurry, dash, rush
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lip'at'ak.

parole.significato: lye (solution of, or common name for sodium hydroxide)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lipëda.

parole.significato: A small cone-shaped drinking or scooping vessel made of a round piece of birchbark or similar material by folding it tw…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lippi, equivalent to lipata + -i, from dialectal lipata (“to throw, cast”), from Proto-Finnic *lip'at'ak (“to throw, to scoop”).
From Proto-Finnic *lisä (compare Estonian lisa, Veps liža), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lisä (compare Northern Sami lassi, Erzya лезэ (lezë, “help; benefit”)).

parole.significato: to add [with illative ‘in/to’] (make an addition, augment, increase; say further information, add on)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lisät'äk, equivalent to lisä (“addition(al)”) + -tä.
From Proto-Finnic *liuha.

parole.significato: to slide (to move in continuous contact with a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liukudak. Related to liukas and probably derived from the same root; liuk- + -ua.

parole.significato: sheet, strip, spline (long, thin piece of some solid material, such as paper, wood or metal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liuska (“inclined”). Compare also luiska, luisu.

parole.significato: A large number; slew, flock, swarm.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liuta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛚᛖᚢᛞᚨ- (*leuda-), from Proto-Germanic *liudīz (“people”).
From Proto-Finnic *lohi, from earlier *loši, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *laśas.
From Proto-Finnic *lohkët'ak (compare Ingrian loheta, Veps lohketa), equivalent to lohke- + -ta, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *loške-.

parole.significato: a piece cut off something; wedge, slice
parole.testo: From lohk- + -o, derived from Proto-Finnic *lohkait'ak (Karelian lohkata, Veps lohkata, Votic lõhgõtõ). Related to Votic lohko.

parole.significato: warp (set of yarns placed lengthwise in a loom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loimi.

parole.significato: to shine, glow, glare, sparkle (to emit light)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loistadak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *glōaną, *glōjaną, and derived further with + -istaa. Related to Veps loštta and dialectal Estonian loistuda.
From Proto-Finnic *loitto-, whence also Karelian loittoni, loittoine, Ludian loitton, Veps loitos.
From Proto-Finnic *loka.

parole.significato: to grate, to snap, to make a sound akin to something detaching and attaching repeatedly
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loksudak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *lolli.
From Proto-Finnic *loma (“gap”). Further cognate with Lule Sami loabme.
From Proto-Finnic *lop'ëttadak.
From Proto-Finnic *loppëdak.
From Proto-Finnic *loppi, a back-formation from loppea and/or loppu, perhaps inspired by soppi.

parole.significato: end, ending, finish, conclusion (terminal, final or closing point of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loppu. Equivalent to (dialectal) loppea (“to finish”) + -u.

parole.significato: to (come to an) end, finish, get over, stop, cease
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loppudak. Equivalent to (dialectal) loppea (“to finish”) + -ua.

parole.significato: to burble (make a loud sound of flowing, of small amounts of liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.

parole.significato: to squelch (make a soft splashing or sucking sound, like that of walking on muddy ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lodistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. The strong grade -t- was levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: to mine (remove ore from the ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *louhidak (compare Karelian louhie), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (*laužija, compare Lithuanian láužti, Latvian lauzt). * (to mine (in computing)): Semantic loan from English mine.

parole.significato: inside corner, nook, cranny, hole, hollow, pit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loukka- + -o.

parole.significato: to brake (flax) with a larger, open-toothed brake
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *louk'uttadak, equivalent to loukku (“flax brake”) + -ttaa
From Proto-Finnic *lovi (compare Ingrian lovi and dialectal Estonian lõvi (“cleft”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ludëk (compare Veps ludeg, Võro lutõq). Related to Estonian lutikas.
luho (“broken, useless”) (dialectal) + -istaa; the root is related to Karelian luho and dialectal Estonian luhku­ma, possibly from Proto-Finnic *luho.

parole.significato: flood meadow, swamp (a low-lying meadow subject to seasonal flooding; intermittently flooded meadow)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luhta, borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian lukštas (“Caltha palustris”).
From Proto-Finnic *luik'at'ak, probably sound-symbolic. For the sense “to sneak (away)”, compare also luikkia.
From Proto-Finnic *luikkoi. Related to Estonian luik.

parole.significato: strong, sound, secure, solid (capable of withstanding great physical force or strain; not likely to fail or give way)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luja. Related to Karelian luja, Ludian luja, Veps luja and also to Northern Sami lodji.

parole.significato: to read (interpret or speak aloud something written)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lukëdak (“to count”) (compare Estonian lugema), from Proto-Uralic *luke- (“to count”) (compare Northern Sami lohkat (“to read, count”), Moksha лувомс (luvoms, “to count”), Udmurt лыдӟыны (lyddźyny, “to count, to read”), Eastern Khanty ԓө̆ӈәтта (łø̆ṇətta, “to read”) and possibly Hu
From Proto-Finnic *lukëja. Equivalent to lukea (“to read”) + -ja (agent noun suffix).

parole.significato: lock (a mechanism used to lock, or fasten such that a key is required to unfasten)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lukko, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *lukǭ (compare *luką (“lock”) and English lock). Cognate to Ingrian lukku, Karelian lukku, Ludian lukk, Estonian lukk, Veps lukol, Votic lukku.

parole.significato: number (abstract entity used to describe quantity; in mathematics, a concept such as a natural number, rational number…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luku. Equivalent to lukea (“to read, count”) + -u. The grammatical and mathematical senses are from the 19th century.

parole.significato: snow (frozen, crystalline state of water that falls as precipitation; sometimes also similar frozen forms of other subs…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lumi, from Proto-Uralic *lume.
From Proto-Finnic *luminën, equivalent to lumi (“snow”) + -inen.

parole.significato: water lily (a flower of the genus Nymphaea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lumbëh (compare Karelian lummeh and Võro lymmuleht'), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *lugmis (compare Lithuanian lugmiai).

parole.significato: charm (ability to persuade, delight or arouse admiration)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lumo, from Proto-Finno-Permic *luma- (compare Northern Sami lapmut, Eastern Mari лумаш (lumaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *lunastadak. Equivalent to lunas- + -taa (for short n instead of nn, compare pakastaa); see lunnaat for the origin of the stem. Cognate with Estonian lunastama.
From Proto-Finnic *lunas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *lunaz (“ransom”). The reason for the geminated -nn- is not clear.

luo- + -(k) (k-lative singular), from Proto-Finnic *loo-, possibly from Proto-Uralic *luwe (“downstream”). Related to Ingrian looks (~ luokse), Karelian luoh (~ luo) and Veps lon (~ luona). The postpositions with luo- are originally Eastern Finnish; their correspondents in Western Finnish (tykö and

parole.significato: to create (bring into existence out of nothing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loodak (compare Estonian looma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *loŋe- (“to throw, push away”) (compare Lule Sami lågŋot, Eastern Mari лоҥаш (loŋaš) and possibly Erzya лиемс (lijems, “to prepare yarn for weaving”)). Semantic development * (to throw): Original sense found already in Proto

From Proto-Finnic *loodëh (compare Estonian loe, Ingrian looe, loove, Karelian luuveh (“west; southwest”), Livonian lūod, Ludian luodeh (“west”), Veps lode (“northwest; west”), lodeh (“northwest; west”), Votic looõ (“northwest”)). Dialectally both the meanings “northwest” and “west” were found, the

From Proto-Finnic *loodëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *flōduz (compare German Flut, Swedish flod) and derived with + -e. Originally meant flood or high tide; the sense "ebb" is a literary invention from the 1830s. See also vuoksi for further details.

parole.significato: hay that is cut/mown and left on the ground to dry
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *looko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], whence Icelandic slægja and dialectal Swedish slog.

parole.significato: mole, nevus (benign lesion on the skin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loomi (“mole, birthmark, eyelid”), from Proto-Uralic *lämä (“scab”).

parole.significato: islet (especially a rocky one or one that is far from any larger land mass and is devoid of larger vegetation such as t…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *looto.

parole.significato: to trust, rely on, count on
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *loottadak. Equivalent to luo (“at”) + -ttaa or luo- (“to cast”) + -ttaa.

From Proto-Finnic *lupa (compare Estonian luba), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] or earlier Proto-Germanic *lubą (“praise”) (compare Old Norse lof (“praise, permission”), Swedish lov (“permission; praise”)). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).
From Proto-Finnic *lurjus.
From Proto-Finnic *lustëh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *luhstǭ.

parole.significato: twig used to hold together an object made of birchbark
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luta (compare Estonian luda, Ingrian luta), possibly from Proto-Uralic *luča, or borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slutą (whence English slot). Also cognate with Proto-Samic *lotē.

parole.significato: bone (one of the rigid structural elements in a skeleton)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luu, from Proto-Uralic *luwe.

parole.significato: to believe, think, suppose, guess (something that one does not know to be true)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luuldak (compare Estonian luuletama). Further cognate with Skolt Sami loollâd.
From Proto-Finnic *luuta (compare Ludian luud and Veps lud), borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Latvian slota, Lithuanian šlúota).
From Proto-Finnic *lubat'ak (compare Estonian lubama, Karelian luvata, Votic luvatõ). Equivalent to lupa (“permission”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *lühentädäk, equivalent to lyhene- (“to shorten, become shorter”) + -tää (factitive verb)
From Proto-Finnic *lühüt.

parole.significato: to postpone, reschedule, delay, put off, procrastinate, defer
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lük'äit'äk (“to push, shove”) (compare Estonian lükkama (“to push”), Veps lükäita (“to throw, push, leave”)), from Proto-Uralic *lükkä-. Distantly related to Hungarian lök (“to push”). * (to postpone, delay): Probably a semantic loan from Swedish skjuta; further corroborated by th
From Proto-Finnic *lülü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lelew. Cognates include Estonian lüli, Komi-Zyrian лолӧд (lolöd) and Northern Khanty лӑл (lăl).
From Proto-Finnic *lümü.

parole.significato: to milk (to express milk from a mammal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lüpsädäk (compare Estonian lüpsma, Votic lühsä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *lüpsä- (“(to) milk”) (compare Erzya ловсо (lovso, “milk”, noun), Eastern Mari лӱшташ (lüštaš, “to milk”)).

From Proto-Finnic *löödäk (compare Estonian lööma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lewe- (“to throw”) (compare Eastern Mari лӱяш (lüjaš), Komi-Zyrian лыйны (lyjny, “to throw, to shoot”), Northern Mansi лыӈкве (lyňkve), Hungarian lő (“to shoot”), and possibly Erzya ледемс (ledems, “to mow, cut; shoot”)).

parole.significato: spring, wellhead (place where water emerges from the ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läktek (compare Estonian läte, Ingrian lähe, Veps lähte, Võro läteq), equivalent to lähteä (“to leave, depart”) + -e, as in “where the water leaves the ground”. Later senses have developed by influence from other European languages (compare e.g. Swedish källa, German Quelle, Engli

parole.significato: to send, dispatch (make something go from one place to another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läktettädäk, equivalent to lähteä (“to leave”) + -ttää. -h- as the weak grade of -ht- is an Eastern Finnish dialectal feature; compare lähdettää, which uses the Standard Finnish gradation -ht- : -hd-.

From Proto-Finnic *lähe- (compare Estonian läheda (adjective), Livonian ležgõl (adverb), Livvi ľähekkäh (adverb)), from Proto-Uralic *läse (compare Eastern Mari лишне (ĺišńe), Tundra Nenets ет’ (yet’) and possibly Hungarian le-).

parole.significato: to leave, go, go away, set off, take off, depart, embark, sail
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läktedäk (compare Livonian lǟ’dõ, Veps lähtta), from Proto-Uralic *läkte- (compare Skolt Sami liõhttâd, Eastern Mari лекташ (ĺektaš, “to leave, travel”), Udmurt лыктыны (lyktyny, “to come”), Eastern Khanty [script needed] (Liɣwǝt-)).

parole.significato: to spill (of a liquid: spread out of a container)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läikküdäk.
From Proto-Finnic *lämbin, from Proto-Uralic *lämpe (compare Moksha лямбе (lämbe)).

parole.significato: to warm, warm up, heat, heat up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lämbittädäk. Equivalent to lämmin (“warm”) + -ttää.
From Proto-Finnic *lämcä.
From Proto-Finnic *länci (“west ~ southwest”). The meaning “southwest” was also found in some Finnish dialects (mainly in and around Kainuu), but only rarely and is now obsolete.

parole.significato: hole (usually for ventilation; depending on location) window, shutter, door
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läpi, probably from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Eastern Mari леп (ĺep)).

parole.significato: flap (anything broad and flexible that hangs loose, or that is attached by one side or end and is easily moved)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läppä (compare Karelian läppä), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *läppɜ (compare Northern Sami leahppi, Lule Sami sliehppá, Komi-Zyrian лапӧд (lapöd), Udmurt липыны (ľipyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (lēp-), Hungarian lep).
From Proto-Finnic *läppä.

parole.significato: to squelch, splash (make a soft splashing or sucking sound, like that of walking on muddy ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lädistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä. The strong grade -t- was levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: puddle (small, often temporary, pool of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lät'äkko (compare Karelian lätäkkö, Veps lätäk, Votic lätikko), apparently derived from an onomatopoeia. First mentioned in a dictionary in 1637.

parole.significato: the steam that rises from the sauna stove (kiuas) or the heat of the sauna
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leülü (compare Estonian leil), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lewle (“spirit, soul”) (compare Northern Sami lievla, Komi-Permyak лов (lov), Udmurt лул (lul), Northern Khanty ԓыԓ (łył), Hungarian lélek (“soul, ghost”)).

parole.significato: to find; to discover; to come across
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leütädäk.

parole.significato: ground, land (surface of the Earth, especially that which is not covered by water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maa (compare Estonian maa, Karelian mua), from Proto-Uralic *mëxe (compare Komi-Zyrian му (mu), Udmurt му (mu), Northern Mansi ма̄ (mā)). Further also probably cognate with the initial component of Erzya мастор (mastor).
From Proto-Finnic *maailma, a dvandva compound of maa (“earth, ground”) + ilma (“air”).
From Proto-Finnic *makjas. borrowed from Proto-Germanic *smakjaz.

parole.significato: to be lying (in a lying or horizontal position)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *magat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *madëh. Possibly equivalent to mataa (“to crawl, creep”) + -e.

parole.significato: belly, stomach (abdomen, especially a round one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maha (compare Karelian maha, Ludian maha, Votic maha), probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Proto-Germanic *magô, Swedish mage).

parole.significato: sap, especially the sugary sap produced by some deciduous trees in spring
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mahla.

parole.significato: barren, sterile, unable to bear children
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maho, theorized to derive with maha.

parole.significato: to be able to, can do
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mahtadak (compare Estonian mahtuma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mačta- (compare Erzya and Moksha маштомс (maštoms), Eastern Mari мошташ (moštaš)).

From Proto-Finnic *mahti (compare Estonian maht, Veps maht), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mahtiz (whence also Old Swedish makt, Swedish makt). A more recent borrowing from Swedish has also been proposed. Probably also influenced by mahtaa. The adjective sense is probably by re-extraction from words

parole.significato: to fit [with illative or allative ‘into/onto’], have enough space [with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (have suf…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mahtudak, equivalent to mahta- (“to be able to”) + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *mainën. Equivalent to maa (“earth, soil”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *mainit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mainijaną. Doublet of meinata.

parole.significato: milk (white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maito.

parole.significato: synonym of muikku (“vendace”), especially vendace living in or fished from the Bothnian Bay
parole.testo: Variant of maima, from Proto-Finnic *maima, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *maiwaz. Also related to Northern Sami máivi.
From Proto-Finnic *maja (compare Estonian maja). Probably related to Latvian māja; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *majaga, from Proto-Finno-Permic *maja. Related to Veps majag and Erzya мия (mija), мияв (mijav).
From Proto-Finnic *makëda, derived from *makjas (whence maajas).
From Proto-Finnic *makkara, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Ingrian makkara, Karelian makkara and Votic makkõrõ. Seemingly has the suffix + -ra.
From Proto-Finnic *mako, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *magô.

From Proto-Finnic *maksa (compare Estonian maks), from Proto-Uralic *mëksa (compare Skolt Sami mueksie, Erzya максо (makso), Eastern Mari мокш (mokš), Komi-Permyak мус (mus), Northern Mansi ма̄йт (mājt), Hungarian máj, Tundra Nenets мыд (mid°)).
From Proto-Finnic *maksadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *maksa- (compare Erzya максомс (maksoms, “to give”)), possibly ultimately borrowed from Iranian.

parole.significato: fee, charge (amount of money levied for a service)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maksu, equivalent to maksaa (“to pay”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *maku, from the same root as *makëda and derived from *makjas (whence maajas).

parole.significato: roof pole (on a birchbark or straw roof); a (thin) wooden pole or beam that extends from the ridge to the eave, with su…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian malka (“firewood, splinter”), Lithuanian malka (“firewood, splinter, log”)).
From Proto-Finnic *maldas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *maltaz (“malt”), variant of *maltą.

parole.significato: flesh (soft, often edible, parts of fruits, vegetables, mushrooms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malto, possibly a conflation of two unrelated Germanic roots, Proto-Germanic *maltaz (“soft”) and Proto-Germanic *smultą (“molten fat, lard”).

parole.significato: saltbush, orach (plant of the genus Atriplex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malcca (compare Estonian malts), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Danish mælde), from Proto-Germanic *meldǭ (compare German Melde).

parole.significato: to control oneself, contain oneself, have restraint; have patience
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malttadak. Cognates include Ludian malttada and Veps maltta.

Probably from Proto-Finnic *mana (compare Southern Sami muonese (“(good or bad) spirit, omen”)). Alternatively possibly a back-formation of manala, which could then originate from maan alla (“under the ground”).
From Proto-Finnic *manat'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *manōną.
From Proto-Finnic *mankudak.

From Proto-Finnic *mancikka. Cognate with Estonian maasikas, Karelian mančikka, Livvi mandžoi and Veps manźikäińe. Probably ultimately derived from the same root as mantu (“soil”) and mantere (“continent”) with -ikka. Compare German Erdbeere, Latvian zemene and Lithuanian žemuogė, derived from their
From Proto-Finnic *marhaminta, a compound derived from two Germanic borrowings, Proto-Germanic *marhaz (“horse”) + Proto-Germanic *minþla (“bridle”).
From Proto-Finnic *marja (compare Estonian mari), from Proto-Finno-Permic *mërja (compare Erzya марь (maŕ), Eastern Mari мӧр (mör)).
From Proto-Finnic *mardas, borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *mr̥tás. Possibly a doublet of murha (see there for more).

parole.significato: to creep, worm, crawl (move slowly with the abdomen close to the ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *matadak. Cognate to Salaca Livonian matt (“to creep”) and possibly to Erzya мадемс (madems, “to lie”).
From Proto-Finnic *matala.

parole.significato: bedstraw (any plant of the genus Galium)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *matara, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *madarǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *matka (compare Ingrian matka, Veps matk), from Proto-Uralic *mëtka (compare Northern Sami muotki, Eastern Khanty мугәт (mugət), Northern Selkup мыты (myty) (Taz)).
From Proto-Finnic *mato (compare Estonian madu (“snake”)), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *mákš ~ *mačás.
From Proto-Finnic *maguk'as, equivalent to maku- (“taste, flavor”) + -kas.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?], borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mauraz. Cognate with Karelian mauroi, Livvi mauroi, and Ludian mauroi.
From Proto-Finnic *mek, from Proto-Uralic *me. The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (met).
From Proto-Finnic *mehi, possibly a variant of mesi.

From Proto-Finnic *mëla, from Proto-Finno-Permic *melä. Cognates include Karelian mela, Ludian mela (“oar”), Veps mela (“oar”), Estonian mõla (“paddle, oar”), Votic mõla (“paddle, oar”), Livvi mela (“paddle, oar”), Northern Sami mealli (“oar”), Erzya миле (mile, “oar, paddle”), Komi-Zyrian маль (maľ

parole.significato: a leprechaun-like creature that is friendly to humans and prefers darkness
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mendinkä(inen), borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *menþingō (later *minþingō), compare Icelandic minning (“memory (of the deceased)”).

parole.significato: to go [with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (move away from a point of reference)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mendäk (compare Estonian minema, Karelian männä), from Proto-Uralic *mene- (compare Northern Sami mannat, Eastern Mari мияш (mijaš), Komi-Zyrian мунны (munny), Northern Mansi минуӈкве (minuňkve), Hungarian megy (men-), Tundra Nenets минзь (myinzʹ°)).

parole.significato: going, course, ride (act of moving oneself)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meno. Equivalent to mennä (“to go”) + -o.

parole.significato: sea (a single area or the seas altogether)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meri, borrowed from some Indo-European language (probably Proto-Balto-Slavic *mári), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *móri.

parole.significato: pot, cage trap (a trap for fishing crabs, fish, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mërta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Swedish mjärde (“pot, trap”)).

parole.significato: nectar (sweet liquid secreted by flowers to attract pollinating insects and birds)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meci (“honey”) (compare Estonian mesi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mete (compare Erzya медь (meď), Udmurt му (mu), Hungarian méz), which is probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu (whence English mead), or more specifically from Pre-Proto-Indo-Iranian. In the sense “honey”,

parole.significato: wood grouse, capercaillie, Tetrao urogallus (large, black bird of grouse family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meccoi. Cognates include Ingrian metso, Livvi mečoi, Veps mecoi, Votic mettso, Ludian metšoi, Karelian meččo and possibly also Estonian metsis. Superficially metsä (“forest”) + -o, but probably rather a folk-etymological adaptation of *mët'os.
From Proto-Finnic *meccä (compare Estonian mets, Ludian mecc, Veps mec, Võro mõts), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *medjas (compare Latvian mežs, Lithuanian medis).
From Proto-Finnic *mëëkka (compare Estonian mõõk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mēkijaz or its Gothic descendant (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *meelehinen, equivalent to mieli (“mind”) + -(h)inen.
From Proto-Finnic *meelet'oin. Equivalent to mieli (“mind”) + -tön.
From Proto-Finnic *meelebä, equivalent to mieli (“mind”) + -vä. The rare sense “clever” was coined by Finnish physician and philologist Elias Lönnrot in 1847.
From Proto-Finnic *meeli, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mäle. Cognates include Estonian meel, Northern Sami miella, Erzya мeль (meľ), Moksha мяль (mäľ) and Komi-Zyrian мыл (myl).

parole.significato: to take to, to grow fond of, to become attached to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meeltüdäk, equivalent to mieli (“mind”) + -tyä.
From Proto-Finnic *mees (compare Estonian mees, Livonian mīez), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mēgaz (compare Gothic 𐌼𐌴𐌲𐍃 (mēgs)).

parole.significato: why (for what cause, reason, or purpose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *miksi, the translative singular of mikä (“what”).

From Proto-Finnic *mi (compare Estonian mis, Veps mi), from Proto-Uralic *mi (compare Erzya мезе (meze), мее (meje), Komi-Zyrian мый (myj), Hungarian mi). The nominative and genitive singular forms, which would have otherwise been monosyllabic, have been extended with -kä (as with joka and kuka), po
From Proto-Finnic *minijä, from Proto-Uralic *mińä. Cognates include Northern Mansi мань (manʹ), Hungarian meny.

From Proto-Finnic *minä, from Proto-Uralic *minä. From the same base as the plural pronoun me, the possessive suffixes -ni and -mme and the first-person verb endings -n and -mme. See the Proto-Finnic entry for more information on inflection.

parole.significato: such (indicates that the thing referred to is something extraordinary)
parole.testo: mo- + -inen, from the pronominal stem mo-, from Proto-Finnic *mo-.

parole.significato: A piece of former forest that has recently been converted to field for growing crops.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *moisa + -io. Cognate with Estonian mõis, Livonian mȯizõ, Võro mõisa and Votic mõizõ. The sense "manor or mansion in Estonia or Livonia" is a semantic loan from Estonian mõis.
From Proto-Finnic *moittidak. Cognates include Ingrian moittia, Karelian moittie and Ludian moittida.
Derived from dialectal mojoa, from Proto-Finnic *mojodak.
Derived from the pronominal stem mo-, from Proto-Finnic *mo-.

From Proto-Finnic *molëmbat, equivalent to mo- + -l(a/e)- + -mmat pl (comparative suffix). The initial component is the pronominal stem mo-, from Proto-Finnic *mo-. The nature of the middle component is uncertain, but may have a cognate in Eastern Mari моло (molo).
From Proto-Finnic *moni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mone; see them for cognates and more information.

parole.significato: bride (woman in the context of her own wedding)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *morcijan, borrowed from Baltic; compare Lithuanian marti (“daughter-in-law”), Old Prussian martin (“bride, sister-in-law”) (accusative singular). Cognates in other Finnic languages include Estonian mõrsja (“bride”), Ingrian morssia (“bride”), Karelian moršien (“bride”), Veps murze
Dialectal muhku + -ra, former from Proto-Finnic *muhku, itself possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *muška.
Variant of muhailla, from muhata + -illa, from Proto-Finnic *muha-
From Proto-Finnic *muikëda (compare Karelian muikie, Veps muiged).
From Proto-Finnic *muinainën, equivalent to muina- + -inen, from the essive plural of muu.
From Proto-Finnic *muistadak (compare Estonian mõistma (“to understand”)), probably from Proto-Uralic *muja- (compare Erzya муемс (mujems, “to find”), Eastern Mari муаш (muaš, “to find”)).
From Proto-Finnic *muju. Cognate with Karelian muju, Ludian muju, Veps muju, all meaning "dye, color". The original meaning was probably "fine dust, ash".

parole.significato: supposedly, allegedly, as if (used to express that what follows is doubtful or untrue)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *muka, probably equivalent to muu (“other, else”) + -ka. Akin to Karelian muka, Livvi muga and Veps muga.
The illative singular of muka-, from Proto-Finnic *muka-, probably from Proto-Uralic *muka (“back”).
From Proto-Finnic *muli, probably borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *mulkku.
From Proto-Finnic *mulli.
From Proto-Finnic *mullikka, equivalent to mulli + -kka.

parole.significato: mold, mull (humus); soil or earth suitable for growing plants, a mixture of mineral soil and humus
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *multa, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *muldō (earlier *muldā), compare Gothic 𐌼𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰 (mulda, “dust”) and English mould. Cognates include Estonian muld, Votic multõ, Ingrian multa, Livonian mūlda.
From Proto-Finnic *mumistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *muna (“egg; ? penis, testes”), from Proto-Uralic *muna (“egg; ? penis, testes”).
From Proto-Finnic *munëidak; equivalent to muna (“egg”) + -ia. Akin to Ludian munida and Veps munda.

parole.significato: to work (shape, form, or improve a material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mook'at'ak, likely borrowed from late Proto-Slavic *mǫka (“torment, torture”) (compare Russian му́ка (múka)), and modified with + -ta.

parole.significato: shape, form, figure (physical appearance or outline)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mooto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mōtą. Doublet with muotti.

parole.significato: crumbly (easy to break into small fragments)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *murëda. Equivalent to mur- + -ea (from the same root as murtaa).
From Proto-Finnic *murëntadak. Equivalent to mureta (“to crumble”) (intransitive) + -taa.

parole.significato: to crumble (break progressively into small pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *murët'ak, equivalent to mur- + -eta.

From Proto-Finnic *murëh (compare Estonian mure, Livonian mur), possibly derived from the onomatopoeic root *mur- also found in murista. The form murhe in particular is a Western Finnish dialectal form derived via metathesis (compare venhe, urho, perhe).
From Proto-Finnic *muristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *murjoidak; contains the suffix -oa.
From Proto-Finnic *murkina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *murginaz (“morning”). The meaning has shifted from "breakfast" to "food".

parole.significato: to break, fragment (to cause to end up in two or more pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *murtadak, from Proto-Uralic *mura-. * (to speak in a dialect): Compare Swedish bryta (“to speak with an accent”, literally “to break”).
From Proto-Finnic *murto, equivalent to murtaa (“to break”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *muru. Equivalent to mur- + -u, from the same root as murea and murtaa.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?]; compare Estonian muserdama, Ludian mutšurdada. Possibly originally sound-symbolic.
From Proto-Finnic *musta.
From Proto-Finnic *mustët'ak. Equivalent to musta (“black”) + -eta.

parole.significato: bilberry, common bilberry, European blueberry, blueberry (Vaccinium myrtillus); a common shrub in Finland, and its fruit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mustikka. Equivalent to musta (“black”) + -ikka (diminutive suffix).
From Proto-Finnic *mustudak. Equivalent to musta (“black”) + -ua.

parole.significato: mire, mud; decaying organic matter in the bottom of a lake, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *muta, from Proto-Uralic *muďa. Cognate with Estonian muda, Veps muda, Karelian muta, Erzya мода (moda).

parole.significato: curve, bend, corner, turn (a change of direction on a path, e.g. on a road)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mutka.
Possibly ultimately from Proto-Finnic *mutti- as a back-formation from a form like *mutukas, *mutukka, although neither is attested in Finnish dialects.
From Proto-Finnic *muu (compare Estonian muu), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mu (compare Northern Sami nubbi, Northern Mansi мо̄т (mōt), Hungarian más).
From Proto-Finnic *mura- (from which cognates are variously derived), from Proto-Uralic *mura.
From Proto-Finnic [Term?]; synchronically, derived from muu. Cognates include Karelian muutoma and Livonian mitmõd. Likely related to muuan (earlier muudan).
From Proto-Finnic *muuttadak, equivalent to muu (“other”) + -ttaa (factitive verb).
From Proto-Finnic *muuttudak. Equivalent to muuttaa (“to change”) (transitive) + -ua (passive verb).
From Proto-Finnic *mühkü.

parole.significato: mute, dumb (not having the power of speech)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mükkä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mükkä. Ultimately possibly borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *muH-ko-, compare Sanskrit मूक (muka, “mute”).
From Proto-Finnic *müllät'äk, ultimately sound-symbolic.
From Proto-Finnic *müristäk, from onomatopoeic root + -istä. Compare Estonian mürisema.

parole.significato: poison (substance harmful to a living organism)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mürkkü, of unclear further origin. Cognate with Estonian mürk.
From Proto-Finnic *mürtüdäk, possibly equivalent to myreä (“grumpy, bitter”) + -tyä or alternatively related to myrkky (“poison”).

From Proto-Finnic *müüdäk ~ *möödäk (compare Estonian müüma, Karelian myyvvä, Veps möda, Võro müümä), from Proto-Uralic *mixe- (“to give”) (compare Erzya миемс (mijems); see the Proto-Uralic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *müüjä ~ *mööjä. Equivalent to myydä (“to sell”) + -jä (“-er”).

parole.significato: cricetid (rodent of the family Cricetidae which includes true hamsters, voles, lemmings, and New World rats and mice)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mükrä. Cognate with Estonian mügri.
From Proto-Finnic *möö.

parole.significato: late (near the end of the day)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mööhä, derived from Proto-Finnic *möö- (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more; compare also myös). Related to Karelian myöhä, Veps möhä and Votic müühe.
