From myö + -ntää, from the same root √myö- (Proto-Finnic *möö-) as myöhä, myös, myötä. Cognate with Karelian myöntyö (“to calm down, cool down”). Originally attested in 1756 in the sense “to give in, give way, yield”; the modern senses are based on the sense “to concede, admit; to grant”, which was

From myö- (“rear, beyond”) + -s (s-lative singular), from Proto-Finnic *möö-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *müŋä (“rear, beyond”) (compare Erzya мей (mej, “reverse (side)”), мейле (mejle, “later”)). For a similar semantic development, see Hungarian meg (“and, plus”).
From Proto-Finnic *möötä. Equivalent to myö- + -tä (separative singular); the stem is the same as in myöhä and myös.

parole.significato: synonym of mädäntyä (“to rot; to degenerate”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mädät'äk. Equivalent to mätä (“rot”) + -(e)tä.
From Proto-Finnic *mäihä. Cognate with Estonian mähk, Veps mäjaz, Võro mäih, Votic mähä and Proto-Samic *muojsē.

parole.significato: hill (a relatively large, usually rounded elevation of earth; generally larger than kukkula (“hill, hillock”) and small…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäki (compare Estonian mägi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mäke (compare Eastern Khanty мӱг (müg)). First attested in 1303 (in the place name Rænthæmækj, modern Räntämäki).

parole.significato: blackfly, buffalo gnat (any insect of the family Simuliidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäkärä (probably from earlier *makara), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian makatas (“gnat”)). Cognate with dialectal Estonian mägar, Karelian mäkärä, Ludian mägär and Proto-Samic *muokēr.

From Proto-Finnic *mämmi. Related to Estonian mämm (“mämmi; badly cooked bread”), Ingrian mämmi (“oven-heated rye and malt gruel”), Karelian mämmi (“a type of sweetened food made of rye flour and malt”), Votic mämmi (“oven-heated rye malt gruel; berry porridge”) and more distantly to Northern Sami m
From Proto-Finnic *mänkidäk.

From Proto-Finnic *mäntü (compare Estonian mänd). Equivalent to mäntä (“mixing utensil made of the top of a young pine”) (archaic) + -y. Originally the word meant a young pine, and petäjä and honka were used of the older trees (but are now less common).

parole.significato: piston (solid disk or cylinder that fits inside a hollow cylinder)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäntä, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian mente). The original senses were for mixing and stirring utensils; the mechanical sense “piston” (probably 19th century) is from “plunger, dasher, churn-staff”.
From Proto-Finnic *märehtidäk, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *märɜ-. Analyzable as märe- + -htiä.
From Proto-Finnic *märistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *märkä (compare Estonian märg), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian mērka (“humidity”)).
From Proto-Finnic *märgät'äk, equivalent to märkä (“wet, pus”) + -tä.

parole.significato: to stuff (to eat in a hearty or greedy manner)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mässät'äk. Ultimately sound-symbolic
From Proto-Finnic *mäccä ~ *mäcä.
From Proto-Finnic *mätei; related to dialectal määhnä, Karelian mähnä and Livvi mähändy. If the original meaning was “soft”, possibly related to *mätä (“rotten”).

parole.significato: to shovel, scoop, draw; to lift (and throw) with a scoop, ladle, shovel, spoon, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mättädäk, possibly borrowed from Proto-Slavic *metati or older Proto-Balto-Slavic *met-.

parole.significato: rotten, putrid (decayed by being overridden with bacteria and other infectious agents)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mätä.

parole.significato: tussock, tuft, hummock (tuft or clump of vegetation forming a small hillock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mät'äs (compare Estonian mätas).
] From Proto-Finnic *mäkrä. Cognate with Karelian mäkrä, Estonian mäger and Veps mägr.

parole.significato: A loop on the ski which is used to fasten the shoes.
parole.testo: From mäys- + -tin, from Proto-Finnic *mädüs (compare Veps mäduz).

parole.significato: to bleat, to baa (of a sheep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *määkidäk (compare Estonian määgima, Karelian meäkie, Livonian mǟgõ, Võro määg'mä, Votic määkkiä), of onomatopoeic origin, from mää (“baa”).
From Proto-Finnic *mökä.

parole.significato: to make noise producing (intentionally) unclear phonemes
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mölistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.

parole.significato: A traditional South Karelian (dessert) dish made of breadcrumbs or (coarse, e.g. rye) flour mixed with sugar and/or mil…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *möllü (“a kind of semi-thick food”).

parole.significato: to growl, murmur, roar; to speak or make another kind of noise in a deep voice
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *möristäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *naaras, probably derived from the same root as nainen; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: scratch, scrape (disruption or mark on a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian narmas, Livonian nārmaz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *narwô (“scar”) (compare German Narbe (“scar”)).

parole.significato: top (the above ground part of a root vegetable)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naatti, borrowed from Old East Slavic *нать (*natĭ), from Proto-Slavic *natь.

parole.significato: beard moss, beard lichen, old man's beard (several genera of lichen that grow hanging from trees)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naava, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *nahistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.

parole.significato: leather (tough material produced from the skin of animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nahka (compare Estonian nahk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *naskiz, *naskaz (“soft leather”) (compare Old English næsc (“soft leather; deer skin”)).

parole.significato: to marry, wed (take as one's spouse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naidak, derived from the same root as nainen (“woman”).

From Proto-Finnic *nainën, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *näxe-; nai- + -nen. Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but vaimo was the more common word for “woman” in the oldest literary Finnish texts.

parole.significato: to marry (to dispose of in wedlock; to give away as wife or husband)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naittadak. Equivalent to naida (“to marry, wed”) + -ttaa.

parole.significato: drain plug, plug (plug on the bottom of a boat, closing the draining hole while the boat is afloat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naka.
From Proto-Finnic *nak'at'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *nalja.
From Proto-Finnic *napsadak, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: tack, thumbtack, pin, pushpin, drawing pin (a small nail-like fastener that can be pushed in with one's finger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nasta, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Norwegian neste, Old English nestila, Old Gutnish nast).
From Proto-Finnic *nato, from Proto-Uralic *nataw.
From Proto-Finnic *nauha (compare Ingrian nauha, Karelian nauha, Votic nauhõ).

parole.significato: to meow (of a cat: to make a meowing sound; by extension of anything else making a similar sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *naukudak ~ *näüküdäk; onomatopoeic. Compare Karelian n’aukuo, Veps näukta.

parole.significato: nail (spike-shaped fastener, now often made of metal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nakla (compare Estonian nael), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *naglaz (compare Swedish nagel). * ((coat) peg): The first coat pegs were often simply nails hammered on a wall and left to protrude out. * (unit of weight): Perhaps a later semantic loan from Germanic; in some varieties
From Proto-Finnic *nakradak, of unknown ultimate origin. Cognates include Estonian naerma, Karelian nakrua.

parole.significato: turnip (white root of a yellow-flowered plant, Brassica rapa subsp. rapa, grown as a vegetable)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nakris, compare Estonian naeris, Karelian nakris. This may be compared to an Ob-Ugric word *nëëɣər (“pine nut”), in which case their common origin would be Proto-Finno-Ugric *nëkrV-, but this is questionable due to the difference in meaning and as the consonant cluster *kr is of a
From Proto-Finnic *nakru. Equivalent to nauraa (“to laugh”) + -u.

parole.significato: cattle; cow, bull (animal of the species Bos taurus, regardless of gender or age)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nauta, borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚾᚨᚢᛏᚨ (nauta) (compare Old Norse naut, Swedish nöt (“cattle”)), from Proto-Germanic *nautą.
From Proto-Finnic *nauttidak (“to use, enjoy”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nautijaną (“to use, employ”).
From Proto-Finnic *näitei, variant of neito.

parole.significato: maiden, maid (girl or young, unmarried woman)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näitoi, derived from Proto-Uralic *näxe-.

parole.significato: virgin (person, especially a female one, who has never had sexual intercourse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näic'üt (compare Estonian neitsi, Karelian neičyt (“girl, maiden”), Livonian neitst, Veps neitšud, Votic neitsüd (“daughter-in-law, fiancée”)), a diminutive derived from the same root as neiti, neito, probably as neit- + -(i)(t)s- + -yt.
From Proto-Finnic *neljikkoi. Equivalent to neljä (“four”) + -ikko.
From Proto-Finnic *neljä (compare Estonian neli), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *neljä (compare Northern Sami njeallje, Erzya ниле (nile), Northern Mansi нила (nila), Hungarian négy).
From Proto-Finnic *neljä kümmentä. Equivalent to neljä (“four”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).
From Proto-Finnic *neljänci, equivalent to neljä (“four”) + -s (“-th”).
From Proto-Finnic *neljä toicta (kümmentä) (literally “four of the second decade”). Equivalent to neljä (“four”) + -toista (“of the second”).
From Proto-Finnic *nenä.
From Proto-Finnic *nëpada, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Old Lithuanian nepuotis), from Proto-Indo-European *népōts. Cognate with Estonian nõbu.

Derived from a dialectal verb nestää (“to drip, ooze, seep”) (compare Ingrian nestää and Livvi nestüö (“to get damp”)), which in turn is probably derived from Proto-Finnic *nepsä (“moist, damp”); thus equivalent to nes- + -tää + -e.

From Proto-Finnic *nëkla (compare Estonian nõel, Ingrian neegla, Karelian niekla /niegla, Votic niglõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nēþlō (compare Gothic 𐌽𐌴𐌸𐌻𐌰 (nēþla), Swedish nål, English needle).
From Proto-Finnic *nëuvo. Cognate with Estonian nõu, Ingrian nevvo, Karelian neuvo, Livonian nõ’v and Votic nõvvo.

parole.significato: to advise, counsel; show [with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’; or with inessive ‘with (something)’] (give advice…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nëuvodak, a denominal verb of neuvo (“advise, counsel”).

parole.significato: A type of treeless wet swamp.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nëva. Related to Estonian nõva, Livvi ńeva and Veps nova. Related to the name of the river Neva (see it for more); either from it, or vice versa.

parole.significato: to swallow, ingest (continuously or more slowly, compare nielaista and nieleskellä)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *neeldäk (compare Estonian neelama), from Proto-Uralic *ńäle- (compare Northern Sami njiellat, Erzya нилемс (nilems), Eastern Mari нелаш (ńelaš), Komi-Zyrian ньывны (ńyvny), Hungarian nyel).

parole.significato: pharynx (part of the throat; the part between the oral cavity and the esophageus and the trachea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *neelu. Equivalent to niellä (“to swallow”) + -u.

parole.significato: cape, ness, headland, promontory, (small) peninsula (form of coastal land jutting into a lake or sea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *neemi.
From Proto-Finnic *niici, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian nīts, Lithuanian nytis).
From Proto-Finnic *niistädäk (compare Ingrian niistää, Karelian niisteä, Ludian niistädä, Veps ništtä and dialectal Estonian niistama), probably onomatopoeic and akin to niiskua.

parole.significato: meadow, lea (open, non-cultivated field which grows grass and flowers)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *niittü, equivalent to niit- (“to mow, reap”) + -ty (an old consonant-stem participle form of niittää (“to mow, reap”)).

parole.significato: to mow, mow down, cut, cut down, scythe, reap (crops, hay, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *niittädäk, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *snīþaną and further derived with *-tadak, thus equivalent to niit- + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *nikka, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: phloem (vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of sugars and nutrients)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nila, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńila. Cognate with Karelian nila, Veps nila, Lule Sami njalle, Erzya нола (nola, “juice”), Northern Khanty ньел (n’jel) and Northern Mansi няль (nâlʹ).
Variant of niljellä, the adessive singular form of the dialectal noun nilki, from Proto-Finnic *nilki.
(dialectal) nilva (“slime”) + -iäinen (from Proto-Finnic *nilpa)

From Proto-Finnic *nimet'oin. Equivalent to nimi (“name”) + -tön (“-less”). * (ring finger): Stems from superstition; compare Ingrian nimetöin sormi, Russian безымянный палец (bezymjannyj palec, literally “nameless finger”), Sanskrit अनामिका (anāmikā, literally “nameless”), Chinese 無名指 /无名指 (wúmíngz

From Proto-Finnic *nimi (compare Estonian nimi), from Proto-Uralic *nime (compare Northern Sami namma, Erzya лем (lem), Eastern Mari лӱм (lüm), Komi-Zyrian ним (ńim), Hungarian név, Tundra Nenets нюмʼ (nyum)); see the Proto-Uralic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *nimittädäk, equivalent to nimi (“name”) + -ittää.
From Proto-Finnic *nirkko. Variants like nirkko, nirppi, nirppu can be found; the term is probably originally a euphemism.

parole.significato: nape, the back of the neck
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *niska. Cognate with Ingrian niska, Karelian niska, Veps nišk, nisk and Votic niskõ.

From Proto-Finnic *nisu (compare Estonian nisu, Livonian ni’zzõz, Veps nižu, Votic nisu). Equivalent to nisä (“udder, breast”) + -u; the sense may have originally been “snack”, from which “wheat, something made of wheat”, or may have evoked a comparison between the white milk secreted from a teat an

parole.significato: mamma (milk secreting organ of mammals, including the mammary gland and the nipple or teat; technically for humans a br…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nisä, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ńimśä. Related to Estonian nisa, Veps ńiža and Votic nisä.
From Proto-Finnic *nitodak (compare Estonian niduma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńiδa- (compare Northern Sami njađđit, Erzya недямс (neďams)).

parole.significato: joint (part of the body where bones join)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nivel, derived from nivoa.

parole.significato: with abnormally oriented or curly grain, but without brown streaks like in visakoivu
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *niverä, compare Võro niverdama (Tarvastu Mulgi dialect). Possibly akin to nivoa, compare nivel.
From Proto-Finnic *nivodak.
From Proto-Finnic *nivu-, probably equivalent to nivu- + -nen
From Proto-Finnic *noita (“shaman”) (compare Estonian nõid), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *nojta (compare Northern Sami noaidi (“shaman”)).

parole.significato: to cast a spell on, to cast a curse on, bewitch, hex
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noitudak (compare Estonian nõiduma, Võro nõidma), equivalent to noita (“witch”) + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *noja.

parole.significato: soot (fine black or dull brown particles)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noki, of unknown further origin. Cognate with Estonian nõgi and Veps nogi.

parole.significato: beak, bill, rostrum (anatomical structure of birds)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nokka (compare Estonian nokk, Karelian n'okka, Votic nokkõ), possibly from Proto-Uralic *nokka.

parole.significato: to peck (strike or pierce with the beak)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nokkidak, equivalent to nokka (“beak, bill”) + -ia.

From Proto-Finnic *nokkë-, probably derived from nokka (“beak”), in reference to the prickliness. Compare Estonian nõges and Votic nõkõn, nõkõz (Mati, Kõrvõttula). Morphologically the word may contain the suffix -onen.
From Proto-Finnic *nolkki.
From Proto-Finnic *nopëda (compare Estonian nobe), possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*snōƀ(r)jaR).

The sense "catkin" is through the development "to flow, drip" → "(tapered) tip" → "catkin"; the word is derived from Proto-Finnic *norkudak (“to flow, drip”) (compare Estonian nõrguma, Karelian norkkuo, Veps norkaita).
From Proto-Finnic *nor(k)udak.

From Proto-Finnic *nostadak. Equivalent to no(u)s- (“to rise”) + -taa. * (to draw, withdraw, take out): Perhaps by analogy with picking up or lifting money out of a box or chest. * (to take legal action): From the figurative sense “to cause, bring about”.
From Proto-Finnic *nockëda (compare Ingrian notkia, Veps notked), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńočka (“bend, curve; bent, flexible”) (compare Erzya нучкамс (nučkams, “to bend”)).
From Proto-Finnic *nocko (compare Estonian nõtk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńočka.

parole.significato: to sag, bend (under or as under a weight)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nockudak, equivalent to notke- (“flexible”) + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *noustak. Cognates include Ingrian noissa, Karelian noussa, Livonian nūzõ, Veps nousta, Votic nõissõ, nõisõ, as well as Estonian tõusma (irregular sound change).
From Proto-Finnic *nousu. Equivalent to nousta (“to rise”) + -u.

parole.significato: to fetch, retrieve, (go) pick up, (come) get
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noutadak, from Proto-Uralic *ńoxe-.

parole.significato: club, cudgel (heavy stick intended for use as a weapon)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nuija.
From Proto-Finnic *nuk'ahtadak (compare Karelian n’ukahtua, Võro nukahtama, Votic nukahtaa (Rajo)), equivalent to nukkua (“to sleep”) + -ahtaa.

From Proto-Finnic *nukkudak (compare Karelian n'ukkuo, Ludian nukkuda, as well as Estonian tukkuma and Livonian tukkõ, for which compare nousta ~ Estonian tõusma). Further possibly also related to Northern Sami nohkkat (which might be borrowed from Finnic).
From Proto-Finnic *nummi. Cognates include Estonian nõmm, Livonian num and Votic nõmmi.

parole.significato: to nod, sway (to move up and down)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nookkudak.

From Proto-Finnic *nooli (compare Estonian nool), from Proto-Uralic *ńële (compare Northern Sami njuolla, Erzya нал (nal), Udmurt ньӧл (ńöl), Northern Mansi ня̄л (nâ̄l), Hungarian nyíl, Kamassian ньа (ńa)).

From Proto-Finnic *nooldak (compare Livonian nūolõ), from Proto-Uralic *ńale- (compare Northern Sami njoallut, Erzya ноламс (nolams), Eastern Mari нулаш (nulaš), Udmurt нюлыны (ńulyny), Hungarian nyal, Tundra Nenets нянсӑш (nyansăš°)).
From Proto-Finnic *noora, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᚾᛟᚱᚨ (*snōra).
From Proto-Finnic *nooruc, equivalent to nuori (“young”) + -uus (“-th, -ness”).
From Proto-Finnic *nootta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nōtō. Cognate with Estonian noot, Ingrian nootta, Karelian nuotta, Livvi nuottu, Ludian nuot, Veps not, Võro nuut and Votic noottõ.
From Proto-Finnic *nuristak, from an onomatopoeic root, perhaps the same root as nurkua, + -ista.

parole.significato: wrong (designed to be worn or placed inward, such as of a side in clothing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nurja.

parole.significato: corner (area in the angle between converging walls or sides)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nurkka. Cognate to Estonian nurk, Votic nurkkõ, and Livonian nūrka.

parole.significato: lawn, grass (low, dense cover of grass plants; area of land with such a cover)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nurmi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńurme. Related to Estonian nurm, Karelian nurmi, Livonian nuŗm, Veps norm, Votic nurmi, Skolt Sami njormm, Northern Khanty [script needed] (ńurəm) and Northern Mansi ню̄рым (nû̄rym).

parole.significato: to fuck, to screw, to have sexual intercourse with
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nussidak (compare Estonian nussima, Karelian nussie, Livonian nuššõ, Võro nus'ma, Votic nussia), possibly a borrowing from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Danish nusse, nosse).

parole.significato: a polled cow, bull or ox; polled cattle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nuti.

parole.significato: to sniff (make a short audible inhalation; over a prolonged period of time, as opposed to just once)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nuhkidak.
From Proto-Finnic *nuuskidak, of onomatopoeic origin. Related to Erzya носкамс (noskams).

parole.significato: to tear, pull, pluck (hair, feathers, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nüktädäk (compare Veps nühtta), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ńüktä- (compare Erzya невтамс (nevtams), Eastern Mari ньыкташ (ńyktaš)).

parole.significato: to jerk (make sudden uncontrolled movements; move unsmoothly in sudden jumps)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nükidäk, from Proto-Uralic *ńüke- (“to rip, tear”) (compare Hungarian nyű).
From Proto-Finnic *nükü (compare Ingrian nyky-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *nükɜ (compare Erzya ней (nej, “now”), Komi-Zyrian нин (ńin, “already”)).
From Proto-Finnic *nuka (*nükä). Related to Estonian nuga, Karelian nykä and Veps nuga.

parole.significato: to skin, flay, fleece (remove the skin of an animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nülkedäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńülke-. Cognate with Erzya нельгемс (neľgems, “to take away”).
From Proto-Finnic *nürhi.
From Proto-Finnic *nürkke-. Related to Ingrian nyrkki, Karelian nyrkki and Veps nürk.
From Proto-Finnic *nüci, from Proto-Uralic *nüδe, *niδe. Cognates include Erzya недь (neď), Hungarian nyél.
From earlier *nyyt (with irregular shortening of the vowel yy > y), from Proto-Finnic *nügüt. Compare nyky-, nytten. Cognates include Estonian nüüd, Livvi nügöi, Ludian nügü, Veps nügüdʹ.

parole.significato: continuative of nytkyä (“to jerk”): to fidget
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nütkidäk.

From Proto-Finnic *näktäk (compare Estonian nägema, Karelian nähä, Veps nähta), from Proto-Uralic *näke- (compare Northern Sami niegadit, Moksha няемс (näjems), Northern Mansi нэ̄глуӈкве (nè̄gluňkve), Hungarian néz). * (to see as, regard): A semantic loan from other European languages, compare Latin

parole.significato: damp, not quite wet nor dry
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näivä (compare Karelian näivälleh, Veps näivištuda), probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian naivà, neivà).
From Proto-Finnic *näkejä. Equivalent to nähdä (“to see”) + -ja.

parole.significato: to be visible, to be seen, to show
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näküdäk. Equivalent to nähdä (“to see”) + -ua (forms stative verbs).
From Proto-Finnic *näko. Equivalent to näke- (“to see”) + -ö. Cognate with Estonian nägu, Veps nägo.

From Proto-Finnic *nälkä, from Proto-Uralic *ńäle- + *-ka. Direct cognates include Estonian nälg and Northern Sami njálggis (“tasty”). Compare the bare root preserved in niellä (“to swallow”), Uralic cognate with nuolla (“to lick”).
From Proto-Finnic *nälkähinen, equivalent to nälkä (“hunger”) + -(h)inen.

parole.significato: nipple, teat (the projection of a mammary gland)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nännei (whence also dialectal Estonian nänn, Karelian nänni, Veps ńäńei), variant of Proto-Finnic *nännä (whence Ingrian nännä, Livonian nǟna, Võro nänn, Votic nänne).

parole.significato: fingertip(s) (when talking about having something on or between one's fingertips)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näppi. Cognate to Estonian näpp, Votic näppi, and Veps ńäp.
From Proto-Finnic *näppä + -y.
From Proto-Finnic *närek.

From Proto-Finnic *närhi, originally an onomatopoeic word; cognate with Estonian -näär, Ingrian -näri, Karelian närhi, Veps näriz, Votic näri. Compare Erzya нармунь (narmuń, “bird”), the initial component of which has a similar onomatopoeic root.
From Proto-Finnic *närä.
From obsolete noun närä + -stää, from Proto-Finnic *närä (whence Livonian närā (“heartburn”)).

From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian näsi- in näsiniin), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *natją (compare Gothic 𐌽𐌰𐍄𐌹 (nati)). The semantic development would be "net" > "bast" (which was used to make nets) > "mezereon".
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *näccä.
From Proto-Finnic *näükkidäk.
From Proto-Finnic *nägüttädäk, equivalent to näkyä (“to be seen, be visible”) + -ttää (causative verb); “to make visible, make seen”.
From Proto-Finnic *näälä. Cognate to Estonian nääl, Ingrian näälä and Votic nääle.

parole.significato: stye, sty, hordeolum (infection of the glands in eyelid)
parole.testo: näärän + näppy, from the genitive of näärä, from Proto-Finnic *näärä.

From Proto-Finnic *näätä, possibly borrowed from early Old East Slavic [Term?], from Proto-Slavic *gnědъ (“brown, chestnut”). Cognates include Karelian niätä and Veps näd. Possibly displaced Proto-Finnic *nuksi (“marten”).

parole.significato: humble, meek (thinking lowly of oneself, not pretentious)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nëtra ~ *neträ (compare Estonian nõder, Votic nõdrõ).
From Proto-Finnic *ogas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. Compare Estonian oga, Ingrian oaz and Veps ogah.

parole.significato: to wait about, to wait around
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *odot'ëldak, equivalent to odottaa (“to wait”) + -ella (frequentative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *odottadak (compare Estonian ootama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *woča- (compare Erzya учомс (učoms), Eastern Mari вучаш (vučaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *ohi. Ultimately possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *woša (“parting, branching (of river, way)”), whence Erzya ужо (užo, “corner; angle”).
From Proto-Finnic *oimo, with later alteration under the influence of ohi. Compare dialectal Finnish oimo- (in oimolla, oimollaan, oimossa) and Estonian oim.

parole.significato: rein (strap or rope attached to the bridle or bit, used to control a horse or other animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ohja (compare Estonian ohi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ansijō (compare Old Norse æs).

parole.significato: to steer, drive (guide the course of a vessel, vehicle, aircraft etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ohjat'ak, equivalent to ohja (“rein(s)”) + -ta.

parole.significato: thin (having little thickness or extent from one surface to its opposite)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ohut (compare Estonian õhuke, Võro ohut), probably from Proto-Uralic *wokše (compare Northern Khanty [script needed] (oχəл)).

From Proto-Finnic *oikëda (compare Estonian õige), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *wojke (“straight”) (compare Erzya виде (vide)). Semantic development * The original sense was "straight". * "straight" → "right, correct": has parallels in other languages, e.g. Latin rēctus and English right from "
From Proto-Finnic *oinas, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *awinas (compare Lithuanian ãvinas, Latvian auns).
From Proto-Finnic *oiva, probably from Proto-Uralic *ojwa (“head”) (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: ditch, trench (especially one used for drainage)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oja.

parole.significato: to reach out (usually with käsi (“hand”)) (to extend one's hand(s) forward)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oigëntadak. Equivalent to oikea + -ntaa; oikea used to mean “straight”, but this sense is no longer used in modern Finnish.
From Proto-Finnic *oka, a variant of *ogas (whence oas).

parole.significato: branch, bough (woody part of a tree arising from the trunk, especially a firm one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oksa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *oksa. Related to Northern Sami oaksi, Eastern Mari укш (ukš).
From Proto-Finnic *oksëntadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *okse-. Cognates include Estonian oksendama, Erzya уксномс (uksnoms), Moksha уксондомс (uksondoms) and Komi-Permyak восны (vosny).
From Proto-Finnic *okci. Related to Erzya овто (ovto, “bear”). This term was displaced by euphemisms such as karhu, mesikämmen and kontio due to traditional Finnic beliefs relating to bears.

parole.significato: shoulder (part of the human torso forming a relatively horizontal surface running away from the neck)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *olka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wolka; cognate with Hungarian váll.
From Proto-Finnic *olki.

parole.significato: to be (indicating that the subject and the complement of the verb form the same thing, or that the complement describes…
parole.testo: Most forms derive from Proto-Finnic *oldak (compare Estonian olema), from Proto-Uralic *wole- / *ole- (compare Moksha улемс (ulems), Eastern Mari улаш (ulaš), Udmurt вань (vań), Northern Khanty вөԓты (wøłty), Hungarian van, volt, and possibly Tundra Nenets ӈэсь (ŋesʹ°)); see the Proto-Uralic entry f

parole.significato: being (the act of being or existing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *olo. Equivalent to olla (“to be”) + -o.

parole.significato: beer, ale (fermented beverage made of malt, originally barley, but also other cereals are used)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *olut, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*ǫluþ-) (compare Swedish öl). Possibly akin to kalja, if it is an early borrowing from an Indo-European language.
From Proto-Finnic *oma (compare Estonian oma, Votic õma). Further related to Northern Sami oapmi. Ultimately probably from the same root as olla (“to be”).

parole.significato: close relative/relation (member of the same family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *omahinën. Equivalent to oma (“own”) + -(h)inen.

parole.significato: to sew (use a needle to join pieces of fabric)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ombëldak. A word adopted into the standard language from eastern Finnish dialects, while the traditional word in western Finnish dialects for sewing is neuloa.

parole.significato: sewing work (sewn item, especially one under work)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ompëlus. Equivalent to ommella (“to sew”) + -us
From Proto-Finnic *onki, from Proto-Finno-Permic *oŋke, borrowed from an Indo-European language, probably Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hankás.
From Proto-Finnic *onnët'oin, equivalent to onni (“happiness, luck”) + -ton (“-less”).
From Proto-Finnic *onni, of uncertain further etymology.
From Proto-Finnic *onci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *omte (“cavity”) or *oŋte. Cognate with Veps onduz, Erzya ундо (undo, “hole, cavity, hollow”) and Hungarian odú (“haunt, animal hole”).
From Proto-Finnic *op'ëttadak. Equivalent to ope- + -ttaa, from the same root as oppia (“to learn”).

From Proto-Finnic *oppidak (compare Estonian õppima), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *woppe-(j-) (“to see, inspect”) (compare Northern Khanty вопиты (wopity, “to visit; to stalk”), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (wopj-)). Originally meant “to go look, check, examine (a trap, etc.)” as part of hunting vocabul

parole.significato: thorn (sharp protective spine of a plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ora, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ora (compare Inari Sami oari, Erzya уро (uro), Moksha ура (ura) and Hungarian ár), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hā́raH (compare Sanskrit आरा (ā́rā)), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ólos (compare Old Norse alr, English awl).

parole.significato: shoot or shoots of cereal or cultivated hay, usually collectively
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oras, from ora + -as.

parole.significato: squirrel (any rodent of the family Sciuridae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oraba (compare Estonian orav), from Proto-Uralic *ora (compare Northern Sami oarri, Erzya ур (ur)).
From Proto-Finnic *orih. Cognates include Veps oreh, Livvi oro.

From Proto-Finnic *orja (“slave, servant”) (compare Estonian ori), from Proto-Finno-Permic *orja (compare Northern Sami oarji (“west”), Erzya уре (ure), Udmurt вар (var)), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *áryas (“Aryan”).

parole.significato: dell (valley, especially in the form of a natural hollow, small and deep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *orko (compare Estonian org, Ingrian Orko).
From Proto-Finnic *orpana, probably from the same root as orpo. Compare also Erzya урьва (uŕva, “daughter-in-law”), Moksha ърьвя (əŕvä, “woman, wife”).

From Proto-Finnic *orpoi (compare Estonian orb), derived from *orpa(s), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hárbʰas (compare Sanskrit अर्भ (árbha)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃órbʰos (compare English orphan, Ancient Greek ὀρφανός (orphanós), Old Armenian որբ (orb)). The same word was also

parole.significato: a wooden beam or bar on which objects, such as tools, are hung from when they are not used
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *orci, from earlier *orti, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian ar̃das (“pole scaffold for drying flax”)).

From Proto-Finnic *osa (compare Estonian osa), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońća (compare Northern Sami oažži and possibly Hungarian ágyék), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hónćos (later *Hánćas, compare Sanskrit अंश (aṃśa)).

parole.significato: to know how (to do something), can (do something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *osait'ak. Probably equivalent to osa (“part”) + -ta. Cognate to Estonian oskama and Votic õzata (Mati).

From Proto-Finnic *ostadak (compare Estonian ostma), derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wosa (compare Komi-Zyrian вуз (vuz, “tax”)) with -taa; in turn, the root might possibly be borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wasaH. * (to buy, believe, accept (a story, etc.)): Semantic loan from Swedish köpa, perha
From Proto-Finnic *ostaja. Equivalent to ostaa (“to buy”) + -ja (“-er”).

parole.significato: to hit, strike, get [with illative] (a spot, target)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *osudak, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońćo- (“to get”). Probably ultimately equivalent to osa- + -ua. Compare sattua (“to hit, strike, touch”).
From Proto-Finnic *ota (compare Estonian oda), possibly from Proto-Uralic.

From Proto-Finnic *otava, from Proto-Uralic *woča. Cognates include Karelian otava, Votic õtavõ, Ludian adam, Estonian odamus (dialectal), Erzya ош (oš, “city”). The suffix, which dated back to Proto-Finnic, has not been explained. The brown bear in Finnish actually became known as otava, which is a
From Proto-Finnic *oncca, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *anþiją.
From Proto-Finnic *vottadak (compare Estonian võtma). * (to do something suddenly, impulsively, usually followed by ja (“and”)): Semantic loan from Swedish ta (och) ....
From Proto-Finnic *vottaja. Equivalent to ottaa (“to take”) + -ja (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *votto. Equivalent to ottaa (“to take”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *outo. Cognate with Estonian õud, õudne, Karelian outo.

parole.significato: door (portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ouvi, possibly from Proto-Uralic *owwe.

parole.significato: to roast (cook food by heating in an oven or fire)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahtadak. Related to dialectal pahtaa, Karelian puahtua, Ludian puahtada and possibly Erzya пуштамс (puštams).

parole.significato: lump (roughly sized relatively small or medium-sized piece of a relatively firm material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paakku. Cognates include Estonian paak and Karelian poakku.

parole.significato: horsefly, breezefly, gadfly, forest fly (fly of the family Tabanidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parma, from Proto-Finno-Permic *parma, probably onomatopoeic. Cognates include Estonian parm, Ingrian paarma, Livonian pārmaz, Veps parm, Votic paarmõz, Erzya промо (promo), пуромо (puromo) and Eastern Mari пормо (pormo).

From Proto-Finnic *paaci. Cognate with Estonian paas (“limestone, slate, top of an oven”), Ingrian paasi, Karelian poaje (“top of an oven, grating on the floor of a fireplace”), poataro (“stone which cleaves to slabs, stone slab”), Livonian pōž (“slate, limestone”), Votic paasi.

parole.significato: to become hardened, callous (of a person, their heart or soul)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paat(t)udak.
From Proto-Finnic *padëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *paþaz.
From Proto-Finnic *pagët'ak, further origin unknown.
From Proto-Finnic *paha.
From Proto-Finnic *pahainën. Equivalent to paha (“bad”) + -inen.

parole.significato: burl (US), bur, burr, gnarl (tree growth in which the grain has grown in a deformed manner)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahka, possibly from Proto-Uralic *pakša.

parole.significato: rod, pole (long, thin object such as a fishing rod)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahla, probably borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: straw chaff, such as used in animal shelters
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahna.
From Proto-Finnic *paija. Compare also Latvian paija and dialectal Russian пай (paj, “kind, nice”).

parole.significato: to patch, mend, sew (up) (a shirt, pants/trousers, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paik'at'ak, equivalent to paikka (“patch, filling”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *paikka (compare Estonian paik and Votic paikkõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spaikǭ (compare English spoke).

From Proto-Finnic *paimën, borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Lithuanian piemuo), from Proto-Indo-European *poh₂imḗn (compare Ancient Greek ποιμήν (poimḗn)), from *peh₂- (“to protect”) (compare Latin pastor). Related to Karelian paimoi.
From Proto-Finnic *paimëntadak (compare Veps paimeta, Võro paimõndama), equivalent to paimen (“shepherd”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *painadak, from Proto-Uralic *pańa-. * (to print (a book)): Semantic loan from Swedish trycka or German drücken.
From Proto-Finnic *painëk. Equivalent to painaa (“to press”) + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *paino, equivalent to painaa (“to press, push; to weigh”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *paisëk. Equivalent to pais- (“to swell”) + -e.

parole.significato: to throw violently or forcefully (once); to hurl (once); to cast (once); to fling (once)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paiskat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *paistadak, probably borrowed from Northwest Germanic *bājan-, from Proto-Germanic *bēaną.

parole.significato: the light and (often) the heat from a source, e.g. shine (sunshine, moonshine, etc.), glow (fireglow, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paistëk, equivalent to paistaa (“to shine, glow”) + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *paistudak. Equivalent to paistaa (“to cook, fry”) + -ua.

parole.significato: to swell, belly, bulge, bilge, inflate (to become bigger, especially due to engorging)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paisudak. Related to Estonian paisuma, Karelian paisuo and Livonian paizõ.
From Proto-Finnic *paita (compare Karelian paita, Veps paid), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *paidō (compare Old High German pheit and Gothic 𐍀𐌰𐌹𐌳𐌰 (paida)).
From Proto-Finnic *pagicci, roughly equivalent to pa- + -itse, from a stem of unknown origin; perhaps related to paeta. Related to Karelian paittše and Livvi paitše.
From Proto-Finnic *paja. Cognates include Estonian paja, Ingrian paja, Karelian paja, Ludian paja, Livvi paja, Veps paja and Votic paja.
From Proto-Finnic *paju (compare Estonian paju), from Proto-Uralic *paje-w (“willow”) (compare Udmurt бадь (baď), Hungarian fagyal (“privet”)).
From Proto-Finnic *pak'ahtudak, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pëkka- (“to burst”). Compare Hungarian fakad (“to spring, burst”).
From Proto-Finnic *pakana, borrowed from Slavic, probably from Old East Slavic поганъ (poganŭ), from Latin pāgānus.

parole.significato: causerie (short informal, often humoristic, writing on a current topic)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pakina. Equivalent to pakista + -na. Related to Veps pagin.

From Proto-Finnic *pagistak. Related to Estonian pagisema, Veps pagišta, Votic pakissõ, and possibly to Lule Sami báhko, Southern Sami baakoe and Northern Sami báhkkodit. The strong grade -k- has been levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: frost, sub-zero temperature of ambient air
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pakkainën. Related to Estonian pakane, Ingrian pakkain, Karelian pakkaine, Veps pakaine and Votic pakkain.

parole.significato: obligation, force, necessity, compulsion, coercion, must, duress
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pakko. Cognate to Estonian pakk (“full”), Ingrian pakko, Karelian pakko, Ludian pakottada, Veps pakutada and Votic pakko.
From Proto-Finnic *pako. Equivalent to paeta (“to flee, escape”) + -o.

parole.significato: thick (relatively great in extent from one surface to the opposite in its smallest solid dimension)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paksu (compare Estonian paks), possibly borrowed from Indo-Iranian (compare Sanskrit बहु (bahu, “much, many, abundant”)), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰn̥ǵʰús (“thick”); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.
From Proto-Finnic *pala (compare Estonian pala, Veps pala), from Proto-Uralic *pala (compare Erzya пал (pal), Hungarian falat (“mouthful”)).
From Proto-Finnic *paladak, from Proto-Uralic *pala-.

parole.significato: to return, come back, go back, get back
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palait'ak. Related to Karelian palata, Livonian pa’llõ.

From Proto-Finnic *paljas. Related to Estonian paljas, Ingrian paljas, Karelian pal’l’aš, Livonian pōļaz, Ludian paľľaz, Livvi paľľas, Veps palʹlʹaz and Votic palʹlʹõz. Possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *failijaz, but the semantic gap makes this unlikely.

parole.significato: bellows (device for delivering pressurized air in a controlled quantity to a controlled location)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palgëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *balgiz (“bag”). Related to Ludian palgiž.
From Proto-Finnic *paljo. Related to Estonian palju, Ingrian paljo and Votic palʹlʹo.

parole.significato: pay, salary, wage (money given in return for work; salary or wages)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palkka (compare Estonian palk, Livonian pālka, Livvi palku, Votic palkkõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Slavic *bȏlgo (compare Russian бо́лого (bólogo), Czech blaho).

parole.significato: a type of horse cart traditionally used to transport barrels of tar
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic [Term?], borrowed from Proto-Germanic *balkuz.
From Proto-Finnic *palko, derived from *palgëh. Related to Ingrian palko, Karelian palko, Veps paug and Votic palko.

parole.significato: hem (border of an article of clothing doubled back and stitched together)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paldëk, probably derived from or from the same root as *palci (whence palsi).
From Proto-Finnic *palmikkoi. Cognates include Estonian palmik, Ingrian palmikko, Karelian palmikko.

parole.significato: fire (event of something burning, an occurrence of fire)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palo, equivalent to palaa (“to burn”) + -o.

parole.significato: hardpan (especially one in the bottom of a body of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palci, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *falþį̄, *falþaz.
From Proto-Finnic *palttina, borrowed from Proto-Slavic *poltьno (whence Old East Slavic полотьно (polotĭno)).

parole.significato: to cure (meat) by roasting and smoking it slowly in relatively mild heat (often 60–100°C or 140-210 F for several hours…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *palvat'ak.

parole.significato: handle (for carrying, e.g. on a pot, bucket or basket)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *panka.

From Proto-Finnic *pandak (compare Estonian panema, Votic pannõ), from Proto-Uralic *pëne- (*pane-) (compare Erzya панемс (panems), Udmurt поныны (ponyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (pin-), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (pen-)).

parole.significato: load, explosive charge (usually including a detonator)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *panos. Equivalent to panna (“to put”) + -os.
From Proto-Finnic *panta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *bandą. Compare English band, Estonian pand.
From Proto-Finnic *panu, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *panu (compare Old Prussian panno (“fire”)).

parole.significato: priest (in the Catholic or Orthodox Church), minister (in a Protestant church)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pappi, borrowed from Slavic, probably from Old East Slavic попъ (popŭ, “priest”) (compare Russian поп (pop, “priest”), whence poppa- in poppamies).
From Proto-Finnic *parantadak, equivalent to parane- (“to get better”) + -taa (factitive verb).
From Proto-Finnic *parat'ak, equivalent to para + -(e)ta; the root is identical to that of paras. Compare Karelian pareta.
Unknown. Possibly from Proto-Finnic *parjat'ak, which could be from Proto-Baltic *bárˀtei (compare Latvian bārt, Lithuanian barti), or a blend of paaruta or paasata and herjata.

parole.significato: A unit of volume for firewood, enough firewood to make a woodpile four kyynärä (around 2.4 metres) long and three kyynä…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parmas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *barmaz.
From Proto-Finnic *pardak'as, equivalent to parta (“beard”) + -kas.
From Proto-Finnic *pardas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *bardaz (“edge”), compare Old Norse barð (“brim, verge”). Cognates include Estonian parras, Livonian pārdaz, Ludian pardaz.

parole.significato: beam (long, usually round piece of timber for hanging goods for storage, historically specifically one used to dry shea…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pärtä. Related to Estonian pars, Karelian parsi, Livonian parž, Veps parzʹ and Votic parsi, and further Eastern Mari пырдыж (pyrdyž, “wall”), Udmurt борд (bord, “wall”) and Northern Mansi па̄рт (pārt, “board”).

From Proto-Finnic *parvi, from Proto-Uralic *parewa ~ *parewe. Cognates include Estonian parv (“flock, group”), Ingrian parvi (“flock, group”), Veps parveh (“flock”), Northern Khanty пөр (pør, “flock, group”) and possibly Erzya пурнамс (purnams, “to collect, compile, gather”).

From Proto-Finnic *paska (compare Estonian pask), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pućka (compare Northern Sami baika, Erzya пскиземс (pskizems, “to have diarrhea”), Eastern Mari пушкедаш (puškedaš, “to defecate”), Hungarian fos). The development of the initial vowel from Uralic to Finnic appears to have bee
From Proto-Finnic *paskantadak, from paska.
From Proto-Finnic *pata (compare Estonian pada), from Proto-Uralic *pata (compare Hungarian fazék).

parole.significato: mattress (a pad on which a person can recline and sleep)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *patja (compare Estonian padi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *badją (compare German Bett). Doublet of peti.

parole.significato: dam, dyke/dike (structure placed across a flowing body of water to stop the flow or a part of it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pato (compare Veps pado), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pada-w (compare Erzya падо (pado), Hungarian fal).

From Proto-Finnic *pac'as (compare Veps pacaz (“post, pylon”)). Possibly further related to Northern Sami bázzi (“grave monument, pylon, a heavy object difficult to move, support”) and Inari Sami pääcis (“statue, pylon”).
From Proto-Finnic *patto.

parole.significato: tissue grown on a scar of tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *patvi.
From Proto-Finnic *pauhat'ak, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: sting (bump on skin after having been stung)
parole.testo: According to LÄGLOS, from Proto-Finnic *pauka, which is borrowed from Proto-Germanic *baugaz (“bend”). Probably further derived with + -ma.
From Proto-Finnic *paukkudak, ultimately onomatopoeic. Cognate with Estonian paukuma, Ingrian paukkaa, Karelian paukkoa and Votic paukka.
From Proto-Finnic *pakla (compare Estonian pael, Ingrian pagla, Livvi paglu, Veps pagl, Votic paglõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fatilaz (compare German Fessel).
From Proto-Finnic *pëhko.

parole.significato: straw chaff, such as used in animal shelters
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëhku.
From Proto-Finnic *pehmedä.

parole.significato: finch (any bird in the Fringillidae family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëippoi.
From Proto-Finnic *peitto, equivalent to peittää (“to cover”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *peittädäk, possibly derived from a borrowing of Proto-Germanic *bē(j)aną. Related to Estonian peitma, Ingrian peittää, Ludian peitada, Veps peittädä and Votic peittää (Kattila).
From Proto-Finnic *pelko. Equivalent to pelätä (“to fear, dread”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *pëllava(s), of unknown further origin. Related to dialectal pellavas, Karelian pelvas and Veps pölvaz.

parole.significato: field (wide, open space used to grow crops)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëlto (compare Estonian põld, Veps pöud, Votic põlto), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *felþą (compare English field).
From Proto-Finnic *pëlu, borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian pélūs).

parole.significato: to fear, dread, be afraid of
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pelgäit'äk, derived from Proto-Uralic *pele- of identical meaning (whence e.g. Northern Sami ballat, Erzya пелемс (pelems), Northern Mansi пилуӈкве (piluňkve) and Hungarian fél).
From Proto-Finnic *peni (compare Estonian peni), from Proto-Uralic *penä (compare Northern Sami beana, Erzya пине (pine), Eastern Mari пий (pij), Udmurt пуны (puny)).

parole.significato: puppy, pup (young animal, especially a dog)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *penikka (compare Ingrian penikka, Karelian penikkä, Votic penikkõ), equivalent to peni (“dog”) + -ikka.

parole.significato: bush, shrub (woody plant smaller than a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pënsas. Compare Karelian penšaš.
From Proto-Finnic *përgat'ak, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *berganą (“to take care of, to keep”), in which case, a doublet with pärjätä. This has been disputed however.

parole.significato: family, nuclear family, immediate family (parents and children)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pereh (compare Estonian pere, Karelian pereh, Veps pereh and Võro pereh), probably derived from *perä (“rear”), referring to the background of a person (compare alkuperä (“origin”), peräisin (“originating from”), perehtyä). Underwent metathesis from *pereh to perhe. First written
From Proto-Finnic *peridäk, equivalent to perä (“rear (end)”) + -ia.

From Proto-Finnic *perkeleh, which derives from the name of the Baltic deity of thunder; compare Lithuanian Perkūnas and Proto-Slavic *Perunъ (“god of thunder”). After Finland's conquest (c. 1250) and subsequent Christianization, its meaning changed to a profanity and a euphemism for Satan at least
From Proto-Finnic *përmanto. Cognates include Estonian põrand (“floor”), Livonian pȭrand (“floor”) and Votic põrmata (“floor”) (Mati). Also related to Northern Sami bearpmet.
From Proto-Finnic *përna (compare Estonian põrn (“spleen”)), possibly from Indo-Iranian.
From Proto-Finnic *persek, possibly a derivative of root found in perä.

parole.significato: rear, back, tail end (aft part of anything)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *perä (compare Estonian pära), from Proto-Uralic *perä ~ *pirä (compare Erzya пря (pŕa, “head”), Komi-Permyak бӧр (bör), Eastern Khanty пӛртӓх (pjərtäh)).
From Proto-Finnic *pestäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *pese- (compare Erzya пезэмс (pezëms)).
From Proto-Finnic *pesu. Equivalent to pestä (“to wash”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *pet'os. Equivalent to pettää (“to cheat, con, swindle, defraud, deceive, delude, mislead. betray”) + -os.
From Proto-Finnic *pettüdäk. Equivalent to pettää (“to betray, deceive, disappoint”) + -yä.
From Proto-Finnic *pettädäk (compare Estonian petma, Livonian piettõ).
From Proto-Finnic *petägä (compare Livonian piedāg, Veps pedai), from Proto-Uralic *pecä(-kä) (compare Northern Sami beahci, Erzya пиче (piče), Eastern Mari пӱнчӧ (pünčö), Udmurt пужым (pužym)).

From Proto-Finnic *peikälo (with varying forms in descendants, such as dialectal peikalo, Karelian peikalo, Veps peigol, Estonian pöial, Livonian pēgal), probably a somewhat irregular derivation of Proto-Uralic *pelkä (compare Northern Sami bealgi, Erzya пелька (peľka, “thumb”), Komi-Zyrian пев (pev

parole.significato: to hold back, restrain, hinder, curb; to suppress; to suspend; to retain
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pidättädäk, equivalent to pitää (“to keep, hold”) + -ttää.

parole.significato: jamb, post (vertical component forming the sides of a door frame, window frame or other opening in a wall)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peeli (compare Estonian peel), from Proto-Uralic *päle (“side”) (compare Moksha пяль (päľ), Hungarian fél).
From Proto-Finnic *peelus; equivalent to pieli (“post, jamb, side”) + -us. Related to Karelian pieluksi and Veps pöluz. In the sense “pillow”, displaced by the borrowed tyyny.

parole.significato: cleat (strip of wood fastened on transversely to something in order to give strength, prevent warping, hold position, e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëëna, perhaps borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spēnuz (“piece of wood”).

parole.significato: small, little (low in size, amount or intensity)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peeni. Cognate with Estonian peen, Veps penʹ.

parole.significato: A strip of land at the margin of some land forms.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peentara.
From Proto-Finnic *peerdäk.
From Proto-Finnic *peeru. Equivalent to piere- (“to fart”) + -u.

parole.significato: yard (small, usually uncultivated area of land adjoining or within the precincts of a house or other building)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piha (compare Karelian piha, Veps piha).

parole.significato: resin, pitch (hydrocarbon secretion of many plants, particularly coniferous trees, in its natural state)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pihka.

From Proto-Finnic *pihlaga (compare Estonian pihlakas, Ingrian pihlaja), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pićlä (compare Erzya пизёл (piźol), Eastern Mari пызле (pyzĺe), Komi-Zyrian пелысь (pelyś), Northern Khanty писяр (pisjar)).

From Proto-Finnic *pihti (compare Estonian piht, Ingrian pihet pl, Karelian pihti, Veps pihthed pl, Votic pihed pl), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pište (compare Moksha [script needed] (peš), Komi-Zyrian [script needed] (peš) and Proto-Samic *pëstë, whence Northern Sami basta).

parole.significato: thorn, prong, tooth or similar element e.g. in a plant, a saw or a rake
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pii (“tooth”), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *piŋe (“tooth”). Cognates include Ingrian pii (“spike”), Erzya пей (pej, “tooth”) and Hungarian fog (“tooth”).
From Proto-Finnic *piikivi. Equivalent to pii (“tooth, prong”) + kivi (“stone”), probably after the shape.

parole.significato: to be hidden (in), lie (in), be latent
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piildäk.

parole.significato: cultured milk, sour milk, fermented milk, soured milk, (cultured) buttermilk (fermented dairy product produced from cow…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piimä (“milk”) (cognate with Estonian piim (“milk”), Votic piime (“milk”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pejmä, probably a loanword from Late Proto-Indo-European *péyh₂-men- (specifically Pre-Proto-Indo-Iranian), reflected as Proto-Indo-Iranian *páyHmā (“milk”), from Proto-Indo-Europea
From Proto-Finnic *piira.

parole.significato: to draw, sketch (produce a picture with a pencil or other similar implement)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piirtädäk. Equivalent to piir- + -tää; piiri also means “(scratched or carved) line, incision (in leather, birchbark, etc.)” in dialects, so the original meaning was probably “to scratch or carve a line, make an incision (in leather, birchbark, etc.)”.
piiskua + -ttaa, from Proto-Finnic *piikcudak.
From Proto-Finnic *piitta (compare Estonian piit, Livonian pīţ, Votic piittõ), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse biti).

From Proto-Finnic *pika (compare Estonian pea, Karelian pika, Livonian pigā, Veps piga, Votic pigaa), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fiką (compare Danish fige, Swedish fika (“to strive (for)”)).

parole.significato: to spoil, ruin, blight, destroy (to cause the ruin of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilat'ak (compare Karelian pilata, Votic pilatõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse bila (“to fail”)).

parole.significato: to mock, deride, ridicule, jeer at, make fun of
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilk'at'ak, equivalent to pilka- (“jeer, mockery, mock, ridicule”) + -ta.

parole.significato: jeer, mockery, mock, ridicule, jest, derision
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilkka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *blikkaz (compare German Blick).
From Proto-Finnic *pilli, ultimately of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: tipcat (game in which a wooden piece is struck with a stick)
parole.testo: From dialectal pilppa (“small piece”) + -u, from Proto-Finnic *pilppa.

parole.significato: cloud (visible mass of water droplets suspended in the air; mass of dust, steam or smoke)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilvi (compare Estonian pilv), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pilwe (compare Northern Sami balva, Erzya пель (peľ), Eastern Mari пыл (pyl), Udmurt пилем (piľem)). * (cloud in computing): Semantic loan from English cloud.
From Proto-Finnic *pilvinen, equivalent to pilvi (“cloud”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *pimedä, from Proto-Uralic *pilmetä.
From Proto-Finnic *pino, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fīnō (“heap”).

parole.significato: surface (top side of something; outer hull of a tangible object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pinta (compare Estonian pind), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spindaz (compare Old English spind, Dutch spint (spinthout)).

parole.significato: drop (a small mass of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pisara (compare Estonian pisar (“tear”)), possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *pića- (“to rain, drizzle”) (compare Erzya пиземе (pizeme, “rain”)).

From Proto-Finnic *pistek (“sting, prick”). Equivalent to pistää (“to sting, prick”) + -e. Originally a synonym of pisto (“sting; prick, puncture”). First used to mean "period, full stop, dot" by Gustaf Renvall in 1826 and "point" in geometry by Wolmar Schildt in 1835; other meanings derive from tho

From Proto-Finnic *pistädäk (compare Estonian pistma), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pistä- (compare Eastern Mari пышташ (pyštaš)). * (to put, tuck, stick): Compare Swedish sticka, German stecken, English stick on the one hand, and Eastern Mari [script needed] (pə̑štem) on the other.
From Proto-Finnic *pitkä, derived from Proto-Uralic *pide. The comparative, superlative and many derived forms are derived from the original stem pide-.
From Proto-Finnic *pitkäinen (compare Estonian pikne, Livonian pițki), equivalent to pitkä (“long”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *pitkällinen (compare Estonian pikaline, Livonian pitkāli, Veps pitkaline), equivalent to pitkä (“long”) + -llinen.
From Proto-Finnic *pito, equivalent to pitää (“to keep, hold”) + -o.

parole.significato: length (distance measured along the longest dimension of an object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piduc, derived by the suffix -uus from the root *pite- (from Proto-Uralic *pide) from which pitkä is also derived.

parole.significato: rural municipality, parish; a regional unit or administrative division comprising multiple villages
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pitäjä. Equivalent to pitää (“to keep, hold”) + -jä (“-er”). As a term for a territorial area or subdivision, first attested in 1465 (as piteest, corresponding to modern elative pitä(j)ästä); probably originally in the sense of each territory which organized their own feasts as a

From Proto-Finnic *pitädäk (compare Estonian pidama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pitä- (compare Erzya педямс (peďams, “to get stuck”), Eastern Mari [script needed] (pə̂ze-, “to hold”)). * (to hold (an event, etc.)): Compare Swedish hålla, English hold. * (to consider, regard): Compare German halten, S
From Proto-Finnic *pivo (compare Estonian peo, Livonian pi’v, Veps pijo).

From Proto-Finnic *pohjainën, equivalent to pohja (“bottom, north”) + -inen. The form pohjoinen was adapted from the Savonian dialects, whence the -oi- (a regular change also seen in e.g. hopioinen < hopea + -inen), and introduced into the standard language by Abraham Poppius in 1818.

parole.significato: synonym of pohtia (“to winnow with a winnowing basket”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pohtadak (compare Ingrian poohtaa, Veps pohtta, Votic pohtaa (Mati)).

From Proto-Finnic *poika (compare Estonian poeg, Livvi poigu), from Proto-Uralic *pojka (compare Komi-Zyrian пи (pi), Udmurt пи (pi), Northern Khanty пух (puh), Northern Mansi пыг (pyg), Hungarian fiú). The Finnic word has also been borrowed into Baltic (Latvian puika) and Swedish (see the descendan
From Proto-Finnic *poikidak, equivalent to poika (“boy, son”) + -ia.
From Proto-Finnic *poikki. Related to Karelian poikki and Votic põičči.

parole.significato: litter (offspring of a mammal born in one birth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *poikovëh. Equivalent to poika (“boy, son”) + -ue.

parole.significato: to pick (remove by plucking, e.g. fruit or berries from a plant, mushrooms from the ground or trash from somewhere wher…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *poimidak. Akin to Estonian põimima, Karelian poimie, Livonian pȯimõ, Ludian poimida, Livvi poimie, Veps poimda and Votic põimia. Probably also related to Proto-Samic *poajmōtēk (whence Northern Sami boaibmut).
From Proto-Finnic *poigintima, derived from *poika (“son”) (whence poika).

parole.significato: to stamp, tread (with one's foot or feet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *polkëdak. Cognate with Estonian põlgama, Karelian polkie, Livonian pȯlgõ, Ludian polgeda, Veps polkta and Votic põlgõttaa (Mati, Pummala).

parole.significato: to burn (to cause to be consumed by fire); incinerate
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *polttadak. Cognates include Estonian põletama, Ludian poltada, Veps poutta, Votic põlõtta, Ter Sami pɨellˈted and Erzya пултамс (pultams). Originally probably a causative derivation of palaa; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more. * (to distill alcohol): Compare Swedish bränna.

parole.significato: knee (joint in the middle of the leg and area around it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *polvi (compare Estonian põlv), from Proto-Uralic *polwe (compare Northern Sami buolva, Moksha пълманжа (pəlmanža)).

parole.significato: anther (pollen-bearing part of the stamen of a flower)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ponci, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ponte or Proto-Uralic *ponče (“tail”).
From Proto-Finnic *porat'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *porëk, equivalent to por- + -e.

parole.significato: to bubble (make sounds like that of bubbling water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *poristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. Possibly related to Erzya пурамс (purams, “to seethe, foam”).
From Proto-Finnic *porkka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*forkaʀ) (compare Old Norse forkr), from Proto-Germanic *furkaz.
From Proto-Finnic *poro (compare Ingrian poro, Karelian poro, Ludian poro, Veps poro, Votic poro).
From Proto-Finnic *porottadak.
From Proto-Finnic *pordas, borrowed from Northwest Germanic *bordaz, from earlier Proto-Germanic *burdą. Cognate with Karelian porras, Veps pordaz. Doublet of pursi.

From Proto-Finnic *porcas (compare Estonian põrsas), from Proto-Finno-Permic *porćas (compare Erzya пурцос (purcos), Udmurt [script needed] (parś), unless these are separate borrowings), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *porśos (> *párśas) (ultimately cognate with English pork).

parole.significato: cheek (soft skin on each side of the face)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *poski, from Proto-Uralic *poske.

parole.significato: to be sick with, have, suffer from (a disease or, figuratively, a mental state)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *potëdak (compare Estonian põdema), possibly from Proto-Uralic *poče- (compare Northern Sami buohcat).
From Proto-Finnic *pocka, from Proto-Finno-Permic *počka.

parole.significato: to set a seine or a fishnet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *potkëdak.
From Proto-Finnic *pockëidak. Equivalent to potka (“hind leg, shank”) + -ia.

parole.significato: a side net guiding fish towards a fyke
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *potku, equivalent to potkea (“to set a seine/fishnet”) + -u.

parole.significato: dry weather; a weather without rain, snow or any other precipitation, and which may be sunny or cloudy
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pouta, possibly borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *pouvi (compare Estonian põu), probably from Proto-Uralic *poŋŋe.
From Proto-Finnic *pudistadak, probably equivalent to pudo- (“to fall, drop”) + -istaa; thus originally "to make fall, drop (by shaking), to shake off".

parole.significato: to fall (from an elevated position); to fall down, fall off; to drop, slip
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pudot'ak (compare Ingrian puota, Livonian pu’ddõ), probably from Proto-Uralic *puďa-w- (“to break off”) (compare Northern Sami bođˈđet, Udmurt пильыны (piľyny), Eastern Mari пудешташ (pudeštaš), Southern Mansi [script needed] (poĺ), Nganasan хоиди (hoidji)).
From Proto-Finnic *puhaltadak. Equivalent to puh- + -altaa (momentane verb); originally puhua itself meant "to blow". Compare puhkua.
From Proto-Finnic *puhtas (compare Estonian puhas, Karelian puhaš, Veps puhtaz), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *puHtás (compare Sanskrit पूत (pūta)), from Proto-Indo-European *puH-tó-s (“clean”).

From Proto-Finnic *puktëk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pukta- (“to shoo”), the semantic development is likely "to shoo" > "to wake (someone) up" > "time of waking up" > "dawn" > "twilight". Compare Erzya пувтамс (puvtams, “to wake (someone) up”).

parole.significato: to pop, burst (of something full e.g. of gas), to rupture (e.g. of something sewn or of an abscess)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puhkët'ak (compare Estonian puhkema, Ludian puhketa, Votic puhgõtõ), from Proto-Uralic *pučke-. The verb shares its root with putkahtaa; the root with -hk- goes back to *-šk-, which has split irregularly from *-čk- (which developed into the -tk- in putkahtaa). The same split is al

parole.significato: to speak, talk (communicate with one's voice)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puhudak (“to blow”) (compare Estonian puhuma), from Proto-Uralic *puše- (“to blow”) (compare Northern Sami bossut, Western Mansi [script needed] (put-)). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552). The semantic shift from “to blow” to “to speak” is found only
From Proto-Finnic *puinën, equivalent to puu (“wood”) + -inen.

parole.significato: to jump from tree to tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puittadak. Equivalent to puu (“tree”) + -ittaa.
From Proto-Finnic *pujo. Cognate with Estonian puju. Probably from the same root as pujottaa, pujahtaa, i.e. pujoa.

parole.significato: to put on, don (clothes; often with päälle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pukëdak (compare Livonian pu’ggõ), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puke-.
From Proto-Finnic *pulistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.

parole.significato: tally, tally stick (piece of wood on which notches or scores were cut, as the marks of number)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pulkka (compare Estonian pulk, Livonian pūlka, Votic pulkkõ).
From Proto-Finnic *puna, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puna (“color, hair”). Cognate with Erzya пона (pona, “hair”).
From Proto-Finnic *punainën, equivalent to puna (“red”) + -inen.

parole.significato: to intertwine, twine, twist (together) (join together by twining or twisting; join by winding around one another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *punodak (compare Estonian punuma), from Proto-Uralic *puna- (“to spin, twist”) (compare Northern Sami botnit, Erzya понамс (ponams), Hungarian fon).

parole.significato: twine, braid (threads twisted or braided together, mainly for decorative purposes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *punos, equivalent to punoa (“to weave”) + -os.
From Proto-Finnic *punta (“old unit of weight”) (compare Estonian pund, Livonian pūnda), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *pundą (“pound, weight”), itself from Latin pondō.
From Proto-Finnic *poola, probably from Proto-Uralic *pale (“berry”).

parole.significato: half (consisting of a half; such that two of them make one whole)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pooli (compare Estonian pool (“half”)), from Proto-Uralic *pälä (compare Northern Sami bealli, Komi-Zyrian пӧв (pöv), Northern Mansi па̄л (pāl, “half, side”), Hungarian fél (“half”), Tundra Nenets пеля (pyelya)).

parole.significato: premasticated food (such as that fed to young children)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puppu.
From Proto-Finnic *pura, from Proto-Uralic *pura-.
From Proto-Finnic *purha, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fursaz.
From Proto-Finnic *purilas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *burilaz (whence Norwegian byrel, byrdel). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.

parole.significato: to make a quiet purring sound
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.

parole.significato: to dismantle, dissemble, take apart, disassemble, deconstruct (into pieces; possibly with osiin (“into parts”) for clar…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purkadak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *purka- (compare Northern Sami borgádit, Erzya порксамс (porksams)).
From Proto-Finnic *purku, from Proto-Uralic *purke.
From Proto-Finnic *purnu, possibly borrowed from Sami language (compare Inari Sami puornâ), ultimately from Proto-Samic *puornë.

parole.significato: to bite (cut into something by clamping the teeth; attack with teeth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purdak (compare Estonian purema, Livonian pu’rrõ), from Proto-Uralic *pure- (compare Northern Sami borrat, Erzya поремс (porems), Eastern Mari пураш (puraš), Udmurt пурыны (puryny), Northern Mansi пуруӈкве (puruňkve)).
From Proto-Finnic *purci, from earlier *purti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *burdą.
From Proto-Finnic *puru. Equivalent to purra (“to bite”) + -u. Compare Estonian puru (“dust”).
From Proto-Finnic *pusërtadak (compare Estonian puserdama, Karelian puzerdua, Veps puzerta and Votic puzõrta), probably from Proto-Uralic *puśerta-. Cognate with Hungarian facsar.
From Proto-Finnic *puskëdak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puske-.

parole.significato: a birchbark container with a lid/top
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pusu (compare Karelian puzu, Livvi puzu, Ludian puzu, Veps puzu).

parole.significato: to pop up, turn up (to appear without warning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puckahtadak, derived from Proto-Uralic *pučke- (the same root as in puhjeta).

parole.significato: tube, pipe, duct, conduit (long, hollow object, often cylindrical, used to convey fluids or loose solids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pucki (compare Estonian putk, Votic putki), from Proto-Uralic *pučke (“hollow plant stalk”) (compare Northern Sami boska (“angelica”), Erzya почко (počko, “roll, coil”), Tundra Nenets пуд (pūd)). The development from “hollow plant stalk” to “pipe, tube” is difficult to date precis
From Proto-Finnic *putu.
From Proto-Finnic *puu (compare Estonian puu, Karelian puu), from Proto-Uralic *puwe / *pawe (compare Eastern Mari пу (pu), Udmurt пу (pu), Hungarian fa, Tundra Nenets пя (pya)).
From Proto-Finnic *putro (compare Estonian puder, Karelian putro, Veps pudr), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian putra (“porridge”)).

parole.significato: gust, blast, scud, bluster (strong, abrupt rush of wind)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puuska.
From Proto-Finnic *puuska.

parole.significato: to be missing; to be lacking [with elative or ablative ‘from’]; (elative/ablative +) to lack
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puuttudak. Related to Estonian puuduma, Karelian puutuo, Livonian pūtõ and Votic puutoz (~ puutos). The long -tt- is probably by contamination with that of puuttua (etymology 2).

From Proto-Finnic *puuttudak. Related to Estonian puutuma, Ingrian puuttua, Livonian pūtõ, Karelian puuttuo, Ludian puuttuda, Veps putta and Votic puuttua. Possibly from earlier *puuttadak (unless a back-formation, whence dialectal puuttaa and Karelian puuttoa), in which case it may also be related
From Proto-Finnic *puutudak, equivalent to puu (“wood”) + -tua.
From Proto-Finnic *pühä (compare Estonian püha), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pišä ~ *püšä (compare Northern Sami bassi, Erzya пежеть (pežeť, “sin”), Udmurt пож (pož, “dirty, foul”)).
From Proto-Finnic *pükälä. Cognates include Estonian pügal, Ingrian pykälä and Votic püčäle.

parole.significato: to strive, endeavour, seek to, pursue [with illative or allative; or (with verbs) with illative of third infinitive] (t…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pürkidäk, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wurkijaną.

parole.significato: upright, vertical (now uncommon as an independent adjective)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pistü, equivalent to pistää (“to stab, sting, prick”) + -y. The expected form pisty is dialectal; the initial vowel has labialized as a result of the latter vowel (compare pystyä, from pistää + -yä). Related to Estonian püsti, Karelian pisty, Livonian pistõ, Veps püšt and Votic pi

From Proto-Finnic *pisüdäk (compare Estonian püsima, Veps püžuda), from Proto-Finno-Permic *pise-w- (compare Erzya пезнамс (peznams, “to pierce; to stick”), Moksha пезомс (pezoms), Eastern Mari пижа́ш (pižáš)), with the second-syllable -y- causing labialization of the initial -i- to -y-.

parole.significato: hazel grouse (Tetrastes bonasia, syn. Bonasa bonasia)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *püü (compare Estonian püü, Veps pü), from Proto-Uralic *püŋe (“hazel hen”) (compare Moksha повне (povne), Hungarian fogoly).
From Proto-Finnic *püüdüs, equivalent to pyytää (“to hunt, fish”) + -us

From Proto-Finnic *pühkidäk (compare Estonian pühkima, Ingrian pyyhkiä, Karelian pyyhkie, Ludian pühkida, Veps pühkta, Votic pühčiä), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiskijaną (compare German wischen, Dutch wissen).

From Proto-Finnic *püütädäk (“to hunt, fish”), probably from Uralic. parole.significato: to rotate, roll, reel, spin, turn (continuously)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pöörittädäk. Equivalent to pyöriä (“to rotate, spin, turn”) (intransitive) + -ttää.

parole.significato: to rotate, turn, revolve, spin, roll (continuously)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pööridäk. Equivalent to pyörä (“wheel”) + -iä.

parole.significato: to faint, pass out, swoon, black out
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pöörtüdäk. Equivalent to pyörä (“wheel”) + -tyä.

parole.significato: to turn around, return (to change to the opposite direction from a previous position)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pöörtädäk. Equivalent to pyörä (“wheel”) + -tää.

parole.significato: wheel (circular device capable of rotating on its axis)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pöörä, from Proto-Uralic *peŋärä.

parole.significato: against, towards, -wards, to [with partitive] (indicating movement or direction straight towards something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päin; the instructive plural of pää.

parole.significato: halter, headgear, headpiece, headstall (harness that fits on a horse's head)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päic'et, derived from pää with an older variant of the -inen suffix (*-ic(c)et).
From Proto-Finnic *päivä (“sun, day”), from Proto-Uralic *päjwä (“sun”). Cognates include Ume Sami beäjvvie, Northern Sami beaivi, Skolt Sami peiʹvv. In the sense “sun”, mostly displaced by aurinko.

parole.significato: ball (of the foot) (front of the bottom of the foot, just behind the toes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päkijä.
From Proto-Finnic *pälk'ähtädäk, from pälk- + -ähtää; probably sound-symbolic

parole.significato: a bald spot, a patch of snow-free ground, especially in the spring as snow begins to thaw
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pälvi.

parole.significato: shake (thin, about 0.5 cm, wooden shingle made by splitting wood)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pärek.

parole.significato: to buzz, rattle (to emit a sound consisting of quick explosive or banging sounds, such as the sound of a moped, ratchet…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päristäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.

parole.significato: short or small piece (of something): stub, stump
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päckä.
From Proto-Finnic *päcci, borrowed from Slavic, probably from Old East Slavic печь (pečĭ), from Proto-Slavic *peťь. Compare Karelian päčči, Veps päč.
From Proto-Finnic *pää (compare Estonian pea, Veps pä), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *päŋe (compare Erzya пе (pe), Komi-Zyrian пом (pom), Northern Mansi пуӈк (puňk), Hungarian fej, fő).
The allative singular of pää (“head”); already used adpositionally in Proto-Finnic as Proto-Finnic *päällek.
From Proto-Finnic *päällikkoi. Equivalent to päällä (“on top”) + -ikkö.
The adessive singular of pää (“head”); already used adpositionally in Proto-Finnic as Proto-Finnic *päällä.
The ablative singular of pää (“head”); already used adpositionally in Proto-Finnic as Proto-Finnic *päältä.

parole.significato: hem (border of an article of clothing doubled back and stitched together)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pärmeh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *barmiz (compare Old Norse barmr (“rim”)).

parole.significato: swallow, martin (bird of the family Hirundinidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pääskü, perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *päčkɜ and/or simply onomatopoeic. Cognates include Karelian piäčkyni, Estonian pääsuke, pääsu, Ingrian pääsky, Livonian pešlinki, Veps päskheińe, Votic pääsko, Erzya пезьгун (peźgun), пезьгата (peźgata), Udmurt пӧськы (pöśky) and Hungarian f

parole.significato: to get to, reach, arrive at/in [with illative or allative; or (with verbs) with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pä(ä)stäk. Cognate with Estonian pääsema (“to escape, to reach”), Votic pääse, and Livvi piästä (“to come off, to come out”).

parole.significato: to let [with illative or allative, (with verbs) along with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (free someone of some…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pä(ä)städäk. Equivalent to päästä (“to get somewhere, to get to do something, get free, get loose”) + -tää (causative aspect).

parole.significato: to end, conclude, terminate, finish, bring to a close
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päättädäk, equivalent to pää (“head, end”) + -ttää. * (to decide, choose; to conclude): Probably a semantic loan from Swedish besluta (from sluta (“to stop, finish”)).
From Proto-Finnic *pölü, likely sound-symbolic in origin (compare pöllähtää), Akin to Karelian pöly, Ludian pölü and Veps pölü; compare Votic pöllü.

parole.significato: rumen, paunch (first stomach of a ruminant)
parole.testo: From Northern Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Related to Karelian pöččö, Ludian pöčöi and Veps pecoi.

parole.significato: table, desk (standing piece of furniture with a flat top)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peütä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *beudaz (compare Old English bēod, Gothic 𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌸𐍃 (biuþs)).

parole.significato: to cut up or dismember a slaughtered animal
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rakjoidak. Equivalent to raaja (“limb”) + -oa. Compare ravio.
From Proto-Finnic *raaka (compare Estonian raag- in Estonian raagnahk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrawaz.

parole.significato: yard (horizontal spar on the mast of a sailing ship)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raaka (compare Estonian raag), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rahō (compare German Rah, Rahe (“yard”), Swedish rå (“yard”)).

parole.significato: to tear, rip, shred, rend (into pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raastadak. Related to Karelian roastoa, Veps rastta and possibly also to Erzya раздемс (razdems).
From Proto-Finnic *raato (compare Ingrian raato, Karelian roato), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*brāđō) (compare Swedish bråd (“piece of meat”)), from Proto-Germanic *brēdô.

parole.significato: robust, strong (especially of an adult man or adult male animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raavas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrawwaz (“full-grown”). Doublet of rahvas (“riff raff, peasantry”).
From Proto-Finnic *ragëh.

parole.significato: money (means of exchange and measure of value)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raha, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skrahā (“squirrel skin”) (later Proto-Germanic *skrahō; compare Old Norse skrá). Originally, this word referred to animal furs (especially squirrel pelts), since they were a common payment instrument before notes and coins were introduced. Attes

parole.significato: footstool, stool, ottoman, pouf, hassock, tumpty
