parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahi. Cognate to Ingrian rahi (“bench”) and Livonian ra’j (“chair”).

parole.significato: trace, tug (strap used to join the shafts of a carriage, sled etc. or a shaft bow to the horse collar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahkëh, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dragiz, from *draganą.

parole.significato: quark, tvorog (soft creamy curd cheese made by souring or fermenting milk and removing the whey from it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahka, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dragjō (“dregs”).
From Proto-Finnic *rahko, from Proto-Finno-Permic *raška-w.

parole.significato: the common people, the lower orders (historically, the common people as opposed to the gentry); rabble, riffraff, vulgu…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rahvas (compare Estonian rahvas (“people”)), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrawwaz (“full-grown”), in which case a variant of raavas, which has remained closer to the original meaning. Compare the sense development in väki.

parole.significato: ailing, sickly, weakened by illness and age; dilapidated, wasted, deteriorated, decrepit, in bad shape
parole.testo: raihna + -as, from Proto-Finnic *raina (with rare dialectal variant raina). The origin of the -h- is not entirely clear.
From Proto-Finnic *ragënta, from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *raippa, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *raipaz (“cord, rope”).
From Proto-Finnic *raiska.
From Proto-Finnic *raiskat'ak, equivalent to raiska (“wretch; litter, mote”) + -ta with an original sense of "to ruin, to spoil, to waste".
From Proto-Finnic *raita, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *spraiþō (compare Old High German spreid, spreida (“bush”)).

parole.significato: sober (that does not drink alcohol; not given to excessive drinking of alcohol)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rait'is, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *raidi(ja)z.

parole.significato: the main road of a village that goes down the middle of it; a lone village road splitting the village in half
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raitti (compare Karelian reitti, Veps rait, Votic raitti), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Swedish vret).

parole.significato: to clear (remove obstructions, impediments or unwanted items from)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raivat'ak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *strawjaną (“to strew”).

parole.significato: synonym of takaraivo (“back of the head”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raivo, by metathesis from earlier *rawjo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *trawją (“bowl, vessel”) (compare English tray).

parole.significato: a worn out object, something worn
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raja (“worn out object”).

parole.significato: fierce, violent, intense, vicious (involving extreme force or motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raju. Cognate with Ingrian raju, Karelian raju and Votic raju.
From Proto-Finnic *rak'as (compare Karelian rakas (“willing, eager, kind, dear”)), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *frakaz (“greedy, lustful”).

parole.significato: bladder (flexible sac that can expand and contract and that holds liquids or gases)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rakko.
From Proto-Finnic *rako (compare Estonian pragu, Ingrian rako, Karelian rako, Votic rako), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian spraga, Lithuanian spraga).

parole.significato: burdensome, hard (demanding a lot of effort to endure)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rankka (compare Estonian rank, ränk, Ingrian rankka, Karelian rankka, Votic rankkõ and possibly Livonian rǟnka).
From Proto-Finnic *randëh.

parole.significato: coaster (someone who lives on the coast)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rantalainën. Equivalent to ranta (“shore, coast”) + -lainen.
From Proto-Finnic *rapa (“crumbly stone, crumbly substance”). Cognates include Estonian raba, Karelian rapa, Livonian ra­bā and Votic rapa.

parole.significato: dregs, draff (settled sediment of alcoholic fermented drinks, such as beer)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rapa (“dregs”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *drabaz. Cognates include Estonian raba, Karelian rapa, Livonian rabād, Veps raba and Votic rapa.
From Proto-Finnic *rapëda. Related to Estonian rabe, Ingrian rappia and Veps rabed.
From Proto-Finnic *rapëda. Related to Karelian ravie, Livonian ra’bdõ and Ludian raved.
From Proto-Finnic *rabistak (compare Estonian rabisema, Livvi rabišta), probably from the same onomatopoeic root as rapea.
From Proto-Finnic *rasëda, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *ranśe.

parole.significato: unburned swidden; a forest that has been cleared for slash and burn but has not yet been burnt
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rasi, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*grasja), from Proto-Germanic *grasą.

parole.significato: box, case, container, casket, carton (mostly one of relatively small size)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *racja (compare dialectal Estonian rasi), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *randjaz (compare Swedish rände).
From Proto-Finnic *raskas. Related to Estonian raske, Ingrian raskas, Karelian raskas and Votic raskõz. Derived from the same root as rasea.

parole.significato: thrush (any of several species of songbirds of the family Turdidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rastas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *trazdas, compare Latvian strazds (“starling, thrush”) and Lithuanian strazdas (“thrush”), from Proto-Indo-European *trosdos.
From Proto-Finnic *rasva, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: greasy (containing a lot of grease; resembling grease; having a slippery surface due to being covered in grease)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rasvainën, equivalent to rasva (“grease, fat”) + -inen.

From Proto-Finnic *rata (compare Estonian rada, Ingrian rata (“The Milky Way”), Karelian rata (“The Milky Way”), Livonian radā), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tradō (compare Dutch tra (“trail, (forest) path”)).

parole.significato: to tear apart, rip under strain (especially of a seam in fabric or similar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ratkët'ak. Cognates include Karelian ratketa, Livonian rakkõ, Ludian ratketa and Veps ratketa. Compare katketa.
Adessive plural of ratsas, from Proto-Finnic *rac'as, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *raidijaz, *raidaz (whence Old English ræde (“ready to ride, mounted (on a horse)”).

parole.significato: mount, steed; riding horse (horse or other animal used for riding)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raccu, from rats- + -u.

parole.significato: peace, harmony, calm (state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rauha, of unclear further origin.

parole.significato: gland (organ that synthesizes and secretes substance)
parole.testo: rauha + -nen, diminutive of a dialectal word that is from Proto-Finnic *rauha (“gland, swelling”) (compare Estonian rahu, Ingrian rauha, Karelian rauhna, Livonian ro’ugõz, Votic ravvu), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse hrœrar (“groin”)).
From Proto-Finnic *raukëda. Related to Estonian rauge, Karelian raukie and Votic raugõta.

parole.significato: poor thing, wretch (someone or something to be pitied)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raukka, possibly from *raukëda.

parole.significato: ruin (remains of destroyed or dilapidated construction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raunijo, possibly equivalent to rauna + -io, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse hraun). Related to Ingrian raunio, Karelian raunivo and Votic raunio.
From Proto-Finnic *rautainën, equivalent to rauta (“iron”) + -inen.

parole.significato: to thresh sheaves (of grain or hay) by beating them against a wall
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rabait'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *rakja.

parole.significato: to work hard; to toil, to drudge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rehkidäk (earlier *reški-), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þreskaną.

parole.significato: span, distance between posts on a fence (now especially a roundpole fence), hayrack, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëhto, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wrehtuz.
From Proto-Finnic *rëhu. Related to Karelian rehu, Votic rõhu and possibly Livonian rõ’v.

parole.significato: hole (relatively small and/or shallow hole that goes through something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raika (compare Veps reig), possibly borrowed from Baltic.
From Proto-Finnic *raici (compare Estonian reis), borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian rietas (“thigh”)).

parole.significato: sleigh (vehicle, generally pulled by an animal, which moves over snow or ice on runners, used for transporting persons…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *reki (compare Estonian regi), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian ragavas, Lithuanian ragės).
From Proto-Finnic *rëngas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrengaz (> *hringaz) (“ring”). Doublet of rinki.

From Proto-Finnic *repidäk. Cognate with Estonian rebima, Ingrian reppiä, Karelian repie, Livvi revitä, Ludian rebitä, Veps rebita, Võro räbimä and Votic reppiä. Also related to Northern Sami rahpat (“to open”) and possibly to riipiä. Possibly of imitative origin, compare to Proto-Indo-European *h₁r

From Proto-Finnic *repoi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *repä (compare Erzya ривезь (riveź)), borrowed from early Indo-Iranian (compare Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawpāćás, Sanskrit लोपि (lopi), Persian روباه (rubâh); Germanic terms like Swedish räv are probably parallel borrowings from Indo-Iranian).
From Proto-Finnic *retki, further origin unknown. Cognate with Livonian rek, riek (“road”).

parole.significato: edge, brink, rim, border, brim, fringe, verge, boundary (outer boundary line of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëuna (compare Karelian reuna, Ludian reun, Veps röun), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian briauna).

From Proto-Finnic *rëëhudak (related to Karelian riehuo and Veps rehuda). Further origin is disputed; theories include relation to riesa, borrowing from Proto-Germanic *rēsōną (compare Middle Dutch rasen), or an original sound-symbolic root.
From Proto-Finnic *rëëmu. Cognates include Karelian riemu and Estonian rõõm. Further etymology unclear, but possibly a sound-symbolic word related to remu.

parole.significato: A traditional thin unleavened bread made from barley, oats and/or potato.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëëska, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *prḗˀskas (compare Lithuanian prėskas (“unflavoured, tasteless, fresh, unleavened”)).

parole.significato: thread (long, thin and flexible form of material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rihma, from earlier *rišma, borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian rišimas (“binding”). Cognate with Estonian rihm, Karelian rihma, Votic rihmõ.
From Proto-Finnic *riideldäk, equivalent to riita (“argument, quarrel”) + -ellä.

parole.significato: A traditional northern European (Fennoscandian and Russian) grain drying and threshing cabin, in which the grain was dr…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riihi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *riŋeše, itself possibly a Wanderwort. Cognates include Estonian rehi, Karelian riihi. Swedish ria and Latvian rija are borrowings from Finnic.

parole.significato: to tear, rip, rend (by pulling with hands, especially something off from plants, like fruit)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riipidäk, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rīfaną.

From Proto-Finnic *rippudak. Cognate to Estonian rippuma, Karelian rippuo, Ludian rippuda, Veps ripuda, Votic rippua and Võro ripma. The -ii- is irregular; expected rippua can be found in dialects. * (to depend, be dependent): Semantic loan from Latin dēpendeō.

From Proto-Finnic *riista of uncertain meaning. Earlier sense probably "object, wares; corn", perhaps adopted as a noa-name for game. Cognates include Estonian riist (“device, instrument; wooden container”), Ingrian riista (“thing, object”), Karelian riista (“game”), Veps rišt (“long time”) and Voti

parole.significato: to take off, doff (clothes, or figuratively other things)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riicudak (compare Estonian riisuma, Karelian riisuo, Livonian rīžõ, Votic riisussõ).

parole.significato: argument, dispute, disagreement, quarrel, verbal fight, contest
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riita (compare Estonian riid, Livvi riidu, Ludian riid, Veps rida), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *strīdaz (compare German Streit, Icelandic stríð).

From Proto-Finnic *riittädäk. Related to Ingrian riittää and Karelian riitteä. The original meaning was "to cover with (thin) ice" (whence riite), from which "to cover" and abstractly "to suffice". If from earlier *riip-tä- (with *-tä-), the root could be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hrīmô (geni
From Proto-Finnic *rik'as (compare Estonian rikas), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rīkaz, *rīkijaz (compare Swedish rik (“rich”)).

From Proto-Finnic *rikki, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Ingrian rikki, Karelian rikki, Ludian rik (“sulfur, earwax”), Veps rik (“sulfur, rheum”) and Votic ričči. Germanic loan origin has been suggested (compare German Dreck), as well as indigenous derivation as rikka + -i.
From Proto-Finnic *rikkodak (compare Estonian rikkuma, Ingrian rikkoa, Livonian rikkõ, Ludian rikkoda, Veps rikta, Votic rikkoa).

parole.significato: breast (section of clothing covering the breast area)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rindus. Equivalent to rinta (“breast, chest”) + -us.

parole.significato: chest, breast, thorax (region of the mammalian body between the neck and the abdomen, especially the front of it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rinta. Cognate to Estonian rind and also more distantly Northern Sami raddi.
From Proto-Finnic *ribistäk, from an onomatopoeic root; rip- + -istä. The strong grade -p- was levelled to all forms.
From Proto-Finnic *rip'oittadak.
From Proto-Finnic *ripsi, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrispō. Related to Estonian ripse, Karelian ripsi, Ludian ripš, Veps rips and Votic ripsi.

From Proto-Finnic *risu, possibly ris- + -u, from risahtaa, thus onomatopoeic of the snapping sound made by dry twigs. Germanic origin has been proposed (compare Icelandic hrís (“brushwood”) and Swedish ris (“twigs in a heap”)), but considered unlikely for phonetic reasons.

parole.significato: A box trap with three walls with the exit closed once the snare is engaged.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rita.

parole.significato: a slender, hanging branch, as of a birch or a willow.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ritva.

parole.significato: pole (delimbed and usually not debarked stem of a small tree, especially one cut to a specified length for a purpose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riuku (compare Ingrian riuku, Karelian riuku, Votic riuku and dialectal Estonian riug), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse þrjúgr).

parole.significato: reef (chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riutta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚷᚱᛖᚢᛏᚨ (*greuta), from Proto-Germanic *greutą (“grit, gravel, sand”), compare with Old Norse grjót (“coarse stones, rubble”).

parole.significato: row, line, rank (objects arranged in a line)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Related to Estonian ribi (“row of traps”) and Veps rivi. Possibly also related to Votic rivi, in which case the word could be of Germanic origin, from Proto-Germanic *ribją.
From Proto-Finnic *rivo.

parole.significato: tow, hards, oakum; the shorter, coarse fibers of linen, hemp, etc.; hackling tow
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rohtin. Related to Ingrian roohtimet, Karelian ruohin, Ludian ruohtim and Veps rohtim.

parole.significato: herb or plant used as a medicine or drug
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rohto.

parole.significato: sheaf of a fiber plant, particularly flax or hemp
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *roivas.

parole.significato: junk (miscellaneous items of little or no value)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *roju.

parole.significato: thick soup, especially one with legumes (peas or beans)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rokka (compare Estonian rokk, Livonian rok, Ludian rokk).

parole.significato: pock (pus-filled swelling caused by pox or similar disease)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rokko (compare Karelian rokko, Veps rok).
From Proto-Finnic *robistak, of onomatopoeic origin. The strong grade -p- has been levelled to all forms.

From Proto-Finnic *rouhidak (compare Livvi rouhie, Ludian rouhida, Veps rouhta), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian krausēt, Lithuanian kraušyti (“to strike”)), from Proto-Indo-European *krus- (compare Ancient Greek κρούω (kroúō), Proto-Germanic *hrusǭ).
From Proto-Finnic *roukka, *roukko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hraukaz. Cognates include Estonian rõuk, Veps rouk, Ingrian roukko.

parole.significato: ground frost (frozen top layer of soil caused by cold weather in winter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *routa, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian grúodas (“frost, frozen street dirt”)).

parole.significato: A small container made of birch bark.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *robëh (compare Ingrian rove, Karelian roveh, Veps robeh). Probably derived from the onomatopoeic root of ropista.

parole.significato: carcass, dead body, especially of a slaughtered animal
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], cognate with Old Norse hrør (“corpse, scrap, wreck, debris”).

parole.significato: prince (ruler or head of a principality; male member of a royal family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruhtinas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *druhtinaz.
From Proto-Finnic *rugis (compare Estonian rukis, Veps rugiž), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rugiz (compare Old English ryġe).
From Proto-Finnic *ruka.
From Proto-Finnic *rukka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rukkaz. Doublet of frakki and rukki.

parole.significato: ugly (displeasing to the eye or ear)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruma, possibly a North Germanic borrowing. Cognates include Estonian rumal (“stupid”), Ingrian ruma (“ugly”), Livonian rumāli (“dirty”), Livvi ruma, Veps ruma (“ugly; coarse”) and Votic ruma. The Finnic word has been borrowed into Sami; compare Northern Sami ropmi.

parole.significato: grass (mass noun); blade of grass (individual specimen)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rooho, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *grōsō- (“grass”).
From Proto-Finnic *rooja.

parole.significato: food (any substance consumed by living organisms to sustain life)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rooka (compare Estonian roog, Ludian ruog, Votic rookõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkā (“care, attention”) (compare Middle High German ruoche, Middle Low German rōke). Compare ruokkia.
From Proto-Finnic *rookkidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną, whence Old English rēcan. Compare with ruoka.
From Proto-Finnic *rookko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōkō (“care, attention”). Doublet of ruoka.
From Proto-Finnic *rooko (compare Karelian ruogo, Veps rogo).
From Proto-Finnic *rooma, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Old Norse drómi).

parole.significato: to scrape, to dig, to paw
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *roopidak.
From Proto-Finnic *roostëk, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *rustaz. Cognates include Estonian rooste, Swedish rost, English rust.
From Proto-Finnic *roostudak, equivalent to ruoste (“rust”) + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *rooto, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *rōdō (“rod, pole”). Cognate to Veps rod.
From Proto-Finnic *rupi (compare Veps rubi, Votic rupi), borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse hrufa (“scab”)).

parole.significato: to pound, pelt, batter, mangle, mutilate (to beat or hit, especially repeatedly)
parole.testo: From obsolete noun rusikka (“fist”) + -oida, from Proto-Finnic *rusikka.

From Proto-Finnic *rutto. Originally an adjective meaning “fast, rapid, quick”; the sense “plague” is by later ellipsis from ruttotauti, literally 'a disease that spreads quickly'. Cognate with Karelian ruttoh (“quickly”), Estonian ruttu (“quickly”), Votic rutto (“hurry”).

parole.significato: dugout (boat made from a hollowed-out log)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruuhi, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þrūhs (“excavated trunk, trough”). Cognates include Estonian ruhi, Karelian ruuhi, Ingrian ruuhi.

parole.significato: congestion, lots of traffic, traffic jam
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruhka, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hrūgǭ (compare modern Swedish råge (“more than full measure”)), perhaps originally meaning "heap".

parole.significato: chaff, husk(s) (inedible parts removed from cereal during threshing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruumën (compare Ingrian rummen, Karelian ruumen, Veps rumen), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *grūdmen-.
From Proto-Finnic *ruumis. Cognates include Ingrian ruumis, Karelian ruumis and Votic ruumõz.

parole.significato: to begin or start to do something
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rubët'ak (akin to Ludian rubeta), probably from ruve- (“scab”) + -ta.

parole.significato: group (number of things or persons being in some relation to each other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rühmä (compare Estonian rühm), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian trūkšmas).
From Proto-Finnic *rükidäk, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: one of the sides of the bow (of a ship)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ründäs. Cognate with Karelian rynnäs and Veps ründäz.

parole.significato: to wallow (roll oneself about in something dirty;)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rüpedäk. Related to Estonian rübelema, Ingrian ryvettyä, Karelian rypie, Votic rüvetä (Mati) and Võro rübimä.
From Proto-Finnic *rüppü. Related to Estonian rüpp, Ingrian rüppü, Karelian ruppi, kruppi and Votic rüppü.

parole.significato: cluster (bunch or group of several discrete items that are close to each other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rübäs (compare Karelian rypäs), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (whence Proto-West Germanic *þrūbō).

parole.significato: to rob, plunder; to loot, sack; to mug
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rööstädäk. Cognate with Estonian rüüstama, Ingrian rööstää, Karelian ryösteä, Livvi rüöstiä, Veps röstta and Votic röösete.

parole.significato: to wade, slog or crawl through
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rähmidäk.

parole.significato: rheum, sleep (substance found in the corner of the eye)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rähmä. Ultimately sound-symbolic.
From Proto-Finnic *räivä, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *hraiwą.
From dialectal räkki (“hot”) + -ttää, from Proto-Finnic *räkki (compare Ingrian räk­ki, räkittää, Karelian räk­ki, räkitteä, Veps räk, räkitada).

parole.significato: mucus, snot (viscous mucus from the nose)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räkä, an early borrowing from Proto-Germanic *hrēką. Cognates include Estonian röga, Old English hrāca, Old Norse hráki.

parole.significato: sleet; rain and snow mixed, wet snow (a mixture of rain and snow)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räntä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian drengti).

parole.significato: vent, flap (especially one located near the ceiling for ventilation purposes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räppänä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *räppä; compare Karelian reppänä. Cognates include Lule Sami riehpen.
From Proto-Finnic *rädistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä. The strong grade -t- was levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: rag, tatter (a piece of cloth torn off; a tattered piece of cloth; a shred, fragment)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rätti.
From Proto-Finnic *räüstäs (compare Estonian räästas, Veps räustaz), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hraustaz (compare Old Norse raust, Swedish röste (“roof truss”)).
From Proto-Finnic *räütüdäk.

parole.significato: to cry loudly (like a small baby); to squawk
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rääküdäk.

parole.significato: to do carelessly or negligently; to skimp, slight, scamp
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rääppidäk ~ *rääpidäk.
From Proto-Finnic *rääp'üs.
From Proto-Finnic *räpäleh.

parole.significato: to grunt, to oink (to make repeatedly pig's grunts)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *röhkidäk (compare Estonian röhkima, Ingrian röhkiä, Karelian röhkie, Veps röhkta, Võro röhk'mä), of onomatopoeic origin, from röh (“oink, grunt”). Equivalent to röh + -hkiä.
From Proto-Finnic *saadak (compare Estonian saama), from Proto-Uralic *saxe- (compare Moksha самс (sams), Eastern Mari шуаш (šuaš), Komi-Zyrian суны (suny)); see it for more.
From Proto-Finnic *saalis, equivalent to saada (“to get”) + -lis. Related to Karelian šualis.
From Proto-Finnic *saarëlainën. Equivalent to saari (“island”) + -lainen.

parole.significato: island (contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saari. First attested in 1295 (as Saris).
From Proto-Finnic *sarna (compare Veps sarn), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ćarńa (“incantation, speech”) (compare Komi-Zyrian сёрни (śorńi)).
From Proto-Finnic *sarni (compare Livonian sǟrna), from Proto-Finno-Permic *särńä (compare Eastern Mari шертне (šertńe), Western Mari шӓртньы (šärtńy)).
From Proto-Finnic *sagarva. Compare Proto-Samic *čeavrēs.
From Proto-Finnic *sasta. Related to Estonian saast and Livonian sastā, as well as Karelian soastua (verb, ~ saastua).

parole.significato: to escort, usher, see, accompany, walk, take
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saattadak. Equivalent to saa- (“to get, arrive”) + -ttaa. Compare Karelian šuattua (“to escort; to be able”), and Erzya савтомс (savtoms, “to cause”).

From Proto-Finnic *saatto (cognates include Estonian saad, Karelian soatto, Veps sat and Votic saatto), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*sātō), from Proto-Germanic *sētǭ (compare Icelandic sáta).
From Proto-Finnic *sadanci. Equivalent to sata (“hundred”) + -s (“-th”).

parole.significato: precipitation (any kind of precipitation from the sky (e.g. rain, snow, sleet, hailstones))
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sadëk. Equivalent to sataa (“to rain, precipitate”) + -e.

From Proto-Finnic *saip(p)u-, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ (“soap”) (compare Swedish såpa) or later Proto-Norse [script needed] (*saipwōn-). The variant saipua is attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552) and modern saippua first in 1609. Doublet of suopa and soopa. The
From Proto-Finnic *sairas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sairaz, compare Swedish sår, English sore.
Derived from Proto-Finnic *saira (with a suffix -va and metathesis). Related to Veps saivarʹ.

parole.significato: point (sharp tip, e.g. of a star)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sakara (compare Estonian sagar, Karelian sakara, Ludian sagar, Veps tšagar, Votic sakarõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian stãgaras).
From Proto-Finnic *sakëda, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sake.
From Proto-Finnic *sakka, probably akin to sakea.
From Proto-Finnic *sakko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sakō.

parole.significato: secret (currently used mostly idiomatically and as modifier in compound terms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sala, from Proto-Uralic *sala (“to hide, steal, thief”). Cognates include Estonian sala (“secretly”), Livonian salātõ (“to hide something”), Northern Sami suoládit (“to keep secret, to conceal”), Northern Sami suola (“thief”), Erzya саламс (salams, “to steal”), Eastern Mari шолышт
From Proto-Finnic *salakka.
From Proto-Finnic *salama, from Proto-Uralic *ćala-. Cognates include Southern Khanty сӑт (săt) and Eastern Mansi са̄л (sāl).
From Proto-Finnic *salaga (compare dialectal salaja, no other Finnic cognates are known), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *salhô (“willow”) (compare Swedish sälg, English sallow).
From Proto-Finnic *salkku. Related to Ingrian salkku, Karelian salkku and Veps šaug. Originally probably meant "bag, bundle".

parole.significato: pole (long and slender piece of metal or especially wood, used for various construction or support purposes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salko, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëlkaw, a loan from an early descendant of Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰalgʰ- (“slat”). Finno-Ugric cognates include Karelian šalko, Northern Sami čuolggu (“lever, crowbar”), Erzya сялго (śalgo, “stick”), Hungarian szál (“fiber”), Northern Mansi са̄гла (sā
From Proto-Finnic *sallidak (compare Estonian sallima, Karelian sallie), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saljaną (compare Swedish sälja, English sell).

parole.significato: strait, sound (narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salmi (compare Estonian salm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćalme (compare Northern Sami čoalbmi and possibly Udmurt сюм (śum, “bay, cove”)). Doublet of jolma (which is a Sami loan).
From Proto-Finnic *salo, probably borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: bolt, bar (bar to prevent a door from being forced open; sliding pin or bar in a lock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salpa (compare Karelian salpa, Veps saub), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stalpą (whence dialectal Swedish stalpe (“pole”)).

parole.significato: to notch (to join by means of notches, especially the logs in the corners of a log house)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salvadak.
From Proto-Finnic *salbat'ak, equivalent to salpa (“bolt, bar, clasp”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *sama (compare Estonian sama, Karelian sama, Votic sama), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *samaz (compare Swedish samma, English same; also borrowed into Sami, compare Northern Sami seamma).
From Proto-Finnic *samëda.
From Proto-Finnic *sammal. Related to Estonian sammal, Ingrian sammal, Karelian sammal, Livonian sōmal, Ludian sammal, Veps samal and Votic sammõl.

parole.significato: cosmic pillar that supported the sky
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sambas, probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *stámbʰHas (compare Sanskrit स्तम्भ (stambha)).
From Proto-Finnic *sampudak (compare Ingrian sammua, Karelian sammuo, Veps sampta). The weak grade -mm- has been levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: sturgeon (any fish of the family Acipenseridae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sampi (compare Estonian samb).

parole.significato: word (unit of language, text or storage)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sana.
From Proto-Finnic *sanko. Equivalent to sanka (“handle”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *sanoidak. Equivalent to sana (“word”) + -oa. Cognates include Ingrian sannoa.

parole.significato: tail of an animal (more specifically the solid part of a tail)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sapa. Related to Estonian saba.

parole.significato: (either of) a pair of sticks used to carry hay
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sapilas, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stapulaz.

parole.significato: the axehead between the bit and the eye
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sapsa.

parole.significato: sedge (any plant of the genus Carex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sara (compare Karelian sara, Ludian sara, Veps šarahin), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *staraz (compare Swedish starr).
From Proto-Finnic *sarana.

parole.significato: series (number of things that follow on one after the other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sarja (“lath board, row of laths; row, bunch”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śarja (“lath, batten, bar”). Adopted as an equivalent to Latin series in the literary language based on the original meanings "row, bunch" and the sense related to chicken eggs listed below which can also be

From Proto-Finnic *sarka, from Proto-Uralic *sarka (“branch?”). Cognates include Estonian sarg, Ingrian sarka, Karelian sarka, Livvi sargu, Veps sarg, Votic sarkõ, Northern Sami suorgi (“branch”), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (tārka, “branch”) and Northern Selkup [script needed] (tolka, “branch”) (

parole.significato: horn (growth of keratin that protrudes from the head of certain animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sarvi (compare Estonian sarv), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śarwe (compare Erzya сюро (śuro) and Hungarian szarv), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćr̥Hwa- (compare Avestan 𐬯𐬭𐬏 (srū, “horn, claw, talon”), 𐬯𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬁 (sruuā, “horn”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂-. Doublet of

From Proto-Finnic *sata (compare Estonian sada), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëta (“hundred”) (compare Erzya сядо (śado), Northern Mansi са̄т (sāt), Hungarian száz), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćatám (compare Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀 (sata), Sanskrit शत (śatá)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm.

parole.significato: to precipitate (to have water in the air fall to the ground): to rain, snow, sleet, hail
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *satadak (“to fall”) (compare Estonian sadama), from Proto-Uralic *śada- (compare Southern Selkup соорогу (soorogu)), possibly borrowed from Indo-Iranian.

parole.significato: harbour/harbor, port, haven (place where ships can shelter or dock for loading or unloading)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *satama (cognate with Estonian sadam (“harbour”)). Two etymologies exist: * Derivation from sataa in the sense "to descend". * Derivation with the suffix + -ma from a root derived from Proto-Germanic *staþaz (compare English stathe, German Gestade).

parole.significato: harvest, crop (natural production for a specific year, particularly of plants)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sato, probably derived from Proto-Uralic *čača- (“to grow”). Related to Erzya чачомс (čačoms, “to be born”).

parole.significato: to hurt, be sore (physically or mentally)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sattudak (compare Estonian sattuma).

According to Aikio (2020), possibly from Proto-Finnic *satu, derived from an unattested verb *sate- + -u, related to Southern Sami soetedh (“to tell something frightening”) and Southern Sami soete (“frightening story”). Alternatively, possibly an obscure derivation from sattua; alternatively derived
From Proto-Finnic *satula, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sadulaz (“saddle”). Cognate with Estonian sadul.
Probably from earlier *sagukkoi, derived from Proto-Finnic *sagarva.

From Proto-Finnic *sakna (compare southeastern dialectal saakna, sakna, Estonian saun), possibly borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *stakna- (later *stakkaz, whence English stack). Older sense "winter dwelling, a pit dug into snow for temporary shelter", compare Northern Sami suovdnji (“pit dug in s
From Proto-Finnic *sapra, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stauraz. Cognate with Karelian soapra, Livvi suabru, Ludian suabr and Veps sabr.

parole.significato: clay (mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sauvi (compare Estonian savi).

From Proto-Finnic *sauvu (compare Livonian so’v), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *śëwwe (“smoke”) (compare Northern Sami suovva and possibly Erzya сув (suv, “fog, curtain”)). * (unit of taxation): Originally defined based on the number of residential buildings with a chimney. Compare Swedish rök,
From Proto-Finnic *seimi ~ *soimi, derived from Proto-Uralic *sewe-, whence syödä (“to eat”).

parole.significato: wall (substantial structure acting as side or division in a building; something with the apparent solidity and dimensio…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saina (compare Estonian sein), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian siena (“wall”)).
From Proto-Finnic *seipi, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *steip-.
From Proto-Finnic *saictak (compare Estonian seisma, Võro saisma), from Proto-Uralic *sańśa- ~ *säńśä-.

From Proto-Finnic *säic'en (compare Estonian seitse (“seven”)), from Proto-Uralic *ćäjćemä (*śäjćemä) (compare Erzya сисем (sisem, “seven”), Eastern Mari шым (šym), Udmurt сизьым (śiźym), Tundra Nenets сӣˮив (syīqyiw°)). The original nominative form (seitsen) has been largely displaced by the geniti
From Proto-Finnic *säic'en kümmentä. Equivalent to seitsemän (“seven”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).

From Proto-Finnic *säic'en toicta (kümmentä) (literally “seven of the second decade”). Equivalent to seitsemän (“seven”) + -toista (“of the second”) (see seitsemän for more information on its development).
From Proto-Finnic *säiccemenci. Equivalent to seitsemä- (“seven”) + -s (“-th”), with third syllable *-e- analogically adjusted to -ä- (see seitsemän).
Proto-Finnic *säic'en; see seitsemän

parole.significato: pole, stake (long and slender piece of wood or other material, pointed at one end so as to be easily driven into the gr…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saibas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *staipas (compare Lithuanian sti̇́ebas). Cognates include Estonian teivas, Livonian tāibaz, Ludian šeibäz, Veps seibaz, Võro saivass and Votic seivez.

From Proto-Finnic *seka, possibly from Proto-Uralic *sekä (“inside, interior”), thus "among" (also see seassa) and later "mixed". The word has (presumably original) front vowels in Võro but back vowels elsewhere.

parole.significato: clear (free of ambiguity, easily understood; not dark or obscured)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *selkedä.

parole.significato: back (the rear of the body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and be…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *selkä (compare Estonian selg), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śelkä (compare Proto-Samic *čielkē, Eastern Mari шӹлӹж (šÿlÿž, “area of the sacrum”)).

parole.significato: clear (not dark or obscured; of more abstract concepts; see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *selvä. Related to Ingrian selvä, Karelian selvä and Kukkuzi selvä.
From Proto-Finnic *seppä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śeppä (“skilled”).
From Proto-Finnic *sepä (“neck”), from Proto-Uralic *śepä (“neck”). Cognates include Erzya сиве (sive).
From Proto-Finnic *setä, from Proto-Uralic *čečä (*śečä) (compare Northern Sami čeahci, Eastern Mari [script needed] (čüčü), Northern Mansi [script needed] (sasi̮γ)).
From Proto-Finnic *sëkla (compare Estonian sõel, Karelian šiekla, Ingrian seegla, Votic siglõ), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēdlą (compare Swedish såll, Icelandic sáld).
From Proto-Finnic *sëkloidak, equivalent to seula (“sieve, sifter”) + -oa. Compare Estonian sõeluma, Karelian šiekluo, Livonian sõ’gļõ, Ludian šiegloda, Veps segloida, Votic sigloa.

From Proto-Finnic *sëpra (compare Estonian sõber), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian sēbrs (“friend”), Lithuanian sėbras (“companion”)). Erzya шабра (šabra) is possibly borrowed from the same source.

parole.significato: bandage, dressing (medical binding or strip of cloth used as a blindfold)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sidek. Equivalent to sitoa (“to bind, tie”) + -e.

siem- + -aista, from the rare dialectal word siemi, from Proto-Finnic *seemi (compare derivations Estonian sõõm (“gulp”), Livonian sēmḑa (“milk”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śäme- (compare Erzya симемс (simems, “to drink”)).

parole.significato: seed (fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *seemen, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *sḗˀmin, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₁mn̥. Doublet of hieman.
From Proto-Finnic *sëëra. Cognate with Ingrian seera, Karelian siera, Ludian sier and Veps ser.

From Proto-Finnic *sëstar (compare Estonian sõstar, Ingrian seestara, Ludian sestroi, Veps sestrikäine, Votic sõssõr). Possibly further related to Erzya [script needed] (šukštorov), [script needed] (čukštorov) and Moksha [script needed] (šukštoru). These words cannot be regularly traced back to a co
From Proto-Finnic *seetädäk.
From Proto-Finnic *sihistäk, ultimately onomatopoeic. Related to Estonian sihisema, Ingrian sihissä, Karelian šihistä, Livvi šihistä, Veps šihišta and Votic sihisse.
From Proto-Finnic *sii, possibly from Proto-Uralic *śiŋe.
From Proto-Finnic *ciidek.

parole.significato: common whitefish, lavaret (Coregonus lavaretus), or any of its subspecies
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *siika, of unknown further origin, but related words are found in Germanic (Swedish sik), Baltic (Latvian sīga) and Slavic (Russian сиг (sig)); the word has been variously thought to originate from any one of those three and might ultimately be from a substrate.
From Proto-Finnic *ciika(inën) ( + -(i)nen), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *dīgas (whence Lithuanian dygas (“thorn”)).
From Proto-Finnic *siima, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīmô. Cognate with dialectal Estonian sihm, Ingrian siima, Karelian siima, Livvi siimu, Ludian šiim, Veps siim, sim and Votic siimõ.
From Proto-Finnic *siipi, possibly a Baltic loan. Cognates include Estonian tiib, Ingrian siipi, Karelian šiipi /šiibi, Livonian tībõz, Livvi siibi, Ludian siib, Veps šīb, Võro siib, Votic siipi.

parole.significato: to move, transfer, relocate; (chiefly math) to translate
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *siirtädäk. Related to Karelian siirdüö, Veps sirta and possibly also Erzya сыргамс (sïrgams, “to move”).
From Proto-Finnic *sigittädäk. Equivalent to siitä (“to be conceived”) + -ttää.
From Proto-Finnic *sigit'äk (compare Estonian sigima).
From Proto-Finnic *siivilä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sīhwila, *sīhila (“sieve”).
From Proto-Finnic *ciivo, probably a back-formation from siivota.

parole.significato: to clean, clean up, tidy up, tidy (make more tidy or clean; make less disorganized, e.g. of a room or space)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ciivot'ak. Related to Ingrian siivota, Karelian šiivota and also to Northern Sami divvut.

parole.significato: place, stead (location or position of or for something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sija (compare Ludian šija), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stiją (compare English sty in pigsty and Swedish stia in svinstia). First adapted to mean “(grammatical) case” by Finnish physician and philologist Elias Lönnrot in 1836.
From Proto-Finnic *cika (compare Estonian siga, Võro tsiga).
From Proto-Finnic *sikedä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śikɜ (“thick, dense, solid”). Related to Erzya сееде (sejede, “frequent; dense”).

parole.significato: smooth, sleek (having a texture that lacks friction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *siledä (compare Karelian silei, Veps siled).
From Proto-Finnic *silittädäk, equivalent to sileä (“smooth”) + -ittää

From Proto-Finnic *silmä (compare Estonian silm), from Proto-Uralic *śilmä (compare Northern Sami čalbmi, Erzya сельме (seľme), Eastern Mari шинча (šinča), Udmurt син (śin), Northern Mansi сам (sam), Northern Khanty сєм (sêm), Hungarian szem, Tundra Nenets сэв (sew°)).

parole.significato: to glance (to look at something quickly)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *silmät'äk, equivalent to silmä (“eye”) + -tä
From Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Related to Karelian silpie and Veps šilʹpta.

parole.significato: bridge (construction or natural feature that spans a divide)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cilta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *tílˀta (compare Latvian tilts, Lithuanian tiltas).

parole.significato: a nonalcoholic or low-alcohol drink made from lemon, various sugars and water, common around vappu (“May Day”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sima, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saimaz (compare German Seim (“syrup”), Old Norse seimr (“honeycomb”)). The original meaning was “mead”, but the common meaning now refers to a different beverage, albeit one that is ultimately developed from mead.
From Proto-Finnic *sini, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sine. Cognates include Erzya сэнь (sëń).
From Proto-Finnic *sininen. Equivalent to sini (“blue”) + -inen.

parole.significato: you (second-person singular personal pronoun, used in familiar or neutral contexts), thou
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cinä, from Proto-Uralic *tinä. See the Proto-Finnic entry for more information on inflection.
From Proto-Finnic *cibistäk, from an Onomatopoeic root + -istä. The strong grade -p- was levelled to all forms.

parole.significato: to become bent, be installed poorly
parole.testo: sipaan perhaps an illative singular from Proto-Finnic *sipa (compare sipale, sivu), related to Karelian šivallah (“tilted”). Compare also sippi, sippiin.
From Proto-Finnic *ciristäk, equivalent to sir- + -istä; from an onomatopoeic root.
From Proto-Finnic *sirkëda.

From Proto-Finnic *cirkka, probably ultimately an imitative root + *-kka; cognates include Ingrian serkka, Karelian čirkka, Ludian tširkku and Votic širkkõ (the initial consonant is irregular, but might be caused by the imitative origin or the affectionate nature of the word).
From Proto-Finnic *cirkku.
From Proto-Finnic *cirppi (compare Estonian sirp, North Karelian čirppi), borrowed from Proto-Slavic *sьrpъ (compare Russian серп (serp)).
From Proto-Finnic *sisar, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *swésō or Proto-Indo-European *swésōr (compare Erzya сазор (sazor)).

parole.significato: common lizard, viviparous lizard, Zootoca vivipara
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sisalikko (compare Estonian sisalik, Karelian čičiliušku), likely from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *sisoi.

parole.significato: inner, internal, interior, inward, inside; indoor; inland
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sicä (compare Estonian sise-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śićä (compare Moksha сезем (sezem, “heartwood”)).

parole.significato: a strip of land to be sowed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sicka-.

parole.significato: tough, durable, resilient, hardy (strong and resilient; lasting attempts to break, flex, bend, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *citkedä (compare Estonian sitke, Ingrian sitkiä, Karelian sitkie, Veps sitked, Võro sikkõ, Votic sitka), which is also more distantly related to Northern Sami dađgat.

From Proto-Finnic *sitodak (compare Estonian siduma, Veps sidoda), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sita- (compare Erzya содомс (sodoms)). * (to bind, oblige): Likely a semantic loan from other languages, ultimately a semantic loan from Latin obligō.
From Proto-Finnic *sitta, possibly from Proto-Uralic *sitta.

parole.significato: a net or mesh in a wing of a seine that is located on the far end; side net or mesh in a seine; outer mesh of a fishing…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cikla (compare Karelian šikla), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian tìkls and Lithuanian tinklas).

parole.significato: page, side (one surface of a sheet of paper; one side of a paper leaf on which one has written or printed)
parole.testo: From earlier *sivu ~ *sipu (compare dialectal sipuun in Eurén 1860 for modern sivuan, form of the verb sivuta, Ingrian sivu, Karelian šivu, šivassa (“tilted, askew, off to the side”), šipah, šipa- in šipatuuli (“crosswind”), Ludian šivud (“small of the back”)), probably derived from Proto-Finnic *si
From Proto-Finnic *sogët'ak, equivalent to sokea (“blind”) + -eta.

parole.significato: to sound (to make a musical sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soidak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śoje- (compare Northern Sami čuodjat, Hungarian zaj).
From Proto-Finnic *soimat'ak, from Proto-Uralic *śojma (compare soida). Cognate with Estonian sõimama.

parole.significato: to play (produce music using a musical instrument; use a device to hear a recording)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soittadak. Equivalent to soida (“to make a sound, ring”) + -ttaa (causative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *sokëda.
From Proto-Finnic *colistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. Compare soljua.

From Proto-Finnic *solki, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *śolke. Related to Erzya сюлгамо (śulgamo). However, the cognates outside Finnic are not entirely regular, which makes the etymology beyond Proto-Finnic uncertain.
From Proto-Finnic *solmëidak. Roughly equivalent to solmu (“knot”) + -ia.
From Proto-Finnic *coma. Related to Karelian šoma, Livvi čoma, Ludian čoma and Veps čoma.
From Proto-Finnic *conkidak.

parole.significato: bull (uncastrated adult male of domesticated cattle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sonni (compare Estonian sõnn).
From Proto-Finnic *sonsar, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ćonča, *ćoča.
From Proto-Finnic *sonta, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śonta. Cognate with Estonian sõnnik and Western Mari шандӹ (šandÿ).
From Proto-Finnic *sopa (compare Estonian sõba, Votic sõpa), from Proto-Uralic *śopa. In the sense “garment, piece of clothing”, displaced by vaate.

parole.significato: to fit [with allative] (to be of the correct size and shape; to be capable of being put into or passing through somethi…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sopidak (compare Karelian sopie, Ludian sopie, Estonian sobima and Votic soppia). Equivalent to sopa (“a suit or piece of clothing”) + -ia.

parole.significato: A small quiet spot; corner, nook.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *coppi.

parole.significato: gravel (small fragments of rock, technical definition: soil with rocks predominantly with a size between 2 and 20, or e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cora (compare Estonian sõra), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćora (“grain”) (compare Erzya сюро (śuro, “grain”)), borrowing from early Proto-Balto-Slavic *śoros.

parole.significato: to babble, to burble, to gurgle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *coristak, equivalent to sor- + -ista, with an onomatopoeic root.

parole.significato: cloven hoof, cleft hoof, cloven foot (divided hoof, as in bovine animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sorkka. Cognates include Estonian sõrg, Votic sorkkõ, Ingrian sorkka.

parole.significato: finger (one of the five extremities of the hand)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sormi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *sorme. Cognates include Estonian sõrm, Northern Sami suorbma, Erzya сур (sur).

parole.significato: ring, finger ring (jewelry worn around the finger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sormus, equivalent to sormi (“finger”) + -us. Cognate with Estonian sõrmus, Karelian sormus, Livonian sūormõks, Veps sormuz, Votic sõrmuz.

parole.significato: spike, prong (in a tool, such as a plough)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *sorsa, of unknown further origin.
From Proto-Finnic *sortadak (“to tip over, knock down”). Cognate with Ingrian sortaa, Karelian šortua, Ludian sortta and Veps sorta.

parole.significato: war (conflict involving organized use of arms; also figuratively, e.g. of a campaign against something or business comp…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sota (compare Estonian sõda, Livonian suodā, Veps soda, Võro sõda), from Proto-Uralic *śoďa (compare Erzya сюдома (śudoma, “to curse”), Eastern Mari шудалаш (šudalaš, “to curse”), Tundra Nenets сайнорць (saynorcʹ°, “to be at war”)).

parole.significato: to be at war, to fight in a war
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sotidak, equivalent to sota (“war”) + -ia.

parole.significato: Any bird of the genus Aythya including scaups, pochards, canvasbacks etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sotka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śoδka.

parole.significato: to mess up, make a mess of, untidy, disorder
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sotkëdak. Cognate to Estonian sõtkuma, Ingrian sotkia, Karelian sotkie, Livonian suotkõ, Ludian soťkida, Veps sotkta, Votic sõtkoa and Võro sõkma.

parole.significato: to row (propel over water using oars)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soutadak, from Proto-Uralic *suxta-.
From Proto-Finnic *sugët'ak.
From Proto-Finnic *suhistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. Related to Estonian suhisema, Ingrian suhissa, Karelian šuhissa and Veps šuhaita.
From Proto-Finnic *suiccëdak. Related to Estonian suitsema, Votic suitsuttaa (Kattila), Võro suitsama.

parole.significato: bridle (headgear with which a horse is directed and which carries a bit and reins)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suic'ët, derived from suu with an older variant of the -inen suffix (*-ic(c)et).
From Proto-Finnic *suiccu. Cognate with Estonian suits and Võro tsuits.

parole.significato: to go, run (usually smoothly or successfully, unless specified with an adverb)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sujudak. Related to Karelian sujuo and Proto-Samic *sojëtēk.

parole.significato: A (coarse) brush, especially one used for brushing animals, such as a currycomb for grooming horses.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suka, probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic [Term?] (compare Latvian suka).

parole.significato: to dive (swim under water or jump into water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cuk'ëldak (compare Karelian čukeltua, Võro tsuklõma) + -taa, possibly ultimately from an onomatopoeic root.

parole.significato: to groom (care for animals by brushing and cleaning them)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sukëidak. Equivalent to suka (“(coarse) brush, currycomb”) + -ia.

From Proto-Finnic *sukka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *sukkaz (“sock”) (compare English sock, Swedish socka), from Latin soccus. Finnic cognates include Ingrian sukka, Karelian sukka, Karelian šukka, Livvi sukku, Ludian suk, Estonian sukk, Livonian sukā and Votic sukkõ.

parole.significato: ski (one of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow, ice or water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suksi, from Proto-Uralic *sukse. Cognate with Erzya сокс (soks).

parole.significato: extended family, kin (in addition to parents and children, includes cousins, uncles, aunts, grandparents and farther re…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suku.

parole.significato: relative, relation (member of one's extended family)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sukulainën, equivalent to suku (“(extended) family”) + -lainen.
From Proto-Finnic *sula (compare Estonian sula), a deverbal from sulaa (“to melt”).

parole.significato: to melt, thaw (change from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suladak, from Proto-Uralic *sula- (compare Moksha соламс (solams), Eastern Mari шулаш (šulaš), Komi-Permyak сывны (syvny), Southern Khanty тӑтә (tătə), Hungarian olvad).

parole.significato: to melt (to cause something to melt)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulattadak. Equivalent to sulaa (“to melt, thaw”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: groom, bridegroom (man who is about to marry)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulhainën. Cognate with Estonian sulane, Ingrian sulhain, Karelian sulhaine and Votic sulhanõ (Kattila).

parole.significato: feather, more specifically a flight feather (stiff feather in a bird's wing or tail used in flying)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulka, probably from Proto-Uralic *tulka (see the Proto-Finnic entry for details). Cognates include Estonian sulg, Erzya толга (tolga) and Hungarian toll.

parole.significato: to close, shut (a door, gate, box, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulkëdak (compare Estonian sulgema), from Proto-Finno-Permic *śulke- (compare Erzya and Moksha сёлгомс (śolgoms, “to close”)).

parole.significato: closing, closure, shutting (act of closing or shutting)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulku (compare Estonian sulg), equivalent to sulkea (“to close, shut”) + -u.
From Proto-Finnic *sum(p)a.
From Proto-Finnic *sumëda. Cognates include Estonian sume, Ludian sume, Livvi sumeh. From the same root as sumu (“fog”).
From Proto-Finnic *sumu (compare Ingrian sumu, Karelian sumu, Veps sumeg). Probably also related to Northern Sami sopmu (which might be borrowed from Finnic).
From Proto-Finnic *suntija, borrowed from Old East Slavic *сѫдиꙗ (*sǫdija) (whence Russian судья́ (sudʹjá)).
From Proto-Finnic *soo, of disputed further origin. Cognates include Estonian soo.

parole.significato: to give, allow, permit, grant, let, afford (generally from someone of higher status to someone of lower status)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soodak (possibly borrowed from Indo-Iranian; see entry for more).

parole.significato: synonym of suojasää (“thaw”) (weather warm enough to melt snow and ice)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sooja, probably a later shift from suoja (etymology 1).

parole.significato: salt (common table salt, sodium chloride, NaCl)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soola (compare Estonian sool, Veps sol), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian sāls), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sḗh₂l. Words of Indo-European origin occur also in many other Uralic languages (compare Erzya сал (sal), Udmurt сылал (sylal), Komi-Permyak сов (sov)); while
From Proto-Finnic *soolainën, equivalent to suola (“salt”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *soolat'ak, equivalent to suola (“salt”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *sooli (compare Estonian sool), from Proto-Uralic *śale (compare Northern Sami čoalli, Erzya сюло (śulo), Udmurt сюл (śul)).

parole.significato: scale (one of the keratin pieces covering the skin of certain animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soomu(s) (compare Estonian soomus, Veps somuz), from Proto-Uralic *śëme (compare Erzya сяв (śav), Udmurt сьӧм (śöm), Komi-Permyak сьӧм (śöm)).

parole.significato: vessel, vas (tube or canal that carries fluid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sooni, from Proto-Uralic *sëne. Cognates include Estonian soon, Erzya сан (san), Northern Mansi та̄н (tān), Hungarian ín (“sinew”).
From Proto-Finnic *coora.
From Proto-Finnic *cooro, probably equivalent to suora (“straight”) + -o.

parole.significato: herd of horses, sheep or reindeers
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soota, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stōdą.
From Proto-Finnic *soova, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian stāvs (“stature, storey”), Lithuanian stovas (“rack, stand”)).

parole.significato: frazil ice, i.e. ice in a frazil form i.e. as a kind of watery sludge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suppo.
From Proto-Finnic *suristak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *surku, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *surgō (compare English sorrow, Swedish sorg).

parole.significato: violent or accidental death (mainly used of humans)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *surma, from Proto-Uralic *śurma. Equivalent to surra + -ma (although the original meaning of surra, “to die”, is not found in Finnish). Cognates include Estonian surm, Karelian šurma.
From Proto-Finnic *surmat'ak. Equivalent to surma (“killing, slaying, murder”) + -ta.

parole.significato: to mourn, grieve (often because of someone's death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *surdak (“to die”) (compare Estonian surema (“to die”)), from Proto-Uralic *śure- (“to die”). The modern meaning is by contamination from surku; the original meaning is still found in the derivative surma (“killing”). May also be related to Erzya сырьмай (sïŕmaj, “death”).

parole.significato: to cram, stuff, crowd (press, force, or drive, particularly in filling, or in thrusting one thing into another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *survodak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śurwa-.
From Proto-Finnic *suci.
From Proto-Finnic *suu (compare Estonian suu), from Proto-Uralic *śuwe (compare Northern Mansi сӯп (sūp), Hungarian száj, Tundra Nenets сё (syo)).

parole.significato: thickener (substance used to thicken something, e.g. a sauce)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suurus, equivalent to suuri (“large”) + -us.

parole.significato: synonym of saattaa (“to be able; might”)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *suuttadak; probably equivalent to suu (“mouth”) + -ttaa.
From Proto-Finnic *suvait'ak, equivalent to suva- + -ita, probably from the same root as suoda (Proto-Finnic *soodak, probably from earlier *suwa-).

From Proto-Finnic *suvi, from Proto-Uralic *suŋe (compare Northern Sami sakŋat (“be thawed”), Nganasan тәӈәә (təŋəə)). Replaced in the standard language in the 19th century with kesä, which was traditionally used in the eastern dialects (as opposed to suvi, which was traditionally a Western Finnish

From Proto-Finnic *südän (compare Estonian süda), from Proto-Uralic *śüdäme (compare Skolt Sami čââʹđ, Erzya седей (sedej), Eastern Mari шӱм (šüm), Komi-Zyrian сьӧлӧм (śölöm), Northern Mansi сым (sym), Hungarian szív, Tundra Nenets сей (syey°)).
From Proto-Finnic *süksü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sükśe. Cognates include Estonian sügis, Karelian šygyžy, Northern Sami čakča, Erzya сёксь (śokś), Hungarian ősz.

parole.significato: arms (in reference to embracing or holding in both one's arms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *süli, from Proto-Uralic *süle. Cognates include Estonian süli, Veps sülʹ, Erzya сэль (sëľ, “fathom”), Hungarian öl.
From Proto-Finnic *sülkedäk, from Proto-Uralic *ćülke-.
From Proto-Finnic *sülki, a deverbal from sylkeä (“to spit”).
From Proto-Finnic *sünkedä (compare Karelian synkie), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian sunkùs (“heavy”)).

parole.significato: to deliver, bear, give birth to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sündüttädäk. Equivalent to syntyä (“to be born”) + -ttää (causative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *süntü, equivalent to syntyä (“to be born”) + -y.
From Proto-Finnic *süntümä. Equivalent to syntyä (“to be born”) + -mä.
From Proto-Finnic *süntüdäk (compare Estonian sündima), from Proto-Uralic *sentew- (compare Nganasan тынтуди (tyntudji)).
From Proto-Finnic *sürjä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *sturjas (compare Latvian stūris (“corner”), dialectal Lithuanian stūrỹs, stùris (“corner”)).
From Proto-Finnic *süci (compare Estonian süsi), from Proto-Uralic *ćüďe (compare Erzya седь (seď)).
Possibly from Proto-Finnic *cüskäit'äk, although the loss of -k- would be irregular.

parole.significato: to scrape or hack off, especially of ice
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sütedäk.

parole.significato: to ignite, be ignited, catch fire (to commence burning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *süttüdäk.

parole.significato: to light, kindle, ignite, set on fire, set fire to, burn, inflame, set ablaze, torch
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *süt'üttädäk. Equivalent to syttyä (“to catch fire, ignite”) + -ttää.
From Proto-Finnic *cüvüc, equivalent to syvä (“deep”) + -yys (“-ness, -th”).
From Proto-Finnic *cüvä (compare Estonian süva), probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tiwä (compare e.g. Northern Sami davvi (“north”), Eastern Mari тӱнӧ (tünö)).

From Proto-Finnic *süü (compare Estonian süü), from Proto-Uralic *siwe (compare Eastern Mari ший (šij), Komi-Zyrian сі (si), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (t̜́ì)). The sense “reason, cause” (and those akin to it) was originally figurative, and is also found elsewhere in Finnic.
From Proto-Finnic *süklä (compare Karelian syplä, Votic sügle), probably from Proto-Uralic *śüklä (compare Erzya сильге (siľge)).
From Proto-Finnic *söödäk (compare Estonian sööma), from Proto-Uralic *sewe- (compare Erzya сэвемс (sëvems), Udmurt сины (śiny), Northern Mansi тэ̄ӈкве (tè̄ňkve), Hungarian eszik).
From Proto-Finnic *sööjä. Equivalent to syödä (“to eat”) + -jä (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *cööstäk.
From Proto-Finnic *sööttädäk. Equivalent to syödä (“to eat”) + -ttaa (curative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *sädek (“spark”). First attested in 1583 writings by Finnish priest and rector Jacobus Finno. Related to säen, Estonian säde, Veps sädeg and Votic säe.

Probably sä(k)e- + -n(e), from the dialectal verb säetä (“to pile up the embers and cover them with ash (to more easily start a fire later)”), from Proto-Finnic *säkedäk; possibly semantically influenced by säde, which originally meant “spark”.
From Proto-Finnic *sähistäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *säigeh, probably derived from *sää (whence sää (“(obsolete) fiber, thread, strand”).

parole.significato: to remain, be preserved, endure (continue unchanged)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?]. Related to Karelian säilyö, Livvi säilyö and Votic säülüä (Pummala).

From Proto-Finnic *säkä, from Proto-Uralic *śäkᴈ ~ *śekᴈ. Related to Estonian säga, Erzya сие (sije), Moksha сия (sijä), Eastern Mari ший (šij), Eastern Khanty сәг (səg), Southern Khanty сәҳ (səḥ) and Northern Mansi сиг (sig).

parole.significato: the withers (part of the back of a draft animal or horse that is the highest)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *säkä. Related to Karelian säkä, Ludian šägä and Veps sägu.
From Proto-Finnic *sälidäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śälä-, *ćälä-.

parole.significato: young horse, particularly one that is older than a foal (around 2–3 years old); colt, filly
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sälko; compare Estonian sälg, Karelian šälkö, sälkö, Ludian sälgü, Votic sʹalko.

parole.significato: to place a burden or load, to lump, to saddle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sälüttädäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *sälä-.
From Proto-Finnic *sänki (compare Veps säng), possibly from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *cäristäk, from onomatopoeic root + -istä

parole.significato: to break, shatter, smash (cause to break into two or more pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *särkedäk (compare Votic särčiä), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ćärke- (compare Lule Sami tjiergav, Northern Mansi [script needed] (saɣr-) and possibly Hungarian sért (“to injure”), although the last of these would be irregular).
From Proto-Finnic *särki (compare Estonian särg), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *särke (compare Erzya сэрьге (sëŕge)).

parole.significato: edge, arris (boundary line of a surface; sharp edge or ridge formed by the intersection of two surfaces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *särmä, according to Aikio (2020) equivalent to särkeä (“to break”) + -mä. Cognate with Estonian särme and Veps särm, särmaine. Probably originally "strip, band, ribbon", later "(sharp) edge". Modern geometry sense was given to it by Finnish physician and author Samuel Roos.
From Proto-Finnic *särpidäk. Related to Karelian särpeä, Ludian särbida, Veps särpta and Votic särpiä.

From Proto-Finnic *säünä-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *säwnä. Derived with various suffixes since; säyne contains -e. Cognates include Estonian säinas, Northern Sami seavnnját, Moksha сеня (senä) and Hungarian őn.
From Proto-Finnic *sää (compare Karelian seä, siä, šiä, Veps sä, Votic sää), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *säŋe (“air”) (compare Hungarian ég (“sky”) and Komi-Zyrian сынӧд (synöd, “warm air”)).
From Proto-Finnic *sää.
From Proto-Finnic *säksi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śäkće ~ *śäkśe.

parole.significato: shank (lower part of the leg); shin and calf
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sääri, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćäŋäre.
From Proto-Finnic *säski (compare Estonian sääsk, Veps säsk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ćëćke ~ *ćäćke (compare Northern Sami čuoika, Erzya сеське (seśke), Moksha сяське (säśke)).

parole.significato: to save, spare (conserve or prevent the wasting of; of resources like money or electricity)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *säästädäk. Related to Karelian seästeä, Livvi siästiä and Ludian šiästädä.
From Proto-Finnic *säätädäk (compare Estonian seadma, Livonian sǟdõ, Veps säta), equivalent to sää (“fiber, thread, strand”) (obsolete) + -tää (compare säie).

parole.significato: this, that (medial between tämä and tuo)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taa, from Proto-Uralic *ta.
From Proto-Finnic *takja (compare Karelian toakie and also Northern Sami dávjá), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian tankus).

parole.significato: burden (heavy load; (figuratively) cause of worry, anxiety, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taakka, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᛏᚨᚲᚲᚨᛉ (*stakkaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *stakkaz (compare Old Norse stakkr (“hay stack, heap”)). Doublet of takka.

parole.significato: kvass, cereal-based beer with relatively low alcohol content
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taari.

parole.significato: great fen-sedge, saw-sedge, swamp sawgrass (Cladium mariscus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarna, ultimately a borrowing from Indo-Iranian (and a distant cognate with English thorn).
From Proto-Finnic *tadëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tadą (compare Old Norse tað, Icelandic tað, dialectal Swedish tad), further derived + -e.

parole.significato: paste, dough (mix of dry substance and liquid that is soft and moist but not thin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tahtas (compare Veps tahtaz), borrowed from an Indo-European language (probably Proto-Balto-Slavic *taištas; compare Proto-Slavic *těsto, Proto-Celtic *taisto-).
From Proto-Finnic *tahkëda.

parole.significato: grindstone (abrasive wheel for sharpening, polishing or grinding)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tahko (compare Estonian tahk, Ingrian tahko, Veps tahk), from Proto-Finno-Permic *taškɜ ~ *tašɜ ~ *tuškɜ (compare Komi-Zyrian тыш (tyš), Udmurt тыш (tyš), Eastern Mari тош (toš)), perhaps of substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *tahma.

parole.significato: authority, organization, institution; any group of humans or human institution (exact type depends on the context)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taho, possibly a variant of tahko.

parole.significato: will (one's independent faculty of choice; intention or decision; conscious intent or volition)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tahto, equivalent to tahtoa (“to want”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *tahtoidak.

parole.significato: magic (use of supernatural rituals, forces etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taika, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *taikną.

parole.significato: dough, pastry (mix of flour and other ingredients)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taikina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?], from *daigaz (“dough”).

From Proto-Finnic *taimën, an extension of Proto-Finnic *taimi (“trout, salmon”). Cognates include Karelian taimen and Estonian taim. Russian тайме́нь (tajménʹ), Latvian taimiņš and dialectal Swedish tajmenlax are borrowed from Finnic. Similar-sounding words include taima (“ceiling joist”) or taimi

parole.significato: sapling (young tree, taller than a seedling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taimi.

parole.significato: a large fish-trap made of wire or sticks, meant to be placed in a flowing body of water with the mouth facing upstream
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tainijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tainijǭ.

parole.significato: to bend, flex, bow, become bent or curved
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taipudak (cognate with Estonian taibuma and Karelian taipuo). Equivalent to *tai- + -pua, from the same root as taittaa (“to fold”). * ((grammar) to inflect): See taivuttaa.

parole.significato: to probably do, think that one does [with first infinitive] (active past participle: tainnut or taitanut)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taitadak (“to know (how to)”).

parole.significato: skill (capacity to do something well, particularly one that is acquired or learned)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taito (compare Võro taid (“sense, reason, grasp, intelligence”)). Equivalent to taitaa (“to know, master, command”) + -o. Cognate with Northern Sami dáidu (“skill”).

From Proto-Finnic *taibal (compare Karelian taival, taipaleh, Ludian taibal, taibaleh; compare also Estonian Taebla, a place name), probably cognate with Proto-Samic *tuojpëlē (whence obsolete Skolt Sami tuibal (“area between lakes, etc.”) (*tuuibâl) and several place names like Northern Sami Duoiba
From Proto-Finnic *taivas (compare Estonian taevas), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *daywás.
From Proto-Finnic *taka, from Proto-Uralic *taka.
From Proto-Finnic *takaicin. Equivalent to taka- (“rear, backside”) + -isin (temporal distributive plural). Sense 2 possibly a semantic loan from Swedish tillbaka or English back.
From Proto-Finnic *tak'ërtadak (compare Estonian takerdama).

parole.significato: tangle, frizz (mass of tightly curled hair)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *takku.

parole.significato: to forge (shape a metal by heating and hammering)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *takodak.

parole.significato: boat shed (simple shelter for boats, nets and other fishing gear)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talas, probably of the same origin as *taloi (which see for more).

parole.significato: hide, fleece (prepared skin of an animal, still with hair or fur)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talja, possibly borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: A traditional Russian (толокно (tolokno)) / Finnish / Estonian (kama) finely milled flour mixture made of roasted barle…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talkkuna, borrowed from Proto-Slavic *tolkъno (*talkuna) (whence Old East Slavic толокъно (tolokŭno) (with pleophony)).

parole.significato: bee, dugnad (gathering for carrying out a major task, such as harvesting, construction or cleaning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talko- (compare Estonian talgud, Karelian talloh, Veps touguh, Votic talko), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *talkōs (compare Lithuanian talka (“cooperated voluntary work”)).

parole.significato: sole (bottom or lower part of anything on which it rests)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talla, probably from the same root as tallata, with a possible secondary Germanic origin (akin to that of talla, etymology 2).
From Proto-Finnic *tallat'ak (compare Estonian tallama).

parole.significato: safe, secure (in a safe place, free from the danger of theft)
parole.testo: The inessive singular of Proto-Finnic *taltë-.

From Proto-Finnic *taltta, borrowed from Proto-Slavic *dolto (*dalta) (whence Old East Slavic долото (doloto) (with pleophony)). Cognates include Karelian tauttu, Ludian talt, Veps taut. First mentioned in a Finnish dictionary in 1787.

parole.significato: to abate, subside (decrease in force or intensity, e.g. of a storm or of anger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talttudak.

parole.significato: to lead (guide or conduct in a certain course, especially assertively; a child, dog etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taluttadak. Equivalent to talua + -ttaa (from a dialectal verb talua), from Proto-Finnic *taludak, probably from Proto-Uralic *talwa-.
From Proto-Finnic *talvi (compare Estonian talv), from Proto-Uralic *tälwä (compare Erzya теле (tele), Western Mari тел (tel), Udmurt тол (tol), Northern Mansi та̄л (tāl), Hungarian tél).

parole.significato: oak (any tree or shrub of the genus Quercus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tammi (compare Estonian tamm, Karelian tammi, Livonian täm), from Proto-Finno-Permic *tamme (compare Erzya тумо (tumo), Eastern Mari тумо (tumo)), possibly ultimately of substrate origin.

From Proto-Finnic *tanhu- (compare Estonian tänav, Ingrian tanvas, Karelian tanhut, Veps tannaz, Votic tanava (Kattila)), borrowed from Proto-Norse ᛏᚨᚾᚺᚢ- (*tanhu-), from Proto-Germanic *tanhwą (compare Old Norse tá (“path”)).
From Proto-Finnic *tankëda, from Proto-Finno-Permic *taŋketa.

parole.significato: habit (action performed on a regular basis)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tapa, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *dabāˀ (compare Latvian daba).

parole.significato: to happen, take place, occur, come about, come up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tapahtudak, possibly from tapa- (“to meet”) + -htua.

parole.significato: to fight, brawl, tussle (to contend in physical conflict; without weapons, with fists etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tap'ëldak, equivalent to tappaa (“to kill, slay”) + -ella (frequentative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *tappadak, from Proto-Uralic *tappa- (compare Erzya тапамс (tapams), Tundra Nenets тӑпӑрць (tăpărcʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *tappaja. Equivalent to tappaa (“to kill”) + -ja (“-er”).
From Proto-Finnic *tappo, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].

From Proto-Finnic *taristak. Ultimately from an onomatopoeic root + -ista. The sense is probably in part inspired by tarina, which has sometimes been considered a derivative of tarista, although a Russian origin is more likely.
From Proto-Finnic *tarit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tarjaną. Related to Karelian tarita, Ludian tarita and Veps tarita.

parole.significato: to (be able to) withstand the cold, be warm enough (in order not to shiver with cold)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarkëdak + -eta (compare Estonian targema, Ingrian tareta), from Proto-Uralic *tarke- (“to shiver, tremble”).
From Proto-Finnic *tarkëda. Doublet of tärkeä.
From Proto-Finnic *tarkka. Related to Estonian tark, Veps tark and Votic tarkkõ. Possibly also related to Erzya тарка (tarka, “place”).

parole.significato: to wade (to walk through something that impedes progress, especially snow or marsh)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarpodak. Cognates include Karelian tarpuo, Livvi tarbua, Veps tarboda and Votic tarpoa (Mati).

From Proto-Finnic *tarttudak. Related to Ingrian tarttua, Karelian tarttuo, Livvi tartuo, Ludian tartuda, Veps tartuda and Votic tarttua. * (to be transmitted, be contagious): Also found in some other Finnic languages. Likely an autochthonous semantic shift from “to stick, cling, adhere”. For a simi

parole.significato: The meaning of this term is uncertain. Possibilities include:
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarvas, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *taurás, from Proto-Indo-European *táwros. Doublet of Taurus, teuras, and torvi.
From Proto-Finnic *tarbëh, nativized form of tarvis. Cognate with Ingrian tarve, Estonian tarve.
From Proto-Finnic *tarbis, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þarbaz, *þarbiz, *þarbijaz (“needed, useful”). Cognate with Ingrian tarvis, Estonian tarvis.

parole.significato: even, equal, equi-, homo-, flat, uniform
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tasa, possibly from Proto-Uralic *taśa.

parole.significato: flat, even (having no variations in height)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tasainën. Equivalent to tasa (“flat”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *tatti, further origin unknown. Related to Estonian tatt (“snot, slime”). Originally "slime", then "slimy mushroom" and "bolete".
From Proto-Finnic *tauko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *taugō.

parole.significato: amadou; fine-grained tinder made from a polypore of species Fomes fomentarius
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *takla (compare Estonian tael, Karelian takla, Votic taglõ), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian dagla, Lithuanian deglis).
From Proto-Finnic *taugot'ak. Related to Ingrian tavveta (“to die”), Votic taugõtõ (“to end, to die”) and also to Northern Sami duovgut and possibly Udmurt дугдыны (dugdyny).

parole.significato: disease (abnormal condition of the body causing discomfort or dysfunction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tauti, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*dauđi) (cf. Proto-Germanic *dauþuz). Cognates include Estonian taud (“a pestilence or infectious disease”), Icelandic dauði (“death”) and Swedish död (“death”).
From Proto-Finnic *tavi. Related to Karelian tavi, Ludian tavi and Veps tavi.

parole.significato: you (second-person plural; when addressing many persons or when addressing politely or formally one person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tek, from Proto-Uralic *te. The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (tet).

parole.significato: black grouse, Lyrurus tetrix, formerly Tetrao tetrix
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tetri, possibly a Baltic loan. Cognate with Estonian teder.

parole.significato: to do, perform, execute, carry out
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tektäk (compare Estonian tegema, Veps tehta), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *teke- (compare Northern Sami dahkat, Erzya теемс (tejems), Hungarian tesz; see the Proto-Uralic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *tekejä. Equivalent to tehdä (“to do, make”) + -jä (“-er”).
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *teko. By surface analysis, teke- (“to do”) + -o. Compare teho.

parole.significato: one of the logs or other (round) pieces of wood placed under something, such as a boat or a pile of firewood, to keep i…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëla (compare Ingrian tela, Karelian tela, Veps tela), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þelą. Doublet of teli.
From Proto-Finnic *tëljo, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *þeljǭ (later Proto-Germanic *þiljǭ). Compare Karelian tel’l’o.

parole.significato: bolt (bar to prevent a door from being forced open; sliding pin or bar in a lock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *telki, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *telgô.

parole.significato: to snatch, grab, jerk, pull, tear, yank
