parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëmbait'ak (compare Karelian temmata, Ingrian temmata, Votic tõmmõtõ, Estonian tõmbama, Ludian tembaita, Veps tembaita), likely borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian tempt, Lithuanian tempti).
From Proto-Finnic *tëmppu. Related to Estonian temp, Ingrian temppu, Livonian temp and Votic temppu. Possibly derived from temmata.
From Proto-Finnic *tenho.
From Proto-Finnic *tërho. Cognates include Estonian tõru, Livonian tõ’rmõz and Votic doro.
From Proto-Finnic *terni, possibly borrowed from early Proto-Indo-Iranian *térunos (later *tárunas).

parole.significato: a piece of pine wood which is more resinous than average
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tërvas. Equivalent to terva (“tar”) + -s.
From Proto-Finnic *tërvat'ak. Equivalent to terva (“tar”) + -ta.

parole.significato: healthy, sane (enjoying health and vigor of body, mind, or spirit)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *terveh, with a root probably borrowed from Indo-Iranian (compare Avestan 𐬛𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬎𐬎𐬁 (dərəuuā, “healthy”)).
From Proto-Finnic *tervehüc. Equivalent to terve (“healthy”) + -ys (“-ness”).
From Proto-Finnic *terä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *terä.
From Proto-Finnic *teräs, equivalent to terä (“blade”) + -s, after its usage in tools.

parole.significato: sharp (able to cut or pierce easily)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *teräbä. Equivalent to terä (“blade, edge”) + -vä (adjective-forming suffix).

parole.significato: An animal to be slaughtered; an animal for slaughter.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëpras (compare Estonian tõbras), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þeuraz (“bull”), from Proto-Indo-European *táwros; originally meant "bull". Doublet of Taurus, tarvas, and torvi.
From Proto-Finnic *tee, from Proto-Finno-Permic *teje.

parole.significato: knowledge (fact of knowing about something; awareness)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *teeto. Equivalent to tietää (“to know”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *teetäjä, equivalent to tietää (“to know”) + -jä; ; compare Karelian tietäjä (“wizard”).
From Proto-Finnic *teetämät'oin, equivalent to tietää (“to know”) + -mätön (negative participle).

parole.significato: to know [with elative ‘about’], be aware of (in some cases implying superficial knowledge, see the usage notes below)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *teetädäk, derived from *tee (whence tie (“road, way”)). Equivalent to tie (“road, way”) + -tää; the original meaning seems to have been “to know the way to” (thus tiedän talon (“I know the way to the house”)) or “to lead to the way to”.
From Proto-Finnic *tihedä. Cognate with Estonian tihe, Ingrian tihhiiä, Veps tihed.
From Proto-Finnic *tiineh, from an Indo-European language (probably Balto-Slavic, compare Lithuanian dieni (“pregnant”) and Sanskrit धेनु (dhenu)).

parole.significato: tern (bird in the subfamily Terninae of family Laridae - gulls and terns)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tiira, of onomatopoeic origin.

From Proto-Finnic *tikka, probably of recent imitative origin. Related to Estonian tikk, Ingrian tikka, Livvi tikku, Veps tik and Votic tikkõ. The sense “dart” is likely by analogy with the sharp, pointed beak of a woodpecker.
From Proto-Finnic *tik'uttadak.

parole.significato: dribble, dash, drop (small amount of liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tilkka. Cognates include Estonian tilk, Ingrian tilkka, Karelian tilkka, Livonian tīlka, Ludian ťilk, Veps tilk and Votic tilkkõ.
From Proto-Finnic *tina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tiną (“tin”).

parole.significato: drop (small quantity of liquid, just enough to hold its round shape)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tippa (compare Ingrian tippa, Veps tipp).

parole.significato: to drip (fall one drop at a time)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tippudak, equivalent to tippa (“drop”) + -ua.

parole.significato: chick, chicken (very young chick of hen, when still yellow with its natal down)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tipu, variant of *tipa, itself probably originally an interjection used to attract a hen or chicken.
From Proto-Finnic *tiristäk, from an onomatopoeic root; tir- + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *tiuhta (whence also Estonian tihv), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *stiftaz (whence German Stift).

parole.significato: A small dam, usually made of logs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *togëh, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *takis, compare Lithuanian takišys, Latvian tacis.
From Proto-Finnic *tohlo.

parole.significato: can bring oneself (to do), to dare ((to) do), venture (to do), have the nerve (to do)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tohtidak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *tošte-.
From Proto-Finnic *too. -i is probably from the plural form noi.
From Proto-Finnic *toimi. Cognate with Estonian toim.

parole.significato: second (after the first in a sequence)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toinën. Equivalent to tuo (“that”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *toipudak. Cognate with Estonian toibuma.
From Proto-Finnic *toivo. Equivalent to toivoa (“to hope”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *toivodak.
From Proto-Finnic *toivottadak. Equivalent to toivoa (“to hope, wish”) + -ttaa.
From Proto-Finnic *tok'at'ak.

parole.significato: a track or trail, especially a skiing track
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tola. Cognate with Proto-Samic *toalē.
From Proto-Finnic *tolma, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian dulkti).
From Proto-Finnic *tolmu. Equivalent to tolma + -u (see tolma for more).

parole.significato: dust (very fine particles of a solid substance)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tomu. Related to Estonian tomu, Ingrian tomu, Ludian tomu and Veps tomu.
From Proto-Finnic *tora, from Proto-Uralic *tora. Cognates include Erzya тюрема (ťurema, “fight, war”).

parole.significato: to repel (an attack), repulse, fend off, ward off, defend from, parry, foil (an attack)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *torjudak. Related to Estonian tõrjuma.
From Proto-Finnic *torudak, equivalent to tora + -ua.

parole.significato: horn (any of several musical wind instruments, especially one used to signal people or animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *torvi (compare Estonian tõri, Karelian torvi, Veps torv), from earlier *towre (with metathesis *wr > *rw, compare järvi, karva), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian taure (“bugle”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *táwros. Doublet of Taurus, tarvas, and teuras
From Proto-Finnic *toci (compare Estonian tõsi), from Proto-Uralic *čoďe (compare Eastern Khanty [script needed] (čăjǝ), Northern Mansi [script needed] (sōĺ)).
From Proto-Finnic *totku.

parole.significato: to get used to, become accustomed to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tottudak. Related to Karelian tottuo, Livvi tottuo and Votic tõttua. Equivalent to tot(e)- (“true”) + -tua.

parole.significato: larva, grub (distinct juvenile form of many animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toukka, of unknown further origin. Cognates include Ingrian toukka, Karelian toukka, toukku, Ludian touk, Estonian tõuk.
From Proto-Finnic *touko (compare Estonian tõug), probably from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *tuhandënci. Equivalent to tuhat (“thousand”) + -s (“-th”).
From Proto-Finnic *tuhat, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *tū́ˀsantis (compare Lithuanian tūkstantis), from Proto-Indo-European *tuHsont-.
From Proto-Finnic *tuhistak, from an onomatopoeic root + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *tuhka, likely borrowed from Proto-Germanic *tuska-, *tuskijaną (“to torch, to burn”). Cognate of Estonian tuhk.

From Proto-Finnic *tuho, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *tukšɜ-. Cognates include Ingrian tuho, Votic tuho, Veps tuho, Veps tuhoze (“astray”, adverb) and possibly Udmurt [script needed] (tiš, “bloody battle”).
From Proto-Finnic *tuima, of unknown further origin. Cognate with Karelian tuima (“tasteless”), Votic tuimõ (“tasteless”); Estonian tuim (“dull, limp”), Livonian tūima (“dull, limp, slow”).

parole.significato: snow blowing or falling in the wind; snowstorm, blizzard
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuisku.

parole.significato: to snow heavily with wind, to blizzard
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuiskut'ak, equivalent to tuisku- (“heavy snowfall with wind, blizzard”) + -ta.
From Proto-Finnic *tuju.
From Proto-Finnic *tukëdak, a denominal verb of tuki (“support, prop”).

parole.significato: sturdy, solid, robust, substantial, stout, hefty
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tukëba, equivalent to tukea (“to support”) + -va.

parole.significato: support, strut, prop, crutch, brace, rest (something which supports physically)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuki, of unknown further origin. Cognate to Estonian tugi, Ingrian tuki, Karelian tuki, Veps tugi, Votic tugõ (Mati), and Livonian ti’g.

parole.significato: hair (cover of hair on a human head); head of hair
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tukka, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *čukka.
From Proto-Finnic *tukku.

From Proto-Finnic *tuli (compare Estonian tuli), from Proto-Uralic *tule (compare Northern Sami dolla, Moksha тол (tol), Eastern Mari тул (tul), Udmurt тыл (tyl), Tundra Nenets ту (tu)). tuli has previously been typical of Eastern Finnish, whereas Western Finnish dialects usually used valkea.
From Proto-Finnic *tulëja. Equivalent to tulla (“to come”) + -ja.
From Proto-Finnic *tulinën. Equivalent to tuli (“fire”) + -inen.

From Proto-Finnic *tuldak (compare Estonian tulema), from Proto-Uralic *tule- (compare Eastern Mari толаш (tolaš), Tundra Nenets тось (tosʹ°)). * (emphatic future tense marker, auxiliary): Likely Swedish influence, after Swedish komma (att) and bli. * (to cum, orgasm): Probably a semantic loan from
From Proto-Finnic *tulo, equivalent to tulla (“to come”) + -o (noun suffix). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: plug (any piece of wood, metal, or other substance used to stop or fill a hole)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tulppa, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*stulpā), from Proto-Germanic *stulpô. Doublet of tolppa.

parole.significato: flint, steel, and tinder (contents of a tinderbox)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tulus, equivalent to tuli (“fire”) + -us.

parole.significato: flood (overflow of a large amount of water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tulva (cognate with Karelian tulva), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *tulwa (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: nucleus, cell nucleus (large organelle found in cells which contains genetic material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuma.
From Proto-Finnic *tumma. Cognates include Estonian tõmmu, Estonian tume, Ingrian tumma, Karelian tumma, Võro tummõ and Votic tummõ.
From Proto-Finnic *tunkëdak.
From Proto-Finnic *tunkijo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dungijǭ.
From Proto-Finnic *tuntëdak (compare Estonian tundma), from Proto-Uralic *tumte- (compare Northern Sami dovdat, Komi-Zyrian тӧдны (tödny), Hungarian tud, Tundra Nenets тумдӑсь (tumdăsʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *tuntëmat'oin, equivalent to tuntea (“to know, be familiar with”) + -maton (negative participle). Formally almost equivalent to Tundra Nenets тумдувдавэй (tumduwdawey°)).
From Proto-Finnic *tuntudak, equivalent to tuntea (“to feel”) + -ua (passive verb).

parole.significato: that (over there) (compare se, see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *too, from Proto-Uralic *to (compare Erzya тона (tona), Hungarian tova). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but only once in all of Agricola's works (for comparison, tämä is attested nearly two thousand times and se over ten thousand times).

parole.significato: to bring, fetch, get (transport toward somebody/somewhere)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toodak (compare Estonian tooma), from Proto-Uralic *toxe- (compare Erzya туемс (tujems), Northern Khanty [script needed] (tu-)); see it for more.
From Proto-Finnic *toohi (compare Estonian toht, Ingrian toohi), borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian tāss).
From Proto-Finnic *toohus, equivalent to tuohi (“birchbark”) + -us.

parole.significato: bird cherry, hackberry, hagberry, Prunus padus (tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toomi (compare Estonian toom), from Proto-Uralic *ďëme (compare Northern Sami duopma, Erzya лём (ľom), Eastern Mari ломбо (lombo), Komi-Zyrian льӧм (ľöm), Northern Mansi ля̄м (lâ̄m), Kamassian лем (lem)).

parole.significato: to sentence, condemn (declare a sentence on a convicted person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toomit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *dōmijaną (“to judge”), compare Swedish döma (“to sentence, to judge”) and Old High German tuomen (“to judge”).
From Proto-Finnic *tooni, borrowed from pre-Germanic (compare later Proto-Germanic *dawīni-, Old Norse dán (“death”), whence modern Swedish dån).
From Proto-Finnic *toorëh, borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian dõras (“good”)).

parole.significato: synonym of tukehtua (“to suffocate, choke, asphyxiate”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tup'ëhtudak, variant of typehtyä.
From Proto-Finnic *tuppi (compare Estonian tupp), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *duppaz (“hollow”).

parole.significato: fur (hairy coat of various mammal species)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turkki. Related to Ingrian turkki, Karelian turkki and Votic turkki.

parole.significato: muzzle (protruding part of an ungulate's head)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turpa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *turpa. Cognates include Erzya турва (turva, “lip”), Moksha търва (tərva, “lip”), Western Mari тӱрвӧ (türvö, “lip”), Udmurt тырпы (tyrpy, “lip”), and Komi-Permyak тырп (tyrp, “lip”).

parole.significato: European chub, chub, common chub, Squalius cephalus (syn. Leuciscus cephalus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turpa, possibly the same as turpa (etymology 1), but this is uncertain due to the distributions of the two words not lining up.
From Proto-Finnic *turpëda, from turp- + -ea, from the same root as turvota (“to bloat, swell”). Related to Ingrian turpia.
From Proto-Finnic *turska (compare Estonian tursk), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þurskaz (“cod”).

parole.significato: to extrude, gush or flow over (to push or thrust out due to excess quantity)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tursudak. Probably ultimately sound-symbolic, compare turskua, pursua.

parole.significato: numb, insensitive, asleep, deadened, insensible, dull (physically unable to feel)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turta (compare Estonian turd, Ingrian turra, Livonian turdõ).

parole.significato: protection, safety, security (condition or feeling of being safe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turva (compare Estonian turv, Ingrian turva, Karelian turva, Livvi turvu, Veps turvane and Votic turvõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *trūwō (compare Swedish tro).

parole.significato: peat, turf (soil formed of dead but not fully decayed plants found in bog areas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turbëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *turbz, whence also English turf. Finnic cognates include Estonian turvas, Ingrian turve, Karelian turveh, Livonian dūrbal, Livvi turveh, Ludian turbiž, turbeh, Veps turbiž, turbaz, turbez, Võro turbas and Votic turvaz (Kattila).

parole.significato: to swell (become bigger, especially due to being engorged)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turbot'ak. Equivalent to turpe- (“swollen, bloated”) + -ota. Related to Estonian turbuma, Karelian turvota, Veps turbota, Votic turpossõ and possibly also Erzya тороземс (torozems).
From Proto-Finnic *tussu, probably sound-symbolic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *tutidak.
From Proto-Finnic *tudistak, ultimately sound-symbolic; compare Estonian tudisema, Karelian tutissa, Ludian dudišta, Veps dudaita.

parole.significato: goad, prick (long, pointed stick used to prod animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tutkain. Equivalent to tutka- + -in (from the same root tutka- as tutkia; see it for more).

parole.significato: acquaintance (person with whom one is acquainted)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuttaba. Equivalent to the present passive participle of the archaic verb tuta (“to feel”) (the consonant stem of tuntea).
From Proto-Finnic *tuulas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian dūlājs, Lithuanian dūlis).

From Proto-Finnic *tuuli (compare Estonian tuul), from Proto-Finno-Permic *towle (compare Western Mari [script needed] (tul, “storm”), Udmurt тӧл (töl, “wind”), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (tol, “cloud”)).

parole.significato: windy, breezy (e.g. of weather or a place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuulinën. Equivalent to tuuli (“wind”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *tuulicpää. Equivalent to tuulis- (“windy”) + pää (“head”).
From Proto-Finnic *tuuldak, a denominal verb of tuuli (“wind”).

parole.significato: to winnow (separate grain from the chaff with air either by letting wind blow the chaff away or throwing the unwinnowed…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuultadak, equivalent to tuuli (“wind”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *tuultudak, equivalent to tuuli (“wind”) + -tua.

parole.significato: ice chisel; a tool for breaking ice, consisting of a heavy chisel-like iron head which is attached to a long wooden han…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuura (compare Estonian tuur, Ingrian tuura, Võro tuur, Votic tuurõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian durà).
From Proto-Finnic *tuutu, possibly equivalent to tuutua + -u
From Proto-Finnic *tutudak, from baby or children's talk.
From Proto-Finnic *tühjä (compare Estonian tühi), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tuskjas (compare Lithuanian tuščias (“empty”), Latvian tukšs (“empty, blank”)).

parole.significato: blunt (having a thick edge or point, as an instrument)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tülppä (compare Estonian tülp, Ingrian tylppä, Karelian tylppä, tylpäkkä, Livonian tilp, Veps tülpäk, Votic tülppe).
From Proto-Finnic *tülc(c)ä (compare dialectal Estonian tülts, Ingrian tyltsä, Karelian tylttšä, Livonian tȭlza, Veps tšültš).
From Proto-Finnic *tülü, equivalent to tyl- + -y; probably from the stem of dialectal tylkeä, with analogous levelling of the weak grade (-lk- > -l-).
From Proto-Finnic *tümä, from Proto-Uralic *ďümä. Displaced by the borrowed liima.

parole.significato: stub, stump (something blunted, stunted, or cut short; short piece of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tünkä, derived from *tüŋe (whence Proto-Finnic *tüvi) at a Pre-Finnic stage.

parole.significato: synonym of tukehtua (“to suffocate, choke, asphyxiate”)
parole.testo: From dialectal typpiä, through type- + -htyä. Further from Proto-Finnic *tüppidäk (compare Karelian typpie, Ludian tüppida, Veps ťüp), and further probably related to Northern Sami dahppat, dohpat.

According to Aikio (2024), from Proto-Finnic *tüperä, cognate with Proto-Samic *tëpër, whence Lule Sami dabár (“prattle, nonsense”). Alternatively, possibly from the same root as tupertua. Cognate with Karelian typerä.
From Proto-Finnic *türä.
From Proto-Finnic *tüssät'äk.
From Proto-Finnic *tüttoi, equivalent to tyttä- + -ö; an affective derivation of tytär (“daughter”) (see it for more).
From Proto-Finnic *tüt'är, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *duktē (compare Lithuanian duktė). Erzya тейтерь (tejteŕ) may be borrowed from the same source.
From Proto-Finnic *tüven.

parole.significato: foot (lowest part of a longish object, e.g. a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tüvi (compare Estonian tüvi), from Proto-Uralic *tüŋe (compare Eastern Mari тӱҥ (tüŋ), Hungarian tő).
From Proto-Finnic *tüüni, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tiwä (compare Northern Khanty тевән (tjewən)). Compare also syvä (< *tiwä).
From Proto-Finnic *tiüris (compare Finnish dialectal tiyris), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *diurijaz.
From Proto-Finnic *tü(ü)tüdäk. Related to Estonian tüdima, tüütama, Karelian tyytyö and Votic tüütüttää (Rudja).

parole.significato: work, toil, effort, labour (effort expended on a particular task)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *töö (compare Estonian töö, Livonian tīe, Votic tüü), from Proto-Finno-Permic *tewe (compare Erzya тев (tev)).
From Proto-Finnic *töö, variant of *tek.
From Proto-Finnic *tööntädäk (compare Karelian työntyä, Livvi työndiä, Veps töntta, Võro tüünämä).

parole.significato: leftover, leavings, residue (whatever remains when something - usually the useful part - has been removed; food left ov…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täkteh, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *täktä (whence Proto-Samic *tāktē).

parole.significato: ear (fruiting body of a grain plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tähkä, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *teškä ~ *tekšä ~ *täškä (compare Erzya тикше (tikše, “grass”), Komi-Permyak тош (toš), Udmurt туш (tuš)), perhaps of substrate origin.
From Proto-Finnic *tähti, from Proto-Finno-Permic *täštä. Cognate to Karelian tähti, Estonian täht and Erzya теште (tešte). Sense 4 is a semantic loan from English star.

From Proto-Finnic *tähtüstädäk, equivalent to tähti + -ystää (based on the dialectal sense “mark, spot” of tähti); originally an eastern/northern dialectal verb, hence no -d-. Cognate with Estonian tähistama and Võro tähüstämä.
From Proto-Finnic *täi (compare Estonian täi), from Proto-Uralic *täje (compare Eastern Mari ти (ti), Komi-Permyak той (toj), Udmurt тэй (tej), Hungarian tetű).

parole.significato: local, from this area or region
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täkäläinen. Cognates include Ingrian täkäläin, Karelian täkäläine, Veps tägalaine and Votic täčäläin. Morphologically tä- + -käläinen.
From Proto-Finnic *tämä, from Proto-Uralic *tä. The nominative and singular genitive forms, which would have otherwise been monosyllabic, have been extended with *-mä.
From Proto-Finnic *täplä.

parole.significato: close, narrow, short (having a small margin)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täpärä.

parole.significato: to shake, shiver, vibrate, tremble (move a relatively small distance from side to side)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täristäk, from an onomatopoeic root + -istä.
From Proto-Finnic *tärkedä. Doublet of tarkea.
From Proto-Finnic *täti (compare Estonian tädi, Veps täti), ultimately probably from baby talk. Possibly already in Proto-Finno-Permic *tätä (compare Moksha тядя (tädä, “mother”)).
From Proto-Finnic *tävü, from Proto-Uralic *täwe(w). Cognates include Erzya тевеляв (teveľav). Displaced by keuhko.

From Proto-Finnic *täüci (compare Estonian täis), from Proto-Uralic *täwde (compare Northern Sami dievas, Eastern Mari тич (tič), Eastern Khanty тӓԓә (täłə), Hungarian tele, Tundra Nenets тер (tyer°)).

parole.significato: to fill, fill up, fill in (make full)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täüttädäk; equivalent to täysi (“full”) + -tää. * (to turn (a certain age)): Compare Swedish fylla, perhaps a semantic loan.

From Proto-Finnic *täütüdäk, equivalent to täyt- (“full”) + -yä. Related to Ingrian täytyä and Karelian täytyö. The original meanings are "to fill up; be filled" and (from the former) "to suffice, be enough". It is not entirely clear how the current sense indicating obligation developed from these t

parole.significato: stump, stub (remains of something that has been cut off; especially the remains of a shortened tail)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *töpoi, ultimately sound-symbolic. Variant of töppö.
From Proto-Finnic *törk'ät'äk.

parole.significato: A steep embankment of earth; a long mound; a berm.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *termä. Cognate with Karelian termä and Proto-Samic *tearmē.
Fronted from dialectal toukata, from Proto-Finnic *touk'at'ak.

parole.significato: bank, embankment (relatively small edge of a river or another body of water)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Finnic *teüräs (no cognates), if borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old English þéor (“swelling, protuberance”)).

parole.significato: to ask questions about, fish for information, pry
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *udëldak. Probably related to Proto-Samic *ocëtēk, implying earlier *uče-.

parole.significato: threat, menace (person or object that is regarded as a danger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uhka. Cognates include Estonian uhal (adverb), Ingrian uhka and Karelian uhka.
From Proto-Finnic *uhkëda, from *uhka. Related to Estonian uhke and Ingrian uhkia.
From Proto-Finnic *uhku, possibly a derivation of *uhka (compare Estonian uhkama (“water or slush on top of ice”)).
From Proto-Finnic *uhma, possibly sound-symbolic; compare uhka, uho, Ingrian uhmata, Karelian uhmoa and dialectal Estonian uhmata (“to struggle”).

parole.significato: to swim (move through water without touching the bottom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uidak, from Proto-Uralic *o(w)je- ~ *uje-. Cognate to Estonian ujuma, Ter Sami vɨjjed, Erzya уемс (ujems) and Hungarian úszik.
From Proto-Finnic *uinudak.
From Proto-Finnic *uiskoi, probably uida (“to swim”) + -sko.

parole.significato: to drift, glide, float, flow (e.g. on water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ujudak. Cognate with Estonian ujuma (“to swim”). Analyzable as ui- + -ua.
From Proto-Finnic *ukko. Probably a Finnic pet form of uros (“man, male”).
From Proto-Finnic *uksi, probably borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian uoksas (“hole”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ulko (compare Estonian ulgu-), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ulka (compare Northern Sami olgu, Komi-Zyrian ылö (ylö, “far”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ulvodak. Cognates include Estonian uluma, Ingrian ulvoa, Livvi ulvuo, Veps uuvata and Votic ulvoa. Likely related to Proto-Samic *(h)olvōtēk.

From Proto-Finnic *umpi, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *umbi (“around, about, by, near”), which was perhaps already borrowed into Proto-Finno-Saamic (compare Northern Sami oppa (“whole; quite a”)).
From Proto-Finnic *uni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *une. Cognates include Erzya он (on), Western Mari ом (om).
From Proto-Finnic *uninën, equivalent to uni (“sleep, dream”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *unohtadak.
From Proto-Finnic *upëda, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare German üppig). No cognates in other Finnic languages are known.
From Proto-Finnic *up'ot'ak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *uppa (“suffocating”). If so, related to Erzya and Moksha опа (opa, “warm, hot, stuffy, suffocating”).
From Proto-Finnic *up'ottadak, equivalent to upota (“to sink”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: track, groove, rut, trail, furrow (mark in the form of a groove or long, narrow depression left by something that has p…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ura, from Proto-Finno-Permic *ura. Related to Karelian ura, Udmurt [script needed] (i̮ri̮-). * (career): A semantic loan from some other European language, compare French carrière (“racecourse, career”), from Medieval Latin carrāria (“path for carts”).
From Proto-Finnic [Term?], from the same origin as *uros.
From Proto-Finnic *uristak, of onomatopoeic root (compare Erzya урномс (urnoms, “to wail, howl”)) + -ista.
From Proto-Finnic *urgët'ak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *urke-. Cognates include Livonian urgõ and Erzya оргодемс (orgodems).
From Proto-Finnic *uros, of disputed further origin.
From Proto-Finnic *usëda. Cognates include Ingrian ussia, Karelian usie and Votic ussa.

parole.significato: to dare ((to) do), venture (to do), have the courage (to do), be bold/brave enough (to do)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uskaltadak, equivalent to uskoa (“to believe”) + -altaa.
From Proto-Finnic *usko, equivalent to uskoa (“to believe, have faith”) + -o

parole.significato: to believe, have faith [with illative ‘in’] (someone's abilities, chances etc.; someone's existence; the power, value e…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uskodak, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wunskijaną.

From Proto-Finnic *udar (compare Estonian udar (“udder”), Livvi udareh (“udder”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *utare (compare Erzya одар (odar, “udder”)), borrowed from an Indo-Iranian language (compare Sanskrit ऊधर् (ūdhar)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ówHdʰr̥ (“udder”).

parole.significato: haze, mist (very fine particles of water vapor in the air slightly limiting visibility)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *utu (compare Estonian udu), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic úði (“drizzle”)).
From Proto-Finnic *uudin, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *owdeme. Related to Eastern Khanty ө̆ԓәп (ø̆łəp) and Eastern Mansi амыл (amyl). Mostly displaced by verho.

parole.significato: ewe, especially one that has lambed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uuhi (compare Karelian uuhi, Veps uhu).

parole.significato: furrow, line (deep wrinkle, such as in the skin of the face, especially on someone's forehead)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uurdëk. Equivalent to uurtaa (“to groove, furrow”) + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *uurtadak, probably derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *owre (“groove”).

From Proto-Finnic *uuci (compare Estonian uus), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wuďe (compare Northern Sami ođas, Erzya and Moksha од (od), Eastern Mari and Western Mari у (u), Komi-Zyrian выль (vyľ), Hungarian új). The vowel was irregularly lengthened possibly as a result of the lost initial *w-.
From Proto-Finnic *ubëh. Cognate with Ingrian uve, Karelian uveh, Livvi uveh, Ludian ubeh and Veps ubeh.

parole.significato: maple (any tree of the genus Acer)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vahtëra, from Proto-Finno-Permic [Term?]. Cognate with Estonian vaher, Ingrian vaaher, Karelian voahteri, Livonian vǭ’dõr, Veps vahtaŕ, Votic vaahtõrõ, Erzya укштор (ukštor), Moksha уштор (uštor) and Eastern Mari ваштар (vaštar).

parole.significato: a giant bird similar to a griffin
parole.testo: vaaka- + lintu, probably from dialectal vaa’as, from Proto-Finnic *vaagas and not related to vaaka
From Proto-Finnic *vaakkudak, of onomatopoeic origin.

parole.significato: Finnish span (distance between the thumb and the index finger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vaksa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *waksa. Cognates include Erzya вакс (vaks).

parole.significato: light, pale (of a shade of colour)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *va(a)lëda (compare Ingrian vaalia, dialectal valea). Probably akin to valkea.

From Proto-Finnic *vapsa-, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vapsva and Old Prussian wobse). Cognate with Estonian vapsik, Karelian voapsahaine, Livonian vaps, Veps bapshaine and Votic vaapsõlain.

From vaap(a)- + -ukka, a blend of Proto-Finnic *vabarna with vatukka. Related to Ingrian vaapukka, Votic baabukõz and dialectal Estonian vaabaka. The long -aa- is probably by analogy with juolukka (< *joolukka), as well as possibly *vaarma (see vaarain).

parole.significato: tenon (projecting member used to connect e.g. wooden parts together)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varna.
From Proto-Finnic *vaarudak.

First attested as faderma in 1637 (Schroderus; modern spelling vaderma, which is itself attested later); -lm- is first attested (as fadelma) in 1786 (Ganander) and could be by influence from words like hedelmä as well as the metathesis valerma > varelma. The -e- is likely secondary, as the word, thr

parole.significato: to wander, roam, travel, trek, ramble; to hike
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajëltadak (compare Karelian vajeltua, Votic vajõlta, Võro vaeldama), probably derived from *vajëh (from which vaihtaa (“to change”) was also derived; thus this word may have originally meant “to change” as well, shifting → “to change one's location” → “to wander, roam”).
Possibly related to Estonian -va seen in some place names, in which case from Proto-Finnic.

parole.significato: accident, mishap (something negative done unintentionally; event caused by human activity with unintentional negative c…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vahinko. Related to Ingrian vahinko, Karelian vahinko, Ludian vahinko and Votic vahinko.

parole.significato: strong, powerful (capable of exerting or withstanding great physical force; possessing power, might, or strength)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vahva (compare Estonian vahva).

parole.significato: Any mushroom in the genus Cantharellus
parole.testo: vahv- + -ero, from Proto-Finnic *vahvoi.

parole.significato: or (exclusive or; either what comes before or what comes after)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vai. Probably ultimately from the same root as vajaa, possibly by analogy with tai.

vai(k)- + -eta, from Proto-Finnic *vaikka (“quiet”), probably a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *waikwaz. Cognate with Ingrian vaiketa as well as adjectival Estonian vaikne, Livvi vaikkaine and adverbial Veps vaikńe.

parole.significato: phase, stage, step (distinct or distinguishable part of a sequence or process)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajëh (“gap”) (compare Estonian vahe), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *waješ.
From Proto-Finnic *va(j)ihtadak. Equivalent to vaihe (“phase, stage; (archaic) gap”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *vaikëda, probably derived from vaiva (with the adjectival suffix -kea). Cognate with Ingrian vaikia, Karelian vaigie and Votic vaikõa.
From Proto-Finnic *vaikka, possibly from *vai. Related to Ingrian vaikka, Karelian vaikka and Votic vaikkõ.
Variant of vaikko, from Proto-Finnic *vaikko (compare Estonian vaik (“resin”), Ingrian vaikko (“earwax”), Karelian vaikku (“earwax”), Votic vaikko (“resin”)).

From Proto-Finnic *vaimo (“spirit, soul”) (compare Estonian vaim (“spirit”)), possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *wajŋe (“(living) spirit”) (compare Northern Sami vuoigŋa (“breath, spirit”), Moksha вайме (vajme), Erzya ойме (ojme, “spirit, soul”), Nganasan бачуˮ (bačuʔ, “soul”)). The original sense
From Proto-Finnic *vainaga, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wainagaz, see it for more.
From Proto-Finnic *vainijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hwainiō), from Proto-Germanic *hwainō (compare English whin, Old Norse hvein and Swedish ven). Cognate with Estonian vain.
From Proto-Finnic *vaino, borrowed from Old East Slavic воина (voina, “war”) (compare Russian война́ (vojná, “war”)). Cognates include Estonian vaen.

parole.significato: scent (odour of a game animal as a trace sensed by a predator)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vainu, probably borrowed from Old East Slavic [script needed] (vonjú), accusative of [script needed] (vonja); compare Russian вонь (vonʹ, “stench, smell”).

parole.significato: diaper (US), nappy (UK), napkin (South Africa) (absorbent garment worn by a baby, or by someone who is incontinent)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vaippa (compare Estonian vaip, Votic vaippa (Kattila)), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waipaz (compare Old Norse veipa (“a kind of piece of clothing”), Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐍀𐍃 (waips, “crown, wreath”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vaipudak, equivalent to vai- + -pua, likely related to vajaa (“incomplete, not full”).
From Proto-Finnic *vaiva, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waiwō (“woe, misery, pain”).
From Proto-Finnic *vaivat'ak, equivalent to vaiva (“inconvenience; ailment”) + -ta.

parole.significato: not full; partial; incomplete (often with connotation of falling short)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajaga. Related to Estonian vaja, Ingrian vaijaa, Livonian vajāg, Veps vajag and Votic vajja. See more at vajota.

parole.significato: to sink [with illative ‘in’] (something heavier than water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajot'ak (compare Estonian vajuma, Ingrian vajota, Karelian vajota, Livonian va’jjõ, Veps vajuda and Votic vajoota (Mati)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waja- (compare Northern Sami vuodjut, Erzya and Moksha ваямс (vajäms), Udmurt выйыны (vyjyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (uj-) a

From Proto-Finnic *vaka (compare Estonian vaga (“righteous”), Ingrian vaka (“peaceful, quiet”), Livonian vagā (“calm, peaceful”)). The long vowel probably emerged as a means to ensure the strong grade in all forms, and may have been inspired by vajaa and vapaa.

parole.significato: A roundish, voluminous container equipped with a cap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vakka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vāks (“lid, cover”), Lithuanian vókas (“cover, eyelid”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vako (compare Estonian vagu), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vaga (“furrow”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vala, from Proto-Uralic *wala (compare Lule Sami vuolle, Erzya вал (val, “word”), Nganasan бәлы (bəly)).

parole.significato: to cast, mold/mould (make a cast by pouring into a mold/mould)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valadak (compare Estonian valama), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wala- ~ *wälä- (compare Moksha валомс (valoms, “to pour; to wet”), Eastern Mari велаш (velaš, “to spill”)).
Through metathesis, from Proto-Finnic *valëh (compare Estonian vale, Karelian valeh), perhaps equivalent to vala + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *valit'ak (compare Estonian valima, Karelian valita, Veps valita, Võro valima, valitsõma, Votic valittsa), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waljaną and further derived with + -ita.

parole.significato: harness (restraint or support consisting of a loop or network of rope or straps)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valjas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian walis (“drawbar”)). Cognate to Estonian valjad (“headstall”), Estonian valjastada, Ingrian valjaat, Votic valʹlʹad (“bridle”), Karelian vaľľahad, Ludian vaľľahad, Veps vaľľastuz.

parole.significato: to whiten, blanch, bleach (to become lighter or whiter in color)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valgët'ak. Equivalent to valkea (“light, white”) + -eta.
From Proto-Finnic *valju.

parole.significato: haven (protected harbour or anchorage for small boats)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valkama, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlka- (“to descend, to go down”). Compare Erzya валгомс (valgoms, “to alight”).

parole.significato: white, (very) light (with a white or off-white color)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valkëda (compare Estonian valge, Karelian valkie /valgie), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlketa (compare Northern Sami vielgat, Erzya валдо (valdo), Eastern Mari волгыдо (volgydo)), from *wëlke (“light”) (compare Hungarian világ).
From Proto-Finnic *valdit'ak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waldaną and further derived with + -ita.
From Proto-Finnic *valmis.
From Proto-Finnic *valmistadak, equivalent to valmis (“ready, finished”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *valo, probably from the same root as valkea.

From Proto-Finnic *valta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waldą (“might, power, authority”) or Proto-Norse [script needed] (*walda-) (compare Swedish våld, German Gewalt, Dutch geweld, Icelandic vald). First attested in 1215 (in the surname Kaikewalde).

parole.significato: to run, flow (slowly), stream (slowly), pour, drip, trickle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valudak, equivalent to valaa (“to cast, pour”) + -ua.

parole.significato: to trickle, run, pour (cause to trickle or stream)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valuttadak, equivalent to valua (“to flow, trickle”) + -ttaa (causative verb).

parole.significato: wake, trail, track (path left behind an object that moves through a fluid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vana (compare Karelian vana, Ludian vana).
From Proto-Finnic *vanha (compare Estonian vana), from Proto-Uralic *wanša (compare Komi-Zyrian важ (važ), Udmurt вуж (vuž)).
From Proto-Finnic *vanhëmpi.

parole.significato: old age, age (latter stage of life)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vanhuc, from vanha (“old”) + -uus.
From Proto-Finnic *vankkuri (compare Estonian vanker, Ingrian vankkuri, Votic vankkuri), of unknown further etymology; possibly a Germanic borrowing from an unidentified etymon.

parole.significato: a staff with a hook at one end; used as a tool for turning over logs in slash-and-burn cultivation
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vanko (cognate with Estonian vang and Võro vang), from Proto-Finno-Permic *waŋka, probably borrowed from Indo-Iranian (compare Sanskrit वङ्क (vaṅka, “crooked”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vatnas (compare Estonian vannas, Livonian va’dmõl (“stem of a ship”), Ludian vannaz, Veps vadnaz), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wagnaz.

parole.significato: hoop, band (of a barrel, or a similar ring used to bind an object)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vandëh, from earlier *vandeš, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wanduz. Cognate with Karelian vanneh, Veps vandeh, Ludian vandeh.
From Proto-Finnic *vannodak.
From Proto-Finnic *vant'us, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wantuz (“glove, mitten”).

parole.significato: to felt, mat (of fabrics, garments: become smaller and more dense, e.g. by becoming wet and then being pressed)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vanudak.

parole.significato: to full, walk (to make cloth denser and firmer by soaking, beating and pressing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vanuttadak. Equivalent to vanua (“to felt, mat”) + -ttaa.

parole.significato: to furrow (cut or make furrows in soil)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vagot'ak. Equivalent to vako (“furrow”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *vapa (compare dialectal Estonian vaba (“fishing rod”), Ingrian vapa (“net drying rack”), Karelian vapa (“pole; fishing rod”), Livonian vabā (“net drying rack”), Votic vapa (“net drying rack”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vapada, probably borrowed from early Proto-Slavic *svabadā (later *svoboda (“freedom”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vabistak (compare Estonian vabisema, Ingrian vavissa, Karelian vavissa). The strong grade -p- has been levelled to all forms, except in the alternative form vavista.

parole.significato: reserve, backup (that which is reserved or kept back, as for future use)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vara (compare Estonian vara), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *warō (compare Swedish vara (“goods”), vara (“care”), English ware (“aware”), aware, ware (“goods”)).
From Proto-Finnic *varak'as, equivalent to vara (“means, resources”) + -kas.
From Proto-Finnic *vargas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wargaz.
From Proto-Finnic *vargastadak, equivalent to varas (“thief”) + -taa. Cognate with Estonian varastama, Karelian varastoa, Veps vargastada, Votic vargõssa.

Through metathesis, from Proto-Finnic *varahin, the instructive plural of Proto-Finnic *varas (compare dialectal Finnish varas, Livonian varāz, Veps varaz, Votic varaz), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *vāras (compare Lithuanian võras (“old”)). Related to Estonian vara, Ingrian varahiin, Karelian varahin

parole.significato: early (near the start of the day or something else; at a time in advance of the usual)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varahainën, equivalent to varha- (dialectal adjective varas) + -inen; see varhain.

parole.significato: hooded crow, grey crow, Corvus cornix
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varis, from Proto-Uralic *warᴈ. Cognates include Estonian vares, Veps variš, Karelian varis, Erzya варака (varaka), Moksha варси (varsi) and Hungarian varjú. Likely an onomatopoeic word, compare Russian воро́на (voróna).

parole.significato: to shed, lose, drop (generally of leaves)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varistak, possibly ultimately sound-symbolic. Compare karista.
From Proto-Finnic *varjëldak, equivalent to varj- + -ella, with a root borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *warjaną.
From Proto-Finnic *varma (“strong, sturdy”) (compare Estonian varmas, Ingrian varma, Karelian varma, Veps varmed, Votic varmõ).
From Proto-Finnic *varpa.
From Proto-Finnic *varp'ëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] *hwerbaną "to turn", (whence Swedish varv (“layer, turn, layer of logs in building”)). Doublet of varvi.

parole.significato: twig, bare twig (small thin branch of a tree or bush, especially one that has been separated from said tree or bush)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varpu, probably derived from *varpa. Cognates include Estonian varb, Livvi varbu and Veps barb. Also related to varvas.
From Proto-Finnic *varpuinën, borrowed from Old East Slavic вороби́и (vorobíi) (compare Russian воробе́й (vorobéj)); nativized with the diminutive -nen suffix.

parole.significato: skewer, spit, broach (pin used to secure food during cooking)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vardas, possibly derived from *varci (whence varsi). Cognate with Estonian varras.
From Proto-Finnic *varsa (compare Livonian vārza), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wŕ̥šā (compare Sanskrit वृषन् (vṛṣan, “male animal”)).

parole.significato: A long, narrow, (relatively) straight part of something:
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varci (compare Estonian vars), probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *warte (compare Eastern Mari вурдо (vurdo)).

Unknown. The predominant variant in Tavastian and Central Finnish dialects, as well as in Värmland Savonian; often considered related to the synonymous vartta, found in most of the other dialects (Southwestern Finland, Ostrobothnia, Lapland, Southeastern Finland and many Savonian dialects). The latt

parole.significato: guard, security guard (a person employed to provide security for specific people or specific property)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vartija, *vartja, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?]. Related to Estonian vardja (“bailiff”), Karelian vartie.
From Proto-Finnic *vartodak, equivalent to vart- + -oa, the root being borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wardāną.

From Proto-Finnic *varbas, possibly from *varpa (“twig”), which is also the origin of varpu. Cognates include Estonian varvas, Ingrian varvas, Karelian varvas/varvaš, Veps barbas, Votic varvõz and Livonian vārbaz.

parole.significato: fawn, calf (of e.g. a deer, elk or antelope)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vasa (compare Ludian vaza), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wasa (compare Inari Sami vyesi, Erzya ваз (vaz)), borrowed from Proto-Iranian *wacáh (“yearling calf”) (compare Digor Ossetian уӕс (wæs)).
From Proto-Finnic *vasama.
From Proto-Finnic *vasara, from Proto-Finno-Permic *waśara (compare Erzya узере (uzere)), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wáȷ́ras (compare Sanskrit वज्र (vájra)).
From Proto-Finnic *vasën, from Proto-Uralic *wasa (originally with the comparative suffix -mpi).
From Proto-Finnic *vasikka. Equivalent to vasa + -ikka (diminutive).

From Proto-Finnic *vaski, from Proto-Uralic *wäśkä ~ *waśke. Cognate with Estonian vask, Erzya уське (uśke) and Hungarian vas. Originally meant “copper” in a broad sense; displaced later by borrowings (e.g. kupari (“copper”), pronssi (“bronze”), messinki (“brass”)) in practically all of these senses
From Proto-Finnic *vaskicca. Equivalent to vaski (“copper”) + -itsa, after their color.

From Proto-Finnic *vasta (compare Estonian vast, Livonian vastõ, Votic vassõ), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wasta (“a place opposite or across”) (compare Northern Sami vuostá (“towards, against”), Erzya вастомс (vastoms, “to meet”), Moksha васта (vasta, “spot, place”), Eastern Mari ваштареш (vaštareš, “

parole.significato: to answer, to reply; to respond
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vastat'ak, equivalent to vasta- (“against”) + -ta. * (to correspond to): Probably a semantic loan, ultimately from Medieval Latin correspondeō (“to correspond”) (from respondeō (“to respond”)). * (to be responsible for, in charge for, accountable to): Semantic loan from Swedish an

parole.significato: a type of small seine (fishing net)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vata, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wadaz (compare Swedish vad, Old Norse vaðr).

From Proto-Finnic *vackat'ak (compare Karelian vatkata), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wačka- (compare Erzya вачкамс (vačkams, “to pile up”), вачкодемс (vačkodems, “to stick”), Eastern Mari вӱчкалташ (vüčkaltaš, “to pat on the back”) and possibly Eastern Khanty [Term?] (“to spread water with one's hand”))

parole.significato: belly, abdomen (part of the body between the thorax and the pelvis, not including the back)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vacca (compare Estonian vats, Karelian vačča, Veps vac).
From Proto-Finnic *vatvodak. Related to Karelian vatvuo, Veps vaduda and Votic vadvoa.

parole.significato: small ring or loop made of wicker
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vakla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wadlaz (whence English wattle).

From Proto-Finnic *vapras (compare Estonian vapper, Karelian vabras, Võro vabras), probably originally meaning "lively, brisk, breezy, healthy", possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wabraz (no exact Germanic descendants are known, but it would be from the same root that gave Old Norse vafra).
From Proto-Finnic *vëhka.
From Proto-Finnic *vëhmas, possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian vešùmas).

From Proto-Finnic *vehnä (compare Ingrian vehnä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wešnä (“spelt, wheat”) (compare Erzya виш (viš, “spelt”)), perhaps of substrate origin. Introduced into the standard language from Eastern Finnish in the 19th century, replacing the Western Finnish word nisu.
From Proto-Finnic *veikko. Cognates include Ingrian veikko, Karelian veikko, Livvi veikoi and Veps veik. Perhaps related to Komi-Zyrian вок (vok).
From Proto-Finnic *väictädäk. Equivalent to vei(t)s- (“knife”) + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *veiterä.
From Proto-Finnic *väicci, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wäŋćɜ (compare Hungarian vés (“chisel”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vëlho, borrowed from Old East Slavic вълхвъ (vŭlxvŭ).
From Proto-Finnic *velji (compare Estonian veli and further also Northern Sami viellja), probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swelijô (compare Old Norse svilar).
From Proto-Finnic *vëlka (compare Estonian võlg, Karelian velka, Veps velg).
From Proto-Finnic *vembel.

From Proto-Finnic *veneh (compare Estonian vene), from Proto-Finno-Permic *weneš (compare Erzya венч (venč)). The word is attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but was originally mainly characteristic of the eastern as well as Ostrobothnian dialects.

parole.significato: absolutely strange, utterly unknown, completely unfamiliar
parole.testo: vento + vieras (“stranger”), the former component from Proto-Finnic *vënto (compare Ingrian ventolain). Cognates include Estonian võnnuvõõras, Karelian ventovieraš, Votic ventõise võõras (hapax)).

parole.significato: to stretch (to cause to become longer by stretching)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *venüttädäk. Equivalent to venyä (“to stretch (intransitive)”) + -ttää.

parole.significato: to stretch (become longer by stretching, or by being pulled)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *venüdäk (compare Estonian venima), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wene-w- (compare Northern Sami vatnat, Erzya венемемс (venemems), Eastern Mari вийнаш (vijnaš)).
From Proto-Finnic *venät (genitive *venäden), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *winidaz (“Slav”).
From Proto-Finnic *veres, derived from *veri (whence veri). Related to Karelian vereš and Veps verez.

parole.significato: fresh, lush (especially of body parts like the skin, face or lips)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *verebä, equivalent to veri + -vä. Cognates include Võro verrev (“red”).

parole.significato: curtain, drape (piece of cloth covering a window)
parole.testo: verha (dialectal) + -o, from Proto-Finnic *vërha.

parole.significato: blood (liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veri (compare Estonian veri, Livonian ve’r), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *were (compare Northern Sami varra, Erzya верь (veŕ), Eastern Mari вӱр (vür), Udmurt вир (vir), Hungarian vér).
From Proto-Finnic *verinen, equivalent to veri (“blood”) + -inen.

parole.significato: broadcloth; a dense but (relatively) thin, short-pile, fairly smooth-faced woolen fabric woven of carded yarn, either p…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vërka, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *werką (“rope, cord”).
From Proto-Finnic *verkilo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wergilaz (whence Old Norse virgill).
From Proto-Finnic *vero, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *werᴈ. Cognate to Karelian vero, and possibly Votic vero and Veps vero.
From Proto-Finnic *vërsodak, equivalent to verso (“shoot (of a plant)”) + -oa.

parole.significato: match (equal or superior in comparison) (now mostly used in a number of idiomatic expressions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vërta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *werþaz (“worthy”). Doublet of väärti and vörtti.

parole.significato: A new shoot or sprout of a plant, especially a new branch of a tree or the new growth at the tip of a branch; a sucker,…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vësa. Cognate to Estonian võsa, Ingrian vesa, Karelian vesa, Livonian võzā, Livvi veza, Ludian veza, Veps veza and Votic võsa.
From Proto-Finnic *veci (compare Estonian vesi), from Proto-Uralic *wete (compare Erzya ведь (veď), Eastern Mari вӱд (vüd), Udmurt ву (vu), Hungarian víz, Tundra Nenets иˮ (yiq)).
From Proto-Finnic *vecinen, equivalent to vesi (“water”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *vetelä, equivalent to vete- (“water”) + -lä.

parole.significato: to become soaked (with water), become waterlogged
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vettüdäk. Equivalent to vesi (“water”) + -tyä.

parole.significato: to pull, drag, draw (to apply a pulling force)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vetädäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wetä- (compare Erzya ветямс (veťams), Hungarian vezet). Semantic development Most senses are straightforward from the original “to pull, drag, draw”. * (to wind (up) a mechanism): Often done by pulling on a part, a string, etc. * (to flush): Older

parole.significato: to take away, take, bring away
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veedäk (compare Estonian viima), from Proto-Uralic *wixe- (compare Skolt Sami viikkâd, Erzya виемс (vijems), Hungarian visz, Northern Selkup ӱ̄ӄо (ǖqo)).
From Proto-Finnic *veelä (compare Estonian veel), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vēl (“yet, still, again”), Lithuanian vėl (“again”)).
From Proto-Finnic *vëëno. Related to Ingrian veeno, Karelian vieno, Veps ven and Votic võõno.
From Proto-Finnic *veeras, probably from *veeri (equivalent to vieri (“side, edge”) + -as). Cognates include Estonian võõras, Veps veraz and Votic võõrõz.

parole.significato: side, edge (region immediately next to something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veeri, from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäre. Akin to Estonian veer, Northern Sami vierra (“ridge”) and Erzya вере (vere, “upside”), вирь (viŕ, “forest”).

parole.significato: to roll (move by turning over and over on a horizontal axis)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veerdäk + -iä. Same root with vieri. Cognate with Karelian vierrä.

parole.significato: wort (liquid extract from the ground malt and grain soaked in hot water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *verdek, borrowed from early Proto-Germanic *wertiz (later *wirtiz), and derived with + -e. Cognate with Estonian virre, Ingrian veerre, Livonian vīrdig and Votic virre.
From Proto-Finnic *veerdäk, a denominal verb of vieri (“side, edge”).
From Proto-Finnic *veertädäk. Equivalent to vieri (“side”) + -tää.
From Proto-Finnic *veettädäk. Equivalent to vie- (“to take away”) + -ttää (causative verb).

From Proto-Finnic *viha (compare Estonian viha), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wiša (compare Northern Sami vašši, Udmurt вож (vož, “hate”), Komi-Zyrian веж (vež, “envy”)), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wišás.
From Proto-Finnic *vihainën, equivalent to viha (“anger”) + -inen.
From Proto-Finnic *vihanta, from *viha (“greenness”) (the same root as in vihreä (“green”)) + -nta. Related to Veps vihand.
From Proto-Finnic *vihat'ak. Equivalent to viha (“hate, anger”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *vihtoin, possibly originally an instructive plural of *vihta (“time, occasion”) (in some dialects, vihdoin is attested with the meaning "once"; some Finnic cognates have different meanings, such as Veps vihtoi (“long ago”)). This could then be cognate with Proto-Samic *vëstē (when
From Proto-Finnic *viheltädäk, of onomatopoeic origin, compare Veps vihelta and Erzya вешкемс (veškems).

parole.significato: In some traditional hunting traps, a fence that serves to guide the prey towards the trap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vihi, probably a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *wīsijaną.
From Proto-Finnic *vihko (“bundle”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiskō, *wiskaz (“bundle of hay”).
From Proto-Finnic *vihma (“rain”).
From Proto-Finnic *vihneh, further origin unknown. Cognate with Ingrian vihne and Karelian vihneh.

Metathesized form of Proto-Finnic *viherä, derived by -rä from Proto-Uralic *wiša (see *viha). Further etymology and cognates. The metathesis -erä > -reä occurred by analogy with other adjectives with the ending -eä. For the unmetathesized form, compare viheriä (“greenish”), vihertää (“to become gre

parole.significato: bath broom, a kind of whip made of birch twigs and used in the sauna to enhance the effect of heat by beating oneself w…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vihta.

parole.significato: rush (any plant of the genus Juncus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vihvilä, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian viksva (“sedge”)).
From Proto-Finnic *viidenci, equivalent to viisi (“five”) + -s (“-th”).
From Proto-Finnic *vik'at'ëh (compare Estonian vikat, Veps vikateh, Votic vikahtõ), possibly borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian izkapts).
From Proto-Finnic *viikko, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᛁᚲᛟ (*wiko) (compare Swedish vecka, Old Norse vika and Icelandic vika), from Proto-Germanic *wikǭ (“week”).
From Proto-Finnic *viilek'eh. Possibly from viile- + -ke.
From Proto-Finnic *viildäk (compare Veps vilʹda).

parole.significato: last, past (most recent, last so far)
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Finnic *viimä- (whence also viimeinen (“last”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wiŋe-mä (same root *wiŋe as in viipyä (“to stay”)). The final vowel may be by analogy with viimein, viimeinen (note however the dialectal viimi, also found in Karelian viimi).
From Proto-Finnic *viimeinen, equivalent to viime (“last”) + -inen.

parole.significato: liquor (US), spirits (UK, AU, NZ) (distilled alcoholic beverage; rather strong and often clear, such as vodka)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viina, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wīną, from Latin vīnum. Doublet of viini.

parole.significato: to stay, remain (for some time); to dwell on, linger
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viipüdäk. Equivalent to vii- + -pyä, from the same root as in viime.
From Proto-Finnic *viiru.
From Proto-Finnic *viisas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wīsaz (compare Swedish vis (“wise”)).
From Proto-Finnic *viici (compare Estonian viis), from Proto-Uralic *witte (compare Erzya вете (vete), Northern Khanty вет (wjet), Northern Mansi ат (at), Hungarian öt, Nganasan бииˮ (biiʔ, “ten”)).

parole.significato: group of five; fivesome, pentad, quintuplet, pentuplet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viicikkoi. Equivalent to viisi (“five”) + -ikko.
From Proto-Finnic *viici kümmentä. Equivalent to viisi (“five”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).
From Proto-Finnic *viici toicta (kümmentä) (literally “five of the second decade”). Equivalent to viisi (“five”) + -toista (“of the second”).

parole.significato: A thicket of young deciduous trees.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viita, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *widuz.

parole.significato: to bother (do something which is of negligible inconvenience), to feel like doing something
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viiccidäk. Cognates include Estonian viitsima, Ingrian viitsiä and Votic viittsiä.

parole.significato: sign (such as a road sign; clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures; especi…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viitta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᛁᛏᚨ (*wīta) (compare Icelandic viti (“sign, omen”)), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *wītaną.
From Proto-Finnic *vika, possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką. Cognate with Estonian viga.
From Proto-Finnic *vilahtadak, equivalent to vil- + -ahtaa

Derived from Proto-Finnic *vila (whence also vilahtaa) + -istä. Cognate with Ingrian vilissä, Karelian vilissä, and the same root is also found in Estonian vile (“quick, swift”), Livonian vi’llõ (“to zip, go past in a blur”).

parole.significato: grain, cereal, corn (type of grass cultivated for its edible grains)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vilja (compare Estonian vili, Karelian vil'l'a, Veps vilʹlʹ), borrowed from Balto-Slavic or Baltic (compare Proto-Slavic *obilъ, whence Russian обилие (obilije, “abundance”) and Czech obilí (“grain”)); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: lively, vivacious, perky (of a living thing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vilk'as. Related to Estonian vilgas, Ingrian vilkas and Karelian vilkas.

parole.significato: to flash, to blink, to flicker
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vilkkudak.

From Proto-Finnic *villa (compare Estonian vill), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *wílˀnāˀ (compare Lithuanian vi̇̀lna, Polish wełna), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ (compare English wool, French laine).
From Proto-Finnic *villainën, equivalent to villa (“wool”) + -inen.

parole.significato: deceit, mendacity, fraud (act of deceiving someone)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vilppi (compare Karelian vilppi, Votic vilppi).
From Proto-Finnic *vilu.
From Proto-Finnic *vimma.
From Proto-Finnic *vimpa.
From Proto-Finnic *vinka.
From Proto-Finnic *vinkudak, ultimately onomatopoeic. Cognate with Estonian vinguma, Livonian vingõ and Veps vinkta.

parole.significato: oblique, askew, crooked, diagonal, skew, lopsided
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vino, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *wińa (compare Ter Sami [script needed] (va̭nnai̭jᵃ), Erzya венежа (veneža)).
From Proto-Finnic *vipu. Cognates include Estonian vibu, Ingrian vipu, Karelian vipu, Livonian vi’b, Veps bibu and Votic vipu.

parole.significato: A light breeze or the small, disappearing waves on top of water produced by a breeze.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virek. Cognate with Estonian vire, Karelian vire and Votic vire.

parole.significato: active, animate, alert, lively, vibrant, vigorous
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viredä (compare Estonian vire), probably originally a variant of virkeä.

parole.significato: to tune, adjust, tweak (a device, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virittädäk, equivalent to vireä (“active, animate”) + -ittää. Related to Karelian viritteä, Votic virittää (Kattila) and possibly Erzya верьгедемс (veŕgedems, “to ignite”).

parole.significato: line or row, especially of traps or snares
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian verdze).
From Proto-Finnic *virkedä. Related to virota, Estonian virge, Karelian virota, Livonian virgõ and Ludian virgota.
From Proto-Finnic *virkkadak. Related to Ingrian verkkaa, Karelian virkkua and Veps virkta.
From Proto-Finnic *virkku, equivalent to virkk- + -u, from the same root as virkeä (“perky, attentive, alert”).
From Proto-Finnic *virna.

parole.significato: to resuscitate, regain consciousness, come to, come to one's senses
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virgot'ak, equivalent to virke- (“alert, attentive”) + -ota.
From Proto-Finnic *virpa, borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian virbs, Lithuanian vir̃bas).
From Proto-Finnic *virpi, a variant of *virpa (whence virpa).
From Proto-Finnic *virdat'ak, equivalent to virta (“current, flow, stream”) + -ta.

From Proto-Finnic *virci, from earlier *virti, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wirdas (compare Latvian vārds (“word, name”) and Old Prussian wīrds), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (compare English word, Latin verbum). Doublet of verbi.
From Proto-Finnic *vircca (“slurry”). Cognate with Estonian virts.

parole.significato: to languish (to live in miserable or disheartening conditions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virudak (compare dialectal Estonian viruma (but standard Estonian virutama), Veps viruda (“to be bed-ridden”)).
From Proto-Finnic *viruttadak, equivalent to virua + -ttaa.

parole.significato: synonym of visakoivu (“wood obtained from a mutation of the silver birch”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *visa (“hard, tough, durable”) (compare Estonian visa, Karelian visa, Livonian vizā). Originally an adjective meaning “hard, tough”; this is now exclusively found in dialects and some derivations, like visakoivu (literally “hard birch”). The modern sense “quiz” is a backformation o

parole.significato: to throw, cast, toss, chuck, fling, hurtle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viskait'ak.

parole.significato: continuative of viskata (“to toss or throw”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viskoidak, equivalent to viskata (“to throw, toss”) + -oa.
Illative singular of the rare dialectal adjective vitka, from Proto-Finnic *vitka.

parole.significato: to scutch, swingle (to beat or flog for extracting the fibers from flax stalks)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vitodak, from Proto-Uralic *wiča-.

parole.significato: birch (stick, rod or bundle of twigs made from birch wood, used for punishment)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vicca, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiþjǭ. Doublet of vitja.

parole.significato: a traditional kind of plough with a sharp knife-like blade, used to dig up hardened soil
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Estonian vihk, Ingrian viuhka (“fang”)).
From Proto-Finnic *voohla (from earlier *(v)oošëla), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian oželis), if not a native *-la diminutive of *voohi.
From Proto-Finnic *voi (compare Estonian või), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waje (compare Northern Sami vuodja, Erzya ой (oj), Western Mari ӱ (ü), Udmurt вӧй (vöj), Hungarian vaj).

parole.significato: oh, bloody, damn, too (used as intensifier before expletives, mild and vulgar alike)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voi (compare Ingrian voi, Karelian voi, Livonian võih, Ludian voi, Veps voi).
From Proto-Finnic *voidëk. Equivalent to voitaa (“to grease, oil”) (obsolete) + -e.
From Proto-Finnic *voima. Equivalent to voi- (“can, to be able”) + -ma.

parole.significato: synonym of voidella (“to grease, oil; to butter; to lubricate”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voitadak. Equivalent to voi (“butter”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *voittadak. Equivalent to voida (“can, to be able”) + -ttaa.
From Proto-Finnic *voitto, equivalent to voittaa (“to win, prevail”) + -o.
From Proto-Finnic *voo, from Proto-Uralic *wuwa (“current, flow”).

parole.significato: bed (prepared spot in which to spend the night; one's place of sleep or rest)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voodëk ~ *voodëh, possibly equivalent to vuota (“hide”) + -e. A native derivation from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aďe- (“to set the bed”) has also been proposed. Cognate with Estonian voodi.

parole.significato: goat, Capra hircus, syn. Capra aegagrus hircus (domestic goat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voohi (compare Ingrian voohi, Votic voho), borrowed from a Baltic language (compare Latvian āzis, Lithuanian ožys, Old Prussian wosee).

parole.significato: pastern (area on a horse's leg between the fetlock joint and the hoof)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voohinën.

parole.significato: to carve, whittle (wood or a similar material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vooldak, from Proto-Uralic *wale-.
From Proto-Finnic *vootna. Related to Ingrian voonna, Karelian vuonu, Veps vodnaz and Votic võdnõ. Possibly derived from *vooci, or borrowed from Baltic.

parole.significato: mountain (large mass of earth and rock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voori, from Proto-Uralic *wëre ~ *ware (compare Udmurt выр (vyr)). Compare vaara, a Sami borrowing possibly from the same Uralic root.

parole.significato: turn (chance to use (something) shared in sequence with others; spell of work; one's chance to make a move in a game)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vooro. Cognates include Estonian voor (“round (of a competition), turn”), Ingrian vooro, Karelian vuoro and Votic vooro.
From Proto-Finnic *vooci, from Proto-Uralic *ëde.

parole.significato: hide, pelt (removed but otherwise untreated skin of an animal, particularly a large animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voota, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian oda).

parole.significato: to leak, run, trickle, flow; to ooze, seep; to drip, drop
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vootadak, equivalent to vuo (“flow”) + -taa.
From Proto-Finnic *viühti (compare Estonian viht, Karelian viyhti, Veps vihťak), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiftiz (“weaving”).

parole.significato: to roll (cause a large mass, e.g. a large rock or a large amount of snow, to descend out of control, like rocks in a ro…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vöörüttädäk, equivalent to vyöryä (“to roll”) (intransitive) + -ttää.

parole.significato: to roll (of a large mass, e.g. a large rock or a large amount of snow: descend out of control, e.g. by turning over and…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vöörüdäk.

parole.significato: little, few, scarce (low in number or amount)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vähä (compare Estonian vähe, Votic vähä), from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäšä (compare Erzya вишка (viška, “little”), веженсь (veženś, “youngest”)).

Either from Proto-Finnic *väijüdäk (compare Livonian ve’jjõ (“to fish”)), or alternatively equivalent to väijä- + -yä (from the same Old Swedish verb as vääjätä), through earlier *väɣjy- (compare third-person plural indicative wäghyuet attested in Agricola's writings).

parole.significato: to claim, contend, assert, argue, maintain, allege
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vägittädäk, equivalent to vä(k)i- (“force”) + -ittää.

parole.significato: chewing louse (any louse of the obsolete suborder Mallophaga)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *väiveh (compare Estonian väiv, Karelian väiveh, Votic väive), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vievesà).

From Proto-Finnic *väkebä, derived from *väki (“strength, power”). Equivalent to väki (“power, force, strength”) (now archaic in this sense) + -vä. As a noun, short for väkevä alkoholijuoma, a legal term for liquor that contains more than 22 percent alcohol by volume.
From Proto-Finnic *väkicin, equivalent to väki (“force”) + -isin, or the instructive plural of väkinen.
From Proto-Finnic *väkä, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wēgǭ, *wēgō (whence German Waage and Swedish våg); see vaaka.
From Proto-Finnic *väljä. Possibly ultimately from the same root as valkea.

parole.significato: to blink, flash (to flash on and off at regular intervals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *välkküdäk.

parole.significato: to avoid, evade, escape, dodge; to avert (a disaster)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *välttädäk. Cognates include Estonian vältama, Ingrian välttää, Karelian välttyä /välttiä, Livvi vältiä and Votic välttä.
From Proto-Finnic *väristäk. Related to Estonian värisema, Ingrian värissä, Livonian ve’ržõ, Veps värišta and Votic värisse.

parole.significato: wagtail (any bird of the family Motacillidae, which includes wagtails and pipits)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *västärikko (compare Estonian västrik, Ingrian väistärikko, Karelian päistärikkö, väistärikkö, Votic vässo), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric (compare Northern Sami beštor, Erzya уськерей (uśkerej), Southern Khanty вәрться̈к (wərt’sjäk), Eastern Mansi уртшых (urtšyh)), but probably
From Proto-Finnic *väsüttädäk, equivalent to väsyä (“to tire, get tired”) + -ttää (causative verb).
From Proto-Finnic *väsüdäk.
From Proto-Finnic *vävü, from Proto-Uralic *wäŋew, cognate to e.g. Estonian väi, Northern Sami vivva, Hungarian vő, Veps vävu and Nganasan биӈи (biŋi).
From Proto-Finnic *väntädäk (compare Estonian väänama, Ingrian vääntää, Livonian vändõ, Veps väta).

From Proto-Finnic *väärä, of unknown further origin. Semantic development * "crooked, bent" is probably the original sense; compare the semantic development of English wrong from its original sense of "crooked, twisted".

parole.significato: core, kernel, nucleus, the central part of something
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *üdin (“bone marrow”) (compare Estonian üdi, Karelian yjin), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wideme ~ *wüdeme ~ *wädeme (“bone marrow”) (compare Northern Sami ađa (“(bone with) marrow”), Erzya удем (udem, “marrow; intellect”), Eastern Mari вем (vem, “marrow”), Hungarian velő (“marrow”)).
From Proto-Finnic *ükteksä kümmentä. Equivalent to yhdeksän (“nine”) + kymmentä (“tens”, partitive).

From Proto-Finnic *ükteksä(n) toicta (kümmentä) (literally “nine of the second decade”). Equivalent to yhdeksän (“nine”) + -toista (“of the second”) (see yhdeksän for more information on its development).
From Proto-Finnic *ükteksänci. Equivalent to yhdeksä- (“nine”) + -s (“-th”).

From Proto-Finnic *ükci (compare Estonian üks), from Proto-Uralic *ükte (compare Northern Sami okta, Erzya вейке (vejke), Eastern Mari ик (ik), Udmurt одӥг (odig), Northern Mansi акв (akv), аква (akva)).
From Proto-Finnic *ükci toicta (kümmentä) (literally “one of the second decade”). Equivalent to yksi (“one”) + -toista (“of the second”).
From Proto-Finnic *ülen, the instructive singular of ylä- (yle-).

parole.significato: over [with genitive] (to or through the space that is above something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *üli, from Proto-Uralic *üle (compare Northern Sami ala, Erzya вель- (veľ-), вельга (veľga), Western Mari вӹлӓн (vÿlän), Udmurt выл (vyl), Northern Khanty єԓ (êł), Tundra Nenets ниʼ (nyih)).
From Proto-Finnic *ülkä, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ülkä (“boy, son”) (cognate with Proto-Samic *ëlkē).

Now analyzed as the consonant-stem allative of the stem ylä-, but originally either from Proto-Finnic *ülek with later influence from the allative ending -lle, or simply analogically created with it based on yllä, yltä (analyzed as the adessive and ablative, respectively).

From Proto-Finnic *üllä (compare Estonian üll), from older *ülnä < *üle-nä, an archaic locative formed with Proto-Uralic *-na (whence the essive suffix -na) from yli- (“over”) (see yli for further etymology). Now analyzed as a consonant-stem adessive of the stem ylä-.
From Proto-Finnic *ülpedä. Related to Estonian ülbe, Ingrian ylpiä, Karelian ylpie and Votic ülpiä. Possibly ultimately from ylä-.
From Proto-Finnic *ültüdäk. Equivalent to yltää (“to reach”) + -yä. Cognates include Veps üldüda.

From Proto-Finnic *ültä (compare Estonian ült), from older *ültä < *üle-tä, an archaic inflected form with the ablative suffix Proto-Uralic *-ta onto yli- (“over”) (see yli for further etymology). Now analyzed as the consonant-stem ablative of the stem ylä-.
From Proto-Finnic *ülä (compare Estonian üla-); see yli for more.
From Proto-Finnic *üles. Equivalent to ylä-/yle- (“upper, above”) + -s (s-lative singular), with labialization from dialectal yles.

From Proto-Finnic *ümbärtädäk. Roughly equivalent to ympäri (“around”) + -tää, thus initially “to go around, surround”. The sense “to understand” could be understood as a figurative development of 'surrounding' something with one's mind.

parole.significato: around (from one state or condition to an opposite or very different one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ümpärik (compare Estonian ümber, Ingrian ympäär, Livonian immõr, Veps ümbri, Votic ümperi), equivalent to lative ympär- + -i, the root ultimately derived from Proto-Germanic *umbi.
From Proto-Finnic *üknä, earlier essive case of yksi (“one”).

Probably fronted from Proto-Finnic *ustava (compare Estonian ustav (“loyal, faithful”)), a consonant-stem variant of the present passive participle of uskoa (vowel stem variant uskottava). Alternative theories posit that the word is a reduction of the present passive participle of *üskätä (“to embra

From Proto-Finnic *öö (compare Estonian öö, Karelian yö, Livonian īe), from Proto-Uralic *üje ~ *eje (compare Northern Sami idja, Inari Sami ijjâ, Moksha ве (ve), Udmurt уй (uj), Komi-Zyrian вой (voj), Southern Mansi йӣ (jī), Hungarian éj).

parole.significato: to gag, retch (to experience the vomiting reflex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *öök'ät'äk, of onomatopoeic origin.
From Proto-Finnic *äges, possibly borrowed from a Baltic language, compare Lithuanian akečios. Cognate to Estonian äke and Veps ägez.
From Proto-Finnic *ägestädäk. Equivalent to äes (“harrow”) + -tää

parole.significato: to grunt, groan, moan (in a continuous manner, such as during physical effort)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ähkidäk, of onomatopoeic origin. Cognate to Estonian ähkima.

From Proto-Finnic *äijä (compare Karelian äijä (“a lot, great, tall, many”), Veps äi (“a lot”)), from Proto-Finno-Permic *äjjä (compare Northern Sami áddjá (“old male relative”), Erzya оя (oja, “friend”), Udmurt айы (ajy, “father, male”)).

parole.significato: A large (and usually blunt-tipped) needle shaped for working with tough materials, such as a leather needle or sailmake…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *äimä, from Proto-Uralic *äjmä (compare Northern Sami áibmi, Eastern Mari име (ime), Komi-Zyrian ем (jem), Tundra Nenets нибя (nyibya)).
From Proto-Finnic *äkedä. Equivalent to *äkä + -eä; the root is probably a front-vowel variant of *aka-, itself borrowed from Proto-Germanic *agaz. Related to Estonian äge and Karelian äkie.
From Proto-Finnic *äkki; see äkkiä for more.
From Proto-Finnic *äkkidä, the partitive singular of *äkki. Cognates include Estonian äkki, Ingrian äkkii, Karelian äkkie, Veps äkkid and Votic äčči.
From Proto-Finnic *ämmä (compare Estonian ämm, Livonian ǟma).
From Proto-Finnic *ängät'äk (compare Estonian ängama, Ludian ängida). The -e- may be by influence from ankea and/or tunkea.
From Proto-Finnic *äpärä, probably fronted from apara (“dregs, mash”).
From Proto-Finnic *äredä. Cognates include Estonian ärev, Ingrian ärrillää and Karelian ärie.

According to Ante Aikio (2020), from Proto-Finnic *äisäk (compare Estonian äsja, Ludian äskei, Võro äisäq), from Proto-Uralic *äńćä. This suggests a development from *äisäk > *äisäk(k)V- > *äiskV- > *eskV-/äskV-.

parole.significato: sound; noise (sound as a perceived or physical phenomenon; the sound emitted by something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ääni (compare Veps änʹ), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *äne (compare Northern Sami jietna, Hungarian ének). * (vote): Semantic loan from Swedish röst.
From Proto-Finnic *ääri (compare Estonian äär, Karelian eäreh (“away”)).
From Proto-Finnic *-s, either reduced from *-kse (translative ending): *-kse > *-ks > *-s, or alternatively from Proto-Uralic *-s (compare Erzya -с (-s) in эйс (ejs, “into”)).

parole.significato: Forms nouns, indicating resemblance or association.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-us. Probably generalized from -s-derivatives of u-stem nominals (e.g. etu- → edus, palvelu → palvelus), or through the loss of a plain u-derivative from the standard language (e.g. keski- → dial. kesku- → keskus), and thus identical to -us (etymology 1). In some cases potentially

parole.significato: Forms an adjective from a noun.
parole.testo: Two theories exist: * Of the same origin as the participle ending above (etymology 1), with the same levelling of the weak grade (*-ba). * Alternatively, from Proto-Finnic *-va, from Proto-Uralic *-ŋa.

From Proto-Finnic *ahma (“glutton”) (compare dialectal Estonian ahm (“glutton”), Ingrian ahmo (“greedy”), Karelian ahmo (“wolverine, glutton”), Ludian ahmo (“wolverine”)), probably ultimately borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Haćman- (compare Sanskrit अश्मन् (aśman, “eater”)). Related also to Proto-

From Proto-Finnic *aivan (an instructive singular, compare ihan), probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háywas, or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *aiwaz (“long time”). Cognate with Votic aiva (“always”) and Estonian aiva (“always”).

From Proto-Finnic *akkuna (compare Estonian aken), borrowed from Old East Slavic окъно (okŭno) (whence also Russian окно́ (oknó)) or from earlier Slavic, from Proto-Slavic *okъno. Compare Udmurt укно (ukno) (borrowed from the aforementioned Russian word).

parole.significato: a plant of the genus Filipendula
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *angër-, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vangarykštė) or alternatively from a hypothetical Proto-Norse [script needed] (*angan-wahstuʀ).
From Proto-Finnic *aukko (compare Estonian auk, Votic aukko), either derived from the same root as avata, aukea, or alternatively proposed to be a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *augô (“eye”).
